The duck meat is irregularly chunky, showcasing its succulent texture. Mushrooms are vibrant, adding varied textures. A delicate scattering of bright green thinly sliced spring onion and fresh coriander leaves floats on the surface, providing a fresh contrast. The bowl sits on a simple light wooden table, accompanied by a white ceramic Chinese soup spoon and a pair of dark wooden chopsticks. A clean white cotton napkin is placed beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting highlights the soup's clarity and rich colors, creating an inviting, authentic casual bistro aesthetic.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with steamed white rice on the side.
Offer a small dish of pickled vegetables (e.g., pickled daikon or cucumber) as an accompaniment.
instructions: Clean duck leg quarters. Pat duck dry.
Place duck in a large pot over medium-high heat. Sear duck skin-side down until golden and fat renders. Flip and sear briefly. Remove excess fat.
Add sliced ginger and smashed garlic to pot. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Return duck to pot. Add 1.5 liters water and 30ml Shaoxing wine.
Bring to a boil. Skim any foam from surface. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 1 hour.
Remove duck from pot. Let cool slightly. Debone duck. Cut duck meat into bite-sized chunks.
Strain broth through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean pot. Discard solids.
Clean chanterelle and shiitake mushrooms. Slice shiitake mushrooms thinly. Leave small chanterelles whole; halve larger ones.
Add prepared mushrooms to strained broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are tender.
Add duck meat chunks back to soup. Heat through.
Season soup with light soy sauce, salt, and white pepper to taste.
Ladle hot soup into individual serving bowls. Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and thinly sliced spring onion.
notes: This soup is best served immediately after preparation.
For richer flavor, use duck bones in the initial broth simmering.

recipes.recipe_name: King Oyster Mushroom & Kimchi Noodle Salad
recipes.visual_description: The King Oyster Mushroom & Kimchi Noodle Salad is plated on a clean white porcelain dish. It features a vibrant base of mixed greens. Thin, golden-brown slices of pan-seared king oyster mushrooms are artfully arranged. Translucent bean thread noodles are tossed with bright red chopped kimchi, julienned cucumber, and carrot. Small, succulent flakes of seared sea bream are sparingly distributed as a subtle protein. The components are lightly coated with a glossy, reddish-orange gochujang dressing. Toasted sesame seeds provide a final garnish. The plate maintains moderate negative space. The setting includes a simple wooden table, with chopsticks and a small rice bowl beside the plate, under natural, even lighting, emphasizing the dish's freshness and inviting appeal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with small individual bowls of extra dressing on the side for guests to add more to taste.
Accompany with a light Korean barley tea.
instructions: Cook bean thread noodles according to package directions. Rinse with cold water. Drain well.
Slice king oyster mushrooms into 0.5 cm rounds. Pan-sear in a hot pan with a little oil until golden brown and tender. Season with salt and pepper.
Pat sea bream fillet dry. Season with salt. Pan-sear skin-side down in hot oil for 3-4 minutes until skin is crispy. Flip and cook for 2-3 minutes until cooked through. Flake into small pieces.
For the dressing, whisk together gochujang, soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, honey, minced garlic, grated ginger, and water until well combined.
In a large bowl, combine mixed greens, julienned cucumber, julienned carrot, chopped kimchi, cooked bean thread noodles, and sliced spring onions.
Add the seared king oyster mushrooms and flaked sea bream.
Pour dressing over the salad ingredients. Toss gently to combine all ingredients evenly.
Divide the salad among four plates. Garnish with toasted sesame seeds.
notes: Adjust gochujang quantity to control the spice level according to preference.
Ensure all vegetables are thoroughly drained after washing to prevent a watery salad.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Carrot & Tomato Consommé, Sweet Onion Air
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents a minimalist, elegant composition within a wide, shallow bone china bowl, resting on a polished white Carrara marble surface. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, sits beside the bowl. The clear, deep amber Roasted Carrot & Tomato Consommé fills the bowl with abundant negative space around its central elements. Precisely diced, jewel-toned confit cherry tomatoes, cut into uniform 5mm cubes, are meticulously placed at the bottom, their deep red contrasting with the consommé's clarity. Floating atop the consommé is an ethereal cloud of bright white Sweet Onion Air, its delicate, stable bubbles catching the light. A single, vibrant green micro basil sprig is artfully positioned on the foam, adding a final touch of color and freshness. The scene is bathed in dramatic professional lighting, casting subtle shadows that enhance the dish's architectural precision and sophisticated simplicity.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss roughly chopped carrots, tomatoes, and yellow onion with a drizzle of olive oil on a baking sheet. Roast for 25 minutes, until slightly caramelized.

Transfer roasted vegetables to a large pot. Add celery, smashed garlic, bay leaf, peppercorns, and cold water. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat. Reduce heat to low. Simmer uncovered for 1.5 hours. Do not boil.
Carefully strain the consommé through a fine-mesh sieve lined with a double layer of cheesecloth. Discard solids. Return liquid to a clean pot. Season with salt. Keep warm over very low heat.

Combine cherry tomatoes, olive oil, sliced garlic, and thyme sprig in a small oven-safe dish. Season with salt and pepper. Bake at 140°C for 40 minutes, until tomatoes are soft and slightly wrinkled. Remove thyme and garlic. Drain tomatoes, reserving oil. Dice tomatoes into small, uniform 5mm cubes.

In a small saucepan, combine thinly sliced sweet onion and vegetable stock. Bring to a simmer. Cook until onion is very soft, about 10 minutes. Strain, reserving liquid. Discard solids. Let liquid cool slightly.
Pour onion liquid into a tall, narrow container. Add soy lecithin and a pinch of salt. Use an immersion blender to blend at the surface, creating a stable foam. Let foam rest for 1 minute.

Ladle 100ml of warm consommé into each of four shallow bowls. Place a small spoon of diced confit tomatoes precisely in the center of the consommé. Gently scoop a generous amount of sweet onion air onto the surface of the consommé, ensuring it floats. Place one micro basil sprig on top of the onion air. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Marinated Cucumber & Thyme Bites
recipes.visual_description: A rustic, shallow ceramic bowl holds thinly sliced Lebanese cucumbers. The cucumber rounds, cut into 3-4 mm thick slices, are bright green and glisten with a generous coating of olive oil. Small, dark green fresh thyme leaves are scattered throughout, adhering to the cucumber slices. The arrangement is casual and inviting, with some slices slightly overlapping and others resting naturally in the bowl, creating an organic, unpretentious mound. The bowl is placed on a well-used wooden dining table, revealing its natural grain. Warm, soft kitchen lighting illuminates the scene. A simple, off-white linen napkin is casually folded beside the bowl. The overall presentation evokes a homely family kitchen setting, emphasizing comfort and simplicity. The bowl is full but not overflowing, showcasing a generous portion ready for sharing.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve chilled as part of a mezze spread.
Offer with warm pita bread or toasted flatbread for scooping.
Pair with labneh or hummus for a complete snack.
instructions: Wash and thinly slice Lebanese cucumbers into rounds or half-moons.
Place sliced cucumbers in a medium mixing bowl.
Drizzle olive oil over the cucumbers.
Add fresh thyme leaves.
Season with sea salt and black pepper.
Gently toss to combine all ingredients.
Let sit for 5-10 minutes to allow flavors to meld.

recipes.recipe_name: Caldo de Arroz con Pimentón Ahumado y Tomate Fermentado (Smoked Paprika & Fermented Tomato Rice Broth)
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of 'Caldo de Arroz' is presented in a handcrafted ceramic bowl with a matte, earthy finish in cream or beige tones. The broth exhibits a rich, warm terracotta hue, a result of the smoked paprika and fermented tomato. Submerged within the liquid are pearly, plump short-grain rice kernels, clearly visible through the savory liquid. A small, vibrant green swirl of olive oil gently floats on the surface, offering a visual contrast. The dish is sparingly garnished with a few fresh, vivid green oregano leaves and a scattering of golden, crisped rice pieces, adding textural interest. The bowl rests on a light, reclaimed wood table, complemented by an undyed linen napkin. A rustic, simple ceramic spoon is placed alongside. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, enhancing the natural textures and colors. The background remains clean and minimalistic, with subtle hints of natural elements like a blurred plant, ensuring the focus remains on the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately, piping hot.
Offer crusty bread (pan rústico) for dipping into the broth.

ingredients.name: Vegetable scraps (e.g., onion ends, carrot peels, celery leaves, mushroom stems)

instructions: Prepare Fermented Tomato Paste: Roughly chop tomatoes. Mix with 1% salt by weight. Place in a clean jar. Ensure tomatoes are submerged under their liquid or a light brine. Ferment at room temperature for 5-7 days until tangy. Blend into a smooth paste. (This step requires pre-preparation).
Make Zero-Waste Vegetable Broth: Combine water, vegetable scraps, and bay leaf in a large pot. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat. Simmer for 45 minutes. Strain broth. Discard solids.
Cook Rice: Rinse rice thoroughly. Cook rice in 300ml water until just tender, about 15 minutes. Drain any excess water. Reserve 2 tablespoons of cooked rice for crispy garnish.
Prepare Crispy Rice Garnish: Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a small pan. Add reserved cooked rice. Fry until golden and crispy. Drain on paper towel. Season lightly with salt.
Sauté Aromatics: In a large pot, heat 2 tbsp olive oil over medium heat. Thinly slice garlic. Add sliced garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown.
Add Spices: Stir in smoked paprika and dried Mexican oregano. Cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Combine & Simmer: Pour in the strained vegetable broth and 100g of fermented tomato paste. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 10 minutes to meld flavors. Season with salt to taste.
Serve: Divide cooked rice among 4 individual bowls. Ladle hot broth over the rice. Drizzle each serving with a little fresh olive oil. Garnish with fresh oregano leaves and crispy rice.
notes: This recipe emphasizes reducing food waste by utilizing vegetable scraps for broth and transforming overripe tomatoes into a flavorful fermented paste.
The fermented tomato paste adds a complex, tangy depth that elevates the broth.

recipes.recipe_name: Veganer Aprikosen-Pflaumen Streuselkuchen mit Weinbrandglasur
recipes.visual_description: A single elegant slice of vegan streusel cake is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The cake slice features distinct layers: a light golden-brown, crumbly streusel topping with visible texture, followed by a vibrant layer of amber-hued apricots and dark, glistening prunes. Beneath the fruit, a soft, pale cake base is visible. A light, delicate drizzle of white brandy glaze cascades over the streusel and fruit, adding a subtle sheen. The cake slice is upright, showcasing its internal structure. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface, complemented by a neatly folded cotton napkin beside it. In the background, slightly out of focus, the remaining whole cake on a simple cake stand provides context. Natural, even lighting highlights the cake's textures and colors, creating an inviting, professional bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm or at room temperature with a cup of strong coffee or black tea.
Enjoy as part of 'Kaffee und Kuchen', a traditional German afternoon coffee and cake ritual.

ingredients.name: For the streusel: Vegan butter, cold and cubed
For the glaze: Water or lemon juice

instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease and flour a 23 cm springform pan.
For the cake base: In a large bowl, cream softened vegan butter and 150g granulated sugar until light and fluffy.
Gradually add vanilla extract and salt. Mix well.
In a separate bowl, whisk together 250g plain flour and baking powder.
Add dry ingredients to wet ingredients alternately with plant milk. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Spread cake batter evenly into the prepared springform pan.
For the fruit filling: In a bowl, combine halved apricots and prunes with 25ml apricot brandy and 15g cornstarch. Mix gently.
Arrange fruit mixture evenly over the cake batter.
For the streusel: In a medium bowl, combine 150g plain flour, 75g granulated sugar, and ground cinnamon.
Add cold, cubed vegan butter. Use fingertips to rub butter into flour mixture until coarse crumbs form. Do not overwork.
Sprinkle streusel topping evenly over the fruit layer.
Bake for 45-55 minutes, or until a wooden skewer inserted into the center of the cake comes out clean.
Remove cake from oven. Let cool in pan for 10 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.
For the glaze: In a small bowl, whisk powdered sugar, 15ml apricot brandy, and water or lemon juice until smooth. Adjust liquid for desired consistency.
Once cake is completely cool, drizzle glaze over the top.
notes: Ensure all ingredients are certified vegan.
For best flavor, use ripe, seasonal apricots when available.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Orchard Petit Fours
recipes.visual_description: Six to nine perfectly uniform miniature petit fours are arranged artfully on a light bamboo serving board. Each petit four features a golden-brown, square potato flour shortbread base, approximately 3cm in size, providing a delicate, crisp texture. A small, glistening quarter of ruby-red wine poached pear, its natural form preserved, sits atop the shortbread. Beneath the pear, a subtle layer of deeply caramelized, sweet red onion compote adds a dark, rich hue. The entire pear and compote are brushed with a clear, glossy chicken consommé glaze, providing a subtle sheen and depth of flavor. A few vibrant, lacto-fermented mixed berries are artfully placed next to each petit four, offering pops of deep red and blue. The composition is clean and minimalist, allowing natural colors and textures to shine. The background is uncluttered, featuring soft natural lighting and a hint of undyed linen. Handcrafted ceramic plates in earth tones are visible, suggesting an eco-conscious and authentic presentation style.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve chilled on an elegant, natural material platter, such as reclaimed wood or stone, reflecting Australia's connection to nature.
Offer as a sophisticated conclusion to a multi-course meal, paired with a light dessert wine or herbal tea.
instructions: Peel, core, and quarter pears. Set aside.
Combine red wine, water, honey, cinnamon stick, and star anise in a saucepan. Bring to a simmer.
Add pear quarters. Poach gently for 15-20 minutes until tender. Remove pears. Reduce poaching liquid by half until syrupy. Strain and cool.
Finely dice red onion. Melt butter in a small pan. Add onion and cook slowly over low heat for 20-25 minutes until deeply caramelized and sweet. Add balsamic vinegar; cook 2 minutes more. Cool.
For shortbread, combine potato flour, plain flour, and icing sugar. Cut in cold butter until crumbly. Add vanilla extract. Knead lightly to form a dough. Chill 30 minutes.
Roll dough to 3mm thickness. Cut into 3cm squares. Bake at 160°C (325°F) for 12-15 minutes until lightly golden. Cool on a wire rack.
For chicken glaze, reduce clarified chicken stock in a small saucepan over medium heat until syrupy and glossy. Cool slightly.

For lacto-fermented berries, lightly crush berries with sugar and a pinch of salt. Place in a small, clean jar. Cover loosely with a lid or cloth. Ferment at room temperature for 1-2 days until lightly fizzy and tangy. Refrigerate.

Assemble petit fours: Place a small dollop of caramelized onion on each shortbread square. Top with a poached pear quarter. Brush lightly with the reduced chicken glaze. Garnish with a few fermented berries.
notes: Using clarified chicken stock made from leftover bones and scraps embodies a zero-waste philosophy. Its subtle umami enhances the sweetness without making the dish savory.
The lacto-fermented berries add a vibrant, tangy element, contributing to the 'fermentation' and 'preservation' aspect of the dish.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Root Vegetable Crackers with Cacao Romesco
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a light-colored stone surface. Four handcrafted ceramic plates, in earthy cream tones, feature 3-4 irregularly shaped, golden-brown root vegetable crackers, 5-8 cm long, showcasing their rustic, textured surface. A rich, dark reddish-brown Cacao Romesco, smooth and thick, is spooned in natural dollops onto some crackers, or served in a small, minimalist ceramic bowl for dipping. The romesco's deep color contrasts with the lighter crackers. Roughly chopped, toasted hazelnuts are scattered around and over the romesco, adding warm brown hues and coarse texture. The composition is clean, ingredient-focused, and unfussy, emphasizing natural beauty. Soft, natural lighting highlights subtle color variations. An undyed linen napkin is casually folded. A small green plant in a terracotta pot sits unobtrusively in the background, reinforcing the eco-conscious theme.

ingredients.name: mixed root vegetables (carrots, parsnips, or beetroot), finely grated

instructions: Combine finely grated root vegetables, sourdough discard, ground flax seeds, water, salt, and pepper in a large bowl. Mix thoroughly until a uniform dough forms.
Cover the bowl with a clean cloth. Let dough ferment at room temperature for 8-12 hours, or until slightly bubbly and tangy.
Preheat oven to 160°C. Line a baking tray with parchment paper. Spread the dough thinly and evenly onto the parchment paper, about 2-3 mm thick. Score into irregular cracker shapes with a knife.
Bake for 30-40 minutes, or until crispy and golden brown. Let cool completely on a wire rack. Break into individual cracker pieces along the scored lines.
In a small bowl, whisk together romesco sauce, unsweetened cacao powder, sherry vinegar, and smoked paprika until well combined and smooth.

Arrange crackers on a serving platter. Spoon small dollops of Cacao Romesco onto each cracker or serve the romesco in a separate bowl for dipping. Sprinkle generously with toasted, roughly chopped hazelnuts.
notes: Adjust fermentation time based on ambient temperature and desired tanginess.
Crackers can be stored in an airtight container for up to 5 days.
This recipe utilizes sourdough discard, promoting zero-waste in baking.

recipes.recipe_name: Puerco Adobado con Salsa de Frijol Negro
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Puerco Adobado con Salsa de Frijol Negro is presented centrally on a round, clean white porcelain dinner plate. Tender, rustic chunks of braised pork, rich with a deep reddish-brown adobo and black bean sauce, are mounded generously. The sauce has a velvety, slightly thick texture, clinging to the pork. A sprinkle of bright green, freshly chopped cilantro and finely diced white onion provides a vibrant contrast on top. Beside the main dish, a small, traditional terracotta or ceramic bowl holds a small serving of vibrant pink pickled red onions. A stack of warm, golden corn tortillas is neatly arranged in a woven basket or wrapped in a clean cloth. The setting is a modern bistro style with a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A folded cotton napkin rests beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting the rich colors and textures of the pork and sauce. The background is minimal and slightly blurred, suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere without distraction. The entire plate and its accompaniments are visible, showing a balanced and approachable composition.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for scooping up the sauce and pork.
Accompany with Mexican red rice or white rice.
Offer pickled red onions or a simple lime-dressed cabbage slaw on the side for freshness and acidity.
instructions: Cut pork shoulder into 5 cm chunks. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear pork chunks on all sides until deeply browned. Remove pork and set aside.
Remove stems and seeds from dried chilies. Toast chilies in the same pot for 1-2 minutes until fragrant. Be careful not to burn them.
Cover toasted chilies with hot water. Let them rehydrate for 20 minutes until soft.
Meanwhile, dice half of the onion. Mince garlic cloves.
Add diced onion and minced garlic to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.

Drain rehydrated chilies. Transfer chilies to a blender with black bean paste, cumin, Mexican oregano, and 250 ml of chicken broth. Blend until very smooth. Strain sauce through a fine-mesh sieve into the pot to remove any solids, pressing solids to extract liquid.
Return seared pork to the pot with the strained sauce. Add remaining 500 ml chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and braise for 2-2.5 hours, or until pork is fork-tender. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Dice remaining half of the onion finely for garnish. Roughly chop fresh cilantro.
Warm corn tortillas before serving.
notes: For extra flavor, toast the chilies lightly in a dry pan before rehydrating.
The sauce can be made a day ahead and refrigerated.
traditional_techniques: Nixtamalization (for corn tortillas, if made from scratch)

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Tomato & Vegetable Consommé with Crispy Tofu
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of clear, amber-hued consommé is presented in a handcrafted, earthy-toned ceramic bowl. The broth is pristine, showcasing its clarified nature. Golden-brown, 2 cm diced crispy tofu cubes are thoughtfully arranged within the consommé, providing a textural contrast. A vibrant green swirl of garlic-chive oil artfully floats on the surface, adding a pop of color and aromatic richness. The plating is minimalistic, allowing ample white space around the bowl on a light bamboo or reclaimed wood table surface. A natural, undyed linen napkin rests subtly nearby. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish, emphasizing its clean lines and organic beauty. Chopsticks rest beside the bowl, hinting at its Chinese origin. The background is clean and uncluttered, with a subtle natural element like a potted plant visible, reinforcing the eco-conscious theme.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a light starter or alongside steamed jasmine rice.
Use a traditional ceramic Chinese soup spoon for serving.
Accompany with small dishes of pickled vegetables (e.g., pickled daikon or cucumber) for added zest.

ingredients.name: Assorted vegetable scraps (e.g., carrot peels, celery ends, mushroom stems)
Neutral cooking oil (e.g., sunflower or canola)
Chive ends or green onion tops

instructions: Prepare broth base. Combine roughly chopped fresh tomatoes, onion, crushed garlic, and vegetable scraps in a large pot. Add 1.5 litres water.
Bring to a simmer. Cook gently for 30 minutes. Do not boil vigorously.
Add fermented tomatoes. Simmer for another 15 minutes. This extracts deep umami and sour notes.
Strain broth through a fine-mesh sieve. Press solids gently to extract liquid. Discard solids responsibly.
Clarify consommé. Return strained broth to a clean pot. Bring to a gentle simmer. Skim any impurities from the surface. Maintain a clear, pure broth.

Prepare garlic-chive oil. Heat 3 tablespoons neutral oil in a small saucepan over low heat. Add chive ends and thinly sliced garlic. Gently fry until fragrant and crispy. Do not brown excessively. Strain oil, discard solids. Stir in 3 tablespoons toasted sesame oil. Set aside.
Prepare crispy tofu. Press firm tofu to remove excess water. Cut tofu into 2 cm cubes. Toss tofu cubes with cornstarch until lightly coated.

Heat 3 tablespoons neutral cooking oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Add tofu cubes in a single layer. Pan-fry until golden brown and crispy on all sides. Remove and drain on paper towel.
Season consommé with salt and white pepper to taste. Adjust seasoning for balance.
To serve, pour hot consommé into individual bowls. Arrange crispy tofu cubes in the consommé. Drizzle generously with garlic-chive oil. Serve immediately.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by utilizing vegetable scraps for a flavorful broth.
Fermented tomatoes add a unique depth of flavor and probiotic benefits, aligning with sustainable food practices.
The garlic-chive oil is made from chive ends, preventing food waste.
Adjust salt carefully as fermented ingredients can contribute salinity.

recipes.recipe_name: Torta de Chocolate Picante con Queso Crema
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegant slice of Torta de Chocolate Picante con Queso Crema is plated on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The cake slice reveals distinct layers: a rich, dark chocolate cake base with a subtle reddish-brown hue from the chili, separated by a thick, creamy white layer of cream cheese frosting. The chocolate cake has a fine, moist crumb. The frosting is smooth, with soft peaks on top of the slice. A few vibrant green, fresh coriander leaves are artfully placed on the plate beside the slice, adding a pop of contrasting color and freshness. In the background, slightly out of focus, sits the remaining whole cake, showcasing its beautifully frosted sides. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple wooden table surface and natural, even lighting, highlighting the cake's refined appearance. A plain white cotton napkin is folded neatly beside the plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve alongside a small cup of strong Peruvian coffee.
Best enjoyed as a dessert after a savory meal.
instructions: Preheat oven to 175°C. Grease and flour two 20 cm round cake pans.
In a large bowl, whisk together flour, sugar, cocoa powder, baking soda, baking powder, and salt.
Add eggs, milk, vegetable oil, vanilla extract, Aji Panca paste, and chipotle powder to the dry ingredients. Beat on medium speed for 2 minutes until well combined.
Carefully stir in hot water until batter is smooth. Batter will be thin.
Divide batter evenly between prepared cake pans.
Bake for 30-35 minutes, or until a wooden skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
Cool cakes in pans for 10 minutes. Invert onto wire racks to cool completely.
For the frosting, beat softened cream cheese and butter together in a medium bowl until creamy.
Gradually add sifted icing sugar, beating until light and fluffy. Add vanilla extract and a pinch of salt. Beat until smooth.
Once cakes are completely cool, level the tops if needed.
Place one cake layer on a serving plate. Spread about one-third of the frosting evenly over the top.
Place the second cake layer on top. Frost the top and sides of the entire cake with remaining frosting.
Garnish the top with fresh coriander leaves before serving.
notes: The chili and chipotle provide a subtle warmth and smokiness, not an overwhelming heat. Adjust quantities to personal preference.
Ensure cakes are completely cool before frosting to prevent melting.

recipes.recipe_name: Sweet Teff & Squash Fritters with Chili-Date Drizzle
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents as a minimalist arrangement of circular, golden-brown fritters, each about 7 cm in diameter. The fritters, made from fermented teff and mashed butternut squash, display a slightly porous texture from the fermentation, with subtle specks of darker date within. They are cooked to a soft interior and a lightly crisp exterior. A vibrant, deep amber chili-date drizzle is artfully spooned across and around the fritters, creating gentle, organic lines. A delicate dusting of toasted, finely crumbled mozzarella, infused with a whisper of cayenne, is scattered sparingly over the fritters, adding a subtle textural contrast and a hint of creamy white. The fritters are casually arranged on a handcrafted, matte cream-colored ceramic plate, leaving ample white space. The presentation emphasizes natural textures and colors, with soft natural light highlighting the fritters' earthy tones and the glaze's subtle sheen. The background is clean and uncluttered, featuring a light reclaimed wood surface and a soft, undyed linen napkin in a natural beige, with a hint of green from a nearby plant providing a touch of organic life.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a light snack alongside traditional Ethiopian coffee (Buna).
Offer as part of a larger spread of sweet and savory finger foods.
instructions: Combine teff flour, 300ml warm water, and yeast in a bowl. Mix until smooth. Cover loosely. Let ferment at room temperature for 12-24 hours until bubbly and slightly sour.
In a separate bowl, combine mashed squash and chopped dates. Mix well.
Gently fold the fermented teff batter into the squash-date mixture. Add 2g cayenne pepper and a pinch of salt. Mix until just combined.

Heat 15ml oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat. Drop spoonfuls (about 50g each) of batter into the pan, flattening slightly into rounds. Cook 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Repeat with remaining oil and batter.
Blend 50g dates and 50ml warm water until smooth. Stir in chili powder.
Spread grated mozzarella on a small baking sheet. Bake at 150°C (300°F) for 5-7 minutes until lightly golden and crispy. Let cool. Mix with a pinch of cayenne.
Arrange warm fritters on a plate. Drizzle with chili-date sauce. Sprinkle with toasted mozzarella crumble.
notes: For zero-waste, use vegetable scraps from the squash for stock.
The fermentation process can vary based on ambient temperature; adjust time as needed.
The mozzarella is a modern addition, offering a subtle creamy note to this traditional-inspired snack.

recipes.recipe_name: Gebackene Apfelspalten mit Aquavit-Zimt-Glasur
recipes.visual_description: A comforting display of baked apple slices arranged casually on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. The thick apple wedges are tender, slightly softened, and coated in a glossy, translucent amber glaze, reflecting the warm kitchen light. Natural hues of the apple skin, ranging from reddish-brown to pale green, contrast with the lighter, tender apple flesh. The slices are gently overlapping, forming a natural, unpretentious mound. The plate sits on a well-worn, light wooden kitchen table, showing subtle grain and character. A casually folded, plain linen napkin rests near the plate. The lighting is warm and soft, mimicking natural light from a kitchen window, casting gentle, inviting shadows. The background is minimal and slightly blurred, suggesting a lived-in family kitchen setting, perhaps with a glimpse of simple ceramic bowls or a wooden cutting board.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Wash apples. Core apples. Cut apples into thick wedges.
Arrange apple wedges in a single layer in a baking dish.
In a small saucepan, combine apple juice, sugar, and cinnamon. Bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Stir in aquavit and vegan butter until melted.
In a small bowl, whisk cornstarch with 15 ml cold water to create a slurry. Add slurry to the simmering glaze, whisking constantly until thickened.
Pour glaze evenly over apple wedges in the baking dish.
Bake for 20-25 minutes. Apples should be tender but still hold their shape.
Serve warm.

recipes.recipe_name: Italian Sausage, Broccoli Rabe, and Ditalini Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of hearty Italian Sausage, Broccoli Rabe, and Ditalini Soup is presented in a rustic, deep ceramic bowl. The rich, savory, reddish-brown broth holds visible pieces of crumbled, browned Italian sausage, tender dark green florets and stems of chopped broccoli rabe, and thin slices of earthy brown cremini mushrooms. Small ditalini pasta tubes are dispersed throughout the soup, adding substance. A generous sprinkle of freshly grated pale yellow Parmesan cheese rests on the soup's surface. The bowl is set on a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table. A simple, casually placed off-white linen napkin and a sturdy stainless steel spoon accompany the bowl. Warm, soft, natural lighting illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, inviting atmosphere typical of a family kitchen. The background is minimal, keeping the focus entirely on the comforting bowl of soup.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add Italian sausage, breaking it up with a spoon. Cook until browned, about 8-10 minutes. Drain excess fat.
Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and red pepper flakes. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add sliced mushrooms. Cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Pour in chicken broth and diced tomatoes. Bring to a simmer.
Add chopped broccoli rabe. Simmer 10 minutes until tender.
Stir in ditalini pasta. Cook according to package directions, about 8-10 minutes, until al dente.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Ladle soup into bowls. Serve with grated Parmesan cheese.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Poblano Peppers with Ricotta-Red Pepper Filling
recipes.visual_description: A single roasted poblano pepper, split lengthwise and carefully deseeded, lies gracefully on a clean white porcelain plate. The pepper, retaining its slight char from roasting, cradles a vibrant, creamy ricotta and red pepper filling. The filling is a warm, inviting orange-red, speckled with finely diced red pepper and hints of green cilantro. A delicate drizzle of pale crema Mexicana zigzags across the top of the filling, contrasting with the pepper's deep green. A light sprinkle of finely crumbled white Cotija cheese adds texture. Fresh, bright green cilantro leaves are artfully scattered for a final touch of color and freshness. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A neatly folded, off-white cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. A small, rustic ceramic bowl with a few lime wedges sits unobtrusively in the background. Natural, soft, even lighting highlights the dish, creating a casual yet refined bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas on the side.
Offer a small dish of salsa roja or salsa verde.
Accompany with a light Mexican beer or agua fresca.
instructions: Roast poblano peppers. Place on a baking sheet. Roast at 200°C for 20-25 minutes. Skin should blister and char.
Transfer roasted poblanos to a bowl. Cover tightly with plastic wrap. Let steam for 15 minutes.
Peel poblanos. Make a slit down one side. Carefully remove seeds and membranes. Keep stem intact.
Dice red bell pepper into small cubes. Finely dice yellow onion. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add diced red bell pepper and minced garlic. Cook for another 5 minutes until tender.
Transfer cooked vegetables to a bowl. Let cool slightly.
Add ricotta cheese, breadcrumbs, cumin, chili powder, salt, and pepper to the bowl with vegetables.
Chop half of the fresh cilantro. Add to the filling mixture. Mix well to combine.
Carefully spoon filling into each poblano pepper. Do not overstuff.
Place stuffed poblanos back on baking sheet. Bake at 180°C for 15-20 minutes, or until heated through and lightly golden.
Squeeze lime juice over roasted peppers. Garnish with remaining fresh cilantro leaves. Serve warm.

recipes.recipe_name: Alfajores de Queso Panela y Manzana
recipes.visual_description: Six to nine delicate, round Alfajores de Queso Panela y Manzana are arranged casually on a rustic, unglazed terra cotta serving platter, reflecting Peruvian artisanal heritage. The cookies are golden-beige, perfectly uniform in size, with a soft, slightly crumbly texture. Each sandwich cookie reveals a creamy, off-white filling peeking slightly from the edges, hinting at the smooth blend of panela cheese, cream, and apple liqueur. A light, even dusting of white powdered sugar covers the top of each alfajor, creating a soft, inviting finish. The arrangement is natural and unforced, as if just placed on a family kitchen table. The scene is bathed in warm, soft light, highlighting the homely appeal of the dessert. The background features a well-worn wooden table surface and a casually draped, simple cotton napkin, emphasizing comfort and traditional preparation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a cup of traditional Peruvian coffee or mate de coca.
Offer alongside other small Peruvian sweets like king kong or chocotejas for a varied dessert spread.
instructions: Prepare Cookie Dough: In a large bowl, cream softened butter and 100 g powdered sugar until light and fluffy. Beat in egg yolks one at a time.
Combine Dry Ingredients: In a separate bowl, whisk together flour, cornstarch, and baking powder.
Mix Dough: Gradually add dry ingredients to wet ingredients. Mix until just combined and a soft dough forms. Do not overmix.
Chill Dough: Wrap dough in plastic film. Refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Roll and Cut Cookies: Preheat oven to 160°C. Lightly flour a surface. Roll dough to 5 mm thickness. Cut out small rounds (approx. 4 cm diameter) using a cookie cutter.
Bake Cookies: Place rounds on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Bake for 10-12 minutes, or until edges are lightly golden and centers are set. Do not brown too much.
Cool Cookies: Transfer cookies to a wire rack. Cool completely.
Prepare Filling: In a medium bowl, whisk heavy cream until soft peaks form. Gently fold in grated panela cheese, apple liqueur, and ground licorice root powder until well combined.
Assemble Alfajores: Spread a generous amount of filling onto the flat side of one cookie. Top with another cookie to form a sandwich. Repeat with remaining cookies and filling.
Dust: Lightly dust assembled alfajores with extra powdered sugar before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Lebanese Halloumi & Grape Bites
recipes.visual_description: The image features 8-12 golden-brown, pan-fried halloumi thick cubes, visibly crusted with finely chopped almonds and fresh green herbs like mint and parsley. Each cube is approximately 2 cm, showcasing a rustic, uneven coating. The vibrant purple and green halved and small diced grapes, mixed with bright orange zest, are casually spooned over and around the halloumi, creating a fresh, colorful contrast. The dish is presented on a simple, slightly irregular, off-white ceramic platter with natural imperfections, placed on a well-used wooden dining table. A neutral-toned linen napkin is casually folded beside the platter. The scene is illuminated by soft, warm kitchen lighting, creating a homely, inviting atmosphere with minimal background distractions, focusing entirely on the appetizing, naturally arranged food.
instructions: Pat halloumi dry. Cut halloumi into 2 cm thick cubes.
Roughly chop blanched almonds. Finely chop fresh mint and parsley.
Combine chopped almonds, mint, and parsley in a shallow dish. Add a pinch of salt and pepper. Mix well.
Drizzle halloumi cubes with 10 ml olive oil. Toss to coat lightly.
Roll each halloumi cube in the almond-herb mixture. Ensure all sides are coated.
Heat remaining 20 ml olive oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat.
Add coated halloumi cubes to the hot pan. Cook for 2-3 minutes per side. Cook until golden brown and crisp.
Remove halloumi from pan. Place on a paper towel-lined plate to drain excess oil.
Wash and halve red and green grapes. Small dice half of the grapes. Leave the other half halved.
Grate the zest from the whole orange. Combine diced and halved grapes with orange zest in a small bowl. Mix gently.
Arrange the golden halloumi bites on a serving platter. Spoon the grape and orange zest relish over and around the halloumi bites. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Brown Sugar Chamomile Orange Steamed Cake
recipes.visual_description: A single slice of moist, light brown steamed cake rests on a simple, slightly imperfect white ceramic plate with a subtle blue floral pattern. The cake slice, cut cleanly into a wedge, reveals a tender crumb with tiny flecks of orange zest. A faint aroma of chamomile is suggested by the soft, diffused lighting. The plate is placed on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table, showing natural grain and minor imperfections. In the background, a portion of the remaining whole cake, still on its cooling rack or a simple ceramic cake stand, is visible, suggesting a larger family dessert. A small, unadorned white porcelain teacup with a subtle steam wispy, containing plain Chinese tea, sits casually beside the plate, along with a basic silver dessert fork. A casually folded, plain cotton napkin is nearby. The scene is bathed in warm, inviting kitchen light, creating a cozy, lived-in family atmosphere with minimal, natural clutter.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a cup of plain, unsweetened Chinese tea like Oolong or Pu-erh to balance the sweetness.
Enjoy as a simple dessert or a snack during afternoon tea.
instructions: Brew strong chamomile tea. Let cool completely.
Grease and line a 18 cm round cake tin or heatproof bowl. Prepare a steamer, ensuring water is boiling vigorously.
In a large bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, and salt.
In a separate bowl, whisk eggs, brown sugar, vegetable oil, milk, cooled chamomile tea, and orange zest until the sugar dissolves and the mixture is well combined.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients. Whisk gently until just combined. Do not overmix.
Pour the batter into the prepared cake tin.
Carefully place the tin into the preheated steamer. Steam cake for 30-40 minutes, or until a skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
Remove the cake from the steamer. Let it cool in the tin for 10 minutes.
Invert the cake onto a wire rack to cool completely.
Serve warm or at room temperature.
notes: Ensure the steamer is preheated and water is boiling vigorously before placing the cake in for steaming. This helps achieve a light and fluffy texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Pear & Almond Fruit Salad with Candied Ginger
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant and elegant fruit salad is presented in a clean, white porcelain dessert bowl, showcasing a harmonious blend of colors and textures. Cubed pears, halved green grapes, half-moon kiwi slices, plump blueberries, and ruby red raspberries are lightly coated in a glistening, translucent pear liqueur-honey dressing. The fruits maintain their distinct shapes and natural hues: creamy white from the pears, deep green from the kiwi, vibrant blues and reds from the berries. Scattered over the top are perfectly toasted, golden-brown sliced almonds, adding a delicate crunch and nutty aroma. Small, translucent pieces of finely diced candied ginger are interspersed, providing subtle amber accents and a hint of spice. A few fresh, bright green mint leaves are artfully placed as a garnish, enhancing the visual appeal. The overall composition is fresh, clean, and balanced, with appropriate negative space around the fruit. The bowl rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table, bathed in soft, natural, even lighting, creating a refined bistro-style presentation.

ingredients.name: Pears (e.g., Bosc or Anjou), firm but ripe

instructions: Wash all fruits thoroughly.
Peel pears. Core pears. Cut into 2cm cubes.
Halve green grapes.
Peel kiwi. Slice into 0.5cm half-moons.
Combine cubed pears, halved grapes, sliced kiwi, blueberries, and raspberries in a large mixing bowl.
For the dressing, whisk pear liqueur, honey, and fresh lemon juice in a small bowl until well combined.
Pour dressing over the mixed fruit. Gently toss to coat all fruit evenly.
Toast sliced almonds in a dry pan over medium heat until golden brown. Cool completely.
Finely dice the candied ginger.
Divide the fruit salad equally among four clean white porcelain dessert bowls or shallow plates.
Sprinkle toasted sliced almonds generously over each serving.
Sprinkle finely diced candied ginger over the almonds on each serving.
Garnish each plate with a few fresh mint leaves for color and aroma. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Bean & Soy Chorizo Crostini
recipes.visual_description: Eight to twelve golden-brown baguette crostini are arranged casually on a rustic wooden serving board, slightly overlapping. Each crostini is generously topped with a chunky, reddish-brown bean and soy chorizo mixture, showcasing visible pieces of both beans and crumbled soy chorizo. The topping has a hearty, textured appearance. A sprinkle of bright green chopped cilantro or parsley adds a fresh contrast. The overall color palette is warm and earthy. The board rests on a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, cozy light from above, simulating a homely kitchen atmosphere. A casually placed, simple checkered cloth napkin peeks from beneath the board. The scene is uncluttered, focusing on the comforting appeal of the bite-sized appetizers, ready for a family gathering.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Slice baguette into 1 cm thick rounds. Arrange on a baking sheet. Brush both sides with 30 ml olive oil. Bake for 8-10 minutes until golden and crisp. Set aside.
Dice the onion into small pieces. Mince the garlic.
Heat remaining 30 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Crumble soy chorizo into the skillet. Cook, breaking it apart with a spoon, for 5-7 minutes until heated through and slightly browned.
Add drained kidney beans and lima beans to the skillet. Stir well.
Pour in the beer. Add smoked paprika, cumin, salt, and pepper. Add red pepper flakes if desired. Stir to combine.

Bring mixture to a simmer. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until liquid reduces slightly and flavors meld. Mash about half of the beans lightly with a fork or potato masher for a chunkier texture.
Remove from heat. Stir in half of the fresh chopped cilantro or parsley.
Spoon a generous amount of the warm bean and soy chorizo mixture onto each toasted baguette slice. Arrange on a serving platter. Garnish with remaining fresh cilantro or parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Moroccan Spiced Tomato & Chipotle Consommé
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a wide, shallow, matte bone china bowl, showcasing abundant negative space. A crystal-clear, deep amber Moroccan Spiced Tomato & Chipotle Consommé fills the bottom, reflecting light. A vibrant emerald green swirl of coriander oil is artfully drizzled across the surface, creating an organic, flowing pattern. To one side, a delicate cloud of golden saffron air rests lightly, adding an ethereal texture. A few precisely toasted, thinly sliced almond shavings are scattered sparingly, providing a subtle textural contrast. The setting features a pristine white Carrara marble surface, a precisely folded white linen napkin, and a traditional, ornate Moroccan brass tea glass placed subtly in the background, enhancing cultural authenticity without distraction. Dramatic professional lighting creates soft shadows, highlighting the dish's minimalist elegance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small piece of freshly baked Khobz (Moroccan bread) on the side.
A tiny dish of olive tapenade or harissa on the table as an optional accompaniment.

ingredients.name: Fresh Coriander Leaves and Tender Stems
Hot Water or Light Vegetable Stock

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Halve tomatoes, place cut-side up on baking sheet with chipotle chiles. Roast 20 minutes until softened and slightly charred.

In a large pot, combine roasted tomatoes, chipotles, adobo sauce, stock, onion, garlic, ginger, toasted cumin, paprika, ground coriander, cinnamon stick, and preserved lemon rind. Simmer gently for 45 minutes. Strain solids, reserving liquid. Season liquid with salt.

In a separate bowl, whisk egg whites until frothy. Combine with ground chicken and coriander stems. Stir into the strained consommé. Bring slowly to a simmer over medium heat without stirring. Allow raft to form on top. Create a small hole in the raft for liquid to bubble through. Simmer gently 20 minutes.
Carefully ladle clarified consommé through a fine-mesh sieve lined with cheesecloth. Do not disturb the raft. Keep warm.

Blanch coriander leaves and tender stems in boiling water for 10 seconds. Immediately transfer to ice bath. Squeeze dry. Blend blanched coriander with neutral oil and a pinch of salt until smooth. Pass through a super-fine mesh sieve for a clear, vibrant oil.

Infuse saffron threads in hot water/stock for 10 minutes. Strain saffron. Whisk in soy lecithin/sucrose ester. Using an immersion blender, create a stable foam by blending just at the surface of the liquid.
Toast thinly sliced almonds in a dry pan over medium heat until golden and fragrant. Watch carefully to prevent burning.

Gently pour warm consommé into shallow bowls. Drizzle a small, artistic swirl of coriander oil. Carefully spoon a cloud of saffron air onto one side. Scatter a few toasted almond shavings. Serve immediately.
notes: The chipotle adds a smoky depth that complements the aromatic Moroccan spices beautifully, creating a unique fusion flavor profile.

recipes.recipe_name: Compressed Cucumber and Heirloom Tomato Salad
recipes.visual_description: The Compressed Cucumber and Heirloom Tomato Salad is presented with extreme restraint on a pristine, matte white bone china plate, allowing abundant negative space to frame the composition. The plate rests on a subtly veined white Carrara marble surface, complemented by a precisely folded white linen napkin. Dramatic, focused lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing the textures. The core elements are arranged in a natural, organic flow, avoiding any rigid symmetry. Compressed cucumber pieces, translucent and vibrant green, are cut into perfect 2 cm cubes or irregular, polished segments, reflecting light. Scattered amongst them are heirloom tomato pieces, varying in size and exhibiting rich hues of red, yellow, and orange, some halved, some artfully segmented, with their glossy, peeled surfaces catching the light. Precisely placed crispy soy chorizo crumbs, deep reddish-brown and irregularly shaped, add a textural contrast and savory depth. A delicate drizzle of the shallot vinaigrette weaves through the elements, adding subtle sheen. The garnish is minimal yet impactful: 2-3 vibrant green basil leaves or a few delicate microgreens, strategically placed to add a pop of color and freshness. The entire presentation embodies sophisticated minimalism and culinary artistry, emphasizing perfect execution of each component.
instructions: Prepare Compressed Cucumber: Wash cucumbers. Peel partially, leaving alternating skin strips. Cut into 2 cm thick rounds or precise 2 cm cubes. In a bowl, combine water, white wine vinegar, sugar, and 5g salt. Stir until dissolved. Add cucumber pieces and dill sprigs. Place in a vacuum seal bag. Vacuum seal on high setting until cucumbers are compressed and translucent. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes. If no vacuum sealer, weigh down in liquid for 1 hour.

Prepare Heirloom Tomatoes: Wash tomatoes. Bring a small pot of water to a boil. Prepare an ice bath. Score the bottom of each tomato with a small 'X'. Blanch tomatoes in boiling water for 10-15 seconds until skin just begins to peel. Immediately transfer to ice bath. Once cooled, peel the skins. Cut larger tomatoes into irregular, artistic segments. Leave cherry/grape tomatoes whole or halve them. Season lightly with 2g sea salt, 1g black pepper, and 15 ml extra virgin olive oil.

Crisp Soy Chorizo: Remove soy chorizo from casing. Heat 15 ml olive oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Crumble soy chorizo into the hot pan. Cook, stirring occasionally, breaking it into small, irregular pieces, until very crispy and browned, about 8-10 minutes. Drain on a paper towel-lined plate.

Make Shallot Vinaigrette: In a small bowl, whisk together minced shallot, white balsamic vinegar, Dijon mustard, a pinch of sea salt, and a pinch of black pepper. Slowly drizzle in 50 ml extra virgin olive oil while whisking constantly until emulsified.

Assemble Salad: Drain compressed cucumbers, discarding dill. Arrange 3-4 pieces of compressed cucumber on each plate, creating an artistic, organic flow. Place 4-5 prepared heirloom tomato pieces around the cucumber. Scatter 1-2 tablespoons of crispy soy chorizo crumbs precisely among the vegetables. Drizzle vinaigrette artfully over the salad elements. Garnish with 2-3 small basil leaves or a pinch of microgreens. Finish with a few flakes of sea salt.

recipes.recipe_name: Cucumber and Tempeh Noodle Salad
recipes.visual_description: The Cucumber and Tempeh Noodle Salad is presented on a natural cream handcrafted ceramic plate. Thin Thai rice noodles form an organic base. Poached pink shrimp and golden-brown tempeh batons are artfully nestled amongst them. Bright green shredded cabbage, thinly sliced pickled cucumbers, and julienned carrots add vibrant color and texture. A generous drizzle of creamy peanut-lime dressing coats the ingredients. The dish is simply garnished with fresh green mint and cilantro leaves, plus coarsely chopped roasted peanuts for texture. The arrangement is natural and unforced, emphasizing each component's inherent beauty. The plate rests on a light, textured bamboo surface, with an undyed linen napkin. Soft natural light illuminates the scene.
instructions: Slice tempeh into 1 cm thick batons. In a shallow dish, combine 60 ml soy sauce, 30 ml rice vinegar, 15 ml maple syrup, 2 minced garlic cloves, and 10 g grated ginger. Add tempeh batons, ensuring they are coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or preferably overnight.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat. Add marinated tempeh batons and pan-fry for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and slightly crispy. Set aside.
Thinly slice cucumber into half-moons. Julienne carrot. Thinly slice red onion. In a heatproof bowl, combine sliced cucumber, julienned carrot, and thinly sliced red onion.

In a small saucepan, combine 120 ml rice vinegar, 120 ml water, 30 ml maple syrup, and 5 g salt. Heat until salt and maple syrup dissolve. Pour hot pickling liquid over vegetables. Let cool to room temperature, then refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.

Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Add rice noodles and cook according to package instructions until al dente, usually 3-5 minutes. Drain immediately and rinse with cold water to prevent sticking. Set aside.
Bring a small pot of water to a gentle simmer. Add shrimp and poach for 2-3 minutes, or until pink and opaque. Drain and set aside.

In a bowl, whisk together 80 g peanut butter, 60 ml lime juice, 45 ml soy sauce, 30 ml maple syrup, 1 minced garlic clove, 5 g grated ginger, and 2 g chili flakes (if using). Gradually add 60-90 ml water or vegetable broth, whisking until desired smooth, pourable consistency is reached.

In a large mixing bowl, combine cooked and cooled rice noodles, thinly shredded green cabbage, drained quick pickled vegetables, poached shrimp, and cooked tempeh batons. Pour most of the peanut-lime dressing over the salad.
Gently toss all ingredients to combine and coat evenly with the dressing. Garnish with chopped fresh mint, fresh cilantro, and roughly chopped roasted peanuts. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Malted Sago Fritters with Tomato Aioli
recipes.visual_description: The Savory Malted Sago Fritters are presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Eight golden-brown, irregularly shaped fritters are casually arranged in a natural cluster, showcasing their crisp exterior texture. Each fritter, approximately 5 cm in diameter, has a slightly puffed appearance. Beside the fritters, a small, elegant white ramekin holds a dollop of vibrant, creamy tomato aioli, its rich orange hue contrasting with the fritters. A sprinkle of finely chopped green chives garnishes both the fritters and the aioli, adding a fresh pop of color. The setting features a simple wooden table surface and a folded white cotton napkin placed to the side, creating a modern bistro ambiance with natural, even lighting that highlights the food's inviting textures and colors. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space, allowing the dish to be the clear focal point.
instructions: Cook Sago: Bring 500 ml tomato stock to a boil in a medium saucepan. Add sago. Reduce heat to low. Simmer, stirring occasionally, until sago is translucent and tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain sago very well in a fine-mesh sieve. Let cool for 10 minutes.
Prepare Fritter Mixture: In a large bowl, combine cooled sago, malted milk powder, grated Parmesan, egg, flour, chopped chives, salt, and pepper. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.

Make Tomato Aioli: Pour 100 ml tomato stock into a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat and cook until liquid is thick and syrupy, about 5-7 minutes. Let cool. In a small bowl, whisk together mayonnaise, reduced tomato stock, minced garlic, and lemon juice. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Fry Fritters: Heat vegetable oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat. Oil should be about 1 cm deep.
Form and Cook: Drop tablespoonfuls of the sago mixture into the hot oil. Flatten slightly with the back of a spoon to form small fritters, approximately 5 cm in diameter. Do not overcrowd the pan.
Flip and Drain: Cook for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and crispy. Remove fritters with a slotted spoon. Place on a wire rack lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.
Serve: Serve the Savory Malted Sago Fritters warm with the Tomato Aioli on the side. Garnish with extra chopped chives if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Crispy Soy Chorizo Pasta with Quick-Pickled Cucumber
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented as a vibrant, elegantly composed single starter portion on a round white porcelain plate. A central mound of al dente ditalini pasta, tossed with savory, crumbled and crisped soy chorizo, forms the base. The soy chorizo exhibits rich reddish-brown hues and a slight char from searing. Thinly sliced, quick-pickled Persian cucumber ribbons are artfully draped over and around the pasta, adding a contrasting bright green color and a refreshing, tangy texture. A light scattering of golden-brown crispy brown rice provides an appealing textural crunch and a nutty aroma. Fresh cilantro leaves are strategically placed for a pop of bright green and aromatic freshness. The overall presentation is clean and inviting, with moderate negative space around the central elements. The colors are natural and harmonious, showcasing the freshness of the ingredients. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, creating a professional yet approachable bistro aesthetic.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Spread cooked brown rice on a baking sheet. Bake 15-20 minutes until crispy. Stir halfway. Cool.
Combine rice vinegar, sugar, salt in a bowl. Stir to dissolve. Thinly slice Persian cucumbers. Add cucumbers to mixture. Sit 10 minutes.
Cook ditalini pasta in salted boiling water until al dente. Drain.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Add soy chorizo. Break apart. Cook 8-10 minutes until crispy and browned. Remove from heat.
In a large bowl, whisk remaining 15ml olive oil, lime juice, garlic powder, smoked paprika, salt, pepper. Add cooked pasta and crispy soy chorizo. Toss.
Plate pasta and chorizo mixture. Arrange pickled cucumber ribbons. Sprinkle with crispy brown rice. Garnish with fresh cilantro.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Poblano & Avocado Salad with Lovage-Lime Vinaigrette
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a round bone china plate with subtle white patterns, centered on a pristine white Carrara marble surface. A precisely folded white linen napkin sits to the side. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing the minimalist aesthetic. The composition features an artful arrangement of vibrant elements against ample negative space. Delicate strips of deep green, roasted poblano form a gentle curve. Alongside, precisely cut cubes of creamy avocado are interspersed. Bright red and yellow heirloom cherry tomato halves provide pops of color. Thin, translucent rings of quick-pickled red onion add a subtle fuchsia hue. A verdant lovage-lime vinaigrette is elegantly drizzled, pooling slightly around the components. A few fresh lovage leaves are meticulously placed as garnish. The overall impression is one of sophisticated simplicity, showcasing pristine ingredients with refined technique and an organic flow.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as an elegant starter in a multi-course fine-dining experience.
Offer small, warm corn tortillas on the side for a subtle traditional accompaniment.
instructions: Roast poblano peppers over an open flame or under a broiler until skin is charred. Place in a bowl, cover, and steam for 10 minutes. Peel, deseed, and slice into elegant 1 cm wide strips.

Thinly slice the half red onion into translucent rings. In a small bowl, combine white vinegar, water, a pinch of salt, and a pinch of agave nectar. Add onion rings and quick pickle for at least 15 minutes.

For the lovage-lime vinaigrette: Roast garlic cloves until soft. In a blender, combine roasted garlic, 30 grams of lovage leaves, juice and zest of 1.5 limes, remaining agave nectar, 60 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Blend until smooth and emulsified.
Carefully slice avocados into 1.5 cm cubes.
Halve the heirloom cherry tomatoes.

To assemble each plate: Arrange a gentle curve of roasted poblano strips on one side. Artfully scatter avocado cubes and halved cherry tomatoes alongside the poblano. Drain and arrange a few pickled red onion rings among the vegetables.
Drizzle a generous amount of lovage-lime vinaigrette over the components. Garnish each plate with 1-2 fresh lovage leaves for visual appeal and aroma. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure avocados are perfectly ripe for creamy texture.
The lovage-lime vinaigrette can be made a few hours in advance and refrigerated.
The minimalist plating emphasizes the quality and preparation of each ingredient.

recipes.recipe_name: Tapioca de Coco com Calda de Amora e Framboesa
recipes.visual_description: Four individual servings of Coconut Tapioca are presented in clear, stemmed dessert glasses on a light wooden table. The tapioca is a creamy, opaque white, filling the lower two-thirds of each glass, showcasing its smooth, slightly gelatinous texture. A vibrant, deep purplish-red blackberry and raspberry sauce is generously spooned over the tapioca, cascading down the sides and creating an appealing contrast. The sauce is slightly chunky, with visible whole and gently crushed berry pieces. Each glass is garnished with a few perfectly ripe, whole fresh blackberries and raspberries, along with a delicate sprig of bright green mint leaves, adding a pop of color and freshness. The arrangement is clean and professional, with ample negative space around each glass. A simple white cotton napkin rests beside one glass. Natural, soft lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the dish's inviting colors and textures against a blurred, modern bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve chilled as a refreshing dessert or snack.
Traditionally enjoyed at breakfast or as an afternoon snack in Brazil.
Often found in Brazilian bakeries or street food markets.
instructions: Combine tapioca pearls, coconut milk, whole milk, 100g sugar, and salt in a large bowl. Stir well.
Cover the bowl. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or preferably overnight, to soften tapioca.
Transfer the tapioca mixture to a medium saucepan. Cook over medium-low heat. Stir constantly until the mixture thickens and tapioca pearls become translucent.
Remove from heat. Stir in the vanilla extract.
Divide the cooked tapioca mixture evenly into four individual serving glasses or small bowls. Chill in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours until firm.
For the berry sauce: Combine fresh blackberries, fresh raspberries, 50g sugar, raspberry liqueur, and water in a small saucepan.
Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer over medium heat. Cook for 5-7 minutes, gently crushing some of the berries with the back of a spoon, until the sauce thickens slightly.
Remove the sauce from heat. Let it cool completely to room temperature.
To serve: Spoon the cooled berry sauce generously over the chilled coconut tapioca in each glass.
Garnish each serving with a few extra whole fresh blackberries, raspberries, and a small sprig of fresh mint leaves.
notes: Ensure tapioca pearls are fully hydrated before cooking for best texture.
The tapioca pudding will thicken further as it chills. Adjust sweetness of the sauce to your preference.
traditional_techniques: Slow-cooking tapioca to achieve creamy consistency

recipes.recipe_name: Carob Dacquoise Bites with Date Crémeux and Cherry Gelee
recipes.visual_description: Four precisely constructed layered snack bites are artfully arranged on a pristine white Carrara marble sharing platter. Each bite is a miniature architectural cube, approximately 3x3x3 cm, showcasing distinct layers: a light, airy carob dacquoise base, a smooth, rich date crémeux, and a vibrant, translucent cherry gelee top. The layers are clean and distinct, with sharp edges. A delicate sprinkle of dark, crunchy carob nib crumble rests on the gelee, providing textural contrast. A single fresh, halved cherry is placed beside each bite. Abundant negative space surrounds the arrangement, emphasizing the minimalist elegance. The plate is a modern designer bone china with a subtle, matte finish. Dramatic professional lighting creates soft shadows, enhancing the textures and depth. The background is ultra-minimalist, drawing full focus to the meticulously crafted snacks. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, is subtly placed to the side.
instructions: For the Carob Dacquoise:
Preheat oven to 170°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Whip egg whites to soft peaks. Gradually add granulated sugar. Whip until stiff and glossy.
Gently fold in almond flour and carob powder.
Spread batter evenly onto the prepared baking sheet. Bake for 15-20 minutes until golden and firm.
Cool completely. Cut into 3x3 cm squares.
For the Date Crémeux:
Soak gelatin sheets in cold water for 5 minutes.
Combine dates, heavy cream, and water in a saucepan. Simmer until dates are very soft. Blend until smooth.
Whisk egg yolks in a separate bowl. Slowly temper hot date mixture into yolks.
Return mixture to saucepan. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until mixture thickens (82°C). Do not boil.
Remove from heat. Stir in squeezed gelatin sheets and unsalted butter until melted and smooth.
Pour crémeux into a shallow dish. Cover surface with plastic wrap. Chill until firm.
For the Cherry Gelee:
Soak gelatin sheets in cold water for 5 minutes.
Pit cherries. Combine cherries, 50 ml water, and lemon juice in a saucepan. Simmer until cherries are soft. Mash lightly.
Strain mixture, pressing solids to extract juice. Discard solids.
Heat cherry juice gently. Stir in squeezed gelatin sheets until dissolved.
Pour gelee into a shallow dish. Chill until firm.
For the Carob Nib Crumble:
Combine carob nibs, flour, and cold butter. Rub with fingertips until crumbly.
Spread on a baking sheet. Bake at 170°C for 10-12 minutes until toasted. Cool.
Assembly:
Cut chilled date crémeux and cherry gelee into 3x3 cm squares, matching dacquoise size.
Place a dacquoise square on a serving platter. Top with a crémeux square. Top with a gelee square.
Repeat for 4 servings.
Garnish each stack with a sprinkle of carob nib crumble and a fresh cherry half.

recipes.recipe_name: Pisco Orange Tartlets with Candied Lime Leaf
recipes.visual_description: A single Pisco Orange Tartlet is centrally placed on a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic plate in a natural cream or beige tone. The tartlet features a crisp, golden-brown shortcrust shell with a smooth, glossy, vibrant orange-yellow Pisco-orange curd filling. The top is elegantly garnished with a few translucent, amber-colored candied orange peel strips and a couple of translucent green candied lime leaves, arranged organically. A small cluster of vibrant fresh orange segments provides a contrasting pop of color and freshness. The plate offers generous white space, emphasizing the tartlet's form and color. The setting features a light bamboo or reclaimed wood table surface. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is folded simply to the side. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene from the side, creating subtle shadows and highlighting the textures. The background is clean and minimalist, with a hint of natural greenery or a plain wall, maintaining focus on the dish's inherent beauty and sustainable aesthetic.
instructions: Prepare tartlet dough: Combine flour, cold butter, powdered sugar, and salt. Rub until crumbly. Add egg yolk. Mix until dough forms. Wrap and chill 30 minutes.
Roll dough. Line four 10 cm tartlet molds. Prick bottoms. Blind bake at 180°C for 15 minutes. Remove weights. Bake 5-7 minutes more until golden. Cool.
Make sugar cane syrup: Combine 100 ml sugar cane syrup and 100 ml water in a saucepan. Bring to a simmer. Reserve 50 ml for curd. Use remaining for candied elements.

Prepare candied elements: Add thinly sliced orange peels and whole lime leaves to the simmering sugar cane syrup (from above, not the reserved 50ml). Simmer gently for 20 minutes until translucent. Remove and cool on a wire rack. Reserve excess syrup.

Make Pisco-Orange Curd: Whisk orange juice, orange zest, pisco, reserved 50 ml sugar cane syrup, whole eggs, and egg yolks in a heatproof bowl. Set bowl over a saucepan of simmering water (bain-marie).
Stir constantly until mixture thickens (coats the back of a spoon, 82°C). Remove from heat. Stir in butter until melted and smooth. Strain curd through a fine-mesh sieve. Cool completely.
Assemble tartlets: Spoon cooled Pisco-Orange Curd into baked tartlet shells. Smooth the top.

Garnish: Arrange candied orange peel strips and candied lime leaves on top of each tartlet. Add a few fresh orange segments. Lightly dust with finely crushed dried lime leaf powder (optional, made from dried excess lime leaves).
Chill tartlets until ready to serve.
notes: For zero-waste, any remaining orange zest or lime leaves can be dried and powdered for future use as garnish or flavoring.

recipes.recipe_name: Kewra Coconut & Berry Entremet
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly formed mini entremet sits centered on a handcrafted cream-colored ceramic plate. The dessert is a pristine cylinder, showcasing three distinct layers. The base is a compressed, earthy brown date and oat crust, firm and uniform. Above it, a thick, creamy white layer of kewra-infused coconut mousse provides a soft contrast. The top layer is a vibrant, deep purple blackberry schnapps gelée, shimmering gently. A single, plump fresh blackberry rests atop the gelée, accompanied by a delicate, thin slice of red date, its rich color a counterpoint. The plate itself is simple, with ample negative space around the entremet. The surface is a light, natural wood, softly illuminated by natural light from the side, casting gentle shadows. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige is subtly visible in the background, along with a hint of a green plant, maintaining a minimalist, eco-conscious aesthetic.
instructions: Prepare the Date & Nut Crust: Combine pitted red dates, rolled oats, mixed nuts, and a pinch of salt in a food processor. Process until a sticky mixture forms.
Press the mixture firmly into the bottom of four 7cm diameter individual entremet molds or ring molds. Chill for 30 minutes.
Prepare the Kewra Coconut Mousse: Open the chilled coconut cream can without shaking. Scoop out the thick cream from the top. Reserve the clear liquid at the bottom.
Whip the thick coconut cream until light and fluffy. Set aside.
In a small saucepan, combine 2g agar-agar powder with 30ml water. Bring to a simmer, stirring until dissolved. Stir in 50ml maple syrup and kewra water. Remove from heat.
Gently fold the agar-agar mixture into the whipped coconut cream until fully combined.
Pour the coconut mousse over the chilled crusts in the molds. Return to the refrigerator and chill for at least 1 hour, or until set.
Prepare the Blackberry Schnapps Gelée: In a saucepan, combine fresh blackberries with 20ml maple syrup and 20ml water. Simmer gently until blackberries soften and release their juices. Mash lightly.
Strain the blackberry mixture through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing to extract all liquid. Discard solids.
Return the strained blackberry juice to the saucepan. Add 1.5g agar-agar powder and blackberry schnapps. Bring to a simmer, stirring until agar-agar is completely dissolved. Remove from heat.
Carefully pour the blackberry gelée over the set coconut mousse layers in the molds. Chill for at least 2 hours, or until completely firm.
To serve, gently unmold the entremets. Garnish each with a fresh blackberry and a thinly sliced red date.

recipes.recipe_name: Bún Nấm Phô Mai Áp Chảo Chay
recipes.visual_description: The Bún Nấm Phô Mai Áp Chảo Chay is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl, showcasing vibrant layers. A base of crisp green lettuce and tender rice vermicelli noodles forms the foundation. Artfully arranged on top are golden-brown, pan-seared farmer cheese pieces, their irregular shapes adding rustic texture. Alongside are earthy, sautéed shiitake mushrooms. Bright orange julienned pickled carrots and pale daikon radish provide refreshing crunch. Thinly sliced cucumber batons add cool green accents. The dish is generously garnished with fresh mint, cilantro, crushed roasted peanuts, and crispy fried shallots. A small ceramic dipping bowl with clear, amber vegetarian Nước Chấm Chấm Chay rests beside the main bowl on a simple wooden table. Chopsticks are neatly placed. Natural, even lighting highlights the fresh ingredients and diverse textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with chopsticks.
Each diner mixes their bowl before eating.
A small dish of vegetarian dipping sauce (Nước Chấm Chay) is offered on the side.
instructions: Press farmer cheese for 30 minutes to remove excess moisture. Cut into 2 cm irregular chunks.
Prepare pickled vegetables: Peel and julienne carrot and daikon radish. In a bowl, combine 100ml warm water, 15g sugar, and 15ml rice vinegar. Add julienned vegetables. Let stand 20 minutes.
Prepare noodles: Cook vermicelli noodles according to package directions. Drain and rinse with cold water. Set aside.
Prepare dressing: Mince 1 garlic clove. In a small bowl, whisk together 120ml water, 60g sugar, 45ml rice vinegar, 30ml lime juice, 30ml soy sauce, and minced garlic. Add sliced chili if desired.

Prepare fried shallots: Thinly slice 2 large shallots. Heat 50ml vegetable oil in a small pan over medium heat. Fry shallots until golden brown and crispy. Remove with slotted spoon. Drain on paper towel. Reserve oil.

Prepare mushrooms: Thinly slice shiitake mushrooms. Mince 2 garlic cloves. Heat 15ml reserved shallot oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add mushrooms and minced garlic. Sauté until tender and lightly browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Cook farmer cheese: In the same skillet, add another 15ml reserved shallot oil if needed. Add farmer cheese chunks. Pan-sear until golden brown and slightly crispy on all sides, about 8-10 minutes.
Assemble bowls: Wash and tear lettuce into bite-sized pieces. Slice cucumber into thin batons. Place lettuce at the bottom of 4 large bowls. Top with cooked vermicelli noodles.
Arrange pan-seared farmer cheese, sautéed mushrooms, pickled carrots and daikon (drained), and cucumber batons over the noodles.
Garnish each bowl generously with fresh mint leaves, cilantro sprigs, crushed roasted peanuts, and crispy fried shallots.
Serve immediately with the vegetarian Nước Chấm Chay dressing on the side for each diner to add to taste.
notes: Ensure farmer cheese is pressed well to remove excess moisture for best pan-searing results.

recipes.recipe_name: Tomato Confit and Poached Carp Salad with Crispy Jasmine Rice Tuiles
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a pristine white bone china plate, centered with abundant negative space. A vibrant composition of red and orange tomato confit clusters mingles with precisely diced heirloom tomato cubes. Small, irregular white pieces of delicately poached carp are artfully nestled among the vegetables. Golden, irregular crispy jasmine rice tuiles stand upright, adding architectural height and textural contrast. A clear, glistening lemongrass-lime emulsion is artfully drizzled around the components, enhancing visual flow. A few micro cilantro leaves provide a final touch of fresh green. The setting features a superpremium light grey marble surface, with a crisply folded white linen napkin. Dramatic professional lighting creates soft shadows, highlighting the dish's elegant simplicity.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served as an individual fine-dining appetizer course.
Best enjoyed immediately to preserve the crisp texture of the rice tuiles.
instructions: Preheat oven to 120°C.
Place cherry tomatoes on a baking tray. Drizzle with olive oil, season with salt and white pepper. Roast for 45 minutes until slightly wrinkled and tender. Set aside.

Bring a small pot of water to a gentle simmer. Add a slice of lemongrass and half a kaffir lime leaf. Gently poach carp fillet for 5-7 minutes, until cooked through. Cool completely. Cut carp into small, irregular pieces, approximately 1 cm.

Cook jasmine rice according to package directions. Blend cooked rice with 50 ml water until a smooth paste forms. Spread rice paste very thinly onto a silicone mat or parchment paper. Dehydrate in oven at 80°C for 2 hours, or until completely dry and brittle. Break into irregular shards.
Heat peanut oil in a small pot to 180°C. Fry rice shards for 10-15 seconds until puffed and golden. Drain on paper towels. Season lightly with salt.

For the dressing: Finely mince shallots, garlic, bird's eye chili. Thinly slice remaining lemongrass and finely shred remaining kaffir lime leaf. Combine minced shallots, garlic, chili, lemongrass, kaffir lime leaf in a bowl. Whisk in fish sauce, lime juice, and grated palm sugar until sugar dissolves.
In a mixing bowl, combine roasted cherry tomatoes, finely diced heirloom tomatoes, and poached carp pieces. Gently fold in cilantro and mint leaves.

To plate: Arrange small, artistic clusters of the tomato-carp mixture on each plate, ensuring abundant negative space. Drizzle the lemongrass-lime dressing around and over the salad.
