Carefully unmold panna cottas onto the center of each pristine white bone china plate, or serve directly in glasses.
Spoon a delicate, flowing 'tear' or 'swoosh' of Jasmine Tea Fluid Gel beside the panna cotta.
Artfully scatter a few toasted coconut flakes around the panna cotta, ensuring abundant negative space on the plate.
Precisely place a single, small fresh mint sprig on or next to the panna cotta for a final touch of fresh color.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Tomato & Pickled Chili Salad
recipes.visual_description: A minimalistic, ingredient-focused salad plated on a round, unglazed cream ceramic plate. The composition is organic and natural, featuring a vibrant array of colors and textures. Fermented red tomatoes, some whole, some gently burst, form the base, their skins slightly wrinkled, revealing a deep red interior. Scattered among them are thin, translucent slices of quick-pickled red onion, providing pops of pale purple. Bright green diced cucumber and sunny yellow diced bell pepper cubes are interspersed, adding crispness and fresh color. Thinly sliced pickled red chilies, fiery red, are strategically placed to offer visual and flavor accents. The salad is lightly dressed, the olive oil sheen visible without pooling. Fresh green basil leaves, roughly torn, are scattered over the top as a simple, natural garnish. The plate rests on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface, accompanied by a folded, undyed linen napkin in natural beige. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the dish, highlighting its fresh, wholesome appearance. The background is clean and uncluttered, with a hint of natural greenery for an eco-conscious feel.

ingredients.name: Ripe cherry tomatoes (or chopped large tomatoes)
Yellow bell pepper, diced into small cubes
Fresh basil leaves, torn or roughly chopped

instructions: To ferment tomatoes (prepare days in advance): Wash tomatoes. Pierce each cherry tomato a few times. For larger tomatoes, chop into 2-3 cm pieces. Place in a clean jar. Dissolve 10g sea salt in 500ml filtered water to make a 2% brine. Pour brine over tomatoes, ensuring full submersion. Cover with an airlock lid or loose lid. Ferment at room temperature for 3-7 days until desired tanginess. Refrigerate once ready.

To quick-pickle red onion (prepare at least 1 hour in advance): Combine 120ml apple cider vinegar, 120ml water, 15g sugar, and 5g salt in a small saucepan. Heat until sugar and salt dissolve. Remove from heat. Add thinly sliced red onion to a heatproof jar. Pour hot pickling liquid over onions. Let cool, then refrigerate for at least 1 hour.

To pickle chilies (prepare at least 1 hour in advance): Combine 60ml white vinegar, 60ml water, 10g sugar, and 3g salt in a small saucepan. Heat until sugar and salt dissolve. Remove from heat. Add thinly sliced chilies to a small heatproof jar. Pour hot pickling liquid over chilies. Let cool, then refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Prepare fresh vegetables: Dice cucumber and yellow bell pepper into small, uniform cubes.
Make dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together 60ml olive oil, 15ml of the quick-pickled onion liquid, salt, and black pepper. Adjust seasoning to taste.

Assemble salad: Gently drain fermented tomatoes, quick-pickled red onion, and pickled chilies. In a large bowl, combine fermented tomatoes, pickled red onion, pickled chilies, diced cucumber, and diced yellow bell pepper.
Dress and serve: Pour dressing over the salad ingredients. Gently toss to combine. Transfer to serving plates. Garnish with fresh basil leaves. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Chanterelles et Morilles, Crème d'Asperges
recipes.visual_description: A single, individual portion is presented on an expansive, pristine white bone china plate. A vibrant, silky smooth asparagus cream forms an organic, flowing sweep across one side of the plate. Adjacent, a cluster of golden, pan-seared chanterelle mushrooms, their natural forms preserved, nestles beside a few deep brown, delicately braised morel mushrooms. A glossy, concentrated morel jus is sparingly drizzled, creating subtle reflections. Each mushroom is presented whole or halved, showcasing its distinct texture. A solitary, delicate sprig of fresh chervil provides a contrasting touch of green. The dish sits on a premium white Carrara marble surface, complemented by a precisely folded white linen napkin and elegant French flatware. Dramatic, directional lighting casts soft shadows, emphasizing the dish's sophisticated simplicity and abundant negative space.
instructions: Trim woody ends from asparagus. Blanch asparagus spears in salted boiling water for 2-3 minutes. Transfer immediately to an ice bath. Drain well.
Chop blanched asparagus into 2 cm pieces. Sauté one minced shallot and one minced garlic clove in 10g butter until translucent. Add chopped asparagus and 50ml vegetable stock. Simmer briefly.
Blend asparagus mixture until silky smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve for ultimate smoothness. Stir in heavy cream. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Clean chanterelles and morels carefully with a brush. Pat dry.
Heat 1 tbsp olive oil and 10g butter in a pan over medium-high heat. Add chanterelle mushrooms. Sear until golden brown and slightly crispy. Season with salt and pepper.

In a separate small pan, sauté remaining minced shallot and garlic in 10g butter. Add morel mushrooms. Deglaze with white wine. Add remaining vegetable stock. Simmer gently until morels are tender and liquid reduces to a glossy jus. Season with salt and pepper.
Warm four plates. Spoon a generous dollop of asparagus cream onto one side of each plate, creating an organic, flowing shape.
Arrange a small cluster of seared chanterelles beside the cream. Place a few braised morels artfully next to the chanterelles.
Drizzle the reduced morel jus sparingly over the mushrooms. Garnish each plate with a small, delicate sprig of fresh chervil. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Daechu-Hibiscus Jelly
recipes.visual_description: A single, individual portion of translucent, ruby-red jelly rests elegantly off-center on a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic plate in a warm beige tone. The jelly, a clean soft shape, showcases visible, thin slices of deep brown fermented red dates within, adding rustic texture and color contrast. A glistening, dark amber espresso-malt syrup is artfully drizzled over the jelly, pooling slightly. The composition emphasizes negative space, allowing natural textures and colors to speak. The plate sits on a light bamboo table surface. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is subtly folded beside. Soft, natural daylight illuminates the scene, creating gentle shadows and highlighting the jelly's shimmer. A minimalist background with a blurred natural plant element maintains focus. The presentation embodies clean lines and an unfussy, ingredient-focused aesthetic, honoring traditional Korean simplicity.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve alongside a small, warm cup of traditional Korean barley tea (boricha) or roasted corn tea (oksusu-cha).
Present in small, simple ceramic bowls or on individual plates, reminiscent of Korean dessert presentations.

ingredients.name: Starter Culture (e.g., kimchi brine or kombucha liquid)

instructions: Wash red dates. Slice thinly.
Place red dates in a clean jar with 200 ml water and starter culture. Cover loosely. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days until slightly tangy.
Strain fermented red dates. Keep dates for jelly. Discard liquid or use in other preparations.
Steep hibiscus flowers in 500 ml hot water for 10 minutes. Strain tea, pressing out all liquid. Discard spent flowers.
In a saucepan, combine strained hibiscus tea, 50 ml malt syrup, and agar-agar powder. Whisk until agar-agar dissolves.
Bring to a gentle boil, stirring constantly for 2 minutes. Remove from heat.
Gently fold in the fermented red dates into the hibiscus jelly mixture. Pour into four individual serving molds or small bowls.
Chill for at least 2 hours, or until set.
For espresso-malt drizzle, combine espresso and remaining 30 ml malt syrup in a small saucepan. Gently heat until well combined and slightly thickened. Do not boil vigorously.
Unmold jelly onto individual plates if using molds. If using bowls, serve directly in bowls. Drizzle generously with espresso-malt syrup. Serve immediately.
notes: This dessert utilizes fermentation for enhanced flavor and probiotic benefits, aligning with sustainable and health-conscious culinary practices.
The use of agar-agar makes it a plant-based, gelatin-free option.
All parts of the red dates and hibiscus are used efficiently, minimizing waste.

recipes.recipe_name: Gochujang Dashi Glazed Chicken Skewers
recipes.visual_description: Four glistening Gochujang Dashi Glazed Chicken Skewers are artfully arranged on a clean, simple white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken cubes, cut into uniform 2.5 cm pieces, exhibit a rich, deep red-orange hue from the caramelized gochujang glaze, with hints of golden-brown charring. Each skewer holds tender, succulent chicken chunks. A scattering of vibrant green, thinly sliced scallions and delicate white toasted sesame seeds provides a fresh contrast. The plate features moderate negative space, enhancing the visual appeal. The setting is a modern bistro, with the plate resting on a simple wooden table surface. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, creating subtle shadows and highlighting the glaze's sheen. The background is minimal and unobtrusive, focusing entirely on the savory snack.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve skewers as a stand-alone snack.
Offer a small bowl of extra glaze for dipping.
Accompany with simple, quick-pickled radish or cucumber for a refreshing contrast.
instructions: Soak wooden skewers in water for 30 minutes. This prevents burning.
Prepare dashi: Combine kombu and 200 ml water in a small pot. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium-low heat. Remove kombu just before water boils. Set aside 100 ml dashi.
Make glaze: In a saucepan, combine gochujang, 100 ml dashi, chicken stock, soy sauce, mirin, minced garlic, grated ginger, sesame oil, and brown sugar. Whisk well.
Simmer glaze over medium-low heat. Cook for 5-7 minutes. Stir occasionally. Glaze should thicken slightly. Remove from heat.
Cut chicken thighs into 2.5 cm cubes.
Thread chicken cubes onto soaked skewers. Place 3-4 cubes per skewer.
Heat vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan or cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat.
Add skewers to hot pan. Cook for 3-4 minutes per side. Rotate skewers for even cooking.
Brush chicken generously with the prepared gochujang dashi glaze. Continue cooking for 2-3 minutes. Turn frequently.
Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove skewers from pan. Arrange on a serving plate.
Garnish with sliced scallions and toasted sesame seeds. Serve immediately.
notes: Soaking wooden skewers prevents them from burning during cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Homestyle Apple Coconut Cake with Cheesy Cream Cheese Frosting
recipes.visual_description: A generous slice of Homestyle Apple Coconut Cake sits on an everyday ceramic plate, placed on a well-used wooden dining table. The slice reveals a moist, golden-brown crumb with soft, cooked apple pieces. A thick, off-white Cheesy Cream Cheese Frosting is spread generously over the top, showing rustic spatula swirls. In the background, the whole round cake rests on a simple stand, partially frosted, highlighting its homemade comfort. A casually draped cloth napkin accompanies the plate. Warm kitchen lighting illuminates the lived-in, family dining atmosphere with natural clutter.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with a cup of coffee or milk.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease and flour a 20 cm round cake tin.
In a large bowl, whisk together flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt.
In a separate bowl, whisk eggs, coconut cream, apple liqueur, jasmine tea, and oil.
Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Fold in grated apple.
Pour batter into prepared tin. Bake 30-35 minutes, or until a skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
Let cake cool in tin for 10 minutes. Invert onto a wire rack to cool completely.
For frosting: Beat cream cheese and butter until smooth and creamy.
Gradually add sifted icing sugar. Beat until light and fluffy.
Stir in finely grated Tex-Mex cheese, vanilla extract, and pinch of salt. Mix until combined.
Once cake is completely cool, spread frosting generously over the top.
Serve immediately or store in an airtight container.
notes: The Tex-Mex cheese adds a subtle savory tang to the frosting, complementing the sweetness of the cake.
Ensure all frosting ingredients are at room temperature for a smooth consistency.

recipes.recipe_name: Nem Nuong (Vietnamese Grilled Pork Patties)
recipes.visual_description: Golden-brown Nem Nuong patties, slightly irregular in shape, are casually arranged on a white rectangular ceramic sharing platter. The surface of each patty shows subtle charring and a glossy sheen from cooking. Scattered around the patties are vibrant green spearmint leaves, thin rounds of bright red bird's eye chilies, and a few crisp lettuce cups. A small, clear glass bowl holds a rich amber-colored Nuoc Cham dipping sauce, topped with a sprinkle of crushed roasted peanuts. Beside it, a neat stack of translucent rice paper wrappers and a small dish of julienned pickled daikon and carrots add contrasting textures and colors. The scene is set on a light wooden table, with natural, soft light illuminating the fresh ingredients.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm water for softening rice paper wrappers.
Encourage communal eating, where diners assemble their own rolls.
Offer various fresh herbs beyond spearmint, such as perilla, cilantro, and Vietnamese balm.

ingredients.name: Red bird's eye chili, thinly sliced (for dipping sauce)

instructions: Prepare Pork Mixture: In a large bowl, combine minced pork, minced garlic, minced shallots, fish sauce, sugar, black pepper, baking powder, and cornstarch.
Mix thoroughly by hand for 5-7 minutes until paste-like and sticky. Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Form Patties: Dampen hands. Form the pork mixture into small, flat patties, about 3-4 cm in diameter and 1 cm thick. This recipe yields approximately 16-20 patties.
Cook Patties: Heat vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat.
Cook patties in batches for 4-5 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature should reach 71°C.
Remove and drain on paper towels.
Prepare Dipping Sauce: In a small bowl, whisk together fish sauce, water, sugar, and lime juice until sugar dissolves.
Stir in minced garlic and sliced chili.
Prepare Accompaniments: Arrange rice paper wrappers, spearmint, lettuce, julienned cucumber, and pickled daikon and carrot on a large serving platter.
Serve: Arrange cooked pork patties on the platter with accompaniments. Serve with Nuoc Cham dipping sauce and crushed peanuts on the side.
Diners dip rice paper in warm water, then wrap patties and vegetables.
traditional_techniques: Quet (whipping/kneading pork mixture): Essential for achieving the characteristic springy texture of Nem Nuong.
Nuoc Cham preparation: Balancing sweet, sour, salty, and spicy flavors.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Goat Milk & Pear Parfait with Spiced Pecan
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of the dessert is presented in a clear, slender glass tumbler, showcasing its distinct layers. The base is a smooth, creamy white layer of fermented goat milk. Above this, thinly sliced, translucent poached pear wedges are artfully arranged, leaning against the glass, their soft golden-amber hues visible. A generous scattering of dark, crunchy spiced pecan crumble tops the parfait, providing textural contrast. A delicate drizzle of pear peel syrup glistens over the top. The glass sits on a light, textured bamboo or reclaimed wood surface. A natural, undyed linen napkin in beige is softly folded beside it. The scene is bathed in soft, natural daylight, with a clean, minimalist background featuring a hint of a green plant, emphasizing the dish's organic and sustainable ethos. The presentation is unfussy, allowing the natural beauty of each ingredient to shine.

ingredients.name: Live yogurt culture or kefir grains

instructions: Gently warm goat milk to 40°C.
Stir in live yogurt culture or kefir grains.
Pour into clean jar. Cover with breathable cloth.
Ferment at room temperature for 12-24 hours until thick and tangy. Refrigerate.
Peel pears. Reserve peels. Halve pears. Remove core.
Combine 500 ml water, 50 ml maple syrup, cinnamon stick, star anise, lemon peel in a saucepan. Bring to a simmer.
Add pears. Poach gently for 15-20 minutes until tender. Remove pears. Cool. Slice thinly before serving.
For pear peel syrup: Simmer reserved pear peels in 100 ml water for 10 minutes. Strain liquid. Reduce liquid to a light syrup.
Preheat oven to 160°C.
Coarsely chop pecans.
Combine pecans, oats, coconut oil, 15 ml maple syrup, salt, and cinnamon powder in a bowl. Mix well.
Spread mixture on a baking sheet.
Bake for 10-12 minutes until golden and crisp. Cool completely.
Spoon fermented goat milk into individual serving glasses.
Arrange sliced poached pears on top.
Sprinkle with pecan crumble.
Drizzle with pear peel syrup. Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust fermentation time for desired tanginess. Use ripe but firm pears for best texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Miso Mushroom and Tofu Noodle Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Hearty Miso Mushroom and Tofu Noodle Soup is presented in a deep, dark grey or earthy brown ceramic ramen bowl, typical of Japanese homeware. The noodles are loosely coiled at the bottom, submerged in the rich, opaque, savory brown broth. Cubes of white, firm tofu and various sliced brown mushrooms (shiitake, enoki) are nestled among the noodles and floating on the surface. Vibrant green wilted bok choy leaves are scattered throughout, adding a fresh contrast. The soup is garnished simply with thinly sliced bright green spring onion rounds and a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds, offering a pop of color and texture. The bowl sits on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table, showing natural grain and minor imperfections. Beside the bowl, a pair of wooden chopsticks rests casually on a small ceramic chopstick holder. A simple, slightly wrinkled off-white linen napkin is placed informally nearby. The lighting is soft and warm, mimicking natural light from a kitchen window, creating a cozy, inviting, and lived-in family kitchen atmosphere. The scene is clean but not sterile, emphasizing comfort and authentic home dining.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately while hot.
Offer shichimi togarashi (Japanese seven-spice blend) on the side for a spicy kick.
instructions: Rehydrate dried shiitake mushrooms in warm water for 20 minutes. Squeeze out excess water. Thinly slice the rehydrated shiitake. Trim enoki mushrooms.
Cut firm tofu into 2 cm cubes. Roughly chop bok choy.
Heat sesame oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in vegetable broth. Bring the broth to a gentle simmer.
Add sliced shiitake mushrooms, enoki mushrooms, and tofu cubes to the simmering broth. Cook for 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are tender.
Add ramen noodles to the pot. Cook according to package instructions, usually 3-5 minutes, until tender.
While noodles cook, scoop miso paste into a small bowl. Ladle a small amount of hot broth into the bowl with the miso. Whisk until the miso paste is fully dissolved and smooth.
Remove the pot from heat. Stir the dissolved miso mixture into the main soup pot. Do not boil the soup after adding miso.
Stir in the chopped bok choy and soy sauce. Cook for 1-2 minutes until bok choy wilts.
Taste the soup and adjust seasoning with more soy sauce if needed.
Ladle the hearty soup into individual serving bowls. Garnish each bowl generously with thinly sliced spring onions and a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds. Serve immediately.
notes: Do not boil the soup after adding the miso paste, as high heat can destroy the beneficial probiotics and delicate flavor of the miso.

For an even richer broth, you can make a simple vegan dashi by simmering a 10 cm piece of kombu (dried kelp) and 10 grams of dried shiitake mushrooms in 1.8 litres of water for 20 minutes before removing them and proceeding with the recipe.

recipes.recipe_name: Clear Beef Dashi with Hijiki and Silken Tofu
recipes.visual_description: An exquisite single portion of clear beef dashi is presented in a deep, dark grey ceramic bowl, resting on a polished white Carrara marble surface. The consommé, a translucent golden amber, forms the pristine base. Nestled within are precisely cut 1.5 cm cubes of pristine white silken tofu and delicate, rehydrated black hijiki seaweed strands. A few perfectly seared, rich brown beef tenderloin cubes (1.5 cm) are thoughtfully placed, offering a savory focal point. The composition features abundant negative space, highlighting the purity of the broth and the distinct forms of each element. A few drops of vibrant green chive oil artfully dot the surface, providing a subtle color contrast and aromatic finish. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, and a pair of elegant wooden chopsticks are positioned beside the bowl, completing a minimalist yet sophisticated Japanese aesthetic under dramatic, focused lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a traditional Japanese ceramic soup spoon.
Offer a small side of steamed short-grain rice, if desired, to accompany the soup.
instructions: Rinse beef bones. Place in large pot. Cover with 2.5 litres cold water. Bring to boil. Skim impurities. Reduce heat. Simmer 4 hours.
Strain beef stock through fine-mesh sieve. Chill completely. Skim all fat.

Prepare dashi: Combine 1 litre of the chilled beef stock with kombu in a pot. Heat gently to 60°C. Remove kombu. Bring to simmer. Add katsuobushi. Simmer 30 seconds. Turn off heat. Let sit 5 minutes. Strain through cheesecloth-lined sieve. Discard solids. Combine with remaining beef stock. This is your beef dashi base.
Prepare consommé raft: In a bowl, mix ground beef, egg whites, chopped leek, carrot, onion, and ginger. Slowly whisk into cold beef dashi base.
Place pot over medium heat. Stir constantly until raft forms and liquid simmers. Stop stirring. Create a small opening in raft for steam release. Simmer gently 45-60 minutes. Do not disturb.
Carefully ladle clear consommé through cheesecloth-lined sieve. Do not press raft. Season with soy sauce and salt.
Rehydrate hijiki: Soak dried hijiki in warm water 20 minutes. Drain. Rinse thoroughly. Set aside.
Prepare chive oil: Blanch chopped chives 10 seconds. Immediately plunge into ice water. Drain well. Blend with neutral oil until smooth. Strain through fine-mesh sieve or cheesecloth for clear oil.
Cut beef tenderloin into small, precise 1.5 cm cubes. Sear cubes quickly in hot pan until lightly browned on all sides. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Season with salt.
Gently cut silken tofu into 1.5 cm cubes.

To serve: Gently warm consommé. Place a few beef cubes, hijiki strands, and tofu cubes into each elegant soup bowl. Ladle hot consommé over ingredients. Drizzle a few drops of chive oil over each serving.
notes: Achieving a perfectly clear consommé requires patience and precise temperature control.
Use premium quality ingredients, especially for the soy sauce, to ensure the finest flavor profile.

recipes.recipe_name: Andean Raspberry-Lime Fermented Petits Fours
recipes.visual_description: Six to nine perfectly uniform miniature cubes of pate de fruits are arranged with precise, consistent spacing on a natural, unglazed Peruvian artisanal ceramic platter in an earthy cream or pale beige hue. Each cube, approximately 2.5cm, showcases a vibrant, deep crimson-red color from the fermented raspberries, with a soft, translucent, gelatinous texture. They are lightly coated in a fine, crystalline sugar-citric acid dusting, providing a subtle matte finish and a hint of sparkle. Tiny flecks of bright green lime zest are visibly suspended within the candy. The composition is clean and minimalist, allowing ample white space around each piece. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the pure colors and textures. The background is simple and unobtrusive, perhaps a blurred natural fiber or a subtle green plant, maintaining focus on the delicate sweets.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve on a natural stone slab or handcrafted ceramic plate, reflecting Andean artisanal traditions.
Accompany with a small cup of delicate herbal tea, such as muña (Andean mint) tea.
instructions: Clean raspberries. Combine 200g raspberries with 20g sugar in a clean jar.
Cover jar loosely. Ferment at room temperature for 2-3 days until slightly bubbly and tangy. Stir daily.
Strain fermented raspberries. Reserve 150g puree. Discard solids or repurpose.
Combine 4g pectin with 20g granulated sugar. Mix well.
In a saucepan, combine 150g fermented raspberry puree, 150g granulated sugar, 25g glucose syrup, and 15ml lime juice. Heat gently.
Bring mixture to a boil. Slowly whisk in pectin-sugar mixture. Stir constantly.
Continue cooking, stirring, until mixture reaches 106°C. Use a candy thermometer.
Remove from heat. Stir in raspberry vodka, elderflower liqueur, lime zest, and 1g citric acid dissolved in 5ml water.
Pour mixture into a lightly oiled 15cm x 15cm square mold lined with parchment paper.
Allow to set at room temperature for at least 4 hours, or overnight.
Once firm, unmold onto a cutting board. Cut into 8 uniform 2.5cm x 2.5cm cubes.
Combine 50g granulated sugar and 0.5g citric acid for coating. Toss each cube gently in the sugar mixture to coat evenly.
Arrange on a serving platter.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by utilizing the entire lime (juice and zest).
Any leftover fermented raspberry pulp can be repurposed for compotes or infused beverages, minimizing food waste.

recipes.recipe_name: Koshi An & Clotted Cream Entremet
recipes.visual_description: A single, pristine slice of entremet stands elegantly centered on a round, white porcelain plate with a delicate gold rim. The cake's cross-section is the focal point, revealing meticulously layered components with distinct textures and subtle color variations. At the base, a thin, light-brown ladyfinger biscotto layer provides a crisp foundation. Above it, a slightly thicker, pale beige mochi génoise layer, airy and subtly chewy, offers a soft contrast. The vibrant, smooth maroon layer of koshi an crémeux sits atop the génoise, its rich color providing a sophisticated visual anchor. Capping the structure is a creamy, off-white clotted cream mousse, light and ethereal, with a perfectly smooth top. The edges of each layer are razor-sharp, showcasing precision. A single, thin, rectangular shard of dark chocolate is placed artfully beside the slice, leaning slightly, offering a deep brown accent. A few delicate, almost invisible flakes of edible gold leaf shimmer atop the mousse. The plate is largely negative space, emphasizing the architectural beauty of the dessert. The setting is a pristine white marble surface, under dramatic, professional lighting that casts soft shadows, enhancing the dessert's sculptural form. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, sits subtly to the side. The overall presentation is one of sophisticated simplicity and restrained elegance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served as a final course in a multi-course tasting menu.
instructions: Prepare Ladyfinger Biscotto Base:
Crush ladyfingers finely. Melt 50g unsalted butter. Combine crushed ladyfingers, melted butter, and pinch of salt.
Press mixture firmly into an 18 cm cake ring lined with acetate on a flat tray. Chill 30 minutes.
Prepare Mochi Génoise:
Preheat oven to 170°C. Line an 18 cm round cake pan with parchment paper.
Whisk eggs and 60g granulated sugar over a bain-marie until warm (40°C) and frothy. Remove from heat. Continue whisking until thick, pale, and tripled in volume.
Sift all-purpose flour and glutinous rice flour together. Fold gently into egg mixture in three additions.
Whisk 15g melted butter and 15ml milk together. Fold into batter.
Pour batter into prepared pan. Bake 15-20 minutes, or until golden and springy. Cool completely on a wire rack. Trim to an 18 cm circle if necessary.
Prepare Koshi An Crémeux:
Bloom 1g gelatin in cold water for 5 minutes.
In a saucepan, whisk egg yolk and 100ml heavy cream. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until mixture thickens slightly. Do not boil.
Remove from heat. Stir in bloomed gelatin until dissolved.
Add koshi an and pinch of salt. Blend until very smooth with an immersion blender.
Pour crémeux over the chilled ladyfinger base in the cake ring. Smooth top. Freeze 1 hour until firm.
Prepare Clotted Cream Mousse:
Bloom 2g gelatin in cold water for 5 minutes.
Whip 150ml heavy cream with 30g granulated sugar and vanilla bean paste to soft peaks.
Gently fold in clotted cream.
Heat 20ml heavy cream gently. Stir in bloomed gelatin until dissolved.
Fold gelatin mixture into the clotted cream mixture gently.
Remove the partially frozen entremet from freezer. Place the cooled Mochi Génoise layer directly on top of the Koshi An Crémeux.
Pour the clotted cream mousse over the génoise layer, filling the cake ring. Smooth top.
Freeze minimum 4 hours, preferably overnight, until completely firm.
Assembly and Garnish:
Carefully unmold the entremet from the cake ring using a hot towel or blowtorch briefly around the sides. Peel off acetate.
Place entremet on a wire rack over a tray.
Allow to thaw in refrigerator for 2-3 hours before serving for optimal texture.
Before serving, cut into 4 precise, clean slices using a hot, sharp knife.
Plate each slice on an elegant dessert plate. Garnish each slice with a small, precise shard of tempered dark chocolate and a few flakes of edible gold leaf.
notes: Ensure all components are chilled or frozen as specified for clean layering and ease of assembly.
Use a sharp, hot knife for clean cuts when slicing the frozen entremet.

recipes.recipe_name: Sopa de Frijol con Queso Oaxaca
recipes.visual_description: A hearty single portion of Sopa de Frijol con Queso Oaxaca is presented in a deep, rustic terracotta or ceramic bowl. The soup is a rich, deep reddish-brown, with visible swirls of melted, creamy white Oaxaca cheese creating inviting pockets of texture. A small mound of shredded Oaxaca cheese rests atop, alongside a scattering of vibrant green, roughly chopped fresh cilantro leaves. A few thin, bright green slices of jalapeño are placed to the side for a pop of color. The bowl sits on a well-worn, natural wooden kitchen table, reflecting a homely setting. A simple, neutral-toned cloth napkin is casually placed beside it. Natural, warm light illuminates the scene, highlighting the comforting steam. A small stack of warm corn tortillas, slightly browned, sits nearby, ready for dipping. The presentation is unpretentious, inviting, and deeply comforting, evoking a family meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for dipping.
Offer a dollop of Mexican crema or sour cream on the side.
Provide extra crumbled cotija cheese for sprinkling.
Serve with a side of pickled red onions or a lime wedge.

ingredients.name: Jalapeño
ingredients.quantity: 1, seeded and thinly sliced (optional, for garnish)

instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add diced white onion. Sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and diced Roma tomato. Cook for 3 minutes until softened.
Stir in drained kidney beans, chicken stock, ground cumin, and dried Mexican oregano.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat and cook for 15 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
Carefully transfer half of the soup to a blender. Blend until smooth.
Return blended soup to the pot. Stir to combine.
Add half of the shredded Oaxaca cheese to the soup. Stir until melted and incorporated.
Stir in chopped fresh cilantro. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve hot. Garnish each bowl with remaining Oaxaca cheese and thin jalapeño slices, if using.
notes: For a richer flavor, you can use dried kidney beans, soaked overnight and cooked until tender before starting the recipe.
Adjust the amount of jalapeño to your preferred spice level, or omit for a milder soup.
traditional_techniques: Licuado (blending ingredients for a smooth consistency)

recipes.recipe_name: Comfort Apple Oat Crumble
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of warm Apple Oat Crumble is presented in a rustic, shallow ceramic bowl with a subtly imperfect rim. The golden-brown crumble topping, made from rolled oats, almond flour, and butter, forms a textured, uneven crust over the soft, bubbling apple filling. Diced apples, cooked until tender and lightly caramelized with maple syrup and cinnamon, peek through the gaps in the topping. A gentle pour of creamy soy milk cascades down one side of the crumble, pooling slightly at the base. The bowl rests on a well-used, light wooden dining table, with a casually folded, simple linen napkin beside it. Warm, soft kitchen lighting highlights the comforting textures and natural colors of the dessert, creating a homely, inviting atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm with a drizzle of soy milk or a scoop of vanilla ice cream.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Lightly grease a 20cm x 20cm baking dish.
Peel, core, and dice the apples into 2cm cubes.
In a large bowl, combine diced apples with 2 tablespoons of maple syrup and cinnamon. Toss to coat evenly. Pour apple mixture into the prepared baking dish.
In a separate bowl, combine rolled oats, almond flour, all-purpose flour, and a pinch of salt.
Cut cold butter into small cubes. Add butter to the oat mixture. Use your fingertips or a pastry blender to rub the butter into the dry ingredients until coarse crumbs form.
Stir in the remaining maple syrup into the crumble mixture.
Evenly sprinkle the crumble topping over the apple mixture in the baking dish.
Bake for 30-35 minutes, or until the topping is golden brown and the apple filling is bubbling and tender.
Remove from oven. Let cool for 10 minutes before serving.
notes: This crumble is best served warm.
Adjust maple syrup quantity to your sweetness preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Caramelized Garlic & Coriander Mousse with IPA Reduction and Saffron Crisp
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegant portion of Caramelized Garlic & Coriander Mousse is presented on a pristine white bone china plate, allowing abundant negative space to highlight its sophisticated simplicity. The mousse, a pale ivory dome with a smooth, silken texture, rests slightly off-center. A glossy, dark amber IPA reduction is artfully swirled beside the mousse, creating a fluid, organic line. A delicate, golden saffron crisp, thin and airy with subtle perforations, stands vertically or leans gracefully against the mousse, providing architectural height. A few vibrant green micro coriander sprigs are precisely placed on the mousse, adding a fresh color contrast. A whisper of edible gold leaf shimmers atop the mousse. The dish is set on a luxurious, veined white Carrara marble surface, complemented by a precisely folded white linen napkin. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing the textures and depth of the minimalist composition.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a final course in a modern Indian tasting menu.
Pair with a light, aromatic digestif or a subtle masala chai.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Roast garlic cloves for 20 minutes until soft and caramelized. Mash into a smooth paste. Set aside.
Bloom gelatin sheets in cold water for 5 minutes.
Gently toast coriander seeds. Grind finely. Infuse 200 ml cream with ground coriander over low heat for 10 minutes. Strain to remove solids.
Heat remaining 200 ml cream with 50g granulated sugar. Add softened gelatin and stir until dissolved. Remove from heat. Stir in roasted garlic paste and strained coriander cream. Mix well.
Pour mousse mixture into small molds or shallow dishes. Chill for at least 4 hours, or until set.

For IPA reduction, combine beer and remaining 50g granulated sugar in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Simmer until syrup thickens to a nappe consistency, about 15-20 minutes. Cool completely.

For saffron crisps, combine flour, powdered sugar, melted butter, and saffron threads. Mix to a smooth batter. Spread thin layers onto a silicone mat or parchment paper. Bake at 160°C for 5-7 minutes until golden and crisp. Cool completely.

To plate, unmold mousse onto a chilled white bone china plate. Drizzle IPA reduction artfully around the mousse. Place one saffron crisp beside the mousse. Garnish with a few micro coriander sprigs and a delicate piece of edible gold leaf.
notes: Ensure garlic is deeply caramelized to remove pungency and enhance sweetness.
The IPA reduction can be prepared in advance and stored in the refrigerator.

recipes.recipe_name: Macadamia Lingonberry Entremet
recipes.visual_description: A single, meticulously cut slice of the Macadamia Lingonberry Entremet is presented with architectural precision on an elegant, pristine white porcelain dessert plate with a subtle gold rim. The slice reveals distinct, perfectly layered components: a glossy, vibrant lingonberry-hued mirror glaze on top, followed by a smooth, creamy white chocolate mousse layer. Beneath the mousse, a vivid, deep red lingonberry gelée insert provides a striking color contrast. The base is a golden-brown macadamia dacquoise, showcasing its delicate, airy texture. Abundant negative space surrounds the dessert, emphasizing its sculptural form. The plate rests on a polished white marble display surface, illuminated by dramatic professional lighting that creates soft shadows, highlighting the dessert's contours and the glaze's high sheen. A crisp, white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, is placed alongside. The background is ultra-minimalist, drawing all focus to the meticulously crafted entremet.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Roast macadamia nuts for 8-10 minutes until lightly golden. Cool completely. Grind finely.
Sift icing sugar and cornstarch. Combine with ground macadamia nuts and 70g granulated sugar.
Whip egg whites until soft peaks form. Gradually add remaining 30g granulated sugar, whip until stiff and glossy meringue forms.
Gently fold the dry nut mixture into the meringue until just combined.
Spread dacquoise batter evenly onto the prepared baking sheet, forming a thin rectangle (approx. 20x15cm).
Bake for 15-20 minutes until golden and firm to touch. Cool completely. Cut into a 16x10cm rectangle.
Bloom 3g gelatin sheets in cold water for 5 minutes.
Heat lingonberry puree, 40g granulated sugar, and lemon juice in a saucepan until sugar dissolves. Do not boil.
Squeeze excess water from gelatin. Stir into warm lingonberry mixture until dissolved.
Pour lingonberry mixture into a 14x8cm rectangular silicone mold. Freeze until solid (at least 2 hours).
Bloom 2g gelatin sheets in cold water for 5 minutes.
Gently heat 100g heavy cream in a small saucepan. Pour hot cream over white chocolate. Let sit 1 minute. Stir until smooth ganache forms.
Squeeze excess water from gelatin. Stir into warm ganache until dissolved. Add vanilla extract.
Whip remaining 200g heavy cream to soft peaks.
Once ganache mixture is cooled to room temperature, gently fold in whipped cream until combined.
Line a 18x12cm rectangular silicone mold with plastic wrap.
Pour half of the white chocolate mousse into the mold. Place the frozen lingonberry insert centered on top.
Pour remaining mousse over the insert, ensuring it is fully covered. Top with the macadamia dacquoise layer, pressing gently.
Freeze the entremet for at least 6 hours, or preferably overnight, until completely solid.
Bloom 6g gelatin sheets in cold water for 5 minutes.
In a saucepan, combine glucose syrup, 100g granulated sugar, and 50g water. Bring to a boil. Remove from heat.
Stir in condensed milk and white chocolate until melted and smooth. Squeeze excess water from gelatin. Stir into hot mixture until dissolved.
Add red food coloring, if desired, for a vibrant hue. Blend with an immersion blender, keeping the head submerged to avoid air bubbles.
Strain the glaze through a fine-mesh sieve. Cool to 35°C.
Remove entremet from freezer. Unmold carefully. Place on a wire rack over a baking sheet.
Pour the tempered glaze evenly over the frozen entremet, ensuring full coverage. Let excess drip off. Use an offset spatula to remove drips from the bottom.
Carefully transfer the glazed entremet to a serving plate. Allow to thaw in the refrigerator for 2-3 hours before serving.
Slice the entremet into 4 portions using a hot, dry knife.
Garnish each slice with a few fresh lingonberries and a tiny piece of edible gold leaf.

recipes.recipe_name: Coconut-Ginger Cashew Layer Cake
recipes.visual_description: A single slice of Coconut-Ginger Cashew Layer Cake rests centrally on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The slice showcases distinct, light golden-brown cake layers alternating with thick, creamy, off-white cashew-ginger frosting. The cake layers have a subtle, moist crumb. The frosting is smooth and substantial. A delicate sprinkle of golden-brown toasted coconut flakes adorns the top of the slice, alongside a few translucent, amber pieces of candied ginger. A small cluster of whole, roasted cashews sits near the base of the slice. The plate is placed on a simple wooden table surface. A crisp white cotton napkin is folded neatly beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene. In the soft-focus background, a small, fully frosted whole cake on a simple cake stand hints at its origin.

ingredients.name: Coconut cream (thick part of full-fat coconut milk)

instructions: Soak raw cashews in hot water for at least 30 minutes, or cold water overnight. Drain well before use.
Preheat oven to 175°C. Grease and flour two 18 cm round cake pans.
In a large bowl, whisk together flour, granulated sugar, baking powder, salt, shredded coconut, and ground ginger.
In a separate bowl, whisk together eggs, coconut milk, vegetable oil, and vanilla extract.
Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Divide batter evenly between prepared cake pans. Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until a wooden skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
Cool cake layers in pans for 10 minutes. Invert onto a wire rack to cool completely.

For the cashew cream frosting: Combine drained cashews, coconut cream, maple syrup, grated fresh ginger, lime juice, and vanilla extract in a high-speed blender. Blend until completely smooth and creamy. Scrape down sides as needed.
Once cake layers are completely cool, place one layer on a serving plate. Spread a generous layer of cashew frosting over the top.
Place the second cake layer on top. Frost the top and sides of the entire cake with remaining frosting.
Garnish the top of the cake with toasted coconut flakes, chopped candied ginger, and roasted cashews.
notes: Ensure cashews are thoroughly soaked and blended for a smooth, lump-free frosting.
For best results, use full-fat coconut milk that has been refrigerated overnight; scoop only the thick cream for the frosting.

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Cream Cheese Revani
recipes.visual_description: A single square portion of Lemon Cream Cheese Revani is presented on a clean, white porcelain dessert plate. The cake is golden brown on top with a moist, light yellow interior, visibly drenched with glistening lemon syrup. Its texture appears soft and tender, with slightly crisp edges. A small scattering of finely chopped pistachios garnishes one corner of the cake, adding a vibrant green contrast. A thin, delicate curl of fresh lemon zest rests beside the cake. The plate sits on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin is placed to the side. The scene is illuminated by natural, even lighting, creating a bright and inviting atmosphere. The background is softly blurred, suggesting a modern bistro setting, keeping the focus entirely on the dessert.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve chilled or at room temperature.
Pairs well with a small cup of traditional Greek coffee (Ellinikos Kafes).
Can be accompanied by a small dollop of extra thick, strained Greek yogurt on the side.
instructions: Prepare the syrup: Combine water, 300g sugar, lemon juice, and lemon slices in a saucepan. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat. Simmer 10 minutes until slightly thickened. Remove from heat. Stir in honey. Let cool completely.
Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease and flour a 20x20 cm baking dish.
Whisk semolina, flour, and baking powder in a bowl. Set aside.
In a large bowl, cream softened cream cheese with 200g sugar until light and fluffy.
Beat in eggs one at a time until well combined.
Stir in Greek yogurt, melted butter, vanilla extract, and lemon zest.
Gradually add dry ingredients to wet ingredients. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Pour batter into prepared baking dish. Spread evenly.
Bake 40-45 minutes. Cake is golden brown and a toothpick inserted comes out clean.
Remove cake from oven. Immediately pour cooled syrup evenly over the hot cake.
Let cake cool completely in the dish. Syrup will absorb fully.
Cut into 4 equal square pieces. Serve.
notes: Ensure the syrup is cool and the cake is hot when combined for optimal absorption.
The cream cheese adds a rich, tender crumb, distinguishing it from traditional Revani.

recipes.recipe_name: Moroccan Pickled Onion & Tomato Salad with Fresh Cheese
recipes.visual_description: A single starter portion of Moroccan Pickled Onion & Tomato Salad is elegantly presented on a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic plate in a natural cream hue. Thinly sliced, vibrant purple-red pickled onion rings are arranged loosely at the center, intertwined with bright red halved cherry tomatoes. Crumbled white fresh cheese is scattered over the vegetables, adding a creamy contrast. Fresh green mint and cilantro leaves are delicately placed on top, providing bursts of color and natural texture. The arrangement is organic and flowing, with ample negative space on the plate, highlighting each ingredient's natural beauty. The plate rests on a light, reclaimed wood surface. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is folded simply beside the plate. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish from the side, creating gentle shadows and enhancing the vibrant colors. The background is clean and minimalist, with a hint of a green plant out of focus, maintaining an eco-conscious and uncluttered aesthetic.
instructions: Thinly slice red onions into rings. Halve cherry tomatoes.
Combine vinegar, water, sugar, and salt in a small saucepan. Heat until sugar and salt dissolve. Remove from heat. Let cool slightly.
Place sliced onions in a heatproof jar. Pour warm pickling liquid over onions. Ensure onions are fully submerged. Let cool to room temperature. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
In a mixing bowl, combine halved cherry tomatoes, cumin powder, smoked paprika, olive oil, and preserved lemon pulp. Toss gently to coat.
Drain pickled red onions. Add to the tomato mixture.
Crumble fresh crumbly cheese over the salad. Gently tear mint and cilantro leaves. Add to the salad.
Toss ingredients gently to combine. Serve immediately as a starter.

recipes.recipe_name: Chili Bean Paste Glazed Vegetable Fritters
recipes.visual_description: A cluster of golden-brown vegetable fritters, irregular in shape, are artfully arranged on a clean, white porcelain snack plate. Each fritter, approximately 5-6 cm in diameter, is visibly studded with shredded vibrant green gai lan and pak choi, interspersed with translucent minced shallots. A rich, glossy reddish-brown glaze, made from chili bean paste, coats the top of each fritter, catching the light. A light sprinkle of finely sliced fresh green scallions provides a contrasting pop of color and freshness. The plate features moderate negative space, showcasing the professional, yet approachable presentation. The setting is a modern bistro, with the plate resting on a simple light wooden table surface. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the dish. A folded grey cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. The overall presentation is clean, appetizing, and inviting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with chopsticks for a traditional eating experience.
Offer a small side dish of light soy sauce for additional dipping if desired.
instructions: Wash gai lan and pak choi thoroughly. Shred both vegetables into fine strips.
Finely mince the shallots.
In a large bowl, combine shredded gai lan, pak choi, and minced shallots.
In a separate bowl, whisk together flour, cornstarch, egg, cold water, salt, and white pepper to form a smooth batter.
Pour the batter over the shredded vegetables. Mix gently until vegetables are evenly coated.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pan or wok to 175°C (350°F).
Carefully drop spoonfuls of the vegetable mixture into the hot oil. Flatten slightly with the back of a spoon to form fritters, approximately 6-7 cm in diameter.
Fry fritters for 3-4 minutes per side, or until golden brown and crispy. Do not overcrowd the pan.
Remove fritters with a slotted spoon. Place on a wire rack lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.

For the glaze: In a small saucepan, combine chili bean paste, soy sauce, rice vinegar, and sugar. Heat over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until the mixture thickens slightly, about 2-3 minutes.
Arrange hot fritters on a serving platter. Brush each fritter generously with the chili bean paste glaze.
Finely slice the green part of the scallions for garnish. Sprinkle over the glazed fritters. Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust chili bean paste quantity to your preferred spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Sea Bass and Braised Beef Short Rib with Fish Stock Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined portion of a sophisticated Modern European dish is presented on a pristine white bone china plate, featuring abundant negative space. A fluid, creamy fish stock risotto is elegantly swirled on one side of the plate. Adjacent to the risotto rests a tender, dark chunk of braised beef short rib, its rich color contrasting with the creamy rice. A golden, pan-seared sea bass fillet, skin-side up with perfectly crisped, scored skin, is carefully positioned atop or beside the risotto, showcasing its delicate texture. A deep, glossy red wine jus is artfully drizzled around the main components, creating a visual flow. A minimal garnish of bright green microgreens or finely chopped chives is precisely placed for a pop of color and freshness. The scene is set on a premium white Carrara marble surface, with a crisply folded white linen napkin in a precise triangle. Dramatic professional lighting casts subtle shadows, enhancing the dish's architectural precision and elegant simplicity, highlighting each perfectly executed component.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C.
Season beef short ribs with salt and pepper. Heat 15 ml olive oil in a heavy oven-safe pot over medium-high heat. Sear beef on all sides until deeply browned. Remove beef from pot. Set aside.
Add diced carrot, celery, and half of the shallots to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring.
Deglaze the pot with red wine. Scrape up any browned bits. Return beef to the pot. Add beef stock, thyme, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.

Cover the pot tightly. Transfer to the preheated oven. Braise for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender. Remove beef from pot. Strain braising liquid through a fine-mesh sieve into a saucepan. Discard solids.
Return saucepan with strained liquid to medium-high heat. Reduce liquid by half to two-thirds until it forms a rich, glossy jus. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

For the risotto: Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil and 15 g butter in a separate saucepan over medium heat. Add remaining shallots. Sauté until translucent, about 3 minutes. Add Arborio rice. Stir for 1 minute until edges are translucent.

Pour in 100 ml white wine. Stir until absorbed. Gradually add warm fish stock, 150 ml at a time, stirring constantly. Allow each addition to be almost fully absorbed before adding the next. Continue for 18-20 minutes, or until rice is creamy and al dente.
Remove risotto from heat. Stir in 40 g butter and grated Parmesan (if using). Season with salt and pepper. The risotto should be fluid, not stiff.
For the sea bass: Pat fish fillets dry. Score the skin lightly with a sharp knife, 2-3 times per fillet. Season skin and flesh with salt and pepper.

Heat a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Add 10 ml olive oil. Once shimmering, place sea bass fillets skin-side down. Press gently with a spatula for the first 30 seconds to ensure even contact. Cook for 4-5 minutes until skin is crispy and golden brown.
Flip fillets. Cook for 1-2 minutes on the flesh side, or until internal temperature reaches 63°C and flesh is opaque and flaky. Do not overcook.

To plate: Spoon a generous swirl of fluid fish stock risotto onto one side of a large, warm plate. Place a chunk of braised beef short rib next to the risotto. Carefully position a pan-seared sea bass fillet, skin-side up, on top of or beside the risotto, showcasing its crispy skin. Drizzle the rich red wine jus artfully around the components. Garnish with a few microgreens or finely chopped chives. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Prickly Pear & Coconut Entremet Cubes
recipes.visual_description: A luxury Michelin setting features a pristine white Carrara marble surface. Eight perfectly uniform 3x3 cm Prickly Pear & Coconut Entremet Cubes are arranged with architectural precision on an elegant white rectangular bone china serving platter. Each miniature cube boasts distinct layers: a vibrant magenta prickly pear gelée, creamy white coconut mousse, and a tender, pale orange sponge base. The entire cube is enveloped in a flawless, glossy orange-cinnamon mirror glaze, reflecting the dramatic professional lighting. The glaze’s sophisticated hue provides subtle contrast to the vibrant interior. Each cube is meticulously placed with generous negative space, creating a clean, minimalist composition. A single, delicate, thinly curled candied orange peel precisely adorns the top of each cube, providing a refined garnish and a pop of contrasting texture. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, rests elegantly beside the platter. The background is ultra-minimalist, emphasizing the exquisite detail and vibrant colors of the petit fours.
instructions: Soak 2g gelatin in ice water.
Combine prickly pear puree and 30g sugar in a saucepan. Heat gently until sugar dissolves. Do not boil.
Remove from heat. Squeeze excess water from gelatin. Stir gelatin into warm puree until dissolved.
Pour a 0.5 cm layer into a small square or rectangular mold lined with plastic wrap. Freeze until firm.
Preheat oven to 170°C. Line a 20x20 cm baking sheet with parchment paper.
Whisk 1 egg and 30g sugar until pale and fluffy.
Fold in 30g all-purpose flour gently.
Fold in 15g melted butter and orange zest.
Spread batter thinly onto prepared baking sheet. Bake for 8-10 minutes. Cool completely.
Soak 2g gelatin in cold water (15ml).
Gently heat 50 ml coconut cream with 20g sugar until sugar dissolves. Do not boil.
Squeeze excess water from gelatin. Stir gelatin into warm coconut cream mixture until dissolved.
Whisk remaining chilled coconut cream until soft peaks form.
Fold warm gelatin mixture into whipped coconut cream.
Line your mold with acetate strips or plastic wrap.
Pour half of the coconut mousse into the mold.
Carefully place the frozen prickly pear gelée layer on top of the mousse.
Pour the remaining coconut mousse over the gelée.
Cut the cooled orange sponge to fit the mold. Place it on top of the mousse.
Freeze for at least 6 hours, or overnight, until completely solid.
Soak 8g gelatin in ice water.
Combine 100g sugar, 50ml water, and 100g glucose syrup in a saucepan. Heat to 103°C.
Remove from heat. Add 70g condensed milk, 100g chopped white chocolate, 30ml orange juice, and 0.5g ground cinnamon. Stir until chocolate melts.
Squeeze excess water from gelatin. Stir gelatin into the glaze until dissolved.
Add food coloring if desired.
Use an immersion blender to emulsify, avoiding air bubbles. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve.
Cool glaze to 32-35°C.
Remove frozen entremet from the mold. Trim edges for neatness.
Using a hot, dry knife, cut the frozen entremet block into 8 uniform 3x3 cm cubes.
Place cubes on a wire rack set over a tray.
Pour the warm glaze evenly over each frozen cube.
Allow excess glaze to drip off. Carefully transfer cubes to a clean serving platter.
Garnish each cube with a delicate candied orange peel strip.
Refrigerate for at least 1 hour to thaw and set the glaze. Serve chilled.

recipes.recipe_name: Chickpea and Fresh Vegetable Salad
recipes.visual_description: A generous portion of vibrant Chickpea and Fresh Vegetable Salad is presented in a deep, earthy-toned ceramic bowl. Diced chickpeas, bright red tomatoes, crisp green cucumbers, and finely chopped red onions are casually mixed, showcasing their natural colors and textures. A light, reddish-orange dressing, incorporating marinara and chili, coats the ingredients evenly. Fresh, bright green cilantro leaves are scattered across the top. The bowl sits on a worn, light wooden dining table. Adjacent is a simple, off-white ceramic plate. A small, shiny stainless steel katori holds a vibrant green chili pickle. A stack of warm, soft chapatis, wrapped in a cloth, rests beside it. Traditional Indian metal spoons are placed for serving. Warm, soft light from an overhead kitchen fixture highlights the homely, inviting atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm chapati or roti.
Accompanied by a side of Indian pickle (achar) or plain yogurt.
instructions: Prepare vegetables: Dice cucumber, tomato, and red onion into small, uniform pieces. Finely chop cilantro and green chili.
Drain and rinse chickpeas thoroughly.
Combine salad ingredients: In a large bowl, mix drained chickpeas, diced cucumber, diced tomato, and finely chopped red onion.
Prepare dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together marinara sauce, olive oil, finely chopped green chili, lime juice, cumin powder, chaat masala, salt, and black pepper.
Dress salad: Pour the prepared dressing over the chickpea and vegetable mixture. Toss gently to coat all ingredients evenly.
Garnish: Stir in fresh chopped cilantro. Serve immediately or chill before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Cabbage and Lentil Salad with Berbere Vinaigrette
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Ethiopian-inspired salad is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate, resting on a simple wooden table. A generous mound of thinly shredded green cabbage forms the base, intertwined with earthy brown lentils. Bright julienned orange carrots, diced red bell pepper, and thinly sliced red onion add bursts of color and varied textures. The vegetables are tender-crisp from a light sauté with aromatic berbere spice. Four perfectly quartered hard-boiled eggs are artfully arranged around the salad mound, showcasing their creamy yellow yolks and firm white. A small, elegant dollop of rich clotted cream sits beside the salad, offering a creamy counterpoint. The entire dish is glistening lightly with a unique lingonberry-rose vinaigrette, infused with subtle berbere notes. Fresh green cilantro leaves are scattered for a final pop of color. The setting features a simple cotton napkin beside the plate, with soft, natural lighting highlighting the fresh ingredients. A side of warm injera bread is subtly visible, ready for traditional scooping.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with injera bread for traditional scooping.
instructions: Rinse lentils. Cook lentils in 600ml water until tender, about 20-25 minutes. Drain any excess liquid.
Place eggs in a saucepan. Cover with cold water. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, simmer 8 minutes. Transfer eggs to ice bath. Peel and quarter when cool.
Heat a large pan over medium heat. Add a splash of olive oil. Sauté sliced red onion for 3 minutes until softened.
Add julienned carrots, diced bell pepper, minced garlic, and grated ginger. Sauté 5-7 minutes until vegetables are tender-crisp.
Stir in 5g berbere spice blend. Cook 1 minute until fragrant. Remove from heat.
In a small bowl, whisk remaining 10g berbere spice, 60ml olive oil, red wine vinegar, lingonberry preserves, rose water, salt, and black pepper.
In a large bowl, combine cooked lentils, sautéed vegetables, and thinly shredded cabbage. Pour dressing over salad. Toss gently to combine.
Divide salad among 4 plates. Arrange 4 egg quarters on each plate. Place a small dollop of clotted cream beside the salad or on top. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro.
notes: This recipe is a fusion, incorporating non-traditional ingredients like clotted cream, rose, and lingonberry into an Ethiopian-inspired savory salad.

recipes.recipe_name: Moroccan Cacao Almond Bites
recipes.visual_description: Six to nine uniform, miniature Moroccan Cacao Almond Bites are elegantly arranged on a round, deep blue and white hand-painted ceramic Moroccan platter. Each bite is a rich, dark chocolate-brown sphere, about 3 cm in diameter, with a slightly cracked, rustic surface. A delicate, fine dusting of reddish-brown sweet paprika lightly coats each bite, offering a subtle contrast. The bites are spaced evenly, creating a balanced, approachable display. The platter sits on a simple light wooden table. A folded white cotton napkin is placed to the side. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the scene, emphasizing the bites' texture and color, with a minimal, blurred bistro-style background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve alongside traditional Moroccan mint tea.
Offer on an ornate platter during social gatherings or as a post-meal treat.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C. Line a baking tray with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, whisk almond flour, granulated sugar, cacao powder, baking powder, and salt.
In a separate bowl, lightly whisk egg whites and orange blossom water.
Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Form small balls, approximately 15g each. Place them on the prepared baking tray. Ensure spacing between each bite.
Bake for 12-15 minutes. Bites should be firm but slightly soft in the center.
Cool the bites completely on a wire rack.
Once cool, lightly dust each bite with sweet paprika.
traditional_techniques: Use of orange blossom water for aroma

recipes.recipe_name: Mini Glazed Almond Financiers
recipes.visual_description: Six to nine mini glazed almond financiers are arranged artfully on an elegant white rectangular porcelain serving platter. Each financier is a small, golden-brown oval cake, topped with a smooth, opaque white glaze. The glaze is evenly applied, with subtle drips on some sides, indicating its fresh application. The cakes exhibit a delicate, slightly crisp exterior, contrasting with a soft, moist interior. Their color is a warm, toasted almond hue. The arrangement is casual yet cohesive, with financiers touching or slightly overlapping. The platter rests on a well-used wooden dining table, beside a casually placed textured linen napkin. Warm, inviting light from kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene, highlighting the glaze's sheen and the cakes' golden tones. The background is minimal, emphasizing the homely, expertly crafted comfort food. No decorative garnishes are used.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served typically with coffee or tea.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Grease and flour a mini financier or mini muffin tin.
Melt butter in a small saucepan over medium heat. Cook until golden brown and fragrant. Strain through a fine sieve. Let cool slightly.
In a large bowl, whisk together icing sugar, ground almonds, and plain flour.
Add egg whites and vanilla extract to dry ingredients. Mix until just combined.
Gradually whisk in the cooled brown butter until smooth.
Pour batter into prepared mini molds, filling about two-thirds full.
Bake for 12-15 minutes, or until edges are golden and centers are set.
Remove from oven. Let cool in the tin for 5 minutes. Transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.
For the glaze, whisk powdered sugar with water or lemon juice until smooth and pourable.
Dip the top of each cooled financier into the glaze. Let excess drip off.
Place glazed financiers back on the wire rack over parchment paper to set.

recipes.recipe_name: Hemp Almond Crisp, Fermented Tofu Date Cream
recipes.visual_description: A pristine white bone china plate holds a minimalist composition. Two or three irregularly shaped, golden-brown hemp seed and almond crisps are artfully arranged, some standing upright, others gently leaning. The crisps exhibit a delicate, slightly uneven texture with visible specks of hemp and finely ground almond. Beside them, a single, perfectly smooth quenelle of pale beige Date-Fermented Tofu Cream rests, its surface subtly glossy. A very fine, almost imperceptible dusting of dark, unsweetened cacao powder lightly coats a small area of the cream and the plate, creating a soft, ethereal shadow. The entire presentation emphasizes abundant negative space, with elements precisely positioned to create visual tension and balance. The plate sits on a polished light grey veined marble surface, accompanied by a crisply folded white linen napkin in the corner. Dramatic, focused lighting highlights the textures and delicate colors, casting subtle shadows to enhance depth. The scene is ultra-minimalist, drawing all attention to the sophisticated snack.

ingredients.name: White fermented tofu (preserved bean curd/furu), drained

instructions: Preheat oven to 150°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper, lightly brush with neutral oil.
For the crisps: Combine ground almonds, hemp seeds, rice flour, and salt in a bowl. Gradually add 50ml water, mixing until a thin, pourable batter forms. Adjust water for consistency.
Pour a small amount of batter onto the prepared parchment. Using an offset spatula, spread batter into an ultra-thin, almost transparent layer. Repeat for more crisps.
Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until crisps are golden brown and extremely dry and crisp. Watch carefully to prevent burning. Remove from oven and cool completely. Break into irregular, elegant shards.
For the cream: Soak pitted dates in warm water for 10 minutes to soften. Drain.
In a high-speed blender, combine softened dates, drained fermented tofu, 50ml filtered water (or rice milk), Chinese black vinegar, and white pepper.
Blend until the mixture is exceptionally smooth and creamy. Pass the cream through a fine-mesh sieve to ensure a perfectly silken texture. Chill until ready to serve.
To plate: Arrange two or three crisp shards on a pristine white bone china plate. Place a single, perfect quenelle of the chilled Date-Fermented Tofu Cream beside the crisps.
Lightly dust a small area of the cream and plate with finely grated cacao powder.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Plum and Sherry Loaf Cake with Green Onion Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A single generous slice of Plum and Sherry Loaf Cake sits on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate with a slightly uneven rim, typical of everyday home dinnerware. The cake slice is golden-brown with a tender, visible crumb, slightly darker where the plum sauce has caramelized. A glossy, opaque off-white glaze, with very fine flecks of bright green from the minced green onion, is casually drizzled over the top of the slice, some drips running down the sides. The rest of the golden-brown loaf cake, still in its simple, light-colored ceramic loaf pan, rests on a rustic wooden cutting board in the soft-focused background. The setting is a well-used wooden kitchen table, bathed in warm, cozy lighting from kitchen fixtures. A simple metal fork is placed beside the plate. A casually folded, plain linen napkin in a neutral tone lies nearby. The overall impression is one of warm, homemade comfort food, inviting and unpretentious, reflecting a lived-in family kitchen atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease and flour a 23x13 cm loaf pan.
In a medium bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, and salt. Set aside.
In a large bowl, cream softened butter and granulated sugar until light and fluffy.
Beat in eggs one at a time, mixing well after each addition.
Stir in plum sauce, sherry wine, milk, and vanilla extract until combined.
Gradually add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Pour batter into the prepared loaf pan. Smooth the top.
Bake for 50-60 minutes, or until a wooden skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
Let cake cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.
For the glaze: In a small bowl, whisk powdered sugar, milk/sherry, and very finely minced green onion until smooth.
Once the cake is completely cool, drizzle the glaze casually over the top of the cake.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Italian Endive and Olive Pasta Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of rustic Italian endive and olive pasta soup is presented in a deep, earthy-toned ceramic bowl with a slightly irregular rim. The soup has a rich, reddish-orange base from the crushed tomatoes, with visible chunks of tender, pale green endive (chopped into 2 cm pieces), dark halved Kalamata olives, and vibrant red julienned sun-dried tomatoes. Small, golden ditalini pasta shapes are suspended throughout the fluid broth. The surface of the soup is lightly speckled with fresh, bright green chopped parsley. The bowl sits on a well-worn, warm wooden dining table. Alongside the bowl, a simple ceramic side plate holds a thick slice of crusty, golden-brown Italian bread. A traditional silver spoon rests casually beside the bowl. The setting is a cozy, lived-in family kitchen, illuminated by soft, warm light from overhead fixtures, creating a comforting, inviting atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping.
Offer grated Parmesan cheese at the table for individual topping.
Enjoy as a comforting main course or a hearty starter.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in vegetable broth and crushed tomatoes. Add oregano, basil, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 15 minutes to allow flavors to meld.
Stir in pasta, chopped endive, halved olives, and julienned sun-dried tomatoes.
Increase heat to medium-low. Cook until pasta is al dente and endive is tender, about 8-10 minutes. Stir occasionally to prevent pasta from sticking.
Remove bay leaf. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Ladle hot soup into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: For a vegan option, omit Parmesan cheese or use a plant-based alternative.
Adjust pasta cooking time based on package instructions and desired tenderness.

recipes.recipe_name: Coconut Milk Spheres, Mandarin Syrup, Sugarcane Crisp
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents twelve perfectly spherical, creamy coconut milk spheres, each about 2 cm in diameter, artfully arranged on a large, shallow white bone china sharing platter. The spheres, cooked to a delicate tenderness, glisten with a shallow pool of pale orange mandarin syrup. Several translucent sugarcane crisps, golden-amber and abstractly curved, are strategically placed among the spheres, offering a stark textural contrast. A whisper of finely grated bright orange mandarin zest is scattered precisely over some spheres, adding vibrant color accents. The composition is minimalist, with abundant negative space highlighting the architectural simplicity and natural organic forms. Professional lighting casts soft, intentional shadows, emphasizing the delicate textures and refined presentation on a luxury marble surface.
cultural_serving_suggestions: This dish, while modern, is designed for communal enjoyment, reflecting the Indian tradition of sharing sweets and small bites during gatherings. It can be served alongside traditional Indian tea or as a refined conclusion to a meal.
instructions: Pour coconut cream into a wide, heavy-bottomed pan.
Simmer over low heat. Stir frequently to prevent scorching.
Reduce until very thick, like a pliable dough. This takes 45-60 minutes.
Transfer reduced coconut cream to a bowl. Chill completely, at least 2 hours.
Roll chilled coconut dough into 12 uniform spheres, approximately 2 cm in diameter. Place on parchment paper.
For the Mandarin-Sugarcane Syrup: Combine mandarin juice, 100g granulated sugar, and 50ml water in a saucepan.
Bring to a boil over medium heat. Simmer for 5 minutes until sugar dissolves and syrup slightly thickens.
Keep syrup warm.
For the Sugarcane Crisp: Preheat oven to 160°C. Line a baking sheet with a silicone mat.
Whisk remaining 50g granulated sugar, 25ml water, flour, and melted butter until smooth.
Pour small, thin circles (5-6 cm diameter) of batter onto the silicone mat. Spread thinly with the back of a spoon.
Bake for 8-10 minutes, or until golden and crisp.
Remove from oven. Immediately drape crisps over a rolling pin or small mould for a curved shape, or leave flat. Cool completely.
To assemble: Gently place coconut spheres into the warm mandarin syrup. Simmer for 2 minutes to warm through.
Arrange all 12 warm spheres artfully on a large, shallow white bone china sharing platter.
Spoon a small amount of mandarin syrup over and around the spheres.
Place several sugarcane crisps strategically among the spheres.
Garnish with finely grated mandarin zest.
Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure coconut cream is reduced slowly over low heat to prevent scorching. The final consistency should be like a thick, pliable dough for shaping.
The sugarcane crisps are delicate; handle with care. They add essential textural contrast to the soft spheres.
traditional_techniques: Shaping of solids (similar to chhena for rasmalai)

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Persimmon & Vanilla Ladyfinger Sandwiches
recipes.visual_description: The dessert features 6-9 delicate miniature ladyfinger sandwiches, precisely cut and arranged on a light bamboo serving platter. Each sandwich is a creamy off-white from the whipped coconut cream, contrasting with the soft, rustic orange of the fermented persimmon puree peeking from between the two ladyfinger halves. The ladyfingers retain their pale, airy texture. A fine, even dusting of dark, earthy hot chocolate powder mixed with finely ground black sesame seeds covers the top, creating a subtle, matte finish with tiny dark flecks. The arrangement is clean and minimalist, showcasing each piece with intentional negative space. The platter rests on a natural, light-colored stone surface. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is subtly placed to one side. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the delicate textures and natural color palette, with a clean, uncluttered background of subtle natural elements.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve alongside a warm cup of roasted barley tea (boricha) or a light green tea.
Offer small, traditional Korean ceramic cups for tea.

ingredients.name: Jocheong (Korean rice syrup) or Maple Syrup

instructions: Peel persimmons. Dice flesh into small cubes.
Combine diced persimmon, water, and 20g sugar in a clean jar.
Cover jar loosely. Ferment at room temperature for 2-3 days until slightly fizzy and tangy.
Strain liquid; reserve. Mash fermented persimmon flesh into a coarse puree.
Scoop solid coconut cream from chilled can into a bowl.
Whip until light and fluffy. Fold in vanilla bean paste and 30ml jocheong or maple syrup.
Gently split each ladyfinger in half lengthwise.
Spread a thin layer of vanilla coconut cream on one half of each ladyfinger.
Top with a spoonful of fermented persimmon puree.
Place the other ladyfinger half on top to form a sandwich.
Combine hot chocolate powder and finely ground roasted black sesame seeds.
Lightly dust each ladyfinger sandwich with the mixture.
Chill assembled sandwiches for 30 minutes to set.
Arrange 6-9 sandwiches neatly on a serving platter.
notes: Adjust sweetness of persimmon puree and cream to taste.
Fermentation time for persimmon may vary based on ambient temperature.
For a firmer cream, ensure coconut cream is well chilled overnight.
traditional_techniques: Fermentation (applied to fruit, reflecting broader Korean fermentation culture)

recipes.recipe_name: Irish Cream Macadamia Caramel Truffles
recipes.visual_description: Small, spherical truffles, approximately 3 cm in diameter. The exterior is evenly coated in rich, dark cocoa powder, presenting a clean matte finish. The interior, if visible from a slight break, reveals a lighter caramel color with visible chunks of roasted macadamia nuts. The truffles are arranged neatly in a small, balanced cluster on a clean, white porcelain dessert plate. A few whole, roasted macadamia nuts are scattered sparingly around the truffles for visual interest. The composition maintains moderate negative space. Lighting is natural and even, highlighting the powdery texture of the cocoa and the subtle sheen of the caramel. A folded light-colored cotton napkin rests beside the plate. The background is minimalist, suggesting a clean, modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve chilled.
Offer alongside small cups of strong black coffee or delicate tea.
Present on individual small plates or a shared platter for casual enjoyment.
instructions: Place soft caramel in a heatproof bowl. Gently warm until pliable.
Stir in Irish cream and sea salt until well combined.
Add chopped macadamia nuts. Mix thoroughly to combine all ingredients.
Cover the mixture. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours, until firm enough to roll.
Scoop small portions, approximately 15g each. Roll into uniform spherical balls.
Place cocoa powder in a shallow dish. Roll each truffle in cocoa powder to coat completely.
Arrange truffles on a parchment-lined tray. Refrigerate until ready to serve.
notes: For a firmer truffle, reduce the Irish cream slightly or add 10g of melted dark chocolate to the mixture before chilling.

recipes.recipe_name: Spiced Treacle Poached Pears with Cultured Red Bean Cream
recipes.visual_description: A single, dark amber poached pear stands upright on a matte cream ceramic plate. Its smooth, translucent skin reveals the pear's form. The pear retains its stem. Beside it, a natural dollop of light brown cultured red bean cream rests, soft and airy. A small pool of dark treacle-chai syrup glistens around the pear and cream. The composition is clean, with ample white space. The setting features a light bamboo surface, an undyed linen napkin, and a subtle green plant in the background. Soft natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the ingredients' natural beauty.

ingredients.name: Probiotic Capsule contents OR non-dairy yogurt with live cultures
