A sprinkle of vibrant green, finely chopped chives garnishes the top, adding a fresh color contrast. The soup fills a simple, round, off-white ceramic bowl, leaving a modest, inviting rim. A silver soup spoon rests casually beside the bowl on the table. Warm, cozy lighting from an overhead kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, highlighting the comforting steam rising from the hot soup. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a relaxed, lived-in kitchen environment.
instructions: Melt butter in a large pot over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute more.
Stir in flour. Cook 2 minutes, stirring constantly, to create a roux.
Gradually whisk in vegetable stock. Bring mixture to a simmer.
Add diced taro. Simmer 15-20 minutes until taro is very tender.
Remove pot from heat. Use an immersion blender to blend soup until smooth.
Return soup to low heat. Add shimeji mushrooms. Simmer 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are tender.
Stir in heavy cream, if using. Heat through, do not boil.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Ladle velouté into individual bowls. Garnish with chopped chives. Serve hot.

recipes.recipe_name: Australian Dark Beer & Onion Chutney with Sourdough Toast
recipes.visual_description: A deep, rich amber-brown onion chutney sits mounded in a rustic, imperfect ceramic bowl. The chutney shows visible strands of soft, caramelized onion. Next to the bowl, two thick, irregular slices of golden-brown sourdough toast are casually placed on a simple wooden cutting board. The toast has a crisp crust and a slightly chewy appearance. The setting is a well-used wooden kitchen table, with natural, warm light. A casually folded, unbleached linen napkin is placed nearby. The overall scene is homely and inviting, suggesting comfort and simplicity. The focus is on the textures and natural colors of the food, presented as if for a family meal.
instructions: Peel and thinly slice onions. Set aside.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or deep pan over medium-low heat.
Add sliced onions to the pot. Cook slowly, stirring occasionally, for 30-40 minutes until onions are very soft and deeply caramelized. They should be dark golden brown.
Pour in dark beer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Simmer for 5 minutes until liquid reduces slightly.
Stir in HP steak sauce, brown sugar, apple cider vinegar, salt, and black pepper.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer, uncovered, for another 20-30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chutney thickens to a jam-like consistency.
Remove from heat. Let cool slightly.
Toast sourdough bread slices until golden brown and crisp.
Serve generous spoonfuls of warm chutney on toasted sourdough slices.

recipes.recipe_name: Lentilles du Puy et Légumes Rôtis à l'Epazote et Paprika Fumé
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of 'Lentilles du Puy et Légumes Rôtis à l'Epazote et Paprika Fumé' is presented on a round, clean white porcelain dinner plate. A bed of deep green-brown Puy lentils, cooked to a tender but firm consistency, forms the base. Artfully arranged on top are roasted vegetables: caramelized rustic 2 cm chunks of vibrant orange carrots, pale parsnips, bright red and yellow bell peppers, and softened purple-edged red onion wedges. The vegetables show slightly browned, tender exteriors from roasting. The overall color palette is earthy and warm, with pops of bright vegetable hues. The dish is garnished with a generous sprinkle of fresh, bright green flat-leaf parsley leaves. Moderate negative space surrounds the dish. Natural, even lighting highlights textures and colors. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and traditional French-style flatware. A small, rustic bread basket with sliced baguette is visible in the soft background, creating a casual bistro dining atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty baguette or rustic bread.
A simple green salad with a light vinaigrette makes a fresh accompaniment.
Consider a small ramekin of a mild plant-based aioli or a fresh herb sauce for dipping.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Wash and peel carrots and parsnips. Cut into rustic 2 cm chunks. Cut bell peppers into 2 cm chunks. Cut red onion into thick wedges.
In a large bowl, toss carrots, parsnips, bell peppers, and red onion with 30 ml olive oil, smoked paprika, salt, and black pepper. Spread vegetables in a single layer on a baking sheet.
Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until tender and lightly caramelized. Turn vegetables halfway through cooking.
While vegetables roast, rinse Puy lentils under cold water. Finely dice shallots and mince garlic.
In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat remaining 30 ml olive oil over medium heat. Sauté diced shallots for 3 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

Add rinsed lentils, vegetable broth, bay leaf, and thyme sprigs to the pot. Season with salt and pepper. Bring mixture to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Simmer, covered, for 20-25 minutes, or until lentils are tender but still hold their shape.
If using fresh epazote, chop finely. Stir epazote into the lentils during the last 5 minutes of cooking. If using dried epazote, add with the broth.
Remove bay leaf and thyme sprigs from lentils. Gently fold in the roasted vegetables.
Serve immediately. Garnish each portion with fresh chopped flat-leaf parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Vegan Rhubarb & Raspberry Lamington Bites
recipes.visual_description: Six to nine perfectly uniform miniature square lamington bites are casually arranged on a simple white porcelain serving platter, placed on a well-used wooden kitchen table. Each bite features a soft, light vanilla sponge cake, precisely cut into 3cm cubes. The cake is deeply soaked, revealing a vibrant pink hue from the rhubarb and raspberry syrup, with some areas showing the natural creamy-white of the sponge. A generous, even coating of finely desiccated coconut covers each cube, providing a contrasting white, slightly textured exterior. The coconut adheres well, giving a neat, homely finish. The arrangement is natural, with bites slightly touching, inviting easy sharing. A casually draped linen napkin sits nearby. Warm, inviting light from a kitchen window illuminates the scene, highlighting the natural colors and inviting texture of the classic Australian treats.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a cup of tea or coffee
Present on a large communal platter for sharing
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Line a 20cm square baking tin with baking paper.
Combine flour, 150g caster sugar, baking powder, and salt in a large bowl.
In a separate bowl, whisk 250ml plant milk, vegetable oil, and 10ml vanilla extract.
Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Pour batter into prepared tin. Bake 25-30 minutes, or until a skewer inserted comes out clean.
Cool cake completely in the tin on a wire rack.
Combine chopped rhubarb, raspberries, 100g caster sugar, and water in a saucepan.
Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Cook 10-15 minutes, until rhubarb is very soft and fruit breaks down.
Remove from heat. Stir in vanilla bean paste. Strain mixture through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing solids to extract all liquid. Discard solids. Let syrup cool completely.
In a shallow bowl, whisk icing sugar, 60ml plant milk, and 5ml vanilla extract until smooth. This is the dipping glaze.
Once cake is completely cool, trim edges. Cut cake into 3cm uniform cubes.
Dip each cake cube into the cooled rhubarb-raspberry syrup, ensuring all sides are coated.
Immediately roll each syrup-coated cube in desiccated coconut, pressing gently to adhere.
Place finished lamington bites on a wire rack to set slightly before serving.
notes: A classic Australian treat, reimagined with a vibrant fruit twist and made vegan.
Ensure cake is completely cooled before cutting and dipping.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Brown Rice Cakes with Raspberry Marjoram Glaze
recipes.visual_description: Several golden-brown, round seared brown rice cakes are arranged on a light beige handcrafted ceramic plate. Each cake displays a crispy, textured exterior. A glossy, deep red-purple raspberry marjoram glaze is drizzled artfully over the cakes, creating vibrant streaks. Fresh green marjoram sprigs are placed alongside the cakes for a natural garnish. The composition emphasizes natural shapes and textures with ample negative space. The ceramic plate rests on a light reclaimed wood table. A natural undyed linen napkin is placed casually nearby. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the dish's earthy tones and fresh elements. The background is clean and minimalist, with subtle hints of green from a distant plant, enhancing the eco-conscious aesthetic. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a sharing portion of individual rice cakes.
instructions: Cook 150g dry brown rice according to package directions. Let cool completely.
Place cooked brown rice in a clean glass jar. Cover with water. Add a small piece of clean vegetable scrap or 1 tablespoon of fermenting liquid for starter.
Cover jar loosely with a cloth. Ferment at room temperature for 2-3 days. Taste for desired tanginess. Drain excess liquid.
Transfer fermented brown rice to a bowl. Mash lightly. Season with salt and pepper.
Form rice mixture into 8-10 small, flat cakes, approximately 5 cm in diameter and 1.5 cm thick.
Heat olive oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat.
Sear rice cakes for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy.
For the glaze, combine raspberry vinegar and a pinch of salt in a small saucepan.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 5-7 minutes until slightly thickened and syrupy.
Remove from heat. Stir in finely chopped fresh marjoram.
Arrange seared brown rice cakes on a serving plate.
Drizzle generously with raspberry marjoram glaze.
Garnish with fresh marjoram sprigs.
notes: This recipe utilizes fermentation, a traditional preservation method, to enhance flavor and digestibility of brown rice.
It promotes zero-waste by using simple, whole ingredients and minimizing food scraps.
Adjust fermentation time based on desired tanginess and ambient temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Jicama and Roasted Poblano Salad
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Mexican salad is presented on a clean, white ceramic plate. Diced jicama, roasted poblano pieces, black beans, and bright yellow corn kernels are artfully distributed, creating a mosaic of colors and textures. Thinly sliced red onion rings and fresh green cilantro leaves are interspersed throughout, adding crispness and aromatic freshness. A light, glistening preserved lemon vinaigrette coats the ingredients, reflecting natural light. The arrangement is organic, allowing individual components to be clearly visible while forming a cohesive, appealing composition. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface, with a folded cotton napkin and a small side bowl of totopos (tortilla chips) completing the casual bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve alongside warm corn tortillas.
Offer as a refreshing accompaniment to grilled meats or seafood.
Serve with totopos (tortilla chips) for scooping.
instructions: Roast poblano chiles over an open flame or under a broiler until skin is charred. Place in a bowl, cover, and let steam for 10 minutes. Peel, deseed, and dice the chiles.
Peel jicama. Dice jicama into 1 cm cubes.
Thinly slice the red onion.
Rinse and drain black beans. If using frozen corn, thaw it.
Prepare vinaigrette: In a small bowl, combine finely minced preserved lemon, lime juice, olive oil, honey or agave nectar, ground cumin, salt, and black pepper. Whisk until well emulsified.
In a large mixing bowl, combine diced jicama, roasted poblano, sliced red onion, black beans, corn kernels, and chopped cilantro.
Pour the prepared vinaigrette over the salad ingredients. Toss gently to coat all components evenly.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Corn and Poblano Salad with Lime-Beer Vinaigrette
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Mexican-inspired salad is presented on a rustic, hand-painted ceramic plate with natural imperfections, placed on a well-used wooden dining table. The salad features a generous base of golden-brown roasted corn kernels mixed with diced dark green roasted poblano peppers, bright red cherry tomato halves, thinly sliced purple-red onion, and dark black beans. Small, flaky pieces of pan-seared arctic char are scattered throughout, providing a light protein accent without dominating the vegetables. Fresh green cilantro leaves are liberally mixed in, adding a pop of color and freshness. The entire salad is lightly coated with a glistening lime-beer vinaigrette, allowing the natural colors of the ingredients to shine. The arrangement is casual and organic, with ingredients touching and slightly overlapping, giving a homely, inviting feel. A traditional Mexican molcajete with a pestle is visible in the soft-focused background, alongside a stack of warm corn tortillas wrapped in a cloth napkin. Natural, warm light illuminates the scene, suggesting a cozy family kitchen atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for scooping.
Offer a side of salsa fresca or guacamole.
Enjoy alongside a glass of horchata or a light Mexican lager.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Place poblano peppers on the baking sheet. Roast for 15-20 minutes until skin blisters. Transfer to a bowl, cover tightly, and let steam for 10 minutes.
Once cooled, peel, deseed, and dice the roasted poblano peppers.

While poblanos roast, heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add corn kernels. Cook, stirring occasionally, until corn is slightly charred, about 5-7 minutes. Transfer to a large mixing bowl.

Season arctic char fillet with salt and pepper. Heat a separate skillet over medium heat. Add a drizzle of olive oil. Cook arctic char for 3-4 minutes per side, until cooked through and flakes easily. Let cool slightly, then flake into small pieces.
Add diced poblano, sliced red onion, rinsed black beans, halved cherry tomatoes, and chopped cilantro to the bowl with corn. Add flaked arctic char.
Prepare the vinaigrette: In a small bowl, whisk together lime juice, olive oil, beer, minced garlic, chili powder, cumin, salt, and pepper until well combined.
Pour vinaigrette over the salad ingredients. Toss gently to combine everything.
Serve immediately or chill before serving.
notes: Any light lager beer can be used for the vinaigrette.
For best flavor, use fresh corn when in season. Frozen corn can be used if fresh is unavailable; char it directly in the skillet.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Tomato & Harissa Consommé
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of a vibrant, clear red consommé is presented in a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic bowl with a natural, earthy beige tone. The consommé, a result of fermented tomatoes and harissa, is translucent and glows with a deep, inviting hue. A delicate, creamy white tahini swirl gracefully unfurls on the surface, creating an organic, abstract pattern. Small, bright green droplets of thyme-infused olive oil dot the consommé, catching the light. A single, fresh thyme sprig is thoughtfully placed on the rim of the bowl, its tiny leaves contrasting with the soup's color. The bowl rests on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. An undyed linen napkin and a simple, small ceramic spoon in a matching earth tone complete the minimalist, eco-conscious setting. The background is clean and uncluttered, with a hint of soft, diffused natural light enhancing the dish's purity.
instructions: Roughly chop 1 kg overripe tomatoes. Place in a clean jar.
Add 2% salt by weight of tomatoes. Add a splash of non-chlorinated water if needed to cover.
Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days until slightly fizzy and tangy. Strain liquid, reserving solids.
Combine reserved fermented tomato solids, garlic cloves, onion skins, and celery ends/leaves in a large pot.
Add 1.5 L water. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 30 minutes.
Strain broth through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing solids to extract all liquid. Discard solids. This is your zero-waste vegetable broth.
Whisk harissa paste into the warm broth.
Gently heat 50 ml olive oil with 3 thyme sprigs in a small saucepan for 5 minutes. Do not boil. Let cool. Remove thyme.
Gently warm the harissa broth. Season with salt and pepper.
Whisk tahini with 60 ml warm water until smooth and pourable. Season with a pinch of salt.
Ladle warm consommé into bowls. Drizzle with tahini swirl. Add a few drops of thyme oil.
Garnish with a fresh thyme sprig.
notes: This recipe prioritizes flavor extraction from ingredients typically discarded, reducing food waste.
Fermentation enhances flavor complexity and shelf life, aligning with sustainable practices.

recipes.recipe_name: Vanilla Bean Panna Cotta Sphere, Boysenberry Gelée, and Macerated Berries
recipes.visual_description: A pristine, perfectly spherical vanilla bean panna cotta sits elegantly off-center on a large, round white bone china plate. Its surface is smooth and subtly iridescent. Adjacent to the panna cotta, a small, organic cluster of whole, plump boysenberries, their deep purple hue vibrant against the white plate, showcases their natural form. Scattered artfully nearby are a few translucent, ruby-red pieces of boysenberry gelée, their irregular shapes adding visual interest. Tiny, precise dots of a vivid boysenberry fluid gel provide intense color accents around the main components. A delicate scattering of golden, finely crushed vanilla sable crumble offers a textural counterpoint. The composition is minimalist with abundant negative space, highlighting each element's perfection. The setting features a white Carrara marble surface, a single polished silver dessert spoon, and a crisp white linen napkin folded precisely into a triangle. Dramatic professional lighting creates soft, inviting shadows.
instructions: For Vanilla Panna Cotta: Bloom 4g gelatin in cold water. Scrape vanilla bean into cream and 50g sugar. Heat cream mixture to a simmer. Remove from heat. Stir in bloomed gelatin until dissolved. Strain. Pour into sphere molds (approx. 7 cm diameter). Chill minimum 4 hours until firm.

For Boysenberry Gelée: Bloom 2g gelatin in cold water. Puree 150g boysenberries with 25g sugar and lemon juice. Heat puree to a simmer. Remove from heat. Stir in bloomed gelatin until dissolved. Pour a thin layer into small, shallow molds or onto a lined tray. Chill until firm. Cut into small, irregular shapes.
For Macerated Boysenberries: Gently wash and dry 100g fresh boysenberries. Toss with 15g sugar and a tiny pinch of scraped vanilla bean. Set aside at room temperature for 15 minutes.

For Boysenberry Fluid Gel: Puree 50g boysenberries with 10g sugar. In a small saucepan, whisk agar-agar into puree. Bring to a boil. Simmer 1 minute. Pour into a shallow container. Chill until firm. Blend gelled mixture until completely smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve. Transfer to a squeeze bottle.

For Vanilla Sable Crumble: Preheat oven to 160°C. Combine flour, powdered sugar, and a pinch of salt. Cut in cold butter and vanilla extract until crumbly. Spread on a baking sheet. Bake 12-15 minutes until golden. Cool completely.

To Assemble: Carefully unmold a vanilla panna cotta sphere onto the center of each chilled plate. Artfully arrange a few small pieces of boysenberry gelée next to the sphere. Place a small, organic cluster of macerated boysenberries beside the panna cotta. Pipe small dots of boysenberry fluid gel around the plate. Sprinkle a small amount of vanilla sable crumble for texture. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Ricotta Cloud with Candied Prosciutto and Citrus Ricotta Crisp
recipes.visual_description: Eight delicate miniature petit fours are precisely arranged on a pristine white Carrara marble slab, serving as an elegant platter. Each piece features a small, impeccably piped quenelle of snow-white Lemon Ricotta Mousse, exhibiting a smooth, ethereal texture. Adjacent to the mousse, a single, translucent amber shard of shatteringly crisp candied prosciutto stands, providing a striking color and textural contrast. Nestled nearby is a thin, pale golden Citrus Ricotta-Semolina Crisp, its irregular, organic shape suggesting handcrafted elegance. Two to three tiny, vibrant purple dots of blueberry gel are artfully placed around each mousse, adding a concentrated burst of color and a subtle sheen. A single, fresh micro basil leaf, its green hue a perfect accent, crowns each composition. The arrangement emphasizes abundant negative space, highlighting the minimalist beauty and precision of each component. Dramatic, professional lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing depth and sophistication. The overall presentation is one of refined simplicity, with each element contributing to a harmonious and visually stunning ensemble, suitable for a Michelin-starred dessert course.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve at room temperature as a concluding sweet bite.
Pair with a small espresso or a glass of Vin Santo.
Present on a refined porcelain or marble serving platter.
instructions: For the Lemon Ricotta Mousse: Soak gelatin leaf in cold water until softened. Whip heavy cream to soft peaks. In a separate bowl, whisk drained ricotta, caster sugar, vanilla bean seeds, and lemon zest until smooth. Gently warm 1 tablespoon of the whipped cream, dissolve squeezed gelatin into it. Fold gelatin mixture into ricotta. Gently fold whipped cream into ricotta mixture until combined. Transfer to a piping bag. Chill for at least 2 hours.

For the Candied Prosciutto Crisp: Preheat oven to 160°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. In a small saucepan, combine water and granulated sugar. Bring to a simmer, stirring until sugar dissolves. Lay prosciutto slices flat on the prepared baking sheet. Brush both sides of each slice with the sugar syrup. Bake for 10-15 minutes, or until deeply golden brown and crisp. Watch carefully to prevent burning. Let cool completely on a wire rack; it will crisp further. Break into small, irregular shards.

For the Citrus Ricotta-Semolina Crisp: In a bowl, combine 00 flour, 10g of the ricotta, egg yolk, melted butter, 10g granulated sugar, and 1/2 teaspoon lemon zest. Mix until a dough forms. Knead briefly until smooth. Wrap in plastic and chill for 30 minutes. Preheat oven to 150°C. On a lightly floured surface, roll the dough extremely thin (almost translucent) using a pasta machine or rolling pin. Cut into small, organic, irregular shapes. Place on a parchment-lined baking sheet. Bake for 8-12 minutes, or until very pale golden and crisp. Let cool completely.

For the Blueberry Gel: In a small saucepan, combine blueberries, 10g granulated sugar, and 1 tablespoon water. Bring to a simmer. Cook until blueberries burst. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing to extract all liquid. Return juice to saucepan. Whisk in agar-agar powder. Bring to a boil, whisking constantly, for 1 minute. Remove from heat. Pour into a shallow dish. Chill until set. Once set, blend until smooth. Transfer to a small piping bag or squeeze bottle.

To Assemble: On an elegant serving platter, pipe 8 small, neat quenelles or domes of Lemon Ricotta Mousse. Arrange 1-2 small shards of Candied Prosciutto Crisp next to each mousse. Place one Citrus Ricotta-Semolina Crisp artfully beside the mousse. Dot 2-3 tiny drops of Blueberry Gel around each petit four. Garnish each with a single micro basil leaf.
notes: Ensure ricotta is thoroughly drained to achieve the desired mousse consistency.
For the prosciutto, watch closely during baking as it can burn quickly due to its thinness and sugar content.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Tomato & Ginger Plantain Bites
recipes.visual_description: A minimalistic presentation on a light stone or reclaimed wood board. Eight to twelve golden, crisp, round plantain chips are arranged with deliberate, unforced spacing. Each chip is topped with a vibrant mound of ruby-red fermented tomato salsa, its texture slightly pulpy. Nestled atop the salsa are delicate, translucent purple strands of quick-pickled red onion, adding a subtle pop of color. A single, fresh green cilantro leaf or a tiny sprig of parsley acts as the sole, natural garnish. The overall composition emphasizes clean lines, natural colors, and contrasting textures—crisp plantain, juicy salsa, tender onion. Soft natural light highlights the ingredients. The background is clean, with minimal, unobtrusive elements.
instructions: Diced tomatoes into 5mm cubes.
Grate ginger finely.
Combine diced tomatoes, grated ginger, and sea salt in a clean jar.
Mix well. Press down to submerge solids in liquid.
Cover with an airlock lid or loose lid. Let ferment at room temperature for 2-3 days until slightly bubbly and tangy.
Refrigerate once desired tanginess is reached.
Slice red onion very thinly.
In a small saucepan, combine apple cider vinegar, water, and sugar. Bring to a simmer.
Pour hot liquid over sliced red onion in a heatproof jar.
Let cool to room temperature. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Line a baking tray with parchment paper.
Peel green plantains. Slice thinly (2-3mm thick) into rounds or ovals.
Toss plantain slices with olive oil and a pinch of salt.
Spread in a single layer on the prepared baking tray.
Bake for 15-20 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden and crisp. Watch carefully to prevent burning. Let cool completely to crisp further.
Arrange crispy plantain bites on a serving platter.
Top each plantain bite with a small spoonful of fermented tomato & ginger salsa.
Place a few strands of quick-pickled red onion on top of the salsa.
Garnish with small cilantro or parsley leaves.
notes: Plantain peels can be used for vegetable broth or composted.
Any leftover pickling liquid can be reused for other quick pickles.
Tomato cores and scraps can be added to a vegetable stock or compost pile.
Fermented salsa improves with age in the refrigerator.
Use the stems of herbs for flavoring stocks or finely mince for other dishes.

recipes.recipe_name: Homestyle Dark Chocolate Huckleberry Cheesecake
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous, thick wedge slice of Homestyle Dark Chocolate Huckleberry Cheesecake rests on a simple, slightly imperfect off-white ceramic plate. The crust is a deep, rich brown, providing a firm base. Above it, the creamy, off-white cheesecake filling is studded with bursts of deep purple huckleberries, which show natural variations in size. The texture is dense yet invitingly smooth. A few fresh, whole huckleberries are scattered casually on top of the slice, alongside a dusting of finely grated dark chocolate. In the soft-focused background, the remaining whole cheesecake sits on a modest cake stand, showing its full round form and homely top. The scene is set on a well-used wooden dining table, with a casually placed cloth napkin and a simple fork beside the plate. Warm, cozy lighting from overhead kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene, creating a relaxed, lived-in family dining atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C. Grease and line a 15 cm springform pan.
For the crust: Crush biscuits finely. Melt butter and 50 g dark chocolate together. Stir in cocoa powder.
Combine crushed biscuits with melted butter-chocolate mixture. Press firmly into the bottom of the prepared pan.
Bake crust for 8 minutes. Remove from oven.
For the filling: In a large bowl, beat softened cream cheese until smooth. Grate Edam cheese finely. Add grated Edam cheese and sugar to cream cheese. Beat until combined.
Beat in the egg and vanilla extract until just incorporated. Do not overmix.
Gently fold in 100 g huckleberries into the cheese mixture.
Pour filling over the baked crust in the pan. Smooth the top.
Bake for 40-50 minutes, or until the edges are set but the center still jiggles slightly.
Turn off oven. Leave cheesecake inside with the door ajar for 30 minutes to cool slowly. This prevents cracking.
Remove from oven. Let cool completely on a wire rack. Chill in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight.
To serve: Grate remaining 10 g dark chocolate. Top cheesecake with remaining 50 g huckleberries and grated chocolate.

recipes.recipe_name: Poached Pears with Earl Grey & Rose, Fermented Oat Crumble
recipes.visual_description: A single poached pear stands elegantly on a light cream-colored handcrafted ceramic plate, positioned slightly off-center to allow ample negative space. The pear retains its natural, smooth, rounded form with its stem intact, showcasing a translucent, soft amber hue from the poaching liquid. At its base, a small pool of glossy, reduced sweet wine liquid collects, reflecting the soft, natural light. Scattered gently beside and partially over the pear's base is a rustic, irregular cluster of golden-brown fermented oat crumble, highlighting its varied textures. A single, delicate fresh rose petal rests near the pear, adding a subtle touch of natural color without being ornate. The overall composition is clean and minimalist. The plate rests on a light bamboo table surface. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is folded simply nearby. The background is clean and uncluttered, with a hint of natural light and a soft, out-of-focus plant element, emphasizing an eco-conscious and serene aesthetic. The entire plate is visible, showcasing the thoughtful arrangement and emphasizing the inherent beauty of each ingredient.
instructions: Peel pears, leaving stems intact. Carefully core each pear from the bottom.
In a medium pot, combine sweet wine, water, maple syrup, Earl Grey tea bags, and dried rose petals. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Gently place peeled pears into the simmering liquid. Ensure pears are mostly submerged. Cover the pot.
Poach pears for 20-30 minutes, or until tender when pierced with a knife. Turn pears occasionally for even cooking. Remove pears from liquid and set aside.
Increase heat on the poaching liquid. Simmer rapidly until liquid reduces to a slightly syrupy consistency. Remove tea bags and rose petals.
In a bowl, combine rolled oats, sourdough starter discard, and a pinch of sea salt. Mix well until oats are evenly coated.
Cover the oat mixture. Let ferment at room temperature for 8-12 hours, or until a slight tangy aroma develops.
Preheat oven to 160°C (320°F).
Add chilled, cubed coconut oil to the fermented oats. Use your fingertips to rub the oil into the oats, forming a coarse crumble.
Spread the oat crumble in a single layer on a baking sheet. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until golden brown and crisp. Let cool completely.

To serve, place one poached pear on a ceramic plate. Spoon some reduced poaching liquid around the base of the pear. Sprinkle generous amounts of the fermented oat crumble beside and lightly over the pear. Garnish with a few fresh rose petals if desired.
notes: For the fermented oat crumble, if sourdough discard is unavailable, use 2 tablespoons of plain vegan yogurt mixed with 1 tablespoon of water as an alternative starter.
Ensure pears are firm but ripe enough to become tender without becoming mushy during poaching.
Adjust maple syrup quantity based on the sweetness of your chosen sweet wine.

recipes.recipe_name: Kidney Bean and Injera Crisp Salad with Berbere-Gochujang Vinaigrette
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on an oversized, white bone china plate, set against a light grey travertine surface under dramatic lighting. Abundant negative space surrounds the central, organic composition. Artfully positioned clusters of earthy red spiced kidney beans form the base. Around them, a vibrant mosaic of finely diced cucumber, red and yellow bell pepper, and blanched green beans creates textural and chromatic contrast, interspersed with delicate, thinly sliced radish. Two to three irregularly shaped, golden-brown Chickpea Flour Injera Crisps stand or are delicately placed for height. A rich, deep red Berbere-Gochujang Vinaigrette is precisely drizzled, its glossy sheen catching the light. Bright green microgreens and fresh cilantro leaves provide a final flourish. A neatly folded injera square on a small side dish and a pristine white linen napkin complete the refined, culturally inspired setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve alongside warm injera bread for scooping the salad.
Traditionally, Ethiopian meals are eaten communally, but this fine-dining interpretation is for individual plating.

ingredients.name: Fresh green beans, blanched and finely diced
Thinly sliced fresh red chili (garnish, optional)

instructions: Heat olive oil in a small pan over medium heat. Add diced red onion. Sauté until translucent, about 3 minutes. Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Add cooked kidney beans. Season with salt and black pepper. Stir gently to combine. Remove from heat. Set aside to cool.

In a bowl, whisk together chickpea flour, water, baking soda, salt, and nigella seeds until smooth. The batter should be thin. Heat vegetable oil in a small pan to 170°C. Pour small amounts of batter (about 1 tablespoon) into the hot oil to form thin, irregular crisps. Fry for 1-2 minutes per side until golden brown and crisp. Remove with a slotted spoon. Drain on paper towels. Season lightly with salt.
In a bowl, combine finely diced cucumber, red bell pepper, yellow bell pepper, thinly sliced radishes, and finely diced blanched green beans. Keep separate until plating.

In a small bowl, whisk together berbere spice blend, gochujang, lemon juice, maple syrup, Dijon mustard, minced garlic, salt, black pepper, and water. Slowly drizzle in extra virgin olive oil while whisking constantly until the vinaigrette is emulsified and smooth. Taste and adjust seasoning.

On each of four large, minimalist plates, create an artistic arrangement. Start by placing small clusters of the spiced kidney beans. Artfully scatter the finely diced Ethiopian vegetable medley around the beans, ensuring a balance of colors and textures. Drizzle the Berbere-Gochujang Vinaigrette elegantly over the components, ensuring it integrates visually. Place 1-2 Chickpea Flour Injera Crisps standing upright or artfully laid on each plate for height and texture. Garnish with fresh cilantro leaves, microgreens, and a few slivers of fresh red chili if desired.
notes: Ensure all vegetables are diced uniformly for a refined appearance and consistent texture.
The chickpea flour crisps should be very thin and delicate, almost like a savory tuile.
The gochujang is used sparingly to add a layer of complex umami and a subtle fermented note, complementing the berbere rather than dominating.

recipes.recipe_name: Tangerine Five-Spice Entremet
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly formed Tangerine Five-Spice Entremet rests off-center on a pristine white porcelain dessert plate with a delicate gold rim. The entremet is a precise geometric shape, perhaps a small cylinder or cube, coated in a flawless, high-gloss mirror glaze of vibrant tangerine orange. Its surface reflects light with architectural precision. A single, impeccably segmented candied tangerine piece, free of pith, is placed artfully on top or beside the entremet, showcasing its translucent, tender flesh. Standing elegantly upright or leaning against the entremet is a razor-thin, amber-colored star anise sugar tuile, its brittle texture contrasting the entremet's creamy smoothness. The plate itself is immaculately clean, with abundant negative space highlighting the dessert as the sole focal point. The background is an ultra-minimalist, soft-focus white marble surface, allowing the dramatic professional lighting to cast subtle, artistic shadows that emphasize the entremet's contours and glossy finish. The overall presentation is one of sophisticated simplicity and absolute perfection, reflecting haute patisserie artistry.
instructions: Soak gelatin sheets for crémeux and mousse in cold water until soft.
For Orange Génoise: Preheat oven to 170°C. Line a small baking tray with parchment paper.
Whisk eggs and 75g sugar in a heatproof bowl over a bain-marie until warm and thick.
Remove from heat. Continue whisking until cool and very voluminous.
Fold in flour and orange zest gently. Fold in melted butter.
Spread batter evenly on prepared tray. Bake 10-12 minutes until golden and springy. Cool completely. Cut into 4 discs using your entremet mold size.
For Star Anise Crémeux: Heat milk and star anise pods in a saucepan until simmering. Remove from heat. Steep 15 minutes.
Whisk 3 egg yolks with 25g sugar until pale.
Remove star anise from milk. Reheat milk gently. Temper hot milk into egg yolk mixture. Return to saucepan.
Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until mixture thickens (nappe consistency). Do not boil.
Remove from heat. Stir in 2g squeezed gelatin. Strain crémeux through a fine-mesh sieve. Pour into a small mold (smaller than entremet mold) to create 4 inserts. Freeze until solid.
For Tangerine-Chinese Five Spice Mousse: Heat tangerine puree and 50g sugar in a saucepan until sugar dissolves. Bring to a simmer.
Whisk 4 egg yolks. Temper hot tangerine mixture into egg yolks. Return to saucepan.
Cook over medium-low heat, stirring, until thickened (nappe consistency).
Remove from heat. Stir in 4g squeezed gelatin and Chinese five spice powder. Cool to room temperature.
Whip heavy cream to soft peaks. Gently fold into cooled tangerine mixture.
For Assembly: Place a génoise disc at the bottom of each silicone entremet mold (4 molds).
Pipe a layer of tangerine mousse over the génoise.
Place a frozen star anise crémeux insert in the center of the mousse.
Cover with more tangerine mousse, filling the mold. Smooth the top.
Freeze entremets for at least 6 hours, preferably overnight, until completely solid.
For Mirror Glaze: Soak remaining 2g gelatin in cold water.
In a saucepan, combine glucose syrup, 50g sugar, and 100ml water. Bring to 103°C.
Remove from heat. Add white chocolate, condensed milk, and squeezed gelatin. Stir until smooth.
Add orange food coloring to desired hue. Blend with an immersion blender, avoiding air bubbles. Strain glaze.
Let glaze cool to 35-40°C. Place frozen entremets on a wire rack over a baking sheet.
Pour glaze evenly over each entremet, ensuring full coverage. Let excess drip off.
Carefully transfer glazed entremets to a serving plate. Allow to thaw in the refrigerator for 30-45 minutes.
For Garnish: Segment fresh tangerines. Remove all pith and membrane. Create 4 perfect segments.
For Star Anise Tuile: Heat isomalt or sugar in a non-stick pan until melted and caramelized to a pale amber.
Carefully pour a very thin layer onto a silicone mat or parchment paper. Place a small star anise pod onto the cooling sugar if desired, or finely crush star anise powder and sprinkle.
Once cool and brittle, break into small, architectural shards or cut precise shapes.
Garnish each entremet with one tangerine segment and one star anise tuile shard.

recipes.recipe_name: Panang Chicken and Tatsoi Crostini
recipes.visual_description: Eight to twelve elegant Panang Chicken and Tatsoi Crostini are artfully arranged on a rustic, light-colored wooden serving board. Each crostini features a crisp, golden-brown baguette slice as its base. A generous mound of rich, reddish-orange panang chicken, diced small, sits atop the bread, its creamy texture visible. Bright green, roughly chopped tatsoi leaves are gently placed over the chicken, adding a vibrant color contrast. A delicate, translucent sheen of coconut vinegar drizzle glistens over the entire topping. The crostini are casually spaced, some slightly overlapping, creating a natural and inviting presentation. The setting is a homely family kitchen, with a warm, cozy light from above. The wooden board rests on a well-used, slightly textured wooden dining table. A simple, off-white cloth napkin is casually folded beside the board, providing a soft, unobtrusive background element. The focus remains entirely on the appealing, bite-sized canapés, showcasing their colors and textures in a comforting, unpretentious style.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Slice baguette diagonally into 1 cm thick pieces. Arrange on a baking sheet. Bake 8-10 minutes until lightly golden and crisp. Set aside.
Dice chicken breast into small, uniform cubes, about 0.5 cm. Mince garlic.
Heat cooking oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add minced garlic. Sauté 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add diced chicken to the skillet. Cook 5-7 minutes, stirring, until chicken is no longer pink. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Stir in panang curry paste. Cook 1 minute, stirring constantly, until fragrant. Pour in coconut milk. Simmer 2-3 minutes, stirring, until sauce slightly thickens and coats chicken. Remove from heat.

Bring a small pot of water to a boil. Add tatsoi leaves. Blanch 30 seconds until bright green. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking. Drain well. Gently squeeze out excess water. Roughly chop tatsoi into small pieces.
In a small bowl, whisk together coconut vinegar, granulated sugar, and a pinch of salt until sugar dissolves. This is your drizzle.
To assemble, spoon a generous portion of the panang chicken mixture onto each toasted baguette slice. Top with a small amount of chopped tatsoi. Drizzle lightly with the coconut vinegar mixture.
Arrange crostini on a serving platter. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Semolina Blancmange, Barberry Consommé, Ghee Tuile
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on an oversized white bone china plate, resting on a cool grey veined Carrara marble surface, with abundant negative space. A perfectly formed, smooth, pristine white semolina blancmange, approximately 5 cm in diameter, sits slightly off-center. Its impeccably smooth surface hints at a delicate, creamy texture. Around its base, a small, vibrant ruby-red pool of translucent barberry-coconut consommé forms a natural, organic halo with soft, flowing edges. Artfully placed beside the blancmange are one or two irregularly shaped, golden-brown ghee tuiles, wafer-thin and crisp, providing subtle height and textural contrast. A single, plump, crimson barberry is precisely positioned as a minimalist garnish. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft, intentional shadows, highlighting the dish's three-dimensionality. The ultra-minimalist background ensures the dish remains the sole, captivating focal point.
instructions: Combine coconut milk, 50 ml water, 40 g sugar, and a pinch of salt in a saucepan. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Whisk in semolina flour gradually. Stir constantly over medium-low heat for 5-7 minutes until mixture thickens.
Dissolve agar-agar in 2 tablespoons hot water. Whisk into semolina mixture. Cook 1 minute.
Pour into four small, lightly oiled molds. Refrigerate at least 2 hours, or until firmly set.
Combine dried barberries, 250 ml water, and 50 g sugar in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer. Cook 10 minutes.
Strain mixture through a fine-mesh sieve lined with cheesecloth. Press solids gently. Discard solids. Chill consommé thoroughly.
Preheat oven to 160°C.
Whisk together melted ghee, 20 g flour, 20 g sugar, 20 ml water, and a pinch of salt until smooth.
Spread a very thin layer of batter onto a silicone mat or parchment-lined baking sheet. Create irregular shapes.
Bake 8-12 minutes, or until golden brown and crisp. Cool completely on the mat. Break into desired pieces.
Unmold chilled blancmange onto the center of four pristine white plates.
Pour a small, elegant pool of barberry consommé around the base of each blancmange.
Place one or two ghee tuile pieces artistically beside or gently leaning on the blancmange.
Garnish each plate with a single fresh barberry placed precisely for visual impact. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Anise & Cacao Millefoglie with Fermented Berries
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegantly layered millefoglie stands tall on a smooth, light-colored handcrafted ceramic plate. The crisp, golden-brown whole grain puff pastry layers are clearly defined, separated by a creamy, pale brown cacao-anise pastry cream. Between the pastry and cream layers, a vibrant ruby-red fermented berry compote is visible, featuring whole or lightly crushed berries. The overall presentation is clean and uncluttered, emphasizing natural textures and colors. A light drizzle of Galliano syrup glistens on the top pastry layer. The plate rests on a light reclaimed wood surface, accompanied by an undyed linen napkin. Soft, natural light illuminates the dessert, highlighting its delicate structure and fresh, organic ingredients. No artificial elements are present; the focus is on the inherent beauty of the ingredients.

ingredients.name: Maple syrup
ingredients.quantity: 50g for cream, 10g for compote, 10g for syrup

instructions: Prepare Fermented Berry Compote one day in advance. Gently crush berries in a clean jar. Add 10g maple syrup, 50ml filtered water, and 1g sea salt. Stir well. Cover jar loosely with a lid or cloth. Let sit at room temperature (20-24°C) for 24-48 hours. Taste for desired tanginess. Refrigerate.
Make Rough Puff Pastry. Cube cold butter into 1 cm pieces. Combine flour and a pinch of salt in a large bowl. Add butter cubes. Work butter into flour using fingertips until pea-sized pieces form.
Gradually add ice water. Mix until a shaggy dough forms. Do not overmix. Form into a rough rectangle. Wrap in beeswax wrap. Chill for 30 minutes.
Lightly flour a clean surface. Roll dough into a 20x40 cm rectangle. Fold dough into thirds, like a letter. Rotate 90 degrees. Roll again to 20x40 cm. Fold into thirds. This completes one 'turn'.
Repeat rolling and folding two more times, for a total of three turns. Chill dough for 30 minutes after each turn. Chill final dough for at least 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Roll chilled pastry dough to 3mm thickness. Cut into 12 rectangles (approximately 4x8 cm each) for 4 portions. Prick pastry with a fork to prevent excessive puffing.
Bake pastry rectangles on a parchment-lined baking sheet for 15-20 minutes. Pastry should be golden brown and crisp. Let cool completely on a wire rack.
Prepare Cacao-Anise Pastry Cream. Whisk egg yolks, cornstarch, and 50g maple syrup in a bowl until smooth. Heat organic milk in a saucepan until simmering.
Slowly pour hot milk into egg mixture while whisking constantly. Return mixture to saucepan. Cook over medium heat, whisking continuously, until cream thickens. Remove from heat.
Stir in Creme de Cacao and Anisette. Pour cream into a clean bowl. Cover surface directly with cling film to prevent a skin. Chill completely in refrigerator.
Make Galliano Syrup. Combine Galliano Liqueur, 30ml water, and 10g maple syrup in a small saucepan. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 2 minutes. Remove from heat. Let cool.
Assemble Millefoglie. Place one baked pastry rectangle on a serving plate. Spread a layer of chilled Cacao-Anise Pastry Cream. Add a generous spoonful of Fermented Berry Compote.
Top with a second pastry rectangle. Repeat with another layer of pastry cream and compote. Place a third pastry rectangle on top.
Repeat assembly for remaining 3 portions. Drizzle each millefoglie with Galliano Syrup. Garnish with a small fresh mint leaf or edible flower. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Deconstructed Chocolate Oat Symphony
recipes.visual_description: A sophisticated, minimalist composition centered on a premium white bone china plate. The main focal point is a series of glossy, dark brown chocolate crémeux dollops, piped with organic, flowing forms. Surrounding the crémeux are thin, irregular shards of dark cocoa oat tuile, exhibiting a delicate crispness. Scattered around these elements are golden-brown toasted oat crumbles, providing textural contrast with their irregular, chunky forms. A delicate, airy cloud of pristine white Truvia oat milk foam floats gently beside the main components, adding a soft, ethereal touch. The plate features abundant negative space, highlighting the architectural precision of each element. Colors are rich and natural: deep browns, golden oat tones, and a subtle off-white. The setting is a luxury Michelin environment, with the dish resting on a pristine white Carrara marble surface. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, emphasizing texture and depth. The background is ultra-minimalist, ensuring the food remains the sole subject. The entire plate is visible, showcasing the thoughtful arrangement for a shareable, interactive experience.
instructions: For Cocoa Oat Tuiles: Melt 40g butter. Whisk 30g Truvia, egg white, and pinch of salt until combined. Fold in 50g flour, 10g cocoa powder, and 20g finely ground rolled oats. Stir in melted butter. Chill batter 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 160°C. Spread thin layers of batter onto a silicone mat or parchment paper, creating irregular shapes. Bake 8-10 minutes until crisp. Cool completely on a wire rack.
For Chocolate Crémeux: Chop 100g dark chocolate finely. In a saucepan, heat 150ml heavy cream and 50ml whole milk until simmering. In a bowl, whisk 2 egg yolks and 15g Truvia until pale.

Temper egg yolk mixture by slowly whisking in hot cream mixture. Return mixture to saucepan. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until mixture thickens slightly and coats the back of a spoon (82°C).
Pour hot custard over chopped chocolate. Let sit 1 minute. Whisk until smooth and glossy. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve. Chill crémeux for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight.
For Toasted Oat Crumble: Preheat oven to 160°C. Melt 20g butter. Combine 50g rolled oats, 10g Truvia, and a pinch of salt in a bowl. Pour in melted butter; mix until coated.
Spread oat mixture onto a baking sheet. Bake 10-12 minutes, stirring halfway, until golden and crisp. Cool completely.
For Truvia Oat Milk Foam: Combine 100ml oat milk, 5g Truvia, 2ml vanilla bean paste, and 1g soy lecithin in a bowl. Blend with an immersion blender until lecithin is dissolved.
Pour mixture into a culinary siphon. Charge with 1-2 N2O cartridges. Shake well. Keep chilled until ready to serve.
To Plate: Pipe small, organic dollops of chilled chocolate crémeux onto a premium white plate. Artfully arrange broken pieces of cocoa oat tuile around the crémeux.
Scatter toasted oat crumble around the crémeux and tuile. Dispense a delicate cloud of Truvia oat milk foam beside the main elements. Serve immediately as a shareable snack.

recipes.recipe_name: Goat Cheese & White Port Cheesecake with Pumpkin Seed Brittle
recipes.visual_description: A single elegant slice of cheesecake is centered on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The slice reveals distinct layers: a compact, golden-brown biscuit crust at the base, topped by a smooth, creamy, off-white cheesecake filling. The surface of the cheesecake is pristine and slightly firm. Around the slice, and leaning against it, are several irregular, amber-hued shards of pumpkin seed brittle, showcasing the vibrant green of the embedded pumpkin seeds. A few whole, toasted pumpkin seeds are scattered on the plate for texture. The overall presentation is clean, refined, and professional, with thoughtful negative space. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and a dessert fork. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and subtle colors. In the soft-focused background, the remaining whole cheesecake, still in its springform pan or on a simple cake stand, offers context.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C. Line a 15cm springform pan with parchment paper. Wrap outside with foil.
Crush biscuits into fine crumbs. Mix with melted butter and salt. Press mixture firmly into bottom of prepared pan.
Bake crust for 10 minutes. Remove from oven. Reduce oven temperature to 150°C.
Beat cream cheese and goat cheese until smooth. Add sugar; beat until combined.
Beat in egg, then egg yolk, then vanilla extract. Mix in white port. Do not overmix.
Pour filling over baked crust. Place springform pan into a larger roasting pan.
Pour hot water into roasting pan to come halfway up sides of springform pan.
Bake for 45-55 minutes, or until edges are set but center jiggles slightly.
Turn off oven. Leave cheesecake in oven with door ajar for 1 hour.
Remove from water bath. Cool completely on a wire rack.
Chill cheesecake in refrigerator for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight.
For brittle: Combine sugar and water in a small saucepan. Heat over medium-low until sugar dissolves.
Increase heat to medium-high. Cook without stirring until caramel turns amber.
Remove from heat. Stir in toasted pumpkin seeds and salt quickly.
Pour mixture onto a silicone mat or parchment-lined baking sheet. Spread thinly.
Let cool completely. Break into shards.
To serve: Run a thin knife around edge of cheesecake. Release from pan.
Cut into slices. Place one slice on each plate.
Garnish with pumpkin seed brittle shards.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Beef Tenderloin with Confit Cherry Tomatoes and Garlic-Oregano Crumble
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Seared Beef Tenderloin is elegantly presented on a pristine white bone china plate, featuring abundant negative space. Three thick, perfectly seared beef medallions, exhibiting a rich golden-brown crust and a tender pink interior, are arranged off-center. Adjacent to the beef, a small, organic cluster of glistening confit cherry tomatoes bursts with vibrant red hues, their skins delicately wrinkled. A rich, glossy dark brown beef jus is artfully painted across the plate, providing a deep, contrasting color. A delicate scattering of golden-brown garlic-oregano crumble, with visible specks of green oregano, is precisely placed over the tomatoes and subtly around the beef, adding textural contrast. The entire composition rests on a premium grey veined marble surface, illuminated by dramatic professional lighting that casts soft, intentional shadows. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, and elegant silver flatware are positioned to complete the luxurious Michelin-starred setting.
instructions: Prepare Beef Jus: Finely dice shallot. In a saucepan, sauté shallot in a knob of butter until translucent. Add red wine. Reduce by half. Add beef stock and thyme. Simmer until reduced by two-thirds to a rich, glossy consistency. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve. Keep warm.

Make Confit Cherry Tomatoes: Preheat oven to 120°C. Place cherry tomatoes in a small oven-safe dish. Add 4 crushed garlic cloves and 50 ml olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Bake for 45-60 minutes until tomatoes are soft and slightly wrinkled but hold their shape.

Prepare Garlic-Oregano Crumble: Finely mince remaining 2 garlic cloves and fresh oregano leaves. In a small pan, melt 20g butter with 20ml olive oil over medium heat. Add minced garlic. Sauté until fragrant, about 1 minute. Add panko breadcrumbs. Toast until golden brown and crispy. Stir in minced oregano. Season with salt. Set aside.

Sear Beef Tenderloin: Pat beef tenderloin dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper. Heat a heavy-bottomed skillet over high heat with 30ml olive oil until shimmering. Add beef. Sear all sides until deep golden brown, about 2-3 minutes per side. Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining butter and a sprig of fresh oregano to the pan. Baste beef continuously for 3-5 minutes, until desired internal temperature is reached (e.g., 55°C for medium-rare).
Rest Beef: Transfer seared beef to a cutting board. Tent loosely with foil. Let rest for 10 minutes.

Plate Dish: Slice beef into thick medallions. Place a few beef medallions on one side of a large, minimalist plate. Arrange a cluster of confit cherry tomatoes beside the beef. Spoon a small amount of beef jus artistically on the plate, either under or beside the beef. Sprinkle garlic-oregano crumble sparingly over the tomatoes and around the beef. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Caramelized Onion and Chihuahua Cheese Empanaditas
recipes.visual_description: A single golden-brown empanadita, approximately 15 cm in length, is presented on a round, matte white porcelain dessert plate. Its crescent shape is crisp, with visible crimped edges from a fork seal, indicating a delicate crunch. A light dusting of powdered sugar subtly covers the top surface, adding a delicate white contrast to the warm, deep golden-brown crust. A small, artful drizzle of rich, amber-colored dulce de leche is placed beside the empanadita, creating a visually appealing contrast. The plate is positioned slightly off-center, allowing for moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple light wooden table surface. A neatly folded cotton napkin in a neutral tone is placed to the side. The scene is illuminated by natural, even lighting, highlighting the textures and warm tones of the dessert.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small bowl of Cajeta (goat's milk caramel) as an alternative to dulce de leche.
Pair with a traditional Mexican hot chocolate or café de olla.
instructions: Melt butter in a large pan over medium-low heat.
Add sliced onions. Cook slowly, stirring occasionally, for 25-30 minutes until deeply golden brown and very soft.
Add brown sugar and pinch of salt. Cook for another 5 minutes, stirring, until sugar dissolves and onions are jammy. Set aside to cool completely.
In a bowl, combine shredded Chihuahua cheese, softened cream cheese, granulated sugar, vanilla extract, and ground cinnamon.
Mix until well combined.
Fold in the cooled caramelized onions.
Lay out one tortilla. Place about 45 g (approx. 2 tablespoons) of the filling on one half of the tortilla, leaving a border.
Fold the other half of the tortilla over the filling to create a half-moon shape.
Press edges firmly to seal. Use a fork to crimp the edges, ensuring a tight seal. Repeat with remaining tortillas and filling.
Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet or deep pan over medium heat. Oil should be about 2-3 cm deep.
Carefully place 2-3 empanaditas into the hot oil. Do not overcrowd the pan.
Fry for 2-3 minutes per side, until golden brown and crispy.
Remove empanaditas with a slotted spoon and place on a wire rack lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.
Dust warm empanaditas lightly with icing sugar.
Serve immediately with a side of dulce de leche for dipping.
notes: Ensure onions are very deeply caramelized for maximum sweetness and flavor.
Do not overfill the tortillas to prevent leakage during frying.
The cheese filling is sweet, but the chihuahua cheese provides a mild, creamy base that balances the caramelized onion.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Cabbage and Carrot Salad
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, deconstructed salad presented on a handcrafted, light cream-colored ceramic plate. The finely shredded, pale green fermented cabbage and bright orange julienned carrots form the base, artfully arranged in a loose, natural mound. Scattered among them are plump, bright green blanched edamame and small, translucent cubes of cucumber, adding pops of color and varied textures. A creamy, subtly orange-hued Panang Lime Dressing is lightly drizzled over the components, with some pooling naturally at the base. Fresh green cilantro leaves are casually placed on top, along with roughly crushed roasted peanuts for earthy tones and crunch. Thinly sliced green onions provide a final delicate garnish. The presentation emphasizes clean lines and natural forms, showcasing each ingredient's unique contribution. The entire plate is visible, with ample negative space. The setting features a light, textured reclaimed wood table, an undyed linen napkin, and soft natural lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a refreshing side dish with rice-based meals.
Offer alongside grilled plant-based proteins.
instructions: Prepare fermented vegetables: In a large bowl, combine finely shredded cabbage and julienned carrots with salt. Massage vigorously for 5-10 minutes until vegetables release liquid and soften. Pack tightly into a clean glass jar, pressing down to ensure vegetables are submerged in their brine. Leave 2-3 cm headspace. Seal with a lid that allows gas release or burp daily. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days, or until desired tanginess is reached. Store in refrigerator.

Prepare dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together Panang curry paste, coconut milk, lime juice, rice vinegar, maple syrup, and grated ginger until smooth. Add a splash of water if a thinner consistency is desired.
Assemble salad: In a large mixing bowl, combine 200 g of the fermented cabbage and carrots (drain excess brine), blanched edamame, and diced cucumber.
Dress and serve: Pour the Panang Lime Dressing over the salad mixture. Toss gently to coat all ingredients.
Garnish: Divide salad among four plates. Garnish each serving with chopped cilantro, crushed roasted peanuts, and sliced green onions.
notes: The fermentation time can be adjusted based on desired sourness.
This recipe utilizes vegetable scraps for fermentation, reducing food waste.

recipes.recipe_name: Carrot and Quick-Pickled Chili-Garlic Salad
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented in a handcrafted, matte finish ceramic bowl in an earthy cream or beige tone, reflecting traditional Indian pottery. Julienne-cut vibrant orange carrots form the base, interspersed with thinly sliced translucent red onion rings and delicate, crisp cucumber rounds. Finely minced green chilies and garlic are visible throughout, adding flecks of deeper green and white. Fresh green cilantro leaves are scattered generously, providing a verdant contrast. A light, glistening lime-based dressing coats the vegetables, reflecting natural light. The arrangement is natural and slightly mounded, showcasing the distinct textures and colors of each ingredient without overcrowding. The bowl rests on a light-colored, reclaimed wooden table surface, its natural grain visible. A simple, undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone is casually draped beside the bowl. A small, traditional Indian katori (small metal bowl) and a simple brass serving spoon are placed nearby, honoring authentic Indian dining. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene from the side, creating gentle shadows and highlighting the freshness. The background is clean and minimalist, with subtle hints of lush green plants, reinforcing the eco-conscious theme. A few fresh carrot tops, if available, are artfully placed as a zero-waste garnish.
instructions: Prepare the quick-pickle brine: In a saucepan, combine water, vinegar, salt, 5g sugar or jaggery, mustard seeds, and fenugreek seeds. Bring to a boil. Stir until salt and sugar dissolve. Remove from heat. Let cool completely.
Prepare carrots: Julienne the carrots. In a bowl, combine julienned carrots with 1/2 of the minced green chilies and 1/2 of the minced garlic.

Quick-pickle carrots: Pour the cooled brine over the carrot mixture. Ensure carrots are submerged. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 24 hours for deeper flavor. This acts as a quick preservation method.
Prepare remaining vegetables: Thinly slice the cucumber into rounds. Thinly slice the red onion. Chop the fresh coriander.

Prepare the dressing: In a separate bowl, whisk together lime juice, olive oil, hot sauce, black salt, roasted cumin powder, Kashmiri chili powder, and 5g sugar or jaggery. Taste and adjust sweetness/spice as needed.

Assemble the salad: Drain the quick-pickled carrots, reserving the brine for other uses (e.g., marinades, flavorings). In a large mixing bowl, combine the drained carrots, sliced cucumber, sliced red onion, and chopped fresh coriander.
Dress and serve: Pour the prepared dressing over the salad ingredients. Toss gently to coat all vegetables evenly. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Yellowfin Tuna, Sweet Corn Velouté, Soy Chorizo Crumble
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Seared Yellowfin Tuna and Sweet Corn Velouté is presented in a wide, shallow matte white ceramic bowl. The vibrant pale yellow velouté forms a flowing pool, its creamy texture visible. A thick, perfectly seared yellowfin tuna fillet, golden-brown and warm pink interior, rests atop the velouté. Tuna is whole. A scattering of dark, crispy soy chorizo crumble adds textural contrast. Bright green garlic-chive oil elegantly encircles the velouté. Micro cilantro sprigs are precisely placed on the tuna, adding verdant color. Abundant white space emphasizes minimalist elegance. The setting features a polished grey-veined marble surface. The bowl is premium bone china. A pristine white linen napkin, precisely folded, sits beside it. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing sophisticated simplicity and refined textures.
instructions: Heat 5ml olive oil in a small pan over medium-high heat. Add soy chorizo. Break apart with a spoon. Cook, stirring frequently, until crispy and browned. Remove from pan. Drain on paper towel. Set aside.

Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Add shallot. Cook until translucent, about 2 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook 30 seconds until fragrant. Add corn kernels and vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5-7 minutes until corn is tender.

Carefully transfer corn mixture to a high-speed blender. Add almond milk. Blend until very smooth. Pass velouté through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean saucepan. Press solids to extract all liquid. Discard solids.
Gently reheat velouté over low heat. Season with salt and white pepper. Keep warm.
Heat 50ml neutral oil in a small saucepan over low heat. Add thinly sliced garlic. Gently infuse for 5 minutes. Do not brown garlic. Remove from heat. Stir in chopped chives. Let cool slightly.
Pat tuna fillets dry with paper towel. Season generously with salt and black pepper on all sides. Heat 15ml olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pan over high heat until shimmering.
Carefully place tuna fillets in hot pan. Sear for 1.5 to 2 minutes per side for rare-medium rare. Tuna should have a beautiful crust and be warm through the center. Do not overcook.
Ladle warm corn velouté into the center of each shallow bowl.
Carefully place one seared tuna fillet atop the velouté.
Sprinkle a small amount of crispy soy chorizo crumble over the tuna and velouté.
Drizzle garlic-chive oil artfully around the velouté.
Garnish with a few sprigs of micro cilantro. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Tapioca Crisps with Spicy Tomato Confit and Manchego Cloud
recipes.visual_description: A minimalist arrangement of 8-10 elegant canapés presented on a polished grey marble slab. Each canapé features an irregularly shaped, translucent, golden-beige tapioca crisp as its base. On top of each crisp rests a small, vibrant dollop of ruby-red spicy tomato confit, showcasing the slow-roasted texture of the halved tomatoes. Adjacent to the confit, a delicate, airy, and pristine white Manchego cloud is precisely placed, offering a soft contrast. A single, tiny green micro-cilantro sprig adorns each piece, providing a precise pop of color. The canapés are artfully spaced across the platter, utilizing abundant negative space to enhance their sophisticated simplicity. The overall composition is organic and flowing, avoiding rigid geometry. The scene is lit dramatically from the side, casting subtle shadows that highlight the textures and forms, set against an ultra-minimalist background, emphasizing the luxurious and refined nature of the dish. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, is subtly placed to the side.
instructions: Prepare Spicy Tomato Confit: Halve cherry tomatoes. Finely mince dried bird's eye chilies and garlic clove. In a small oven-safe dish, combine halved tomatoes, minced chili, minced garlic, 2 tablespoons olive oil, a pinch of sugar, and salt and pepper to taste. Toss to coat. Roast in a preheated oven at 120°C (250°F) for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until tomatoes are slightly shriveled and intensely flavored. Cool completely.

Prepare Tapioca Crisps: In a bowl, combine tapioca flour, 100 ml water, and a pinch of salt. Mix until smooth. Spread a very thin layer of batter onto a silicone baking mat or parchment-lined baking sheet. Bake in a preheated oven at 160°C (325°F) for 8-10 minutes, or until crisp and translucent. Break into irregular, bite-sized pieces. Store in an airtight container.

Prepare Manchego Cloud: Grate Manchego cheese. In a small saucepan, gently heat heavy cream with grated Manchego cheese over low heat until cheese is melted and incorporated. Do not boil. Strain the mixture through a fine-mesh sieve to ensure smoothness. Chill the mixture thoroughly in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours, or until very cold. Once chilled, whip the Manchego cream with an electric mixer until light, airy, and cloud-like. Do not over-whip.

Assemble Canapés: Arrange irregular tapioca crisp pieces artfully on a serving platter. Place a small dollop of spicy tomato confit onto each crisp. Carefully add a delicate spoonful of Manchego cloud beside the tomato confit on each crisp. Garnish each canapé with a single, tiny sprig of micro-cilantro or micro-basil. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Jajang Udon Bites with Pork
recipes.visual_description: A modern bistro setting features a simple light wooden table. A pristine white rectangular porcelain platter holds 10-12 elegant Jajang Udon Bites. Each bite consists of a small, glossy mound of dark brown udon noodles, coiled neatly. A single, perfectly seared 1.5 cm cube of pork loin rests atop each noodle portion, exhibiting a golden-brown crust. The bites are uniformly spaced across the platter, showcasing their refined presentation. A vibrant sprinkle of thinly sliced green onion and a few toasted sesame seeds provide a fresh, contrasting garnish. The lighting is natural and even, highlighting the rich colors and textures of the dish. A folded white cotton napkin lies beside the platter, completing the clean, approachable restaurant-style presentation.
instructions: Cook udon noodles according to package directions. Drain. Rinse with cold water. Drain well. Toss with 5ml sesame oil to prevent sticking. Set aside.
Cut pork loin into 1.5 cm cubes.
Heat 5ml vegetable oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Sear pork cubes until browned and cooked through. Remove pork. Set aside.
Add remaining 10ml vegetable oil to the pan. Add black bean paste. Stir-fry for 2 minutes over medium heat until fragrant. Remove paste from pan. Set aside.
Add diced onion to the pan. Sauté until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add diced zucchini and shredded cabbage. Sauté for 3 minutes until slightly tender.
Return the stir-fried black bean paste to the pan with vegetables. Stir well to combine.
Pour in water or chicken stock, soy sauce, sugar, and mirin. Bring to a simmer.
Combine cornstarch and 15ml cold water to make a slurry. Stir slurry into the simmering sauce. Cook, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens to a glossy consistency.
Add 15ml toasted sesame oil to the sauce. Mix well.
In a large bowl, combine the cooked udon noodles with the Jajang sauce. Toss gently until noodles are evenly coated.
To assemble canapés: Using tongs, coil small portions of Jajang udon noodles into neat mounds. Place each mound onto a clean white porcelain serving platter or individual serving spoon.
Top each udon mound with one seared pork cube.
Garnish with thinly sliced green onion and a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Mozzarella and Tomato Puffs
recipes.visual_description: Golden-brown, puffed pastry triangles are arranged casually on a rustic, round ceramic plate with a slightly uneven, handmade texture. The pastry is flaky, revealing glimpses of the rich red tomato and passata filling, studded with softened halved cherry tomatoes. Melted, slightly browned smoked mozzarella oozes gently from the edges, showcasing its creamy texture. A sprinkle of vibrant green, freshly chopped basil leaves is scattered over the top of the puffs, adding a fresh contrast. The puffs are presented in natural, slightly overlapping portions, suggesting a generous home-cooked snack. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, with a simple, folded linen napkin placed casually beside it. Warm, inviting light from a kitchen window illuminates the scene, highlighting the comforting appeal of the dish. The overall presentation is unpretentious and homely, inviting immediate enjoyment.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm as an appetizer or snack.
Offer alongside a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.
Present on a large wooden board for sharing during a casual gathering.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Line a baking tray with parchment paper.
Heat olive oil in a small pan over medium heat. Add minced garlic. Cook 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in passata. Add halved cherry tomatoes. Simmer 5 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
Roll out puff pastry on a lightly floured surface. Cut into 8-10 squares (approx. 10x10 cm each).
Place a spoonful of tomato mixture onto the center of each pastry square.
Top with diced smoked mozzarella. Sprinkle with chopped fresh basil.
Fold one corner of the pastry over to meet the opposite corner, forming a triangle. Press edges firmly to seal.
Brush tops of puffs with beaten egg wash.
Bake 15-20 minutes, or until pastry is golden brown and puffed, and cheese is melted and bubbling.
Remove from oven. Serve warm.

recipes.recipe_name: Grilled Tropical Fruits with Coconut Farofa and Honey-Lime Drizzle
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of grilled tropical fruits is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dessert plate. Two halved nectarines, their cut sides displaying distinct dark char marks and soft, juicy flesh, are arranged slightly overlapping. Beside them, two thick rounds of pineapple exhibit beautiful caramelized edges and prominent grill lines. The fruits glow with warm orange and golden hues. A generous scattering of golden-brown coconut farofa, a coarse, crumbly texture, surrounds the fruits, adding a rustic element. A glossy, clear honey-lime drizzle cascades over the fruits and onto the plate. The composition is natural and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple light wooden table. A folded white cotton napkin and dessert fork are placed to the side. Natural, even lighting highlights textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small scoop of 'sorvete de coco' (coconut ice cream).
Offer a side of 'creme de leite' (Brazilian table cream) for a richer experience.
Garnish with a fresh mint sprig, a common herb in Brazilian desserts.
instructions: Prepare coconut farofa. Combine flour, sugar, and salt in a bowl.
Add cold diced butter. Rub with fingertips until crumbly.
Mix in shredded coconut. Spread on a baking sheet.
Bake at 180°C for 10-12 minutes. Bake until golden and crisp. Let cool.
Prepare fruits. Halve nectarines, remove pits. Cut pineapple into 1.5 cm thick rounds.
Heat a grill pan over medium-high heat.
Grill nectarines cut-side down for 3-4 minutes. Grill until tender with grill marks.
Grill pineapple slices for 2-3 minutes per side. Grill until caramelized with grill marks.
Make honey-lime drizzle. Whisk honey and juice of 1 lime in a small bowl.
Assemble dessert. Place grilled fruits on serving plates.
Spoon coconut farofa over and around fruits.
Drizzle generously with honey-lime sauce. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Red Date Annatto Mini Cakes
recipes.visual_description: Six to nine delicate, perfectly uniform miniature cakes are arranged organically on a handcrafted, cream-colored ceramic platter. The cakes possess a soft, reddish-brown hue from the annatto and fermented red dates, with a subtle golden-baked crust. Their surfaces are lightly brushed with a sheer malt syrup glaze, adding a gentle sheen. The interior reveals a tender, moist crumb. A few finely chopped red date pieces or tiny, fresh green leaves are sparingly placed for subtle accent. The platter rests on a light, reclaimed wood table, complemented by an undyed beige linen napkin. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the cakes' natural colors and textures against a clean, minimalist background with a hint of green foliage.
instructions: Rinse red dates. Place in clean jar. Add 100ml water. Cover loosely. Ferment at room temperature 24-48 hours. Dates should soften, liquid slightly bubbly.
Grind annatto seeds lightly. Steep in 50ml hot water 15 minutes. Strain, reserve liquid.
Preheat oven to 180°C. Lightly grease mini cake molds.
Drain fermented dates, reserving liquid. Mash dates into a paste.
In a bowl, whisk mashed dates, malt syrup, vegetable oil, reserved annatto liquid, and orange zest.
In a separate bowl, whisk flour, baking powder, and salt.
Add dry ingredients to wet ingredients. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Spoon batter into prepared molds. Fill 3/4 full.
Bake 12-15 minutes. Cakes are done when edges are golden and a toothpick inserted comes out clean.
Remove from oven. Let cool in molds 5 minutes. Transfer to wire rack to cool completely.
notes: This recipe prioritizes natural sweetness and minimal processing.
Fermentation enhances flavor complexity and contributes to digestive health.
Store cakes in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 days.

recipes.recipe_name: Poached Plum, Prune Fluid Gel, Cinnamon Crumble, Plum Sorbet
recipes.visual_description: A modern dessert presented on a pristine white bone china plate with generous negative space. A quenelle of vibrant plum sorbet anchors the composition. Around it, precisely cut segments of ruby-red poached plum are arranged organically, showcasing their smooth, tender texture. Scattered meticulously are golden-brown cinnamon butter crumble pieces, providing textural contrast. Small, artful dots or a delicate swipe of deep purple prune fluid gel complete the dish, adding visual depth and intense fruit flavor. The overall presentation is minimalist and elegant, highlighting the natural beauty and contrasting textures of the fruit. The plate rests on a polished grey veined marble surface, accompanied by a single silver dessert spoon and a precisely folded white linen napkin. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, emphasizing the dish's architectural precision.
instructions: Prepare Plum Sorbet: Halve 2 plums. Remove pits. Blend into a smooth puree. Pass through a fine sieve.
Combine 150g caster sugar, 150ml water, and glucose syrup in a saucepan. Heat until sugar dissolves. Cool completely.
Mix plum puree with sugar syrup. Chill mixture completely. Churn in an ice cream maker. Freeze until firm.
Poach Plums: Halve remaining 2 plums. Remove pits. Cut each half into 3-4 segments.
In a saucepan, combine 100g caster sugar, 500ml water, cinnamon stick, and juice of half lemon. Bring to a simmer.
Add plum segments. Poach gently for 3-5 minutes until tender but hold shape. Do not overcook. Remove plums with a slotted spoon. Reserve poaching liquid. Cool plums completely.
Make Prune Fluid Gel: Soak prunes in 100ml hot water for 15 minutes. Blend prunes with soaking water until very smooth.
In a small saucepan, combine prune puree with 150ml reserved plum poaching liquid and agar-agar. Bring to a boil. Simmer for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
