Pour into a shallow dish. Chill until set (about 30 minutes). Once set, cut into chunks. Blend until completely smooth and fluid. Transfer to a squeeze bottle.
Bake Cinnamon Crumble: Preheat oven to 170°C. Combine flour, 50g granulated sugar, and 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon in a bowl. Add cold butter cubes. Rub with fingertips until coarse crumbs form.
Spread crumbs on a baking tray lined with parchment paper. Bake for 12-15 minutes, or until golden brown and crisp. Cool completely.

Assemble Dish (for 4 portions): Place a quenelle of plum sorbet slightly off-center on each plate. Arrange 3-4 poached plum segments artfully around the sorbet. Scatter 1-2 tablespoons of cinnamon crumble around the plums and sorbet. Add 3-4 small dots of prune fluid gel using a squeeze bottle. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Cherry Peach Chocolate Crumble
recipes.visual_description: A deeply golden-brown Baked Cherry Peach Chocolate Crumble is presented in a rustic, well-loved ceramic baking dish, placed on a simple wooden kitchen table. The crumble topping is unevenly textured with delightful peaks and valleys, showing hints of melted dark chocolate peeking through. The fruit filling beneath is bubbling around the edges, revealing vibrant hues of softened, cooked peaches and dark red cherries. A large, well-used serving spoon rests beside the dish, ready to scoop generous portions. The scene is bathed in warm, natural light, suggesting a cozy, lived-in family kitchen atmosphere. Portions are generous and comforting, inviting immediate enjoyment.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm, optionally with a scoop of vanilla ice cream or a dollop of whipped cream for extra indulgence.

ingredients.name: Dark chocolate
ingredients.quantity: 100 g, chopped into small chunks or chips

instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
In a large bowl, combine diced peaches, pitted cherries, kirsch liqueur, and 25g of granulated sugar. Mix gently.
Stir in the chopped dark chocolate with the fruit mixture.
Pour the fruit mixture into a 20x20 cm (8x8 inch) baking dish.
In a separate bowl, combine flour, remaining 75g granulated sugar, and salt for the crumble topping.
Add cold, cubed butter to the flour mixture. Use your fingertips or a pastry blender to rub the butter into the flour until coarse crumbs form.
Evenly sprinkle the crumble topping over the fruit mixture in the baking dish.
Bake for 30-35 minutes, or until the topping is golden brown and the fruit filling is bubbly.
Let cool slightly before serving warm.
notes: Adjust sugar quantity based on sweetness of fruit.
Frozen fruit can be used; thaw and drain excess liquid first.
This crumble is excellent for casual gatherings or a cozy night in.

recipes.recipe_name: Andean Dawn: Tomato-Rocoto Gel, Mozzarella Cloud, Caramelized Onion Crisp
recipes.visual_description: A pristine white bone china plate cradles a composition of sophisticated simplicity. A vibrant vermillion arc of roasted tomato-rocoto gel sweeps gracefully across one side. Adjacent, a cloud-like quenelle of ethereal mozzarella mousse, pristine white and softly mounded, rests delicately. Interspersed are two shards of amber-hued, caramelized red onion crisps, offering a translucent, brittle texture. Three precise droplets of bright emerald basil oil punctuate the negative space, alongside two slender, glistening threads of candied Aji Limo, adding a subtle warmth and visual interest. The presentation emphasizes fluidity, negative space, and refined contrasts, showcasing precise knife work and expert plating on a premium marble surface with dramatic lighting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C (325°F).

For Tomato-Rocoto Gel: Halve cherry tomatoes. Toss with 50g sugar. Roast 30 minutes until softened. Blend roasted tomatoes with diced rocoto until smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve. Heat strained puree with 4g agar-agar. Simmer 2 minutes, stirring. Pour into a shallow dish. Chill until set. Once set, blend until smooth and pipeable. Store chilled.

For Mozzarella Cloud: Dice mozzarella into small cubes. Soak in cold water 30 minutes. Drain. Blend mozzarella with heavy cream, 50g sugar, and vanilla bean paste until very smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve. Transfer to a siphon canister. Charge with N2O. Chill 1 hour.

For Caramelized Onion Crisps: Thinly slice red onions using a mandoline. Heat olive oil in a pan. Add onions. Cook over very low heat 45-60 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply caramelized and very soft. Spread thinly on a silicone mat. Dehydrate at 60°C (140°F) for 4-6 hours until brittle. Break into shards. Store in an airtight container.

For Basil Oil: Blanch basil leaves 10 seconds in boiling water. Immediately transfer to ice bath. Squeeze dry. Blend blanched basil with grapeseed oil until smooth. Strain through a cheesecloth-lined sieve. Chill.

For Candied Aji Limo Threads: Thinly slice Aji Limo into julienne. Combine 50g sugar and 50ml water in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer. Add Aji Limo threads. Simmer 5-7 minutes until translucent. Drain. Separate threads. Store on parchment paper.

To Plate: Swipe a small arc of Tomato-Rocoto Gel on a pristine white plate. Dispense a cloud-like quenelle of Mozzarella Cloud adjacent to the gel. Arrange two Caramelized Onion Crisp shards artfully. Dot 3-4 drops of Basil Oil around the elements. Place 2-3 Candied Aji Limo threads precisely on the mozzarella cloud or gel. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure mozzarella is very fresh and low-moisture for best texture. Soaking helps reduce salinity.
Caramelizing onions slowly is crucial for sweetness and depth of flavor.
Use a very small amount of rocoto and aji limo to provide warmth, not intense heat, balancing the sweetness.

recipes.recipe_name: Corn and Black Bean Fiesta Salad
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Corn and Black Bean Fiesta Salad is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The base consists of fluffy white rice mixed with bright yellow corn kernels, dark black beans, and a medley of finely diced red and green bell peppers. Halved crimson cherry tomatoes and finely diced red onion are interspersed throughout, adding pops of color and texture. Chunks of creamy green avocado are gently folded in, maintaining their shape. The salad is lightly coated in a zesty lime-cilantro dressing, glistening subtly. Fresh, vibrant green cilantro leaves are scattered generously over the top as a garnish. The overall composition is organized yet natural, showcasing the diverse colors and textures of the fresh ingredients. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a neatly folded cotton napkin beside it. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its freshness. A small, rustic bowl of tortilla chips is placed nearby, suggesting a culturally authentic accompaniment.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas.
Offer a side of tortilla chips for scooping.
Accompany with a small dish of fresh salsa verde.
instructions: Cook rice according to package directions. Cool completely.
If using fresh corn, blanch or grill kernels. If frozen, thaw and drain.
Drain and rinse black beans thoroughly.
Finely dice red onion, red bell pepper, and green bell pepper. Halve cherry tomatoes. Chop cilantro.
In a large bowl, combine cooled rice, corn, black beans, diced red onion, diced red bell pepper, diced green bell pepper, and halved cherry tomatoes.
Prepare dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together lime juice, olive oil, ground cumin, chili powder, salt, black pepper, and maple syrup (if using).
Pour dressing over salad ingredients. Add chopped cilantro. Toss gently to combine all ingredients.
Just before serving, dice avocado into chunks. Gently fold avocado into the salad.
Serve immediately or chill for 30 minutes for flavors to meld.

recipes.recipe_name: Pavê de Morango e Caramelo com Creme de Castanha de Caju
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Brazilian Strawberry and Caramel Pavê presented in a clear, wide-mouthed glass dessert bowl, showcasing its distinct layers. The bottom layer consists of softened Maria cookies, subtly soaked. Above, a generous, creamy off-white cashew milk custard forms a smooth layer, followed by vibrant, thinly sliced fresh strawberries. This sequence repeats, creating visible strata of creamy, fruity, and cookie textures. A glistening, rich amber caramel sauce is generously drizzled over the strawberry and cream layers, with a final artistic swirl on top. The surface is garnished with a few bright red, halved fresh strawberries. The dessert rests on a simple, slightly imperfect ceramic plate on a warm, well-used wooden dining table, with a plain metal spoon beside it. Natural, cozy kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the inviting, homemade appeal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve well chilled.
Often prepared in a large glass dish for family gatherings.
Accompanied by strong Brazilian coffee after a meal.
instructions: Combine cashew milk, whole milk, sugar, and cornstarch in a saucepan. Whisk until smooth.
Heat over medium heat. Stir continuously until mixture thickens to a custard consistency. Do not boil vigorously.
Remove from heat. Stir in vanilla extract. Let cream cool slightly.
Wash and hull strawberries. Slice strawberries thinly.
Dip Maria cookies quickly in water or milk. Do not over-soak.
Arrange a single layer of soaked cookies at the bottom of four individual dessert glasses or a medium glass dish.
Spread a layer of cashew milk cream over the cookies.
Arrange a layer of sliced strawberries over the cream.
Drizzle caramel sauce over the strawberries.
Repeat layers: cookies, cream, strawberries, caramel, until ingredients are used. Finish with a cream layer.
Garnish top with a few fresh strawberry slices and an extra drizzle of caramel.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, until well chilled and set.

recipes.recipe_name: Grilled Chicken Mint Kofta Skewers
recipes.visual_description: A single starter portion of two golden-brown grilled chicken kofta skewers is elegantly presented on a clean white porcelain plate. Each kofta is an elongated, cylindrical shape, showcasing a slightly charred, crispy exterior from grilling, with visible flecks of green mint and red onion. A small, creamy dollop of smooth white labneh rests beside the skewers. Scattered artistically over and around the kofta are vibrant pink and purple rings of thinly sliced pickled red onion. Fresh, bright green chopped parsley is sprinkled over the dish, adding a pop of color and freshness. The composition is balanced with moderate negative space, highlighting the dish's vibrant colors and varied textures. The plate sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and standard flatware, under natural, even lighting that evokes a casual bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm pita bread on the side for scooping
Offer a simple side salad of cucumbers and tomatoes
instructions: Thinly slice half of the red onion into rings. Combine with white vinegar, water, and sugar in a small bowl. Set aside to pickle for at least 30 minutes.
Finely mince the remaining half of the red onion and all garlic cloves. Finely chop the fresh mint leaves and parsley.
In a large bowl, combine ground chicken, minced onion, minced garlic, chopped mint, cumin, coriander, sumac, salt, and black pepper. Mix thoroughly until well combined.
Divide the mixture into 8 equal portions. Form each portion into an elongated cylindrical shape around a wooden skewer.
Heat olive oil in a large grill pan or cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat. Place skewers in the hot pan.
Cook skewers for 4-5 minutes per side, rotating until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
While kofta cooks, whisk labneh with lemon juice until smooth.
Remove kofta from heat. Arrange two skewers per serving on a plate.
Spoon a dollop of labneh beside the kofta. Garnish with pickled red onion rings and fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Yam and Pickled Daikon Salad
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a handcrafted, earthy-toned ceramic plate, likely cream or light beige, highlighting its natural texture. Roasted yam cubes, golden-orange and caramelized, are scattered, showcasing their organic shapes. Bright white pickled daikon cubes contrast with vibrant green spinach or mizuna and blanched edamame. A glossy umami dressing lightly coats ingredients, reflecting natural light. Toasted white sesame seeds and minimal, tiny, crispy beef crumbles (if used) are sprinkled for texture, not dominating. The composition emphasizes natural beauty, simple lines, and ample negative space. The plate rests on a light reclaimed wood or stone surface with an undyed linen napkin. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene. The clean, minimalistic background may include a blurred plant. Subtle Japanese elements, like chopsticks, reinforce cultural authenticity. The overall impression is fresh, wholesome, and mindfully simple.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small bowl of steamed short-grain rice.
Offer a side of miso soup.
Serve individual portions using traditional ceramic salad bowls or deep plates.
Use wooden chopsticks for eating.

ingredients.name: Beef trimmings or lean beef (for garnish, optional)

instructions: Combine water, rice vinegar, sugar, and salt in a bowl for the pickling brine. Stir until dissolved.
Add 1 cm diced daikon to the brine. Cover. Let pickle at room temperature for at least 2 hours, or refrigerate overnight.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss 2 cm diced yam with a pinch of salt. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes until tender and slightly caramelized. Let cool.
Heat a small pan over medium-high heat. Add very finely diced beef. Cook until crispy and rendered, stirring frequently. Drain excess fat. Set aside on paper towel.
In a small saucepan, combine chicken stock, soy sauce, rice vinegar, mirin, and grated ginger. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 2 minutes. Remove from heat. Stir in sesame oil. Let cool.
In a large bowl, combine roasted yam, drained pickled daikon, spinach or mizuna, and blanched edamame.
Pour dressing over salad. Gently toss to combine. Divide among four plates. Sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds and crispy beef garnish (if using). Serve immediately.
notes: For a deeper fermented flavor, the daikon can be lacto-fermented for several days.
Yam skins can be crisped in the oven or air fryer and used as an additional zero-waste garnish.
The crispy beef garnish is entirely optional for a fully plant-forward salad. If omitted, consider adding toasted nuts or seeds for extra crunch.

recipes.recipe_name: Cherry, Honey, and Manchego Tartlets
recipes.visual_description: A single golden-crusted tartlet rests on a simple, slightly worn ceramic plate, placed on a warm, well-used wooden dining table. The tartlet's edges are a rustic golden brown, with a slightly irregular, homemade charm. Its creamy, pale yellow filling is visible, studded generously with plump, deep red cherries, some peeking through the surface, others nestled within the custard. A light dusting of powdered sugar subtly enhances the top. Beside the plate, a simple, silver dessert fork rests on a casually folded beige linen napkin. The scene is illuminated by soft, natural light, creating a cozy, lived-in atmosphere of a family kitchen. The background shows a hint of natural kitchen clutter, like a rustic wooden cutting board or a simple tea towel, reinforcing the homely French comfort.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve simply as is, with a cup of coffee or tea.
instructions: Combine flour, powdered sugar, and salt in a bowl.
Add cold butter. Rub with fingertips until crumbly.
Add egg yolk. Mix until dough forms. Add water if too dry.
Form into a disc. Wrap in plastic. Chill 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Roll dough 3 mm thick. Cut four 10 cm circles.
Line four 10 cm tartlet molds with dough. Prick bottoms with a fork.
Line with parchment paper. Fill with pie weights.
Bake 15 minutes. Remove weights and parchment.
Bake 5 more minutes until lightly golden. Cool shells.
Whisk eggs, cream, honey, and vanilla extract until smooth.
Stir in grated Manchego cheese.
Distribute pitted cherries evenly in cooled tartlet shells.
Pour the Manchego custard mixture over the cherries.
Bake 20-25 minutes, or until filling is set and lightly golden.
A knife inserted near the center should come out clean.
Let tartlets cool completely on a wire rack before serving.
notes: Ensure dough is well-chilled for best results.
Do not overbake the tartlets; the filling should be just set.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Rye Toasts with Sausage and Artichoke
recipes.visual_description: Four rectangular slices of dark rye bread, each generously topped, are arranged slightly offset on a rustic, light-colored wooden serving board. The rye bread is toasted to a deep golden-brown with a visible crisp crust. Each slice is spread with a thick, creamy layer of pale green artichoke spread, showing a pleasingly chunky texture from the mashed artichoke hearts. On top, golden-brown, finely crumbled Italian sausage is evenly distributed, creating a rich contrast. A sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped fresh chives garnishes each toast, adding a pop of color and freshness. The arrangement is clean and inviting, with moderate negative space on the board. A simple white linen napkin is casually folded beside the board. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and warm tones of the dish. The scene suggests a casual, yet refined bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as part of a "Brotzeit" spread with gherkins or pickled onions on the side.
Pair with a crisp German beer.

ingredients.name: Fresh chives
ingredients.quantity: 15g, finely chopped, plus extra for garnish

instructions: Remove sausage from casing. Crumble into a pan.
Cook sausage over medium heat until browned and cooked through. Break up with a spoon. Drain excess fat. Set aside.
Heat olive oil in the same pan. Sauté diced shallot until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add drained artichoke hearts to the pan. Sauté for 2-3 minutes, lightly mashing some with a fork.
Transfer artichoke mixture to a bowl. Add cream cheese, mustard, chopped chives, and lemon juice.
Mash and mix until well combined and slightly chunky. Season with salt and pepper.
Toast rye bread slices until golden and crisp.
Spread a generous layer of artichoke mixture onto each toasted rye slice.
Top evenly with crumbled cooked sausage.
Garnish with extra fresh chives. Serve immediately.
notes: For extra flavor, a pinch of smoked paprika can be added to the artichoke spread.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Cherry & Hazelnut Tartlets
recipes.visual_description: A single golden-baked tartlet rests on a round, unglazed ceramic plate in a natural cream tone, centered on a light, reclaimed wooden surface. Its flaky, crisp crust holds a delicate hazelnut frangipane filling. Nestled within the frangipane are several deep crimson, plump fermented cherries, their natural color a striking contrast. A glistening, clear cherry pit syrup is lightly drizzled over the tartlet. The presentation is minimalist and clean, highlighting the natural textures and colors of the ingredients. A single, small green mint leaf or a delicate edible flower is placed beside the tartlet. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, with a subtle, blurred background hinting at natural elements like a potted plant.

ingredients.name: Fresh mint leaves or edible flowers

instructions: Prepare fermented cherries: Wash cherries. Pit cherries, reserving all pits. In a clean jar, combine 200 ml water and 50 g sugar to create a brine. Stir until sugar dissolves. Add pitted cherries to the brine. Seal jar. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days until slightly fizzy and tart. Refrigerate.

Make cherry pit syrup: Rinse reserved cherry pits. In a small saucepan, combine pits, 100 ml water, and 50 g sugar. Simmer gently for 15-20 minutes until liquid reduces and is fragrant. Strain, discard pits. Cool syrup.

Prepare tart dough: In a bowl, combine 150 g flour and pinch of salt. Cut in 75 g cold butter until crumbly. Add iced water gradually, mix until dough forms. Do not overwork. Form into a disc. Wrap. Chill 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).

Roll dough on a lightly floured surface to 3 mm thickness. Cut out four circles to fit 10 cm tartlet tins. Press dough into tins. Prick bottoms with a fork. Line with parchment paper, fill with baking weights or dried beans. Blind bake for 10 minutes. Remove weights and parchment. Bake for another 5 minutes until lightly golden. Cool.
Prepare hazelnut frangipane: In a bowl, cream 50 g softened butter and 50 g caster sugar until light. Beat in egg gradually. Stir in hazelnut butter. Fold in 20 g flour until just combined.
Fill cooled tartlet shells with hazelnut frangipane, spreading evenly. Arrange a few fermented cherries on top of the frangipane.
Bake tartlets for 20-25 minutes, or until frangipane is golden brown and set. Cool completely on a wire rack.
To serve, drizzle cooled tartlets with cherry pit syrup. Garnish each with a small fresh mint leaf or an edible flower.
notes: This recipe emphasizes eco-conscious practices through fermentation for flavor development and zero-waste utilization of cherry pits for syrup.
Use locally sourced, seasonal cherries for best flavor and sustainability.

recipes.recipe_name: Deconstructed Cheesecake with Toasted Brioche, Raspberry Rose Gel, and Vanilla Bean Crème Diplomat
recipes.visual_description: A minimalist, ultra-sophisticated sweet snack presented on a pristine white bone china plate. The composition features small, organically shaped mounds of creamy white cream cheese mousse. Delicately scattered around are golden, irregularly shaped toasted brioche crumbs, offering a textural contrast. Precisely placed are vibrant, translucent shards of raspberry rose gel, adding a pop of deep red color and subtle tartness. Small, perfect dots of pale vanilla bean crème diplomat are strategically piped, creating visual interest. The entire presentation maintains abundant negative space, highlighting each component's precise execution and visual appeal. A single, fresh micro mint leaf or a few tiny edible rose petals provide a refined, understated garnish. The plate rests on a luxurious white Carrara marble surface under dramatic, focused lighting, casting subtle shadows to enhance depth. The background is clean and uncluttered, emphasizing the artistry of the dish.

ingredients.name: Micro mint leaves or edible rose petals

instructions: Prepare Cream Cheese Mousse: Bloom gelatin in cold water. Beat cream cheese with 50g sugar and vanilla until smooth. Gently warm bloomed gelatin to dissolve. Whip 150ml heavy cream to soft peaks. Fold gelatin into cream cheese. Gently fold whipped cream into cream cheese mixture. Chill in piping bag for at least 2 hours.

Prepare Toasted Brioche Crumble: Preheat oven to 160°C. Tear brioche into small, irregular pieces. Toss brioche with melted butter and 10g sugar. Spread on baking sheet. Toast for 10-12 minutes until golden and crisp. Cool completely. Crush lightly into varied crumbs.

Prepare Raspberry Rose Gel: Combine raspberries, 30g sugar, and lemon juice in a saucepan. Cook over medium heat until raspberries break down. Press through fine-mesh sieve to remove seeds. Return purée to clean saucepan. Whisk in agar-agar powder. Bring to a boil, stirring constantly, for 1 minute. Remove from heat. Stir in rose water. Pour thin layer onto small, flat dish. Chill until set, about 30 minutes. Cut into small, irregular shards.

Prepare Vanilla Bean Crème Diplomat: Split vanilla bean. Scrape seeds into milk. Heat milk to a simmer. In a bowl, whisk egg yolks, 50g sugar, and cornstarch until pale. Slowly temper hot milk into egg mixture, whisking constantly. Return mixture to saucepan. Cook over medium heat, whisking, until thickened to a pastry cream. Remove from heat. Stir in diced cold butter until melted and smooth. Transfer to a bowl. Cover surface with cling film. Chill completely. Once cold, remove vanilla bean pod. Whip 150ml heavy cream to soft peaks. Gently fold whipped cream into pastry cream until smooth and light. Chill in piping bag.

Assemble Dish: On a premium bone china plate, pipe small, organic mounds of chilled cream cheese mousse. Artistically scatter toasted brioche crumble around the mousse. Place irregular shards of raspberry rose gel precisely. Pipe small, delicate dots of vanilla bean crème diplomat. Garnish sparingly with micro mint leaves or edible rose petals. Serve immediately on a sharing platter.

recipes.recipe_name: White Chocolate Coconut Caramel Entremet
recipes.visual_description: A pristine, individual mini entremet stands centered on a clean white porcelain dessert plate. Its surface is encased in a mirror-smooth, glossy white chocolate glaze, reflecting soft light. The entremet is perfectly round, with clean, defined edges. A delicate scattering of golden-brown toasted coconut flakes adorns one side of the top, contrasting with the pure white glaze. A faint, precise dusting of dark cocoa powder graces the opposite side, adding a subtle visual depth and color accent. The plate has ample negative space. The dessert sits on a simple wooden table surface, beside it a plain white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dessert's textures and sheen.
instructions: Prepare Salted Caramel Inserts: Combine 100g sugar and 30ml water in a saucepan. Cook over medium heat until golden caramel forms. Remove from heat. Slowly whisk in warm 50ml heavy cream. Stir in cold 30g butter and 2g salt until smooth. Pour into small silicone molds (2-3 cm diameter). Freeze until solid.

Prepare Cocoa Financier: Preheat oven to 170°C. Melt 60g butter until browned (beurre noisette). Sift 30g almond flour, 30g all-purpose flour, 15g cocoa powder, 60g sugar, and pinch of salt into a bowl. Add 2 egg whites. Mix until just combined. Stir in cooled browned butter. Pour into a 15x15 cm baking pan lined with parchment. Bake 12-15 minutes. Cool completely. Cut out 4 rounds (approx. 5 cm diameter).

Prepare Coconut Mousse: Bloom 2g gelatin in cold water. Gently heat 150ml coconut cream, 50ml heavy cream, and 20g sugar until sugar dissolves. Remove from heat. Stir in bloomed gelatin until dissolved. Pour over 50g chopped white chocolate. Let sit 1 minute, then whisk until smooth. Cool to room temperature. Chill slightly until thickened but still pourable.

Assemble Entremets: Place 4 individual silicone entremet molds (6-7 cm diameter) on a tray. Pour a layer of coconut mousse into each mold. Place a frozen caramel insert in the center of each mousse. Cover with more coconut mousse, filling molds about two-thirds full. Place a financier round on top of each mousse layer, pressing gently. Freeze entremets for at least 4 hours.

Prepare White Chocolate Glaze: Bloom 1g gelatin. Combine 50ml heavy cream, 15ml glucose syrup, and 20ml water in a saucepan. Bring to a simmer. Remove from heat. Stir in bloomed gelatin. Pour over 100g chopped white chocolate. Let sit 1 minute, then whisk until smooth. Strain the glaze. Let cool to 35-40°C.
Glaze Entremets: Remove frozen entremets from molds. Place on a wire rack over a baking sheet. Pour glaze evenly over each frozen entremet, ensuring full coverage. Let excess glaze drip off.
Garnish and Serve: Carefully transfer glazed entremets to serving plates. Garnish with toasted coconut flakes and a light dusting of cocoa powder. Serve chilled.
notes: Ensure all ingredients are at specified temperatures for optimal texture and setting.

recipes.recipe_name: Potato and Daikon Salad with Spicy Miso Vinaigrette
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on an expensive bone china plate, off-white with a subtle rim, set on a dark, polished wood table. Natural light casts soft shadows. The composition is organic and flowing, centered with abundant negative space. Precisely sliced, warm waxy potato rounds, about 2cm thick, are layered amongst delicate, paper-thin daikon radish slices. The potatoes, with their pale yellow flesh and slightly darker skin, contrast with the translucent white daikon. A rich, deep reddish-brown spicy miso vinaigrette is artfully drizzled and pooled around the components, highlighting their shapes and adding a glossy sheen. The arrangement is natural, avoiding strict geometry. Garnish is minimal: a sprinkle of toasted black sesame seeds provides a textural speckle, and a few vibrant green microgreens add a fresh pop of color. A single, irregularly shaped, golden-brown sesame crisp shard stands upright, adding architectural height and a crisp texture. The overall impression is one of sophisticated simplicity, showcasing the vegetables' natural beauty and precise culinary execution.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served individually as a refined appetizer or side dish.
Can be part of a larger Korean meal (hansik), though presented in a modern, fine-dining style.
instructions: Wash potatoes. Boil whole in salted water until tender but still firm, about 15-20 minutes. Drain. Cool slightly. Cut into 2cm thick slices.
Using a mandoline or sharp knife, slice daikon into paper-thin rounds.
For the dressing, combine dark miso paste, gochujang, hot bean paste, rice vinegar, toasted sesame oil, soy sauce, maple syrup, and 30ml water in a bowl. Whisk until smooth.
For the sesame crisp, whisk rice flour, 60ml water, white sesame seeds, and a pinch of salt until smooth.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium-low heat. Lightly brush with oil.

Pour about 1 tbsp of crisp batter into the pan, swirling to create a thin, even circle (8-10 cm diameter). Cook until edges crisp and golden, about 2-3 minutes. Flip and cook briefly. Transfer to a wire rack to cool and crisp. Break into irregular shards.
In a large bowl, gently toss the warm potato slices and daikon rounds with half of the dressing.
Artfully arrange the dressed potatoes and daikon on individual shallow plates, creating an organic, flowing composition.
Drizzle remaining dressing over the salad.
Garnish with toasted black sesame seeds, microgreens, and 1-2 shards of sesame crisp.
notes: The hot bean paste (doubanjiang) adds a unique layer of fermented umami and spice, deepening the complexity of the dressing.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Cheddar Espuma, Soy Chorizo Pavé, Chipotle-Habanero Essence
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of a highly refined dish rests on a pristine white bone china plate with a subtle, delicate pattern. The plate itself is positioned on a luxurious white Carrara marble surface, creating an expansive negative space that emphasizes the minimalist composition. A precisely cut, rectangular block of seared soy chorizo pavé, exhibiting a light, golden-brown crust and deep reddish-brown interior, is artfully placed slightly off-center. Adjacent to the pavé, a delicate, airy quenelle of pale yellow smoked cheddar espuma gently settles, its texture light and ethereal. A vibrant, glossy red-orange chipotle-habanero essence is meticulously drizzled or dotted around the elements, providing a bold, contrasting color and liquid texture. A few sprigs of bright green micro cilantro are precisely placed atop the pavé, offering a final delicate touch of color and freshness. The scene is illuminated by dramatic professional lighting, casting subtle shadows that add depth and dimension to the composition. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, is subtly visible in the background, reinforcing the elegant, ultra-minimalist setting.
instructions: For the Soy Chorizo Pavé: Sauté soy chorizo in 5ml olive oil over medium heat for 5 minutes. Press firmly into a small, parchment-lined terrine mold or wrap tightly in plastic wrap to form a compact block. Chill for at least 2 hours. Once firm, cut into four precise rectangular pavés.

For the Smoked Cheddar Espuma: Gently heat heavy cream in a saucepan. Add smoked cheddar, stirring until fully melted and smooth. Season with a pinch of salt. Pass the mixture through a fine-mesh sieve. Pour into a culinary siphon. Charge with one N2O cartridge. Keep warm in a bain-marie or warm water bath.

For the Chipotle-Habanero Essence: Carefully deseed and finely mince habanero chili. In a small saucepan, combine minced habanero, chipotle peppers, adobo sauce, apple cider vinegar, sugar, and vegetable stock. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat and cook until liquid is reduced by half and slightly syrupy. Blend until very smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve to remove any solids. Season with salt to taste. Keep warm.

To Serve: Heat 10ml olive oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Sear each soy chorizo pavé for 2-3 minutes per side until a light crust forms. Do not overheat. Place one seared soy chorizo pavé slightly offset on each plate. Dispense a delicate, airy quenelle of smoked cheddar espuma next to the pavé. Drizzle or dot the chipotle-habanero essence artfully around the elements. Garnish each plate with a few sprigs of micro cilantro.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Sausage & Pesto Grain Bowl with Fermented Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of this Sustainable Sausage & Pesto Grain Bowl is presented in an unglazed, handcrafted ceramic bowl. A bed of tender farro forms the base. Scattered across are browned chunks of Italian sausage, alongside vibrant roasted bell pepper (2cm chunks) and zucchini (1.5cm half-moons), some lightly caramelized. Creamy havarti cheese cubes (1.5cm) are interspersed. Distinct dollops of vivid green pesto add visual interest. Thin, translucent slices of quick-pickled red cabbage, carrots, and radishes provide vibrant color and refreshing contrast. A few fresh parsley leaves serve as a simple garnish. The bowl rests on a light, reclaimed wood table with an undyed linen napkin. Soft, natural light creates a clean, minimalist aesthetic, emphasizing the natural textures of each ingredient.
instructions: Prepare Quick-Pickled Vegetables: Thinly slice carrots into rounds or half-moons. Thinly shred red cabbage. Thinly slice radishes. Place all in a clean jar. Dissolve 10g sea salt in 250ml warm water to create a brine. Pour brine over vegetables, ensuring full submersion. Cover loosely. Let sit at room temperature for at least 1 hour, or until serving.
Cook Grains: Rinse 200g farro or pearl barley. Cook in 600ml salted water according to package directions, typically 25-30 minutes, until tender but al dente. Drain any excess water.

Cook Sausage: Remove casings from 400g Italian sausage. Crumble into a large pan. Cook over medium-high heat, breaking up the meat with a spoon, until thoroughly browned and cooked through. Drain any excess fat.

Roast Vegetables: Preheat oven to 200°C. Cut bell pepper into 2cm chunks. Cut zucchini into 1.5cm thick half-moons. Toss vegetables with 15ml olive oil, salt, and black pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 15-20 minutes, until tender-crisp and slightly caramelized.
Prepare Havarti: Cut 150g havarti cheese into 1.5cm cubes.

Assemble Bowls: Divide cooked grains evenly among 4 individual bowls. Top each with portions of the cooked sausage chunks, roasted bell pepper and zucchini, and havarti cubes. Add a generous dollop (about 20ml per bowl) of pesto sauce. Drain and add a portion of the quick-pickled vegetables. Garnish each bowl with a few fresh parsley or basil leaves.
notes: For a truly zero-waste approach, save vegetable scraps (e.g., carrot peels, bell pepper cores) to make a vegetable broth.
The quick-pickled vegetables can be made ahead and stored in the refrigerator for up to a week.

recipes.recipe_name: Kirsch-Brandy Cherry Loukoumades
recipes.visual_description: A generous, inviting pile of golden-brown Kirsch-Brandy Cherry Loukoumades sits on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. The Loukoumades are irregularly shaped, showcasing their homemade nature, with some slightly overlapping. A glossy, amber-colored syrup clings to their surfaces, pooling subtly at the base of the pile. Scattered amongst and on top of the Loukoumades are vibrant red halved fresh cherries, their natural juiciness glistening. A light dusting of ground cinnamon adds a warm, earthy contrast. The entire plate is visible, placed on a well-used wooden dining table. A casually draped, light-colored cloth napkin is nearby. The scene is bathed in warm, cozy kitchen lighting, creating a relaxed, lived-in atmosphere. The presentation is unpretentious and abundant, typical of a comforting homestyle Greek snack.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm, allowing the syrup to remain slightly runny.
Often enjoyed with a sprinkle of ground cinnamon.
Best served alongside strong Greek coffee.
instructions: Prepare the syrup: Combine honey, 50g sugar, 100ml water, and cinnamon stick in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat. Simmer for 5 minutes. Remove from heat. Stir in kirschwasser and brandy. Let syrup cool completely.
Prepare the dough: In a large bowl, dissolve yeast and 15g sugar in 200ml warm water. Let sit 5 minutes until foamy.
Add flour and salt to the yeast mixture. Mix well with a wooden spoon or by hand until a sticky, shaggy dough forms.
Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a clean cloth. Let dough rise in a warm place for 1 hour, or until doubled in size.
Heat oil: Pour vegetable oil into a deep, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven. Heat to 170°C.
Fry Loukoumades: Dip a spoon in oil. Scoop small, irregular portions of dough (about 2.5cm diameter) into the hot oil. Do not overcrowd the pot.
Fry Loukoumades for 3-4 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden brown and puffed.
Remove Loukoumades with a slotted spoon. Transfer to a plate lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.
Soak Loukoumades: Immediately transfer hot Loukoumades to the cooled syrup. Let soak for 30-60 seconds, ensuring they are fully coated.
Remove Loukoumades from syrup. Arrange on a serving platter.
Garnish: Halve the fresh cherries. Scatter cherries over the Loukoumades. Sprinkle with ground cinnamon. Serve warm.
notes: Ensure oil temperature is consistent for best frying results.
Adjust kirschwasser and brandy amounts to personal preference for a stronger or milder alcohol flavor in the syrup.

recipes.recipe_name: Japanese Seafood Brown Rice Soup
recipes.visual_description: A clear, golden amber dashi broth fills a pristine white porcelain Japanese chawan. At the bottom, a bed of plump, individual brown rice grains is visible. Resting elegantly on the rice and partially submerged are 3-4 vibrant pink, curled shrimp and several open, succulent cockles, revealing their tender meat. The surface of the soup is adorned with a generous scattering of finely sliced bright green scallion rings, providing a striking color contrast. A few delicate, translucent ginger slivers float. The bowl is positioned on a simple, light-colored wooden table. Beside it, a pair of dark wooden chopsticks rests neatly. A small, pristine white ceramic dish holds a pinch of reddish-orange shichimi togarashi. A folded white cotton napkin completes the setting. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small ceramic soup spoon.
Offer shichimi togarashi on the side for optional seasoning.
May be accompanied by a small portion of tsukemono (Japanese pickled vegetables).
instructions: Prepare Dashi: Add kombu to 1 litre cold water. Bring to a simmer. Remove kombu just before boiling. Add katsuobushi. Simmer 30 seconds. Strain through fine mesh sieve. Discard solids.
Cook Rice: Rinse brown rice. Cook according to package directions until tender but firm.
Prepare Seafood: Ensure cockles are purged of sand. Peel and devein shrimp.
Assemble Soup Base: Pour dashi into a pot. Add sake, mirin, and soy sauce. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat.
Cook Seafood: Add cockles to simmering dashi. Cook 2-3 minutes until shells open. Discard any unopened cockles. Add shrimp. Cook 1-2 minutes until shrimp turn opaque pink.
Chop Scallions: Thinly slice green parts of scallions.
Serve: Divide cooked brown rice among 4 soup bowls. Ladle hot soup with seafood over rice. Garnish each bowl with sliced scallions and a thin ginger slice if desired. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Yuzu & Cocoa Nib Entremet
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegant, and perfectly formed mini entremet sits centrally on a light beige handcrafted ceramic plate. The entremet has clean, crisp sides, revealing subtle layers. The top is smooth, lightly dusted with a scattering of dark, glossy cocoa nib crunch, providing textural contrast. The color palette is natural and muted: creamy white from the tofu mousse, a faint yellow hue from the yuzu jelly peeking through if visible, and deep brown from the cocoa nibs. The dacquoise base is a light golden-brown. The plate is simple, round, and has a slightly unglazed, natural texture. Beside the entremet, a single, small, vibrant green shiso leaf is placed minimally. The setting features a light, textured bamboo table surface. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is folded neatly to one side. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene from the side, creating gentle shadows and highlighting the clean lines of the entremet. The background is clean and minimalistic, hinting at natural elements like a subtle plant out of focus.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small cup of unsweetened green tea.
Present on individual, simple ceramic plates.
Offer small, delicate dessert forks.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Yuzu: Combine sliced yuzu, 20g cane sugar, and 100ml water in a clean jar. Seal loosely. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days. Observe small bubbles. Strain liquid, reserve yuzu solids for other use.

Make Yuzu Jelly: Heat strained yuzu liquid with scraped vanilla bean and 3g agar-agar powder. Bring to a simmer. Stir constantly until agar-agar dissolves. Pour into four 4cm diameter silicone molds. Freeze until solid.

Bake Dacquoise Base: Preheat oven to 170°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Whip egg whites until soft peaks form. Gradually add 50g caster sugar, whip until stiff and glossy meringue. Sift almond meal and icing sugar. Fold into meringue. Fold in 15g crushed cocoa nibs. Spread mixture thinly onto prepared baking sheet. Bake 12-15 minutes until lightly golden. Cool completely. Cut into four 5cm diameter circles.

Prepare Vanilla Tofu Mousse: Blend drained silken tofu, 50g maple syrup, and vanilla extract until smooth. In a small saucepan, heat 50ml water with 3g agar-agar powder. Simmer until agar-agar dissolves, about 1 minute. Slowly pour hot agar-agar mixture into tofu mixture while blending until fully combined.

Assemble Entremets: Place four 6cm diameter individual entremet rings on a clean tray. Place one dacquoise base in each ring. Pipe a layer of vanilla tofu mousse, filling about one-third of the ring. Gently press one frozen yuzu jelly disc onto the mousse layer. Pipe remaining vanilla tofu mousse to fill each ring. Smooth tops. Freeze entremets for at least 4 hours, or until completely solid.

Make Cocoa Nib Crunch: Toast 30g cocoa nibs in a dry pan over medium heat for 2 minutes. Add 10g maple syrup and a pinch of sea salt. Stir until syrup coats nibs. Spread on parchment paper to cool. Break into small clusters.
Plate and Serve: Unmold frozen entremets. Place each entremet on a serving plate. Let thaw in refrigerator for 30 minutes before serving. Sprinkle cocoa nib crunch over each entremet.
notes: Ensure all equipment for fermentation is sterilized to prevent unwanted mold growth.
Adjust sweetness of mousse based on personal preference.
The recipe yields 4 individual entremets.

recipes.recipe_name: Rose Gel with Brazil Nut Cream and Poppy Seed Crumble
recipes.visual_description: A single bone china plate holds a minimalist dessert composition. Three organic dollops of creamy, off-white brazil nut cream are artfully placed. Alongside, a small cluster of irregularly shaped, translucent rose gel cubes, a delicate ruby-pink. A scattering of coarse, dark poppy seed crumble provides textural contrast. A single, perfectly preserved candied rose petal rests on one cream dollop. Abundant white space surrounds the elements. The plate sits on a white Carrara marble surface. A pristine white linen napkin is precisely folded. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows.
instructions: Prepare Brazil Nut Cream: Soak brazil nuts in water overnight. Drain and rinse. Blend soaked brazil nuts with 200 ml fresh filtered water, 30 ml maple syrup, and vanilla extract until very smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve or nut milk bag for ultra-smooth consistency. Chill until serving.

Prepare Rose Gel: Combine 300 ml filtered water, 100 g granulated sugar, and dried rose petals in a saucepan. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5 minutes. Strain out rose petals. Return liquid to saucepan. Whisk in agar-agar powder. Bring to a boil, stirring constantly, for 1 minute. Remove from heat. Stir in rosewater. Pour into a shallow, flat dish to a thickness of 1 cm. Chill until firm. Once firm, cut into small, irregular cubes.

Prepare Poppy Seed Crumble: Preheat oven to 160°C. In a bowl, combine flour, poppy seeds, 30 ml maple syrup, and cold vegan butter. Rub with fingertips until coarse crumbs form. Spread on a baking sheet. Bake 15-20 minutes, or until golden brown and crisp. Cool completely.
Prepare Candied Rose Petals: Gently brush fresh rose petals with aquafaba. Dust evenly with powdered sugar. Place on parchment paper. Let air dry for several hours or overnight until crisp.

Assemble Dish: On each plate, artfully place three small dollops of brazil nut cream. Arrange a small cluster of rose gel cubes next to the cream. Scatter poppy seed crumble around the elements. Gently place one candied rose petal on a dollop of cream. Serve immediately.
notes: This dish is a modern, deconstructed interpretation of traditional Turkish delight (Lokum), focusing on its core flavors and textures.
For best results, prepare the brazil nut cream and rose gel several hours in advance to ensure proper chilling and setting.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Berry Granita with Plum Wine Reduction
recipes.visual_description: The vibrant, ruby-red fermented berry granita, with its delicate icy flakes, is presented in a chilled, handcrafted ceramic bowl with an organic, earthy tone. A glossy, deep amber plum wine reduction is elegantly drizzled over the granita, creating a beautiful contrast. A light, effervescent splash of champagne, subtly tinted pink with grenadine, pools gently at the base. The presentation is clean and minimalistic, allowing the natural colors and textures of the ingredients to shine. A single, small edible flower or a fresh mint leaf offers a natural, zero-waste garnish. The entire scene is set on a light reclaimed wood surface, accompanied by an undyed linen napkin, bathed in soft natural light. The focus remains entirely on the dish, celebrating its pure, simple beauty.

ingredients.name: Edible flowers or fresh mint leaves

instructions: Wash berries gently. Place in a clean jar.
Add 1 tablespoon raw sugar and 100ml water to berries. Cover loosely.
Let berries ferment at room temperature for 1-2 days until lightly bubbly. Strain, reserving liquid and berries.
Blend fermented berries and their liquid with apple brandy. Add raw sugar or maple syrup to taste. Strain mixture through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing solids.
Pour berry mixture into a shallow metal pan. Freeze for 1 hour.
Scrape granita with a fork to break up ice crystals. Repeat every 30 minutes for 3-4 hours until fully frozen and flaky.
Combine plum wine and 1 tablespoon raw sugar (optional) in a small saucepan.
Simmer plum wine gently over medium-low heat until reduced by half and slightly syrupy. Cool completely.
Combine champagne and grenadine in a small bowl for the sparkling drizzle.
Spoon granita into chilled individual dessert bowls. Drizzle generously with plum wine reduction.
Finish with a light splash of the champagne-grenadine mixture. Garnish with an edible flower or mint leaf.

recipes.recipe_name: Autumn Persimmon Fruit Salad with Maple-Prune Glaze
recipes.visual_description: An individual portion of a vibrant, rustic fruit salad is presented in a simple, deep ceramic bowl with natural imperfections, placed on a well-used wooden dining table. Warm, cozy lighting from kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene. The salad features generous chunks of bright orange persimmon wedges, crisp 1.5 cm diced red apples, juicy orange segments, and halved red grapes, all glistening with a rich, amber-hued maple-prune glaze. The fruits are casually arranged, overlapping naturally, showcasing their varied shapes and textures. A casually placed, folded linen napkin rests beside the bowl. The background is a soft blur of a lived-in kitchen, highlighting the homely, unpretentious comfort food aesthetic.
instructions: Wash all fruits thoroughly.
Quarter persimmons. Remove any core or stem. Slice into 1 cm thick wedges.
Core apples. Dice into 1.5 cm cubes. Place in a large bowl. Toss immediately with 5 ml of lemon juice to prevent browning.
Peel oranges. Section oranges, removing all white pith and membranes.
Halve red grapes.
Add persimmon wedges, orange sections, and halved grapes to the bowl with the apples.
Prepare the glaze. In a small saucepan, melt butter over low heat.
Add prune juice, maple syrup, and vanilla extract to the saucepan. Whisk to combine.
Bring glaze to a gentle simmer. Cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly reduced and warm.
Pour the warm glaze over the fruit in the bowl. Gently toss to coat all fruit evenly.
Serve immediately or chill briefly before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Tropical Orgeat Mousse Petit Fours
recipes.visual_description: Six to nine perfectly uniform miniature petit fours are arranged with deliberate spacing on a pristine white rectangular porcelain platter, resting on a premium grey veined marble surface. Each petit four boasts a flawless, high-gloss white chocolate mirror glaze, reflecting subtle ambient light. The glaze has a whisper of peach undertone from the fruit, creating a sophisticated ivory hue. A single, vibrant green micro mint leaf is meticulously placed on top of each petit four, providing a precise pop of color and natural contrast. The arrangement is organic and flowing, avoiding rigid lines or patterns, allowing abundant negative space on the platter to emphasize the individual artistry of each piece. The setting is ultra-minimalist, with dramatic professional lighting casting soft shadows, highlighting the architectural precision and delicate nature of the miniature desserts. A crisply folded white linen napkin sits to the side, enhancing the luxurious, restrained aesthetic. The focus is entirely on the exquisite details of the petit fours, showcasing their perfect form, glossy finish, and elegant simplicity.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve after dinner with espresso or a selection of fine teas.
Present on a multi-tiered stand or an elegant serving platter for a sophisticated presentation.
instructions: Prepare Pineapple-Mango Gelee inserts: Dice pineapple and mango into 5mm cubes. Combine with 30 grams sugar and lime juice in a small saucepan. Simmer gently for 5 minutes until fruit softens slightly. Bloom 3 gelatin sheets in cold water for 5 minutes. Squeeze excess water. Stir bloomed gelatin into warm fruit mixture until dissolved. Pour mixture into small silicone molds (e.g., 2.5cm spheres or small cubes). Freeze until solid, at least 2 hours.

Prepare Orgeat Mousse: Bloom 2 gelatin sheets in cold water. In a saucepan, combine 60 grams sugar and 30 ml water. Heat to 121°C. While syrup heats, whisk egg yolks in a stand mixer. Slowly pour hot sugar syrup into egg yolks, whisking until thick and pale (pâte à bombe). Fold in squeezed bloomed gelatin. Fold in orgeat syrup. In a separate bowl, whip heavy cream to soft peaks. Gently fold whipped cream into the orgeat mixture.

Assemble Petit Fours: Fill larger silicone molds (e.g., 4cm spheres or elegant shapes) halfway with orgeat mousse. Place one frozen pineapple-mango gelee insert into the center of each mousse-filled mold. Top with more orgeat mousse to fill the mold. Smooth the surface. Freeze completely, at least 4 hours or overnight.

Prepare White Chocolate Mirror Glaze: Bloom 4 gelatin sheets in cold water. In a heatproof bowl, combine white chocolate, glucose syrup, and condensed milk. In a saucepan, bring 75 ml water to a boil. Pour hot water over chocolate mixture. Let stand for 1 minute. Add squeezed bloomed gelatin. Stir gently until smooth and emulsified. Use an immersion blender to remove air bubbles, keeping the head submerged. Strain glaze for ultimate smoothness. Cool glaze to 32-35°C for optimal pouring.

Glaze and Garnish: Remove frozen petit fours from molds. Place on a wire rack set over a baking sheet to catch excess glaze. Pour mirror glaze evenly over each frozen petit four, ensuring full coverage. Let excess glaze drip off. Carefully transfer glazed petit fours to an elegant serving platter using an offset spatula. Garnish each petit four with one micro mint leaf. Serve immediately or keep refrigerated until serving.
notes: For best results, ensure all components are chilled or frozen to the correct temperature before assembly and glazing.
The mirror glaze temperature is crucial for a smooth, even finish.
traditional_techniques: Pâte à Bombe (French egg yolk foam base for mousse)

recipes.recipe_name: Pastis Semifreddo with Miso-Port Glaze and Oaxaca Crisp
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pastis Semifreddo rests elegantly on a large, pristine white designer plate, offering abundant negative space. The semifreddo, a pale, creamy rectangle with a smooth, firm texture, holds its shape perfectly. Beside it, a rich, glossy stream of amber-brown Miso-Port Glaze creates a fluid, organic line, catching the light with a subtle sheen. Scattered delicately are irregular, golden-brown Oaxaca cheese shards, thin and translucent, providing a contrasting crisp texture and visual lightness. The composition is minimalist yet impactful, showcasing precise execution and sophisticated restraint. The plate is set on a premium grey veined marble surface, accompanied by a precisely folded white linen napkin, under dramatic, focused lighting that creates soft shadows.
instructions: For the Pastis Semifreddo: Whisk egg yolks and 80g caster sugar in a heatproof bowl. Place over a bain-marie. Whisk continuously until mixture is pale, thick, and reaches 80°C. Remove from heat. Continue whisking until cool. Fold in pastis. In a separate bowl, whip heavy cream to soft peaks. Gently fold whipped cream into the cooled egg mixture. Pour into a lined loaf tin or individual molds. Freeze for at least 6 hours, or until firm.

For the Miso-Port Glaze: Combine white port, 50g caster sugar, and water in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer. Stir until sugar dissolves. Remove from heat. Whisk in dark miso until fully dissolved and smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve for a silky consistency. Cool to room temperature. The glaze will thicken slightly upon cooling.

For the Oaxaca Crisp: Gently melt butter in a non-stick pan over low heat. Add Oaxaca cheese, shredded or in small pieces. Sprinkle with a pinch of caster sugar. Cook slowly until the cheese melts and caramelizes, forming a thin, lacy crisp. Once golden brown and crisp, carefully remove from pan using an offset spatula. Place on parchment paper to cool. Break into organic, irregular shards once cooled and firm.

To Assemble: Remove semifreddo from freezer 10 minutes before serving. Slice or scoop individual portions onto chilled designer plates. Artfully drizzle a generous amount of Miso-Port Glaze beside the semifreddo. Arrange 2-3 Oaxaca cheese shards elegantly around the semifreddo. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Almond & Port Cantaloupe Tartlet
recipes.visual_description: A single elegant Smoked Almond & Port Cantaloupe Tartlet is centered on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The tartlet features a golden-brown, fluted pâte sablée shell holding a baked smoked almond frangipane. Vibrant orange cantaloupe spheres are neatly arranged atop the frangipane. A glossy, ruby-red port wine gel is drizzled over some cantaloupe pieces. Around the cantaloupe, a scattering of roughly chopped, glistening candied walnuts provides contrasting texture. A small, fresh green mint sprig rests delicately beside the cantaloupe. The plate exhibits moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, with the plate on a simple wooden table. A white cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the pastry's textures and colors.
instructions: Prepare Pâte Sablée: Combine flour, icing sugar, and salt. Rub in cold butter until crumbly. Add egg yolk; mix until dough forms. Do not overmix. Wrap dough; chill 30 minutes.

Preheat oven to 180°C. Roll out dough to 3 mm thick. Cut four circles to fit 10 cm tartlet molds. Press dough into molds. Prick bases with a fork. Line with parchment paper; fill with baking beans. Blind bake 15 minutes. Remove paper and beans.
Prepare Smoked Almond Frangipane: Finely grind smoked almonds. Cream softened butter and sugar until light. Beat in egg. Fold in ground almonds and flour.
Spoon frangipane into partially baked tartlet shells. Bake 15-20 minutes, or until golden and set. Let cool completely in molds.

Prepare Port Wine Gel: In a small saucepan, combine port wine, sugar, and agar-agar. Bring to a simmer, whisking constantly for 2 minutes. Pour into a shallow dish. Chill until set. Once set, cut into small cubes or blend until smooth gel.
Prepare Cantaloupe: Halve cantaloupe. Scoop out seeds. Using a melon baller or small knife, create small cantaloupe spheres or precisely cut small cubes.
Assemble Tartlets: Carefully remove cooled tartlet shells from molds. Place each tartlet on a serving plate. Arrange cantaloupe spheres/cubes neatly on top of the frangipane.
Spoon or pipe a small amount of port wine gel over the cantaloupe. Roughly chop candied walnuts. Sprinkle candied walnuts around the cantaloupe. Garnish each tartlet with a small fresh mint sprig.

recipes.recipe_name: Causa Rellena de Halibut con Chervil
recipes.visual_description: Four individual cylindrical causa rellena are presented neatly on clean white porcelain plates. Each causa is approximately 8 cm in diameter and 6 cm high, showcasing distinct, vibrant layers: a smooth, sunny yellow potato base and top, sandwiching a creamy, white halibut filling. The potato layers are perfectly smooth, indicating meticulous mashing. The halibut is flaked into irregular, tender chunks, providing textural contrast. A delicate sprinkle of bright green chopped chervil garnishes the top of each causa, alongside a thin slice of a hard-boiled egg and a few dark black olive rounds. The overall presentation is clean and precise, with moderate negative space on the plate. The setting features a simple wooden table surface and natural, even lighting, creating an inviting, casual bistro atmosphere. The entire plate is visible, maintaining focus on the dish's balanced composition.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as an individual appetizer or elegant finger food.
Often accompanied by a small side of aji sauce (e.g., huancaína or rocoto sauce) for dipping.
instructions: Boil potatoes until very tender. Peel and pass through a potato ricer while hot.
Mix riced potato with 30 ml lime juice, aji amarillo paste, 15 ml vegetable oil, and salt to taste. Knead until smooth and pliable. Set aside.
Poach halibut gently in lightly salted water or steam until cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Flake the halibut into small chunks.
In a bowl, combine flaked halibut, finely diced red onion, remaining 30 ml lime juice, mayonnaise, and half of the chopped chervil. Season with salt and pepper. Mix gently.
Line four 8 cm diameter ring molds with plastic wrap. Press a 2 cm layer of potato mixture evenly into the bottom of each mold.
Spread a layer of halibut mixture over the potato.
Top with another 2 cm layer of potato mixture, pressing gently to compact.
Refrigerate causa molds for at least 30 minutes to firm up.
To serve, carefully invert each mold onto a plate. Remove plastic wrap and ring mold.
Garnish each causa with a slice of hard-boiled egg, a few black olive slices, and remaining fresh chervil. Add a thin slice of aji limo if desired.
notes: Use yellow potatoes for authentic texture and color.
Adjust aji amarillo paste quantity to desired spice level.
traditional_techniques: Mashing potatoes for a smooth, pliable masa

recipes.recipe_name: Oxtail & Bone Marrow Conserva Bites
recipes.visual_description: A minimalist arrangement of 8-12 elegant canapés on a large, pale ceramic platter. Each canapé features a golden-brown, irregularly shaped fermented root crisp (approx. 4x4 cm) as its base. A compact, dark brown cube of slow-braised oxtail conserva (approx. 2x2 cm) sits neatly atop each crisp. A small, creamy-white dollop of roasted bone marrow is placed on the oxtail. A single, vibrant, thinly sliced pickled radish (translucent pink/red) adds a pop of color and tang. A delicate drizzle of green-tinted herbed oil glistens. The composition utilizes ample negative space. The platter rests on a light-colored, reclaimed wood surface. A simple, undyed linen napkin in natural beige is subtly placed to the side. Soft, natural daylight illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures and clean lines of each ingredient.
instructions: Season oxtail pieces with salt and pepper. Brown oxtail in a heavy pot over medium-high heat. Remove oxtail. Add onion, carrot, celery, garlic, bay leaf to pot. Sauté until lightly browned. Return oxtail to pot.
Deglaze with red wine (if using), scraping up browned bits. Pour in beef stock. Bring to a simmer. Cover and transfer to oven. Braise at 150°C for 3-4 hours, until oxtail is extremely tender.

Remove oxtail from pot. Strain braising liquid, reserving liquid and discarding solids. Shred oxtail meat, discarding bones and large fat pieces. Mix shredded meat with 50 ml of strained braising liquid. Press firmly into a small, shallow mould. Chill for at least 4 hours, or overnight, until firm.
Combine root vegetable pulp, rye flour, active sourdough starter, water, and salt. Mix until a shaggy dough forms. Cover and let rest at room temperature for 2-4 hours, until slightly bubbly.
Preheat oven to 160°C. Roll dough very thinly between two sheets of parchment paper. Cut into 4x4 cm squares. Place on a baking sheet. Bake for 15-20 minutes, until golden and crisp. Cool completely.

Bring white wine vinegar, 100 ml water, sugar, 5 g salt, peppercorns, and dill (if using) to a boil. Stir until sugar and salt dissolve. Remove from heat. Arrange thinly sliced radishes in a small heatproof jar. Pour hot pickling liquid over radishes. Cool to room temperature, then refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.

Preheat oven to 200°C. Place bone marrow bones on a baking sheet. Roast for 15-20 minutes, until marrow is soft and translucent. Scoop out the roasted marrow. Mash lightly with a fork, season with a pinch of salt.
Finely chop fresh Herbes de Provence leaves. Combine with olive oil in a small bowl.
Unmould the chilled oxtail conserva. Cut into neat 2x2 cm cubes (8-12 pieces total).

Arrange Fermented Root Crisps on a serving platter. Top each crisp with an Oxtail Conserva cube. Place a small dollop of roasted bone marrow on top of the oxtail. Drain pickled radishes and place one or two slices neatly on each canapé. Drizzle lightly with Herbed Oil. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pine Nut & Mascarpone Delice, Candied Prosciutto, Tomato-Vanilla Geleé
recipes.visual_description: The minimalist presentation centers on a large, round bone china platter on a white Carrara marble surface. Quenelles of creamy white mascarpone delice are artfully placed with abundant negative space. Irregular, golden-brown shards of candied prosciutto provide a striking textural contrast. Small, precise cubes of deep red, glistening tomato-vanilla geleé are scattered. A golden-hued pine nut crumble provides a base texture. A few vibrant green micro basil leaves are precisely positioned as the sole garnish. The entire platter is visible. Dramatic, focused lighting creates elegant shadows, highlighting the sophisticated simplicity and premium ingredients. The background is ultra-minimalist and unobtrusive.
instructions: Prepare Candied Prosciutto: Preheat oven to 160°C. Line baking sheet with parchment. Arrange prosciutto in single layer. Sprinkle with 15g granulated sugar. Bake 10-12 minutes until crisp and golden. Cool completely. Break into irregular shards.

Make Tomato-Vanilla Geleé: Combine tomato paste, 50ml water, 20g granulated sugar, and 1/4 scraped vanilla bean in small saucepan. Bring to simmer. Cook 5 minutes, stirring. Whisk in agar-agar and pinch of salt. Cook 1 minute, stirring constantly. Pour into shallow dish. Chill 2 hours until firm. Cut geleé into small, precise cubes.

Prepare Pine Nut Crumble: Toast pine nuts lightly in dry pan. Cool. In food processor, combine toasted pine nuts, 20g granulated sugar, cold butter, and pinch of salt. Pulse until crumbly. Do not overmix into a paste.
Whip Mascarpone Delice: In chilled bowl, combine mascarpone, heavy cream, powdered sugar, and remaining 1/4 scraped vanilla bean. Whip until soft peaks form. Do not overmix.

Assemble Platter: On a large, minimalist bone china platter, artfully arrange small quenelles of mascarpone delice. Scatter irregular shards of candied prosciutto around. Place small, glistening cubes of tomato-vanilla geleé. Sprinkle pine nut crumble generously. Garnish with a few delicate micro basil leaves. Serve immediately as a shareable snack.

recipes.recipe_name: Lebanese Seasonal Fruit & Ferment Salad
recipes.visual_description: Individual portions of vibrant fruit salad arranged naturally on a simple, handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy tone. Fruits are loosely piled, showcasing their natural shapes and colors. A natural palette of deep reds from berries and pomegranate, purples from figs and grapes, with hints of green from mint. The fruit scrap infusion provides a subtle sheen. Textures include juicy fruit, crunchy pomegranate arils, soft figs, and a sprinkle of crushed pistachios. Garnish with fresh, torn mint leaves and crushed pistachios. The plate rests on a light bamboo or reclaimed wood table. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is draped beside it. Soft, natural lighting. Minimalistic background with a hint of green foliage, maintaining an eco-conscious feel.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served as a refreshing dessert or a light snack.
Often accompanied by strong Lebanese coffee or mint tea.
Can be part of a larger mezze spread.

ingredients.name: Fruit scraps (berry tops, fig ends, grape stems, pomegranate membranes) for infusion
Honey or date molasses for infusion

instructions: Collect clean fruit scraps. Combine with water and 20ml honey/molasses in a small saucepan.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 10-15 minutes. Mash gently to extract flavors.
Strain liquid through a fine-mesh sieve. Press solids to extract all liquid. Discard solids. Let infusion cool completely.
Gently wash all fresh fruits. Quarter figs. Halve grapes. Deseed pomegranate.
Place all prepared fruits in a large mixing bowl.
Add orange blossom water, rose water, and remaining 30ml honey/molasses to the cooled fruit infusion. Stir well.
Pour dressing over the fruits.
Gently toss fruits to coat evenly. Add torn mint leaves. Toss again.
Cover and chill salad for at least 30 minutes before serving.
Spoon fruit salad onto individual ceramic plates. Garnish with crushed pistachios.
notes: Adjust sweetness of the fruit scrap infusion based on fruit ripeness and personal preference.
Best served chilled.
traditional_techniques: Minimalistic preparation to highlight natural ingredients

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Artichoke & Salami Brodo with Creamy Polenta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of hearty soup is presented in a deep, handcrafted cream-beige ceramic bowl. The rich, amber-colored broth cradles tender quartered artichoke hearts and savory diced salami. Creamy, soft polenta is gently spooned into the base, partially submerged. A vibrant swirl of verdant pesto oil floats on the surface, garnished with a light scattering of fresh, finely chopped parsley. The bowl rests on a light reclaimed wood table, accompanied by a simple, natural wood spoon. Soft natural light illuminates the dish, highlighting its rustic elegance and emphasizing the natural colors and textures of the ingredients. The background is clean and minimalist, allowing the dish to be the sole focus.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping
instructions: Dice salami into small cubes. Quarter artichoke hearts. Dice onion. Mince garlic.
Heat a large pot over medium heat. Add diced salami. Render fat until crispy. Remove salami; set aside. Keep rendered fat in pot.
Add diced onion to pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add vegetable broth, quartered artichoke hearts, and Parmesan rind (if using) to pot. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat. Cook for 15 minutes to allow flavors to meld. Remove Parmesan rind.
In a separate saucepan, prepare polenta according to package directions. Cook until creamy and smooth. Season with salt.

Ladle soup into individual bowls. Spoon a dollop of creamy polenta into each bowl. Top with reserved crispy salami. Swirl a generous amount of pesto into each serving. Garnish with fresh, chopped parsley. Serve immediately.
notes: Use homemade fermented vegetable broth for deeper flavor and zero-waste.
Ensure chicken (salami in this case) is cooked thoroughly for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Kudzu & Fermented Cabbage Salad with Jasmine Tea-Lime Dressing
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of the salad is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone, centered with ample white space. The arrangement is organic and flowing, showcasing the natural textures and colors of the ingredients. Thinly sliced, translucent kudzu root forms a delicate base, layered with vibrant green shredded fermented cabbage and bright orange julienned carrots. Scattered amongst these are crisp half-moon cucumber slices, thin strips of ruby red bell pepper, and diagonally cut spring onion rings. Fresh green coriander and mint leaves are gently folded in, adding bursts of verdant color. The entire composition is lightly coated with a translucent, pale amber jasmine tea-lime dressing, which glistens subtly. A scattering of roughly chopped roasted peanuts adds a contrasting texture and a warm, earthy hue. The presentation is clean and unfussy, emphasizing the purity of the plant-based components. The plate rests on a light reclaimed wood table surface, revealing its natural grain. Beside the plate, a pair of simple bamboo chopsticks and a small, undyed linen napkin in natural beige are placed. The background is minimalist, with soft natural light illuminating the dish, and a hint of a leafy green plant subtly blurred in the distance, reinforcing the eco-conscious theme. The overall scene conveys a sense of calm, natural beauty and sustainable dining.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a refreshing complement to spicier Thai dishes.
Offer small bowls of additional lime wedges, fresh chilies, or roasted peanuts for personalized seasoning.
Traditionally, salads like this might be served alongside sticky rice.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Cabbage: In a large bowl, combine shredded cabbage, julienned carrots, and salt. Massage vigorously for 5-10 minutes until vegetables release water. Pack tightly into a clean glass jar. Press down to remove air bubbles. Ensure vegetables are submerged in brine. If not, add salted water (1 tsp salt per 250ml water) to cover. Seal with an airlock lid or cover loosely. Ferment at room temperature (20-24°C) for 3-5 days. Store in refrigerator.
Prepare Kudzu: Peel kudzu root. Thinly slice or julienne. Blanch in boiling water for 1-2 minutes until slightly tender-crisp. Immediately transfer to an ice bath. Drain well and pat dry.

Prepare Dressing: In a small bowl, whisk cooled jasmine tea, lime juice, palm sugar, soy sauce, dissolved vegemite, red pepper flakes, minced garlic, and grated ginger. Whisk until sugar dissolves. Taste and adjust sweetness, sourness, and spice.
Assemble Salad: In a large mixing bowl, combine blanched kudzu, drained fermented cabbage, cucumber, red bell pepper, spring onions, fresh coriander, and fresh mint.
Dress and Serve: Pour dressing over salad. Toss gently to combine all components. Garnish with chopped roasted peanuts. Serve immediately.
notes: This recipe embraces zero-waste by utilizing full vegetable components and promoting fermentation as a preservation method.
Adjust fermentation time for cabbage based on desired tanginess and ambient temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Galaktoboureko with Lotus Seed Cream
recipes.visual_description: A single, rectangular slice of Galaktoboureko is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The top crust is a rich, golden-brown, showcasing the crisp, delicate layers of baked phyllo pastry. A light dusting of ground cinnamon adorns the surface. The side of the slice reveals the creamy, off-white lotus seed custard layer nestled between the flaky phyllo. The custard has a smooth, tender texture, glistening slightly from the absorbed syrup. The edges of the phyllo are crisp and well-defined, indicating proper scoring and baking. The plate is positioned on a simple wooden table surface. A folded white cotton napkin rests beside the plate. In the background, slightly out of focus, is a small, traditional Greek coffee cup or a clear glass of water, enhancing the authentic Greek casual dining atmosphere. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors without harsh shadows.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve at room temperature or slightly warm.
Often accompanied by a small, strong Greek coffee.
Traditionally enjoyed as a dessert after a meal or with afternoon coffee.
instructions: Soak lotus seeds in hot water for 4 hours. Drain. Cook lotus seeds in fresh water until tender, about 30 minutes. Drain and puree until smooth. Set aside.
Prepare the syrup: Combine 250 ml water, 250 g sugar, and lemon zest in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil. Simmer for 5 minutes. Remove from heat. Let cool completely.
Prepare the custard: In a medium saucepan, whisk together 750 ml milk, 200 g sugar, 50 g flour, and a pinch of salt. Cook over medium heat, whisking constantly, until thickened. Remove from heat.

In a separate bowl, whisk the 3 eggs. Gradually temper eggs into the hot milk mixture, whisking constantly. Return pan to low heat. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring, until custard is very thick. Remove from heat.
Stir in pureed lotus seeds and vanilla extract into the custard. Set aside to cool slightly.
Preheat oven to 175°C. Lightly butter a 20x30 cm baking dish.
Lay 6 sheets of phyllo pastry in the prepared dish, brushing each sheet generously with melted butter. Allow excess phyllo to hang over the edges.
Pour the warm lotus seed custard evenly over the phyllo base. Spread smoothly.
Fold the overhanging phyllo edges over the custard. Cover the custard with the remaining 6 phyllo sheets, brushing each with melted butter.
Trim any excess phyllo. Score the top layers of phyllo into 4 equal slices, cutting only through the top layers, not the custard.
Bake for 45-55 minutes, or until the phyllo is golden brown and puffed.
Immediately remove the hot galaktoboureko from the oven. Slowly pour the cooled syrup evenly over the entire hot pastry. The syrup will sizzle and absorb.
Let the galaktoboureko cool completely at room temperature for at least 2 hours, preferably longer, before serving. This allows the syrup to fully absorb and the custard to set.
notes: Ensure the syrup is cold and the pastry is hot for best absorption.
Allow ample cooling time for the custard to set properly and flavors to meld.
Phyllo pastry can dry out quickly; keep unworked sheets covered with a damp cloth.

recipes.recipe_name: Cherry Marzipan Tartlets
recipes.visual_description: A single, round cherry marzipan tartlet rests on a simple, off-white ceramic plate with a slightly rustic edge. The tartlet features a golden-brown, flaky pastry crust holding a pale, slightly puffed marzipan filling. Whole pitted cherries are nestled into the filling, some showing gentle caramelization from baking, their deep red color contrasting with the light filling. A generous, soft dollop of freshly whipped vanilla cream sits beside the tartlet, its creamy white texture inviting. The plate is placed on a warm, well-used wooden dining table, suggesting a cozy home kitchen. A casually folded, light-colored cloth napkin lies nearby. The scene is bathed in soft, inviting light, highlighting the comforting textures and natural colors of the homemade dessert.
instructions: Prepare the pastry dough. Sift flour, icing sugar, and salt into a large bowl.
Add diced cold butter. Rub butter into flour mixture with fingertips until it resembles breadcrumbs.
Add egg yolk and 1-2 tablespoons cold water. Mix until dough comes together. Do not overmix.
Form dough into a disc. Wrap in cling film. Chill for 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Roll out chilled dough on a lightly floured surface. Cut out four circles to fit your tartlet tins.
Press dough into four 10cm tartlet tins. Trim edges. Prick bases with a fork.
Prepare the marzipan filling. In a bowl, cream softened butter and granulated sugar until light.
Crumble marzipan into the butter mixture. Beat until well combined.
Beat in the egg and vanilla extract until smooth.
Divide marzipan filling evenly among the four tartlet shells.
Arrange pitted cherries on top of the marzipan filling in each tartlet.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until pastry is golden and filling is set and lightly browned.
Remove from oven. Let tartlets cool completely in their tins on a wire rack.
Prepare the vanilla cream. In a cold bowl, whip heavy cream with 1-2 tablespoons of icing sugar (to taste) and a dash of vanilla extract until soft peaks form.
Carefully remove cooled tartlets from tins. Serve each tartlet with a generous dollop of vanilla cream.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearts of Palm and Seafood Salad
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing vibrant colors and diverse textures. Sliced hearts of palm, cut into neat rounds, form the base. Interspersed are plump, whole poached shrimp, delicate flakes of white fish, and small, tender cockle meats. Diced red bell pepper, finely diced red onion, halved cherry tomatoes, and diced cucumber add bursts of red, white, and green. Fresh chopped cilantro is generously scattered throughout, providing a verdant contrast. The Fermented Black Bean & Lime Vinaigrette lightly coats all ingredients, creating a subtle sheen. The arrangement is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. A few fresh cilantro sprigs and a lime wedge garnish the plate.
