The setting features a simple wooden table and a folded cotton napkin, with traditional flatware placed beside the plate, conveying a casual, authentic Brazilian dining experience.

ingredients.name: white fish fillet (e.g., cod or tilapia), skinless

instructions: Prepare seafood: Steam cockles until shells open, about 3-5 minutes. Discard any unopened cockles. Remove cockle meat from shells.
Poach shrimp: Bring a small pot of water to a gentle simmer. Add shrimp. Cook for 2-3 minutes until pink and opaque. Drain immediately.
Poach fish: In the same simmering water, add fish fillet. Cook for 5-7 minutes until opaque and flakes easily. Remove, let cool, then gently flake into bite-sized pieces.
Prepare vinaigrette: In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, lime juice, minced fermented black beans, minced garlic, salt, pepper, and red pepper flakes (if using).
Assemble salad: In a large bowl, combine sliced hearts of palm, diced red bell pepper, finely diced red onion, halved cherry tomatoes, diced cucumber, and chopped cilantro.
Add seafood: Gently add cooked shrimp, flaked fish, and cockle meat to the vegetable mixture.
Dress and serve: Pour vinaigrette over salad ingredients. Toss gently to coat. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Liver Pâté with Fermented Cactus Relish
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegantly plated starter portion features a smooth, creamy quenelle of light brown lamb liver pâté, centrally placed. Adorning the pâté is a small mound of vibrant green, translucent diced fermented cactus relish, offering a bright textural contrast. Alongside, several irregularly shaped, puffed crispy rice wafers stand upright, showcasing their airy, brittle texture and off-white hue. The dish rests on a handcrafted ceramic plate in a natural cream or beige tone, highlighting the ingredients' pure colors. The setting is a light bamboo or reclaimed wood table surface, complemented by an undyed linen napkin in natural beige. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, emphasizing the minimalist, ingredient-focused presentation.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Cactus Relish: Clean cactus paddles. Remove spines. Dice cactus into 5mm cubes. Blanch cactus cubes in boiling water for 2 minutes. Drain. Rinse under cold water. Combine cactus, vinegar, sugar, and a pinch of salt with 50ml water in a clean jar. Seal jar. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days. Refrigerate after fermentation.

Prepare Crispy Rice Wafers: Cook rice in 200ml water until tender. Spread cooked rice thinly and evenly on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Bake at 120°C for 1.5-2 hours until completely dry and brittle. Heat olive oil for deep frying to 180°C. Deep fry dried rice until puffed and crisp. Drain on paper towels. Lightly salt.

Prepare Lamb Liver Pâté: Clean lamb liver. Remove any membranes or sinew. Dice liver into 2cm pieces. Melt 50g butter in a pan over medium heat. Sauté diced shallots for 3 minutes until soft. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

Increase heat to medium-high. Add diced liver to the pan. Sear for 2-3 minutes per side until browned but still slightly pink inside. Do not overcook. Deglaze the pan with 50ml pork stock. Simmer for 1 minute.

Transfer liver mixture to a food processor. Add remaining 50g butter and remaining 100ml pork stock. Process until smooth and creamy. Season with salt and pepper to taste. For extra smoothness, pass the pâté through a fine sieve. Press pâté into small ramekins or a terrine mold. Chill for at least 2 hours until firm.

Assemble the Dish: Spoon chilled pâté onto individual starter plates. Top the pâté with a generous spoonful of fermented cactus relish. Arrange several crispy rice wafers alongside the pâté. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley or chives. Serve immediately.
notes: This recipe embraces a zero-waste philosophy by utilizing often-overlooked offal and transforming ingredients through fermentation and preservation. It highlights seasonal ingredients and minimalistic plating.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Yogurt & Smoked Tofu Delight
recipes.visual_description: A single, pristine slice of the cake rests on a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic plate in a natural cream tone. The slice distinctly reveals two layers: a creamy, off-white top layer, smooth and firm, indicating the yogurt and tofu blend, and a contrasting, slightly darker, textured base of the oat and walnut crumble. On the surface of the cake slice, two to three thin, translucent, pale yellow pear wedges are arranged naturally, slightly overlapping. The whole cake, on a simple reclaimed wood cake stand, is subtly blurred in the soft-focus background, showcasing its organic, unadorned form. The setting features a light-colored, matte stone surface. A natural, undyed linen napkin in beige is folded simply to the side. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, creating gentle shadows that highlight textures. The background is minimalist, with a hint of green foliage blurred to suggest a natural environment. The composition is clean and uncluttered, emphasizing the inherent beauty of the ingredients.
instructions: Prepare a 15 cm springform pan. Line the base with parchment paper.
For the crust, combine rolled oats, walnuts, and maple syrup in a food processor. Process until a coarse, sticky mixture forms.
Press the oat mixture evenly into the base of the prepared springform pan. Chill in the refrigerator for 30 minutes.
For the filling, combine yogurt cheese, smoked tofu, Chinese sweet bean paste, vanilla extract, lemon zest, and a pinch of salt in a clean food processor. Process until completely smooth and creamy.
Pour the creamy filling over the chilled crust in the springform pan. Gently tap the pan to release any air bubbles. Smooth the top with a spatula.
Cover the cake loosely with plastic wrap. Chill in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, until firm.
For the poached pears, peel and core the pears. Cut them into thin, even wedges. Place pear wedges in a small saucepan.

Pour white port over the pears. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium-low heat. Cook for 8-10 minutes, or until pears are tender but still hold their shape. Remove from heat and let cool in the liquid.
To serve, carefully remove the cake from the springform pan. Slice the cake into individual portions.
Arrange a few cooled poached pear wedges artistically on top of each cake slice. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Chili Shrimp with Charred Scallions
recipes.visual_description: An individual portion is presented on a round, handcrafted, cream-colored ceramic plate, emphasizing minimalistic elegance and natural textures. The vibrant orange-red chili shrimp, with plump, curled shrimp, is centrally placed. Alongside, charred scallion whites display their dark, smoky char contrasting with bright green tips. Thinly sliced, crisp quick-pickled vegetables (carrot, cucumber, daikon) are artfully arranged, adding pops of fresh color and a slight tang. The plating respects ample white space, showcasing the inherent beauty of each ingredient. Garnished simply with fresh red chili slices and finely julienned scallion greens. The dish rests on a light, natural bamboo or reclaimed wood table. A small, white ceramic rice bowl and dark wooden chopsticks are placed beside. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige completes the setting. Soft, natural daylight illuminates the scene, with a subtle, out-of-focus green plant in the background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice.
Offer a side of fresh herbs like cilantro or Thai basil.

ingredients.name: Large raw shrimp, peeled, deveined, tails on
Lemongrass, tender inner part, thinly sliced

instructions: Prepare Quick Fermented Chili Paste: Blend 100g fresh red chilies, 20g garlic, 5g salt, and 100ml filtered water until smooth. Transfer to a clean jar. Cover loosely. Let ferment at room temperature for 24-48 hours. Refrigerate after. (Alternatively, use 60g store-bought fermented chili sauce or chili jam).

Prepare Quick Pickled Vegetables: Thinly slice cucumber, carrot, and daikon. In a small saucepan, combine rice vinegar, 30g sugar, and 5g salt. Heat until sugar and salt dissolve. Pour hot brine over sliced vegetables. Chill for at least 30 minutes.
Prepare Shrimp: Pat shrimp dry with paper towels.

Char Scallions: Heat a dry cast-iron pan or grill pan over high heat. Add whole scallions. Char until softened and slightly blackened in spots, about 2-3 minutes per side. Remove. Reserve some whole for plating. Slice some green parts thinly for garnish.
Cook Shrimp Mixture: Heat vegetable oil in a wok or large frying pan over medium-high heat. Add sliced shallots, sliced lemongrass, and torn kaffir lime leaves. Sauté until fragrant, about 1 minute.

Add 60g of the prepared quick fermented chili paste (or store-bought alternative) to the pan. Stir-fry for 1 minute until aromatic. Add shrimp. Cook until shrimp turn pink and opaque, about 2-3 minutes.
Stir in light coconut milk, fish sauce, palm sugar, and fresh lime juice. Simmer gently for 2 minutes, allowing sauce to slightly thicken.

Assemble Dish: Serve the chili shrimp mixture immediately. Arrange charred scallions and quick-pickled vegetables alongside. Garnish with fresh sliced red chilies and thinly sliced scallion greens. Serve with steamed jasmine rice.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by utilizing whole scallions (charred whites, green garnish) and promoting quick fermentation/preservation methods for flavor and longevity.
Adjust chili paste quantity to desired spice level.
For plant-forward variation, substitute shrimp with pan-seared firm tofu or king oyster mushrooms.
traditional_techniques: Balancing Thai flavors (sweet, sour, salty, spicy)
Preparation of a chili paste (Prik Pao style)
Quick pickling for flavor and preservation

recipes.recipe_name: Crispy Cheese Curd Fritters with Tangy Coconut Dip
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of crispy cheese curd fritters is casually arranged on a simple, round ceramic plate with a slight beige hue. Four golden-brown fritters, approximately 6 cm in diameter and 2 cm thick, are stacked loosely in the center, showcasing their irregular, rustic edges. Their surfaces are visibly crisp and speckled with tiny bits of green onion. A small, white ceramic ramekin, about 8 cm in diameter, sits beside the fritters, holding a clear, amber-colored coconut vinegar dipping sauce with visible flecks of minced garlic and red chili slices. The plate rests on a well-worn, light brown wooden dining table. A casually folded, off-white linen napkin is placed nearby. Warm, soft kitchen light illuminates the scene, creating a comforting, inviting atmosphere typical of a home kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a main course or substantial snack.
Traditionally enjoyed with a side of steamed rice, though optional here.
instructions: Drain cheese curds. Pat dry using paper towels.
In a large bowl, combine cheese curds, flour, egg, chopped green onions, garlic powder, salt, and black pepper. Mix gently until just combined. Do not overmix.
Form the mixture into 12-16 small, round patties, about 2 cm thick.
Heat vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat.
Place patties in the hot oil. Do not overcrowd the pan. Cook in batches if necessary.
Fry patties for 3-4 minutes per side. Fry until golden brown and crispy.
Transfer cooked patties to a wire rack. Let excess oil drain.
For the dip, combine coconut vinegar, soy sauce, sugar, minced garlic, sliced chili (if using), and water in a small bowl. Stir until sugar dissolves.
Serve fritters hot with the tangy coconut dip.
notes: Ensure cheese curds are well-drained for crispy fritters.
Adjust chili in dip to taste.

recipes.recipe_name: Warm Chorizo, Brown Rice, and Roasted Chili Bowl
recipes.visual_description: A single generous starter portion is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl. The warm chorizo, brown rice, and roasted chili bowl fills the bowl naturally, showcasing a hearty, comforting presentation. Diced, crisped chorizo pieces are interspersed with fluffy brown rice and tender black beans. Small, vibrant red pieces of roasted chili add color and char. The dish is simply garnished with fresh, roughly chopped bright green cilantro. Textures vary: crisp chorizo, chewy rice, soft beans. Colors are earthy and warm. The bowl sits on a well-worn wooden dining table, suggesting a homely family kitchen. A simple metal spoon rests on a plain cloth napkin. Warm kitchen lighting illuminates the cozy, lived-in scene. The entire bowl is visible, full but not overflowing.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas on the side for scooping
Offer a small bowl of salsa verde or hot sauce
instructions: Rinse 200g brown rice. Combine with 400ml water in a pot. Bring to boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer 40-45 minutes until tender. Let stand 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.

Halve 2 medium red chilies lengthwise. Remove seeds. Lightly coat with 1 tablespoon olive oil. Roast in oven at 200°C (390°F) for 15-20 minutes until softened and slightly charred. Let cool slightly. Dice into small pieces.

Dice 200g chorizo into 1cm cubes. Heat a large skillet over medium heat. Add chorizo. Cook 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until crispy and fat is rendered. Remove chorizo with a slotted spoon. Drain excess fat, leaving 1-2 tablespoons in skillet.

Dice 1 medium onion. Mince 2 cloves garlic. Add onion to skillet with chorizo fat. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened. Add garlic, 1 teaspoon smoked paprika, and 0.5 teaspoon cumin. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Drain and rinse 1 x 400g can black beans. Add cooked brown rice, black beans, and diced roasted chili to skillet. Stir to combine. Cook 3-5 minutes until heated through.
Stir in cooked chorizo. Squeeze juice of 1 lime over mixture. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Roughly chop 30g fresh cilantro. Stir in half the cilantro.
Ladle warm mixture into bowls. Garnish with remaining fresh cilantro.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Fried Mackerel with Cabbage Salad and Sautéed Maitake
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-fried mackerel is casually plated on a rustic, off-white ceramic plate. The mackerel fillet, golden-brown and crispy-skinned, rests at the center, its flaky white flesh peeking through. Beside it, a generous mound of vibrant green and white shredded cabbage salad, mixed with thinly sliced red onion and fresh green dill, is piled naturally. Sautéed maitake mushrooms, torn into irregular, earthy-brown pieces, are loosely scattered around the fish and salad. A bright yellow lemon wedge sits near the mackerel. The dish is presented on a well-used wooden dining table, alongside a simple metal fork and knife. Warm, natural light illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, lived-in family kitchen atmosphere. No fanning of fish, just whole pieces.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of traditional Turkish tea or a glass of refreshing ayran (yogurt drink).
Offer additional lemon wedges for guests to squeeze over their fish.
Serve with fresh, crusty Turkish bread (ekmek) to soak up any pan juices.
instructions: Thinly slice cabbage. Place in a large bowl.
Thinly slice red onion. Add to cabbage.
Squeeze half lemon juice into a small bowl. Add 2 tablespoons olive oil, salt, and pepper. Whisk well.
Pour dressing over cabbage and onion. Add chopped fresh dill. Toss well to combine. Set aside.
Tear maitake mushrooms into bite-sized pieces.
Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add maitake mushrooms. Cook until golden and tender, about 5-7 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Remove from pan and set aside.
Pat mackerel fillets dry with paper towels. Season skin and flesh generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 2 tablespoons fresh olive oil in the same pan over medium-high heat. Place mackerel fillets skin-side down in the hot pan. Cook for 3-4 minutes until the skin is crispy and golden brown.

Flip the mackerel fillets. Cook for another 2-3 minutes until the fish is cooked through and flakes easily. Ensure an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) if cooking chicken, though fish cooks faster.

To serve, place one mackerel fillet on each plate. Serve alongside a generous portion of the prepared cabbage salad and sautéed maitake mushrooms. Garnish with a fresh lemon wedge and a sprinkle of red pepper flakes if desired.
notes: Ensure mackerel is very fresh for best flavor. Ask your fishmonger to fillet it for you if possible.

recipes.recipe_name: Kulfi Opera Cake Monoportion
recipes.visual_description: A single, rectangular Kulfi Opera Cake, meticulously constructed with distinct, clean horizontal layers. The top is coated in a mirror-like, glossy dark chocolate glaze, reflecting light. Below the glaze, a thin layer of deep brown chocolate ganache is visible. Beneath, alternating layers of light green pistachio-infused joconde biscuit and pale, creamy Kulfi buttercream (infused with cardamom and pistachio) are precisely stacked, creating a striking striped effect. The cake is positioned off-center on an elegant, pristine white porcelain dessert plate with a subtle gold rim. Abundant negative space surrounds the cake. A single, delicate gold-dusted chocolate curl or a few finely chopped pistachios are placed precisely beside the cake as a garnish. The overall presentation is minimalist, showcasing the architectural precision and rich, sophisticated colors of the cake. Lighting is dramatic, creating subtle shadows and highlighting the glaze's sheen. The background is a clean white marble surface, accentuating the fine-dining aesthetic.
instructions: Prepare Pistachio Joconde Biscuit:
Preheat oven to 190°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Whip egg whites with granulated sugar to stiff peaks. Set aside.
In a separate bowl, whisk egg yolks, almond flour, and icing sugar until light and fluffy. Add all-purpose flour, melted butter, and pistachio paste. Mix until combined.
Gently fold the whipped egg whites into the almond mixture in three additions.
Spread batter evenly onto the prepared baking sheet. Bake for 10-12 minutes, until golden and springy. Cool completely. Trim edges. Cut into 8 rectangles (approx. 4x8 cm for individual portions).
Prepare Saffron Cardamom Syrup:
Combine water, granulated sugar, crushed cardamom pods, and saffron threads in a small saucepan.
Bring to a simmer, stirring until sugar dissolves. Remove from heat. Let steep for 15 minutes. Strain and cool.
Prepare Dark Chocolate Ganache:
Heat heavy cream until simmering. Pour over chopped dark chocolate. Let sit for 1 minute, then whisk until smooth.
Stir in cubed butter until fully incorporated and ganache is glossy. Cool to room temperature until spreadable.
Prepare Kulfi Buttercream:
In a small saucepan, combine granulated sugar and water. Heat until sugar dissolves and syrup reaches 118°C (soft ball stage).
While syrup heats, whisk egg yolks until pale. Slowly pour hot sugar syrup into egg yolks in a steady stream, whisking continuously until mixture is thick and cooled (pâte à bombe).
Gradually add softened butter, piece by piece, whisking until buttercream is light and fluffy. Do not curdle. Mix in vanilla sugar, ground cardamom, and pistachio paste.
Assemble Opera Cakes:
Place one Joconde biscuit rectangle on a cooling rack over a tray. Brush generously with saffron cardamom syrup.
Spread a thin, even layer of Kulfi buttercream over the biscuit.
Place a second biscuit rectangle on top. Brush generously with syrup.
Spread a thin, even layer of dark chocolate ganache over the second biscuit.
Repeat this layering for each of the 4 individual cakes.
Chill assembled cakes for at least 30 minutes to firm up layers.
Prepare Chocolate Glaze:
Melt dark chocolate and butter together gently over a bain-marie or in microwave. Stir until smooth. Add neutral glazing gel if using, for extra shine.
Ensure glaze is warm and fluid, but not hot (around 35-40°C).
Glaze Cakes:
Place chilled cakes on a clean cooling rack. Pour chocolate glaze over each cake, ensuring full coverage and smooth finish. Let excess drip off.
Carefully transfer glazed cakes to a clean plate using an offset spatula. Chill until glaze is set.
Serve immediately or keep refrigerated. Allow to come to room temperature for 10-15 minutes before serving for best texture.
notes: Ensure all components are at the correct temperature for assembly to achieve clean, distinct layers.
Chill layers thoroughly between steps to prevent mixing.
For the buttercream, ensure the butter is soft but not melted, and the pâte à bombe is cooled before incorporating butter to prevent a greasy or curdled texture.
The chocolate glaze should be fluid enough to pour, but not too hot, to prevent melting the layers below.

recipes.recipe_name: Marsala, Sherry, and Armagnac Layer Cake
recipes.visual_description: An elegant slice of Marsala, Sherry, and Armagnac Layer Cake stands on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The slice reveals distinct, clean layers: dark, coffee-soaked cocoa sponge alternating with pale, creamy mascarpone filling. The sponge is subtly moist, the cream smooth and airy. The top is generously dusted with unsweetened cocoa powder, creating a rich, matte brown contrast. Delicate dark chocolate shavings are scattered lightly over the cocoa, adding sheen and texture. The color palette features inviting browns and creams. The cake is presented on a simple wooden table surface, with a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even light highlights the cake's refined textures. A full, uncut cake rests on a simple cake stand in the background, subtly out of focus, reinforcing a professional, casual bistro ambiance.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Line a 20x20 cm square pan with parchment paper.
Beat eggs and 60g granulated sugar until pale and thick.
Sift flour and 15g cocoa powder together. Gently fold dry ingredients into egg mixture.
Pour batter into prepared pan. Bake 12-15 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean. Cool completely. Cut cake into two equal rectangles.
Combine espresso, Marsala, Cream Sherry, and Armagnac in a bowl. Mix well.
Whisk egg yolks and 50g granulated sugar in a heatproof bowl over a simmering pot of water until pale and thick, about 5 minutes. Remove from heat. Whisk until cool.
Gently fold mascarpone cheese and vanilla extract into the yolk mixture until smooth.
In a separate bowl, whip cold heavy cream to soft peaks. Fold whipped cream into mascarpone mixture.
Place one sponge cake layer on a serving plate. Brush generously with half of the soaking syrup.
Spread half of the mascarpone cream evenly over the sponge.
Place the second sponge layer on top. Brush with remaining syrup.
Spread remaining mascarpone cream over the top and sides.
Refrigerate cake for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight, to set.
Just before serving, dust generously with cocoa powder. Garnish with dark chocolate shavings. Slice into 4 individual portions.

recipes.recipe_name: Larb Pla Tuna (Spicy Tuna Salad)
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Larb Pla Tuna is presented in a shallow, white porcelain bowl, positioned slightly off-center on a simple wooden table. The minced, lightly seared tuna, mixed with finely sliced shallots, chopped spring onions, and vibrant green herbs, creates a textured, colorful mound. Red chili flakes and toasted rice powder flecks are visible, adding depth. A generous portion of sticky rice, traditionally served in a small woven bamboo basket, sits beside the bowl. Fresh, crisp accompaniments like bright green cabbage wedges, thin cucumber slices, and long beans are neatly arranged on the side, offering a refreshing contrast. The scene is illuminated by natural, even lighting, highlighting the freshness and authentic Thai flavors. A cotton napkin is folded beside the plate, completing the casual bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with sticky rice (khao niao) or jasmine rice.
Accompany with fresh raw vegetables like cabbage, long beans, and cucumber.
Eat communally, sharing dishes among diners.
instructions: Rinse rice thoroughly. Cook according to package instructions. For sticky rice, soak for 4 hours, then steam.
Pat tuna dry. Cut tuna into small, uniform cubes.
Heat vegetable oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Sear tuna cubes quickly, about 30 seconds per side. Tuna should be mostly raw in the center. Remove from heat.
Let tuna cool slightly. Lightly flake the seared tuna into smaller pieces with a fork.
In a large mixing bowl, combine flaked tuna, lime juice, fish sauce, toasted rice powder, thinly sliced shallots, chopped spring onions, dried chili flakes, and sugar.
Mix gently until all ingredients are well combined.
Taste and adjust seasoning. Add more lime, fish sauce, chili, or sugar as desired.
Just before serving, fold in fresh mint leaves and chopped coriander. Mix lightly.
Serve Larb Pla Tuna immediately with cooked rice and a side of fresh cabbage wedges, cucumber slices, and long beans.
notes: Toasted rice powder (khao khua) is essential for authentic larb flavor and texture.
Adjust chili flakes to your preferred spice level.
Fresh herbs are key; use them generously.
traditional_techniques: Balancing the four fundamental Thai flavors: spicy, sour, salty, sweet.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Oat & Ruby Port Pear Cake
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegantly cut slice of Fermented Oat & Ruby Port Pear Cake rests on a matte, unglazed ceramic plate in a warm cream tone. The cake exhibits a rustic, wholesome texture from the oat flour, with visible specks of dark brown sugar. Thin slices of tender, pale yellow pear are artfully arranged on top of the cake, some peeking through the golden-brown crust. A glistening, deep ruby-red reduction made from ruby port is drizzled sparingly over the slice, pooling slightly at its base. The plating emphasizes negative space, allowing the cake's natural beauty to shine. In the soft-focused background, the remaining whole cake, round and golden-brown, sits on a simple wooden cake stand, hinting at its complete form. The table surface is light, reclaimed wood. A folded undyed linen napkin and a single, small, fresh sprig of thyme are placed subtly beside the plate, adding a touch of natural color without distraction. Natural, diffused light illuminates the scene, highlighting the cake's textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a dollop of unsweetened vegan oat or coconut cream.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease and flour a 20cm round cake tin.
Combine oat milk and apple cider vinegar in a bowl. Let stand 10 minutes to curdle and ferment slightly.
Process 200g rolled oats into fine flour using a blender or food processor.
In a large bowl, whisk together oat flour, 150g brown sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt.
Peel and core pears. Cut two pears into 1cm cubes. Reserve one pear for slicing.
In a saucepan, combine 50ml ruby port and 50g brown sugar. Add pear cubes. Simmer 5 minutes until slightly softened. Strain pears, reserving liquid.
Add melted vegan butter, vanilla extract, and fermented oat milk to the dry ingredients. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Gently fold in the cooked pear cubes.
Pour batter into prepared cake tin. Smooth the top.
Thinly slice the remaining pear. Arrange slices decoratively on top of the cake batter.
Bake for 35-40 minutes, or until a skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.

While cake bakes, combine remaining 100ml ruby port with the reserved pear liquid in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat and cook until liquid thickens into a syrup. This is the port reduction.
Remove cake from oven. Let cool in the tin for 10 minutes before transferring to a wire rack.
Once cool, drizzle port reduction over the cake before serving.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by using pear cores and peels to enrich the port reduction, though this step is optional.
The 'fermented oat milk' is a quick method using apple cider vinegar to create a buttermilk-like texture and tang, aiding in leavening and flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Japanese Peach Parfait with White Chocolate Cream
recipes.visual_description: A single Japanese Peach Parfait is elegantly presented in a tall, clear stemmed glass. Distinct layers are visible through the glass: a smooth, creamy white layer of white chocolate infused pastry cream, followed by vibrant, pale orange cubes of fresh diced peach, and then a rich, deep reddish-brown layer of koshi an (sweet red bean paste). The layers are clean and defined, creating a striking visual contrast. The top is crowned with another dollop of white chocolate cream, garnished with a single, crisp green mint leaf placed delicately off-center. The parfait sits on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, offering moderate negative space around the base of the glass. A folded cotton napkin rests beside the plate. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple wooden table surface and natural, even lighting that highlights the dessert's fresh colors and textures. This clean, approachable presentation showcases the dessert's refined simplicity.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with a small, delicate Japanese tea spoon for ease of layering.
Can be accompanied by a small cup of sencha green tea to balance the sweetness.
instructions: Prepare pastry cream: Whisk egg yolks, sugar, and cornstarch in a bowl until pale.
Heat milk in a saucepan until simmering. Slowly pour hot milk into egg mixture, whisking constantly.
Return mixture to saucepan. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until thickened and bubbling. Cook for 1 minute more.
Remove from heat. Stir in vanilla extract. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean bowl.
Stir white chocolate liqueur into the warm pastry cream. Cover surface directly with plastic wrap to prevent a skin. Chill completely, at least 2 hours.
Peel, pit, and dice peaches into small, uniform cubes.
To assemble parfaits: Spoon a layer of koshi an into the bottom of four clear stemmed glasses.
Add a layer of diced peaches over the koshi an.
Spoon a generous layer of chilled white chocolate pastry cream over the peaches.
Repeat layers: koshi an, peaches, and then white chocolate pastry cream, until glasses are full.
Garnish each parfait with a fresh mint sprig.
notes: Ensure pastry cream is fully chilled before assembly for best texture and defined layers.
Use very ripe, fragrant peaches for optimal flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Kefir & Red Date Panna Cotta with Blueberry Essence
recipes.visual_description: A pristine, round white ceramic plate holds a single, perfectly molded, creamy off-white kefir panna cotta. The panna cotta has a soft, delicate sheen, indicating its smooth texture. Adjacent to it, a small, organic dollop of deep reddish-brown red date compote provides a contrasting earthy tone and subtle texture. A thin, glossy drizzle of dark purple blueberry essence gracefully arcs over a portion of the panna cotta and compote, adding a vibrant, concentrated color. A cluster of three to four plump, fresh blue-purple blueberries are artfully placed near the panna cotta, offering a pop of natural color and fresh texture. The composition is clean and minimalist, with abundant white space on the plate emphasizing the natural beauty and distinct forms of each ingredient. The setting features a light, textured stone surface, an undyed linen napkin in natural beige, and soft, diffused natural lighting from above, creating a serene and elegant presentation.

ingredients.name: Natural sweetener (maple syrup or agave nectar)
Dried red dates, pitted and finely chopped

instructions: Prepare Panna Cotta: In a small bowl, whisk kudzu starch with 40 ml cold water until dissolved.
In a saucepan, gently heat kefir and 30g natural sweetener over low heat. Do not boil.
Gradually whisk in kudzu mixture. Stir constantly until mixture thickens slightly and coats the back of a spoon.
Pour panna cotta mixture into four small serving glasses or molds.
Chill for at least 4 hours, or until set.
Prepare Red Date Compote: Combine chopped red dates and 100 ml water in a small saucepan.
Bring to a simmer over medium-low heat. Cook for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until dates are very soft and liquid is absorbed, forming a thick compote.
If desired, stir in 10g natural sweetener. Let cool completely.
Prepare Blueberry Essence: Pour blueberry schnapps into a small saucepan.
Bring to a gentle simmer over low heat. Reduce by half to create a concentrated syrup.
Let cool.
Assemble Dessert: Unmold panna cotta onto individual plates or serve directly in glasses.
Spoon a small amount of red date compote alongside or on top of the panna cotta.
Drizzle a small amount of blueberry essence over the panna cotta and compote.
Garnish with a few fresh blueberries.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Almond & Herb Bites
recipes.visual_description: Golden-brown, savory pastry bites, approximately 4-5cm in diameter, are neatly arranged in two rows on a rustic dark wooden mezze board. Each bite features a crisp, slightly flaky semolina-based crust, encasing a rich, creamy almond butter and herb filling. The tops are subtly brushed with a hint of orange flower water, providing a delicate sheen and aromatic touch. A few finely toasted almond slivers are scattered on top of each canape, offering textural contrast. Small, vibrant green fresh mint leaves are strategically placed beside or on a few pieces, adding a pop of color and freshness. The arrangement is clean and professional, with consistent spacing between the pieces. The background is a blurred, warm-toned bistro setting, with natural, even lighting highlighting the canapes. A simple white linen napkin is folded beside the board.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Mezze style presentation on a traditional wooden board or elegant platter.
instructions: Combine semolina, flour, and salt in a bowl. Add olive oil. Rub with fingertips until mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Gradually add cold water, mixing until a smooth dough forms. Do not overknead. Cover and let rest 30 minutes.
In a separate bowl, combine almond butter, chopped toasted almonds, parsley, mint, minced shallot, sumac, salt, and pepper. Mix well.
Roll out dough thinly (2-3mm) on a lightly floured surface. Use a small round or square cookie cutter (approx. 4-5cm diameter) to cut out shapes.
Place a small spoonful of filling in the center of half the dough cut-outs. Top with another dough cut-out. Gently press edges to seal. Crimp edges with a fork for decoration if desired.
Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Place bites on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Bake for 12-15 minutes, or until lightly golden.
Let cool slightly. Arrange on a serving platter. Lightly mist or drizzle with orange flower water.
Garnish each bite with a few toasted almond slivers and a tiny fresh mint leaf. Serve warm or at room temperature.
notes: Can be served warm or at room temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Daikon with Spicy Doenjang Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A single, thick-cut daikon medallion, braised to a tender, translucent white, sits off-center on a pristine white bone china plate. The daikon is generously coated in a rich, glossy, reddish-brown glaze, glistening under dramatic professional lighting. A delicate, artful drizzle of the concentrated glaze extends subtly from the daikon, creating a flowing composition. Scattered precisely atop the daikon are a few golden-brown, crispy garlic chips, offering textural contrast. Alongside, a vibrant green, blanched scallion ribbon curves gracefully, adding a fresh color accent. Abundant negative space surrounds the dish, emphasizing its minimalist elegance. The plate rests on a dark, polished wooden surface, with a single, elegant pair of chopsticks positioned to the side, maintaining cultural authenticity and a sophisticated dining experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a sophisticated main dish, traditionally accompanied by steamed rice.

ingredients.name: Daikon Radish
ingredients.quantity: 800 g (peeled, cut into 3 cm thick rounds)

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.quantity: 4 cloves (2 thinly sliced for chips, 2 minced for sauce)

ingredients.name: Scallions
ingredients.quantity: 2 stalks (green part only, cut into 5 cm ribbons)

instructions: Prepare Daikon: Peel daikon. Cut into 3 cm thick rounds.
Make Glaze Base: In a pot, combine vegetable broth, soybean paste, sweet soy sauce, chili pepper flake, mirin, and minced ginger. Whisk until smooth.
Braise Daikon: Add daikon rounds to the pot. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and braise for 30-40 minutes. Daikon should be tender but still hold its shape.
Reduce Glaze: Remove daikon from pot. Increase heat to medium-high. Reduce sauce until it thickens to a glossy glaze. This takes 10-15 minutes. Stir occasionally.
Prepare Garlic Chips: Heat vegetable oil in a small pan over medium-low heat. Add thinly sliced garlic. Fry until golden brown and crispy. Remove with a slotted spoon. Drain on paper towel.
Blanch Scallions: Quickly blanch scallion ribbons in boiling water for 10 seconds. Immediately transfer to ice water. Drain well.
Finish Dish: Return daikon to the thickened glaze. Gently coat each piece. Drizzle with sesame oil.
Plate: Place one or two daikon rounds on each plate. Spoon extra glaze over the daikon. Garnish with crispy garlic chips and blanched scallion ribbons.
notes: Braising time for daikon may vary based on thickness and desired tenderness. Check for fork-tenderness.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Striped Bass with Verjus Butter Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A pan-seared striped bass fillet, golden-brown and slightly crispy on the skin, rests centrally on a simple, off-white ceramic plate. The flaky, white interior of the bass is visible where a fork has gently touched. A shimmering, pale yellow verjus butter sauce is artfully drizzled over the fish and pools slightly at its base. Alongside the bass, several roasted potato wedges, with their skins on and a light golden hue, are casually arranged. A small cluster of vibrant green steamed green beans adds a touch of fresh color. A sprinkle of fresh, chopped parsley is scattered over the fish and sauce. The dish is presented on a well-used wooden dining table, with a simple fork and knife beside the plate. The lighting is warm and inviting, typical of a cozy family kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette slices to sop up the delicious sauce.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with a light vinaigrette.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss potato wedges with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until tender and golden.
While potatoes roast, season striped bass fillets generously with salt and pepper on both sides.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat until shimmering.

Carefully place bass fillets skin-side down in the hot pan. Sear for 4-5 minutes until skin is crispy and golden. Flip fillets and cook for another 3-4 minutes, or until fish is opaque and flakes easily. Internal temperature should reach 63°C. Remove fish from pan and set aside on a plate.
Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the same pan. Add minced shallot and garlic. Sauté for 1-2 minutes until softened and fragrant.
Pour in the verjus. Bring to a simmer and cook for 2-3 minutes, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan, until liquid slightly reduces.
Remove pan from heat. Gradually whisk in the cold butter cubes, one at a time, until the sauce is smooth and emulsified. Do not boil. Stir in chopped fresh parsley.
Serve each pan-seared striped bass fillet with a generous spoonful of verjus butter sauce. Arrange roasted potato wedges and steamed green beans alongside. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure your pan is hot enough to achieve a good sear on the fish skin.
Adding cold butter off the heat helps emulsify the sauce and keeps it from breaking.
traditional_techniques: Emulsifying a butter sauce (similar to beurre blanc)

recipes.recipe_name: Moroccan Spiced Chickpea and Lentil Soup
recipes.visual_description: A hearty, comforting Moroccan chickpea and lentil soup is presented in a rustic, deep ceramic bowl with a slightly irregular rim. The soup is a warm, earthy red-orange hue, thick with tender, whole chickpeas and soft, disintegrated red lentils, interspersed with small, visible pieces of diced tomato and onion. A generous spoonful of a vibrant green herb topping, speckled with dark toasted sesame seeds and flecks of red chili, rests on the surface, its freshness contrasting with the rich soup. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple, off-white cloth napkin is casually placed beside the bowl. The setting is homely, with warm, natural lighting suggesting a cozy kitchen atmosphere. A piece of rustic Moroccan khobz (bread) is torn and placed next to the bowl, inviting dipping.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with traditional Moroccan khobz (round flatbread) for dipping.
Offer dates on the side as a traditional accompaniment.
Serve in deep, rustic tagine-style soup bowls.

ingredients.name: Dried bird's eye chili, finely chopped

instructions: Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and finely chopped dried bird's eye chili. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in ground cumin, ground turmeric, ground ginger, and smoked paprika. Cook for 30 seconds, stirring constantly.
Pour in diced tomatoes and vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer.
Add rinsed chickpeas and red lentils. Stir well.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 25-30 minutes, or until lentils are tender and soup has thickened slightly. Stir occasionally.

While soup simmers, prepare the topping: In a small bowl, combine chopped cilantro, chopped parsley, toasted sesame seeds, wasabi paste, 1 tbsp olive oil, and lemon juice. Mix well to form a coarse paste.
Season soup with salt and black pepper to taste.
Ladle hot soup into bowls. Top each serving with a spoonful of the spicy herb topping. Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust the amount of dried bird's eye chili and wasabi paste to your preferred spice level.
For a smoother soup, a portion can be blended with an immersion blender before adding the herb topping.
traditional_techniques: Sautéing aromatics (onion, garlic) as a base

recipes.recipe_name: Elderberry Cinnamon Soufflé
recipes.visual_description: Four individual Elderberry Cinnamon Soufflés are presented in classic, simple white ceramic ramekins. Each soufflé is generously risen, with a beautiful golden-brown crust and a slightly cracked, airy top, indicating its light internal texture. A light dusting of powdered sugar gently coats the surface, highlighting the warm, inviting color. The ramekins sit directly on a well-used, light-colored wooden kitchen table, suggesting a homely, relaxed setting. There are no elaborate garnishes; the focus is solely on the comforting, freshly baked dessert. The background is minimal, perhaps a soft blur of a kitchen counter, with warm, natural lighting illuminating the scene, emphasizing the soufflés' comforting glow and inviting textures. The presentation is unpretentious and natural, as if just pulled from a home oven and placed directly on the family table.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C. Butter four 175ml ramekins generously. Coat interiors with granulated sugar. Tap out excess.

Prepare elderberry compote: Combine elderberries, 50g sugar, water, and lemon juice in a small saucepan. Cook over medium heat for 8-10 minutes. Stir until berries soften and mixture thickens. Mash lightly. Set aside to cool.
Make soufflé base: Melt 20g butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Stir in flour. Cook for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in milk until mixture thickens and is smooth. Remove from heat.
Whisk in egg yolks one by one until fully incorporated. Stir in the cooled elderberry compote and 2g ground cinnamon. Set aside.

Whip egg whites: In a clean, dry bowl, whisk egg whites with a pinch of salt until soft peaks form. Gradually add remaining 100g sugar and 3g ground cinnamon. Continue whisking until stiff and glossy peaks form.
Combine: Gently fold one-third of the whipped egg whites into the elderberry base to lighten it. Then, carefully fold in the remaining egg whites until just combined. Do not overmix.
Fill ramekins: Spoon the soufflé mixture into the prepared ramekins. Level the tops. Run a thumb around the rim of each ramekin to create a clean edge for rising.
Bake: Place ramekins on a baking sheet. Bake for 12-15 minutes, or until soufflés are well-risen, golden brown, and slightly firm to the touch. The center should still be soft.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Brown Butter Financiers with Prune and Cherry
recipes.visual_description: Golden-brown financiers are presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Each financier has slightly crisp edges and a moist, tender crumb. Visible within the light amber-colored cake are distinct pieces of dark, rich prunes and vibrant red halved cherries. A very light dusting of white icing sugar graces the top of each financier, creating a subtle contrast. The financiers are arranged casually, three per plate, allowing for ample negative space. The setting is a simple wooden table surface, with a folded off-white cotton napkin placed beside the plate. Natural, even light illuminates the scene, highlighting the texture and color of the pastries. A small, elegant white teacup with a handle is subtly visible in the soft-focus background, suggesting a relaxed bistro atmosphere. No overcrowding; the focus remains on the cleanly presented pastries.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with coffee
Serve with tea
instructions: Melt butter in a small saucepan over medium heat. Cook until butter turns golden brown and smells nutty. Strain brown butter into a bowl. Let cool slightly. This is beurre noisette.
Chop dried prunes into small pieces. Place prunes in a small bowl. Pour prune juice over prunes. Let soak 15 minutes. Drain prunes, discard juice.
Pit fresh cherries. Halve cherries.
Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease and flour a financier mold or mini muffin tin.
In a large bowl, whisk together almond flour, icing sugar, all-purpose flour, and salt.
In a separate bowl, lightly whisk egg whites until just frothy, not stiff.
Pour egg whites into dry ingredients. Mix until just combined.
Gradually add cooled brown butter and vanilla extract to the batter. Mix until smooth. Do not overmix.
Gently fold in soaked prunes and halved cherries.
Fill prepared molds two-thirds full.
Bake 12-15 minutes, or until edges are golden brown and tops are set.
Let financiers cool in molds for 5 minutes. Transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Beer & Soy Chorizo Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single generous serving of hearty Spicy Beer & Soy Chorizo Soup is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl, showcasing its rich, reddish-brown broth. Visible chunks of crumbled soy chorizo intermingle with vibrant red and green diced bell peppers and tender, golden potato cubes. A scattering of fresh, roughly chopped cilantro leaves provides a pop of green on the surface. The soup has a robust, chunky texture, inviting warmth. The bowl rests on a well-worn, natural wooden dining table, suggesting a cozy, lived-in family kitchen. A simple, off-white cloth napkin is casually draped beside the bowl. Soft, warm overhead lighting illuminates the dish, emphasizing its comforting appeal. The scene is uncluttered, allowing the soup to be the focal point, embodying simple, wholesome home cooking.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and yellow curry paste. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add crumbled soy chorizo to the pot. Cook, breaking it up, until browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in diced red and yellow bell peppers and diced potatoes. Cook for 5 minutes.
Pour in the beer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Add canned diced tomatoes and vegetable broth. Stir well.
Bring the soup to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until potatoes are tender.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Ladle hot soup into bowls. Garnish with fresh cilantro or parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Pork Belly with Crispy Rice and Yuzu Mustard
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegantly plated starter portion on a premium white bone china plate. A perfectly braised, deep golden-brown pork belly cube, approximately 3cm, sits beside a golden-crisp, rectangular pan-fried rice cake. The pork belly has a glossy, rich surface, showcasing its tender texture. A delicate, pale yellow swirl of yuzu mustard emulsion is artfully placed on the plate, providing a soft contrast. A small, vibrant cluster of bright orange tobiko rests precisely atop the pork belly, adding a pop of color and texture. The composition is minimalist, with abundant white space around the elements, emphasizing clean lines and precise execution. The plate is set on a premium white Carrara marble surface with a pristine white linen napkin folded into a precise triangle. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, highlighting the dish's textures. The background is ultra-minimalist, drawing full attention to the sophisticated starter.
instructions: Cut pork belly into four 100g portions. Score skin lightly. Season with salt and pepper.
Sear pork belly, skin-side down, in a hot pan until golden brown and crispy. Sear all sides until browned.
Transfer pork belly to an oven-safe pot. Add dashi stock, soy sauce, mirin, sake, ginger, and garlic.
Bring liquid to a simmer. Cover pot tightly. Braise in oven at 150°C (300°F) for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until pork is fork-tender.
Remove pork from braising liquid. Strain liquid and reserve. Press pork belly between two heavy objects for 1 hour to flatten and set.
Cook sushi rice according to package directions. Season cooked rice with rice vinegar, sugar, and a pinch of salt.
Form rice into four small, rectangular cakes, approximately 4cm x 2cm x 1.5cm.
Heat a non-stick pan with a little oil. Pan-fry rice cakes until golden brown and crispy on both sides.
For the yuzu mustard emulsion, combine Dijon mustard, yuzu juice, and 15ml of the strained braising liquid in a small bowl.
Slowly whisk in neutral oil until emulsion forms and is smooth. Season with salt to taste.
Slice cooled, pressed pork belly into neat 3cm cubes. For serving, sear pork cubes in a hot pan or torch briefly to crisp skin and reheat.
Plate one crispy rice cake centrally on a minimalist plate. Place one seared pork belly cube beside or slightly on the rice cake.
Spoon a small, artistic swirl or dot of yuzu mustard emulsion next to the pork belly.
Carefully place a small quenelle or cluster of tobiko on top of the pork belly cube.

recipes.recipe_name: Gai Lan & Bok Choy Salad with Fermented Stems
recipes.visual_description: A minimalistic, natural presentation of a vibrant green salad. Blanched gai lan leaves and tender stalks, cut into 5 cm pieces, are artfully arranged alongside quartered bok choy heads. Thinly sliced quick-pickled gai lan stems are interspersed, adding textural contrast. The ingredients are coated with a rich, reddish-brown Szechuan dressing, highlighting the natural colors. A scattering of coarsely chopped roasted peanuts and fresh cilantro leaves provides a final flourish, adding earthy tones and freshness. The salad is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone, which sits on a light bamboo table surface. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is subtly placed to the side. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the dish, creating gentle shadows. The background is clean and minimalist, with a hint of lush green foliage from a nearby plant, emphasizing an eco-conscious, natural setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a refreshing side dish alongside steamed rice.
Offer chopsticks for traditional enjoyment.
instructions: Prepare gai lan. Separate leaves and tender stalks from tougher stems. Cut leaves and tender stalks into 5 cm pieces. Slice tougher stems thinly.

Prepare quick pickle. In a small pot, combine 125 ml water, 60 ml white vinegar, 1 tsp salt, and 1/2 tsp sugar. Bring to a boil. Pour over thinly sliced gai lan stems in a heatproof jar. Let cool completely. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
Prepare bok choy. Quarter bok choy heads lengthwise.
Make Szechuan peppercorn oil. Heat 4 tbsp vegetable oil in a small pan over low heat. Add Szechuan peppercorns. Cook until fragrant, about 5 minutes. Strain oil, discard peppercorns.
Prepare dressing. In a bowl, combine chili bean paste, soy sauce, Chinkiang vinegar, sesame oil, 1 tsp sugar, minced garlic, and grated ginger. Whisk in the prepared Szechuan peppercorn oil.

Blanch vegetables. Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add gai lan leaves and tender stalks. Blanch for 2-3 minutes until tender-crisp. Remove with a slotted spoon. Immediately plunge into ice water. Drain well.
Add bok choy to the same boiling water. Blanch for 1-2 minutes until tender-crisp. Remove and plunge into ice water. Drain well.
Assemble salad. In a large bowl, combine blanched gai lan, blanched bok choy, and quick-pickled gai lan stems (drained).
Pour dressing over vegetables. Toss gently to coat all ingredients.
Serve immediately. Garnish with chopped roasted peanuts and fresh cilantro.
notes: This recipe emphasizes sustainability by utilizing the tougher gai lan stems through quick pickling, minimizing food waste.
Fermentation adds a unique tang and depth of flavor, aligning with eco-conscious preservation methods.
The dressing can be prepared in advance and stored in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.

recipes.recipe_name: Plum Raspberry & Rose Entremet
recipes.visual_description: Four pristine individual mini entremets are elegantly presented on clean white porcelain dessert plates, set on a simple wooden bistro table. Each entremet, approximately 7cm in diameter and 4cm high, boasts a flawless, highly reflective rose-pink mirror glaze that shimmers under natural, even lighting. The glaze evenly coats the perfectly formed cylindrical pastry. A delicate cross-section, subtly visible or implied by the clean lines, reveals distinct layers: a vibrant raspberry mousse, a creamy peach schnapps crémeux, a darker plum confit insert, and a thin, golden almond biscuit base. The entremet is centrally placed on the plate, surrounded by moderate negative space. Each is minimally garnished with two or three fresh, plump red raspberries nestled against its base and a very thin, almost translucent slice of fresh plum placed delicately on top. A small, elegant dessert fork and spoon are positioned beside the plate on a folded white cotton napkin. The background features a subtle, blurred restaurant ambiance, maintaining focus on the dessert while suggesting a refined dining experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served as a sophisticated dessert after a meal
Often accompanied by a small espresso or a dessert wine

ingredients.name: Granulated sugar
ingredients.quantity: 100g (for biscuit), 30g (for plum confit), 30g (for crémeux), 40g (for mousse), 50g (for glaze)

instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Whip 3 eggs and 100g sugar until pale and thick.
Gently fold in almond flour and all-purpose flour.
Fold in melted butter.
Spread batter thinly onto prepared baking sheet. Bake 10-12 minutes, until lightly golden. Cool completely.
Cut out 4 circles (approx. 6cm diameter) for entremet bases.
Bloom 2g gelatin in cold water.
Combine diced plums, 30g sugar, and 15ml rose wine in a small saucepan.
Cook over medium heat until plums soften and liquid slightly reduces. About 5-7 minutes.
Remove from heat. Stir in bloomed gelatin until dissolved.
Pour into 4 small silicone molds (approx. 4cm diameter, thinner than entremet molds). Freeze until solid.
Bloom 1g gelatin in cold water.
Whisk 2 egg yolks and 30g sugar in a bowl.
Heat 50ml cream and peach schnapps in a saucepan until simmering.
Slowly pour hot cream mixture into egg yolk mixture, whisking constantly.
Return mixture to saucepan. Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until thickened. Do not boil.
Remove from heat. Stir in bloomed gelatin until dissolved.
Stir in cold diced butter until fully incorporated and smooth.
Pour into a shallow dish. Cover surface with plastic wrap. Chill until firm.
Once firm, pipe or spoon a small amount onto the center of the frozen plum confit discs. Return to freezer.
Bloom 4g gelatin in cold water.
Puree 150g raspberries. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve to remove seeds.
Heat raspberry puree, 40g sugar, and raspberry liqueur in a saucepan until sugar dissolves.
Remove from heat. Stir in bloomed gelatin until dissolved. Let cool completely.
Whip 200ml cold heavy cream to soft peaks.
Gently fold cooled raspberry mixture into whipped cream until combined.
Prepare 4 individual entremet molds (e.g., silicone rings, 7-8cm diameter, 4-5cm high).
Pour a layer of raspberry mousse into each mold, filling about one-third.
Place a frozen plum confit/peach schnapps crémeux insert into the center of the mousse, pressing gently.
Top with more raspberry mousse, filling molds almost to the top.
Place an almond biscuit circle on top of the mousse, pressing gently so it is flush with the top of the mold.
Freeze entremets for at least 6 hours, preferably overnight, until completely solid.
Bloom 4g gelatin in cold water.
Combine 50g sugar, 50ml water, and 50ml rose wine in a saucepan. Bring to a boil until sugar dissolves.
Remove from heat. Add chopped white chocolate and stir until melted and smooth.
Stir in bloomed gelatin until dissolved.
Add a few drops of red food coloring if desired for a richer color.
Blend with an immersion blender, keeping the blender head submerged to avoid air bubbles.
Strain glaze through a fine-mesh sieve. Let cool to 32-35°C (89-95°F) for glazing.
Place frozen entremets on a wire rack over a baking sheet.
Pour the mirror glaze evenly over each frozen entremet, ensuring full coverage.
Allow excess glaze to drip off. Use a small offset spatula to clean the bottom edge.
Carefully transfer glazed entremets to individual serving plates using two spatulas.
Thaw in the refrigerator for 2-3 hours before serving.
Garnish each entremet with fresh raspberries and a thin slice of plum. Add edible gold leaf for an extra touch of elegance.

recipes.recipe_name: Doenjang-Glazed Tofu with Quick-Pickled Daikon
recipes.visual_description: Two pan-seared extra-firm tofu chunks, about 5cm thick, are coated in a glossy, dark reddish-brown doenjang glaze, showcasing a rich, caramelized surface. They are centrally placed on a handcrafted, matte cream-colored ceramic plate, leaving generous white space. Beside the tofu, a neat mound of crisp, translucent white daikon batons, about 5cm long, provides a contrasting texture. A golden, aromatic lemongrass-ginger infused sesame oil is artfully drizzled over both, forming glistening pools. The dish is garnished simply with finely sliced bright green scallions and toasted sesame seeds. The plate sits on a light, natural wood surface, with dark wooden chopsticks and a small, empty ceramic rice bowl. An undyed linen napkin rests nearby. Soft, natural lighting highlights the dish's clean lines and natural beauty, with a subtly blurred background featuring a minimalist plant.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm short-grain rice and a light vegetable soup.
instructions: Press tofu blocks for 30 minutes to remove excess water. Cut each block into 4 thick chunks.
Peel daikon. Cut into thin batons (approx. 5cm long, 0.5cm thick). In a bowl, combine 60ml rice vinegar, 30g sugar, 5g salt, and 120ml water. Add daikon batons. Let pickle for at least 30 minutes.

Mince 3 cloves garlic. In a small saucepan, combine 60g doenjang, 30ml soy sauce, 30ml maple syrup, 30ml water, and minced garlic. Whisk until smooth. Simmer over medium-low heat for 5 minutes, stirring, until slightly thickened. Remove from heat.

Thinly slice the lower 10cm of lemongrass. Mince 5cm piece of ginger. In a small heatproof bowl, combine 60ml sesame oil, sliced lemongrass, and minced ginger. Heat briefly until warm. Let infuse for 15 minutes. Strain out solids before serving.
Heat 30ml vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Sear tofu chunks for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and crisp.
Reduce heat to medium-low. Pour doenjang glaze over seared tofu. Gently spoon glaze over tofu, turning to coat evenly. Cook for 2-3 minutes, allowing glaze to cling to tofu.

Finely slice 2 scallions (green parts only). Drain pickled daikon. Arrange 2 glazed tofu chunks per plate. Place a neat pile of pickled daikon batons beside the tofu. Drizzle infused sesame oil generously over tofu and daikon. Garnish with sliced scallions and a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds.
notes: Consider using daikon greens for garnish if available, for a zero-waste approach.

recipes.recipe_name: Mini Apple-Cherry Cakes with Grenadine-Lemon Glaze
recipes.visual_description: Eight uniform miniature cakes are arranged artfully on an elegant white ceramic serving platter. Each cake is small, round, and boasts a light golden-brown, moist crumb. The tops are coated with a glossy, vibrant red-pink grenadine-lemon glaze, which gently cascades down the sides. Visible within the tender cake crumb are finely diced pale apple pieces and contrasting deep red chopped cherry fragments. The presentation is neat yet inviting, with consistent spacing between each delicate treat. The platter sits on a light-colored, subtly textured surface, illuminated by soft, warm lighting, creating a refined yet approachable dessert display.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a sweet bite alongside espresso or strong Italian coffee.

ingredients.name: small apple, peeled, cored, finely diced
fresh or frozen pitted cherries, chopped

instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Line a mini muffin tin (for 8-9 cakes) with paper liners or lightly grease and flour molds.
In a large bowl, whisk together flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt.
In a separate bowl, combine plant-based milk, oil, and vanilla extract.
Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Gently fold in finely diced apple, chopped cherries, and lemon zest.
Divide batter evenly among prepared mini molds.
Bake for 15-18 minutes, or until a skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
Remove cakes from oven. Let cool in the tin for 5 minutes. Transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.
While cakes cool, prepare glaze. Whisk icing sugar, grenadine, and lemon juice in a small bowl until smooth. Adjust consistency with more sugar or juice if needed.
Once cakes are completely cool, dip tops into the glaze. Let excess drip off. Place on wire rack with parchment paper underneath to set.
notes: Ensure cherries are well-drained if using frozen to prevent excess moisture.
Do not overmix the cake batter; mix only until ingredients are just combined.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Rice & Spiced Chicken Bites with Pickled Okra
recipes.visual_description: Eight to twelve elegant, bite-sized canapés are artfully arranged on a light, rectangular reclaimed wood platter. Each canapé features a compact, square base of off-white fermented glutinous rice, measuring approximately 2cm by 2cm, showcasing its natural, slightly irregular texture. A small, neatly mounded portion of finely shredded, golden-brown spiced chicken sits atop each rice square, its savory aroma visually suggested by the rich, earthy tones. On top of the chicken, two to three vibrant green, thin slices of quick-pickled okra are carefully placed, adding a bright pop of color and a delicate, crisp texture. A sparse, almost imperceptible sprinkle of fresh microgreens or finely sliced spring onion green provides a final touch of natural freshness. The canapés are spaced consistently, creating a clean, inviting composition with ample negative space. The platter rests on a light bamboo table surface. The backdrop is clean and minimalist, with a hint of natural light and subtle green plant elements. The lighting is soft and natural, emphasizing the organic textures and vibrant colors of the ingredients. A single, undyed linen napkin in natural beige is subtly draped nearby, reinforcing the eco-conscious aesthetic. The entire arrangement exudes a calm, refined, and sustainable culinary artistry.

ingredients.name: Microgreens or finely sliced spring onion green

instructions: Rinse glutinous rice. Soak rice in 300ml water for 4-6 hours at room temperature for slight fermentation. Drain rice.

Cook soaked rice with 250ml fresh water in a rice cooker or pot until tender. Stir in 15ml rice vinegar and 2g salt. Press cooked rice into a shallow tray. Cool completely. Cut into 2cm x 2cm squares.
Boil chicken breast until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Shred chicken finely.
Heat 10ml oil in a pan. Sauté minced shallots, garlic, red chili until fragrant. Add coriander, cumin, turmeric powder. Stir for 1 minute.

Add shredded chicken, bruised lemongrass, and torn kaffir lime leaves. Pour in coconut milk. Add 3g salt and palm sugar. Cook until liquid reduces and chicken is well coated and dry. Remove lemongrass and kaffir lime leaves.
Wash okra. Trim ends. Slice okra into 0.5cm thick rounds.
In a small pot, combine 100ml rice vinegar, 50ml water, 10g sugar, 5g salt, and crushed peppercorns. Bring to a simmer.
Pour hot pickling liquid over sliced okra. Let cool to room temperature. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.

Place each fermented rice square on a serving platter. Top each rice square with a small mound of spiced shredded chicken. Arrange 2-3 pickled okra slices on top of the chicken. Garnish minimally with microgreens or finely sliced spring onion green.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Tatsoi Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Creamy Chicken and Tatsoi Skillet is presented on a simple, off-white ceramic dinner plate with a slightly rustic edge. The seared golden-brown chicken chunks, roughly 3-4 cm in size, are nestled in a rich, creamy white sauce. Vibrant green, wilted tatsoi leaves, some still whole and others gently folded, are interspersed among the chicken and sauce, adding a fresh contrast. The sauce is fluid, coating the chicken and tatsoi naturally without being overly thick or stiff. A scattering of fresh, finely chopped parsley provides a subtle green garnish. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, revealing its natural grain and warmth. A casually placed, folded cloth napkin in a neutral tone rests beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by warm, cozy kitchen lighting, creating a relaxed, lived-in atmosphere typical of a family meal. The background is minimal, showing just a hint of a familiar kitchen setting, keeping the focus entirely on the comforting dish. The portion is modest and approachable, reflecting a true home-cooked meal.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Cut chicken thighs into thick, bite-sized chunks.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks. Sear chicken for 4-5 minutes until golden brown on all sides and cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the skillet. Sauté for 3-4 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Bring to a simmer.
Add cream cheese and heavy cream. Whisk continuously until cream cheese is melted and sauce is smooth. Season sauce with salt and pepper.
Return cooked chicken chunks to the skillet. Stir to coat with sauce.
Add tatsoi leaves to the skillet. Cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring gently, until tatsoi is wilted. Do not overcook.
Serve immediately. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley, if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted King Oyster Mushroom with Candlenut-Galangal Emulsion
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented as a refined, minimalist composition on an exquisite, matte white bone china plate with a subtle, organic rim. A generous, glossy pool of the creamy, off-white candlenut-galangal emulsion forms an organic base, its surface reflecting the dramatic professional lighting. Two to three thick, deeply roasted king oyster mushroom medallions, each with a beautifully seared, golden-brown exterior and a tender, ivory interior, are artfully arranged atop the emulsion. Their surfaces show subtle crosshatch scoring. Scattered precisely around the mushrooms are a few delicate, golden-brown crispy shallots, adding a textural contrast and a hint of warmth. A single, vibrant green cilantro sprig is placed with precision, offering a fresh pop of color. The plating emphasizes abundant negative space, with each element positioned with architectural precision. The overall impression is one of sophisticated simplicity and luxurious restraint. The dish rests on a polished dark wood table, accompanied by a pristine white linen napkin folded into a precise triangle. The background is ultra-minimalist, showcasing the dish as the sole focal point.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).
Toast candlenuts in a dry pan over medium heat for 5-7 minutes until lightly golden and fragrant. Set aside.
Thinly slice 50g of shallots for crispy shallots. Roughly chop remaining 100g shallots, galangal, and garlic.
In a small blender, combine toasted candlenuts, chopped shallots, galangal, and garlic with 50ml of vegetable stock. Blend until a very smooth paste forms.
Heat 15ml neutral oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the blended aromatic paste. Sauté for 8-10 minutes, stirring constantly, until fragrant and slightly darkened.
Pour in remaining vegetable stock and coconut milk. Bring to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat and cook for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens slightly.
Season the emulsion with soy sauce, maple syrup, lime juice, salt, and white pepper. Keep warm.

Heat 80ml neutral oil in a small pot over medium-low heat. Add thinly sliced shallots. Fry slowly for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply golden brown and crispy. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Season lightly with salt.
Clean king oyster mushrooms. Trim ends. Cut each mushroom into 2-3 thick medallions (approx. 2-3 cm thick). Score the cut surfaces lightly in a crosshatch pattern.
Heat 5ml neutral oil in a large oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear mushroom medallions for 3-4 minutes per side until deeply golden brown.
Transfer pan to the preheated oven and roast for 8-10 minutes until tender.
Ladle a generous pool of the warm candlenut-galangal emulsion onto the center of each plate.
Arrange 2-3 roasted king oyster mushroom medallions artfully on top of the emulsion.
Garnish with a few crispy shallots scattered precisely and one small cilantro sprig. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Giant Bean & Tomato Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Mediterranean Giant Bean & Tomato Bake is served in a deep, rustic, earthy-toned ceramic bowl. The creamy white giant beans are nestled in a rich, thick, reddish-orange tomato sauce with finely diced onion and minced garlic visible throughout. A vibrant green scattering of fresh spearmint leaves is sprinkled generously over the top, contrasting beautifully with the warm tones of the dish. A light sheen of olive oil glistens on the surface. The components are naturally arranged, slightly overlapping, creating a comforting, abundant feel. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table. Beside it, a piece of crusty rustic bread is torn and casually placed. A simple, sturdy metal spoon rests in the bowl. The scene is bathed in warm, soft, natural light, reflecting a homely family kitchen atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty rustic bread for dipping.
Accompany with a simple green salad.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Rinse and drain giant white beans.
Heat 50 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe pot over medium heat. Add finely diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, vegetable broth, dried oregano, black pepper, and salt. Bring to a simmer.
Add rinsed giant white beans to the sauce. Stir gently to combine.
Cover the pot. Transfer to the preheated oven. Bake for 30 minutes.
Remove lid. Stir in chopped spearmint. Drizzle with remaining 50 ml olive oil.
Return to oven, uncovered. Bake for another 15-20 minutes, or until sauce has thickened and beans are tender.
Check for seasoning. Serve hot.
notes: Ensure beans are fully tender but not mushy.
Adjust salt and pepper to personal preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Lotus Seed & Red Date Coconut Truffles
recipes.visual_description: A pristine white rectangular porcelain platter showcases six to nine perfectly spherical, miniature truffles. Each truffle, approximately 3 cm in diameter, is uniformly coated in finely toasted, crisp desiccated coconut, offering a delicate, textured exterior. The interior, subtly revealed by a clean cut on one truffle, is a smooth, creamy beige lotus seed paste, interspersed with tiny, deep crimson flecks of red date. A few delicate slivers of candied red date are artfully scattered on the platter as elegant garnish. The arrangement is professional, with consistent spacing, creating a balanced, inviting display. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a light wooden table surface and a crisp white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the refined textures and subtle colors, focusing entirely on the meticulously crafted sweets.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve chilled with hot tea, such as jasmine or oolong.
instructions: Soak lotus seeds in water overnight. Drain. Rinse.
Place soaked lotus seeds in a pot. Cover with fresh water. Boil until very soft, about 45-60 minutes. Drain well.
Blend cooked lotus seeds with 50ml coconut cream until a smooth paste forms. Add a little water if needed for blending. Push through a fine-mesh sieve for extra smoothness, if desired.
Pit red dates. Chop finely. Or soak in hot water for 15 minutes, then blend into a paste.
Combine lotus seed paste, red date, sugar, remaining coconut cream, apple liqueur, and salt in a non-stick pan.
Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until the mixture thickens and pulls away from the sides of the pan. This takes about 10-15 minutes.
Transfer mixture to a shallow dish. Cover with plastic wrap, pressing it directly onto the surface. Chill in refrigerator for at least 2 hours, or until firm.
Scoop chilled mixture using a small spoon or mini ice cream scoop. Roll into uniform 3 cm spheres.
Place toasted desiccated coconut in a shallow bowl. Roll each truffle in the coconut until fully coated.
Arrange truffles on an elegant serving platter.
notes: For best texture, ensure lotus seed paste is very smooth.
Adjust sugar to your preferred sweetness level.
Truffles can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Swiss Cheese and Bacon Soup
recipes.visual_description: A hearty, creamy Swiss cheese and bacon soup is presented in a rustic, deep ceramic bowl on a well-used wooden dining table. The soup is a rich, warm off-white color, thick and inviting. Small, golden-brown diced crispy bacon pieces are scattered generously over the surface, providing a textural contrast. Bright green, finely chopped chives are sprinkled on top, adding a fresh pop of color. The soup fills the bowl adequately, showing a natural, comforting portion. The setting is a homely family kitchen, with warm, cozy lighting. A simple, sturdy spoon rests beside the bowl on the wooden table, and a casually placed cloth napkin completes the relaxed, lived-in atmosphere. The entire bowl is visible, showcasing the comfort food in its natural, appetizing state.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping.
Offer a simple green salad as a light accompaniment.
instructions: Cook diced bacon in a large pot over medium heat until crispy. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon. Drain excess fat, leaving 1 tablespoon in the pot.
Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Melt butter in the pot. Stir in flour to create a roux. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Gradually whisk in chicken stock until smooth. Bring to a simmer, stirring, until slightly thickened.
Stir in milk. Heat gently. Do not boil.
Remove pot from heat. Gradually stir in grated Emmentaler and Gruyere cheeses until melted and smooth.
Whisk in Hollandaise sauce.
Season with salt, black pepper, and a pinch of nutmeg.
Ladle hot soup into bowls. Garnish each serving with crispy bacon pieces and chopped fresh chives.

recipes.recipe_name: Wild Rice and Roasted Sweet Potato Salad
recipes.visual_description: The Wild Rice and Roasted Sweet Potato Salad is presented on an everyday, cream-colored ceramic plate, capturing a homely, comforting aesthetic. Diced, golden-orange roasted sweet potato cubes are mingled with dark, earthy wild rice grains. Bright red bell pepper pieces and translucent slices of red onion add pops of color and varied textures. Freshly chopped green parsley is generously mixed throughout, providing a vibrant herbaceous note. The salad is loosely piled, allowing components to naturally overlap and touch, creating a casual, unpretentious mound. A light sheen of raspberry vinaigrette coats the ingredients, reflecting the warm, cozy light from above. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, accompanied by a simple silver fork and a casually folded cloth napkin, suggesting a relaxed family meal.

ingredients.name: Sweet potato
ingredients.quantity: 400g, peeled and diced into 1.5 cm cubes

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.

Rinse wild rice. Combine rice and water or broth in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 40-45 minutes, or until rice is tender and water is absorbed. Fluff with a fork.

Toss diced sweet potato, bell pepper, and sliced red onion with 30ml olive oil, 2g salt, and 1g black pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes, stirring halfway, until tender and lightly caramelized.
While vegetables roast, prepare vinaigrette. In a small bowl, whisk remaining 30ml olive oil, raspberry vinegar, Dijon mustard, maple syrup (if using), 3g salt, and 1g black pepper until emulsified.
In a large bowl, combine cooked wild rice, roasted vegetables, chopped parsley, and toasted nuts (if using).
Pour vinaigrette over the salad. Toss gently to combine all ingredients thoroughly.
Serve warm or at room temperature, optionally over a bed of fresh spinach or mixed greens.

recipes.recipe_name: Maple Cinnamon Madeleines with Vanilla Glaze
recipes.visual_description: Six to nine golden-brown Maple Cinnamon Madeleines are elegantly arranged on a clean white porcelain serving platter.
