Each miniature cake features the classic shell-shaped ridge on one side and a delicate hump on the other, indicating a perfect bake. One side of each Madeleine is dipped in a smooth, translucent vanilla glaze, creating a subtle contrast. The glaze has a slight sheen, highlighting the warm, inviting color of the cake beneath. A light dusting of finely ground cinnamon is scattered artfully over a few Madeleines. The platter is placed on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting, with natural, soft lighting illuminating the scene. A folded cotton napkin rests beside the platter, adding a touch of casual elegance. The composition is clean and professional, focusing solely on the refined presentation of the delicate pastries.

ingredients.name: Unsalted butter
ingredients.quantity: 125g, melted and cooled, plus extra for molds

instructions: Prepare Madeleine molds: Grease molds with melted butter. Dust with flour. Tap out excess. Chill molds for 10 minutes.
Whisk dry ingredients: In a bowl, whisk together flour, maple sugar, cinnamon, baking powder, and salt.
Add wet ingredients: Add eggs and vanilla extract to dry ingredients. Whisk until just combined. Do not overmix.
Fold in butter: Gradually fold in cooled melted butter until smooth batter forms.
Chill batter: Cover batter. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour, or overnight.
Preheat oven: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Fill molds: Spoon batter into prepared Madeleine molds, filling each cavity about two-thirds full.
Bake Madeleines: Bake for 10-12 minutes. Edges should be golden. Centers should be set.
Cool Madeleines: Remove Madeleines from molds immediately. Transfer to wire rack to cool completely.
Prepare glaze: In a small bowl, whisk powdered sugar, milk, and vanilla extract until smooth. Adjust consistency with more liquid or sugar.
Glaze Madeleines: Dip one side of each cooled Madeleine into the glaze. Let excess drip off. Place on wire rack for glaze to set.

recipes.recipe_name: Chili-Infused Vegetable Custard with Crispy Potato & Sunflower Sprouts
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a pristine rectangular white bone china platter, showcasing elegant minimalism. Four delicate, paper-thin potato crisps, each a pale golden hue, are arranged with generous negative space. Each crisp is precisely topped with a small, perfectly spherical dollop of creamy, pale yellow chili-infused vegetable custard. The custard exhibits a smooth, almost glossy texture. Perched atop the custard are vibrant green clusters of fresh sunflower sprouts, their tiny leaves unfurling delicately, providing a striking color contrast and fresh texture. A single, minute drop of deep crimson smoked paprika oil is artfully placed beside each crisp, adding a subtle visual accent and depth of color. The arrangement is organic, flowing, and uncluttered, emphasizing precision and restraint. The entire composition is illuminated by dramatic, focused lighting, casting soft shadows that enhance the dish's architectural quality. The background is an ultra-minimalist white Carrara marble surface, reinforcing the luxury aesthetic.
instructions: Prepare chili-infused vegetable stock: Bring vegetable stock to a simmer. Add deseeded red chili half. Simmer for 10 minutes. Remove chili. Strain stock through a fine-mesh sieve.

Make chili-infused vegetable custard: Whisk egg yolks and heavy cream in a bowl. Slowly whisk in the warm chili-infused stock. Season with salt and white pepper. Pass mixture through a fine-mesh sieve. Pour into small heatproof molds or ramekins. Cook in a water bath (bain-marie) at 150°C (300°F) for 25-30 minutes, or until set but still tender. Cool completely. Gently unmold.

Prepare crispy potato: Peel potato. Using a mandoline, slice potato into paper-thin rounds. Arrange slices on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Season lightly with salt. Bake at 140°C (285°F) for 20-30 minutes, or until golden and crisp. Let cool completely on a wire rack.

Make smoked paprika oil: Heat neutral oil gently in a small saucepan. Add smoked paprika. Stir well. Remove from heat immediately. Let infuse for 15 minutes. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve lined with cheesecloth. Discard solids.

Assemble the snack: Place a crispy potato round on a serving platter. Carefully place one piece of chili-infused vegetable custard onto the potato crisp. Arrange a small cluster of fresh sunflower sprouts delicately on top of the custard. Drizzle a precise, small amount of smoked paprika oil next to the assembled crisp. Repeat for remaining portions. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Tempeh with Sriracha-Ginger Glaze and Quick Pickled Radishes
recipes.visual_description: A minimalist, plant-forward dish presented on a handcrafted, natural beige ceramic plate. Two thick, pan-seared tempeh rectangles, deep golden-brown with a glossy sriracha-ginger glaze, are centrally placed. Scattered around the tempeh are vibrant pink quick-pickled radish rounds, adding a pop of color and crisp texture. A thin drizzle of the dark, rich glaze artfully pools around the tempeh. Bright green, thinly sliced green onion diagonals are sprinkled over the tempeh and plate, providing fresh contrast. The plate sits on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is casually placed beside the plate. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, creating gentle shadows. The background is clean and uncluttered, with a subtle hint of green foliage from a houseplant, reinforcing the eco-conscious theme. A single portion is depicted, showcasing clean lines and natural beauty.

ingredients.name: Green onions
ingredients.quantity: 4 stalks (white parts minced, green parts sliced thinly diagonally)

instructions: Prepare quick pickled radishes: Combine 60ml rice vinegar, 120ml water, sugar, and salt in a clean jar. Stir to dissolve sugar and salt. Add thinly sliced radish rounds. Seal and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
Prepare tempeh: Slice the tempeh block into 8 thick rectangular pieces. Steam the tempeh pieces for 10 minutes to reduce any bitterness. Pat them thoroughly dry with a clean cloth.
Make sriracha-ginger glaze: In a medium bowl, whisk together sriracha sauce, grated fresh ginger, 15ml toasted sesame oil, minced white parts of green onions, low-sodium soy sauce, and maple syrup.
Sear tempeh: Heat neutral cooking oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Add the dried tempeh pieces. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side until deeply golden brown and crispy.

Glaze tempeh: Pour the prepared sriracha-ginger glaze over the seared tempeh in the pan. Reduce heat to medium-low. Cook, turning tempeh frequently, until the glaze thickens and evenly coats each tempeh piece, about 2-3 minutes.

Plate and serve: Arrange 2 glazed tempeh pieces on each plate. Scatter quick pickled radish rounds alongside the tempeh. Drizzle any remaining glaze from the pan over the tempeh. Garnish generously with thinly sliced green parts of green onions. Finish with a few drops of fresh toasted sesame oil.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Soppressata Crostini with Whipped Pecorino and Pickled Zucchini Rind
recipes.visual_description: A clean, minimalist presentation of 8-12 elegant canapés arranged with consistent spacing on a light ceramic platter or reclaimed wood board. Each features a golden, crisp sourdough crostini. A generous dollop of creamy, off-white whipped Pecorino Romano spreads across the base. Resting atop is a single, thinly sliced, ruby-red soppressata round, naturally folded for dimension. Vibrant green, translucent strips of pickled zucchini rind provide a pop of color and texture beside the soppressata. A tiny, fresh basil leaf garnishes each. The composition is clean, highlighting natural colors and textures. The background is simple, featuring a light bamboo or stone surface, with soft, natural light. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is subtly placed. Focus is on pure, natural elements.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a crisp, dry Italian white wine like Vermentino or Pinot Grigio.
Present as part of an antipasto spread before a main meal.
Offer alongside other small, savory Italian bites.
instructions: Prepare Pickled Zucchini Rind: Wash zucchini. Carefully peel green rind into long strips using a vegetable peeler. Avoid white pith. In a small saucepan, combine white vinegar, water, sugar, and 5g salt. Bring to a boil. Add zucchini rind strips. Simmer 2 minutes. Remove from heat. Let cool in brine.
Prepare Crostini: Preheat oven to 180°C. Slice baguette into 1 cm thick rounds. Brush lightly with olive oil. Bake 8-10 minutes until golden and crisp. Rub warm crostini with a cut garlic clove.

Prepare Whipped Pecorino Romano: Grate Pecorino Romano. In a food processor, combine grated Pecorino Romano, 20ml olive oil, and a pinch of salt. Process until smooth and creamy. Add a tablespoon of water if too thick.
Prepare Soppressata: Slice soppressata into very thin rounds.
Assemble Canapés: Spread a generous dollop of whipped Pecorino Romano onto each crostini. Top with a folded slice of soppressata. Place a few strips of pickled zucchini rind on top.
Garnish: Drizzle lightly with remaining olive oil. Garnish with a small basil leaf. Arrange 8-12 pieces on a serving platter.
notes: Using a food processor for the Pecorino Romano ensures a very smooth, whipped texture.
The pickled zucchini rind adds a bright, acidic counterpoint to the rich soppressata and cheese.
This recipe minimizes waste by utilizing the often-discarded zucchini rind.

recipes.recipe_name: Moroccan Orange Ginger Raisin Briouats
recipes.visual_description: Six to nine perfectly uniform, golden-brown Moroccan Briouat triangles are neatly arranged on a polished, ornate brass serving tray. Each delicate pastry is lightly dusted with fine white powdered sugar, creating a subtle contrast. A small, artfully placed pile of vibrant green finely chopped pistachios rests in one corner of the tray, adding a pop of color and texture. The briouats exhibit a crisp, flaky exterior, hinting at the sweet, aromatic filling of raisins, orange zest, and ginger within. The setting is a clean wooden table in a modern bistro, illuminated by natural, even lighting. The background is minimal, focusing entirely on the elegant presentation of the traditional Moroccan sweets.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm or at room temperature with traditional Moroccan mint tea.
Offer as a sweet accompaniment to a post-meal coffee.
instructions: Prepare filling. Combine finely chopped raisins, diced candied ginger, blanched and finely ground almonds, orange zest, cinnamon, and orange blossom water in a bowl. Mix well.
Cut pastry. Cut warqa or phyllo sheets into 5 cm wide strips. Keep covered with a damp cloth to prevent drying.

Form briouats. Place a teaspoon of filling at one end of a pastry strip. Fold corner over filling to form a triangle. Continue folding strip into a triangle until end. Brush end with melted butter to seal.
Arrange on tray. Place formed briouats on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Bake briouats. Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until golden brown and crisp.
Prepare honey syrup. While briouats bake, heat honey and water in a small saucepan. Simmer gently for 5 minutes.
Dip briouats. Remove briouats from oven. Dip warm briouats immediately into warm honey syrup. Drain excess syrup.
Cool and garnish. Place briouats on a wire rack to cool. Dust lightly with powdered sugar. Garnish with finely chopped pistachios.
traditional_techniques: Folding warqa pastry into briouat triangles

recipes.recipe_name: Green Pea and Rice Salad
recipes.special_requests: qsr style PAPER bowl with crunchy topping
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Green Pea and Rice Salad is presented in a modern, clean QSR-style paper bowl, set on a simple light wooden table. The base layer features fluffy white basmati rice, interspersed with bright green blanched peas, small diced ruby-red cherry tomatoes, and finely diced purple-red onion. Shredded Parmesan cheese is lightly mixed throughout, adding subtle texture. A light, glistening lemon-herb dressing coats the ingredients, reflecting the natural light. The salad is generously crowned with a mound of golden-brown, irregularly shaped crispy fried onion pieces, providing a dramatic textural contrast. The overall presentation is fresh and appealing, with natural light highlighting the varied colors and textures. A cotton napkin is placed beside the bowl.
instructions: Cook rice according to package directions. Cool completely.
Blanch green peas in boiling salted water for 2 minutes. Drain immediately. Plunge into ice water to retain color. Drain well.

Prepare crispy onions. Toss thinly sliced onion with flour until coated. Heat vegetable oil in a pan to 170°C. Fry onions in batches until golden brown and crispy. Remove with a slotted spoon. Drain on paper towels. Season lightly with salt.
Dice cherry tomatoes. Finely dice red onion.
Prepare dressing. Whisk together olive oil, lemon juice, Dijon mustard, chopped parsley, salt, and pepper in a small bowl.
In a large mixing bowl, combine cooled rice, blanched green peas, diced cherry tomatoes, finely diced red onion, and shredded Parmesan cheese.
Pour dressing over salad ingredients. Gently toss to combine all components evenly.
Transfer salad into QSR style paper bowls. Top each serving generously with crispy fried onions. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Green Pea and Chicken Rice Salad
recipes.visual_description: The Green Pea and Chicken Rice Salad is presented in a pristine white porcelain bowl. Fluffy rice, mixed with bright emerald green peas, forms the base. Small, evenly diced seared chicken pieces are interspersed throughout. Crisp, julienned strips of vibrant orange carrot, cool green cucumber, and red bell pepper are scattered for crunch and color. The salad is lightly coated in a glistening, savory Asian dressing. Roughly chopped, golden-brown toasted cashews, thinly sliced spring onions, and fresh coriander leaves garnish the top, adding texture and aroma. The presentation is clean, organized, and inviting, with moderate negative space. The bowl rests on a simple light wooden table, accompanied by a cotton napkin and chopsticks, evoking a modern bistro setting with natural lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately as a refreshing main course or side dish.
Can be accompanied by small bowls of chili oil or sriracha for those who prefer extra heat.
instructions: Cook rice according to package directions. Fluff with a fork. Let cool completely.

Dice chicken breast into 1.5 cm cubes. Heat a pan over medium-high heat. Add a little oil. Sear chicken cubes until cooked through and lightly browned. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Season with salt and pepper. Let cool.
Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Add green peas. Cook for 1-2 minutes until tender-crisp. Drain immediately and plunge into ice water. Drain well.
Spread cashews on a baking sheet. Toast in a preheated oven at 160°C for 5-7 minutes, or in a dry pan over medium heat until golden and fragrant. Let cool. Chop roughly.
Julienne cucumber, carrot, and red bell pepper. Thinly slice spring onions. Chop fresh coriander.
In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, honey/maple syrup, grated ginger, minced garlic, and lime juice (if using).
In a large bowl, combine cooled cooked rice, blanched green peas, cooled cooked chicken, julienned cucumber, carrot, red bell pepper, and most of the sliced spring onions and chopped coriander.
Pour dressing over salad ingredients. Toss gently to combine all ingredients evenly.
Transfer salad to individual serving bowls or plates. Garnish with remaining sliced spring onions, chopped coriander, and toasted chopped cashews.
notes: Ensure rice is completely cooled before mixing to prevent sogginess.
Adjust dressing sweetness and tanginess to personal preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Coconut Almond Tart with Jasmine & Raspberry
recipes.visual_description: An individual Coconut Almond Tart sits centrally on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The tart features a golden-brown, crisp pâte sablée crust with fluted edges. Inside, a creamy, pale almond frangipane filling is visible, baked to a light golden hue. Topping the frangipane is a smooth, ivory-colored jasmine tea-infused white chocolate ganache, set firm and even. A vibrant, glossy framboise glaze, rich red in color, covers the ganache. The tart is garnished simply with two fresh, plump red raspberries and a sprinkle of toasted coconut flakes. The composition is clean and elegant, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a light wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and modern cutlery. Natural, even lighting highlights the tart's refined textures and vibrant colors against a subtle restaurant background.
instructions: Prepare the tart dough: In a food processor, combine flour, cold butter, caster sugar, and salt. Pulse until crumbly. Add egg yolk and pulse until dough just comes together. Do not overmix. Form into a disc, wrap in cling film, and chill for at least 30 minutes.

Blind bake tart shells: On a floured surface, roll out dough to 3 mm thickness. Line four 10 cm tart rings. Prick bases with a fork. Chill for 15 minutes. Preheat oven to 180°C. Line tart shells with parchment paper and fill with baking beans. Bake for 15 minutes. Remove beans and paper. Bake for another 5-7 minutes until light golden. Cool completely.
Make almond cream (frangipane): In a bowl, cream softened butter and powdered sugar until light. Beat in egg, then mix in almond flour and framboise eau de vie until combined. Do not overmix.
Bake frangipane: Reduce oven temperature to 170°C. Fill cooled tart shells with almond cream, spreading evenly. Bake for 20-25 minutes, until golden brown and set. Cool completely on a wire rack.

Prepare jasmine tea ganache: Heat heavy cream in a small saucepan until just simmering. Remove from heat. Add jasmine tea bags and steep for 10 minutes. Remove tea bags, squeezing out liquid. Reheat cream gently. Pour hot cream over chopped white chocolate in a bowl. Let stand for 1 minute, then whisk until smooth and emulsified.
Fill tarts with ganache: Pour jasmine tea ganache into cooled frangipane-filled tart shells. Smooth the tops. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or until ganache is set.

Make framboise glaze: In a small saucepan, combine fresh raspberries and granulated sugar. Cook over medium heat, stirring, until raspberries break down and sugar dissolves. Pass mixture through a fine-mesh sieve to remove seeds, creating a smooth purée. Return purée to saucepan. Heat gently until warm. Stir in framboise eau de vie.

Glaze and garnish: Once ganache is firm, carefully pour or spread the warm framboise glaze over the chilled tarts, ensuring an even coating. Refrigerate for 30 minutes to set the glaze. Garnish each tart with fresh raspberries and toasted coconut flakes before serving.
notes: Ensure tart shells are fully cooled before adding frangipane to prevent a soggy crust.
Chill the ganache thoroughly before glazing for a clean, even finish.

recipes.recipe_name: Jasmine Framboise Coconut Almond Twice-Baked Croissant
recipes.visual_description: A single, generously sized twice-baked croissant rests centrally on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The croissant boasts a rich, crisp, deeply golden-brown exterior, contrasting with the visible, soft, creamy interior where it's been gently split and filled. A thick layer of baked coconut-almond frangipane peeks from the center, topped with beautifully toasted slivered almonds and a light dusting of white powdered sugar. Scattered toasted shredded coconut adds a textural garnish. The overall presentation is professional and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate is placed on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and a small, delicate teacup, suggesting a relaxed bistro setting under natural, even lighting. The focus remains on the croissant's inviting textures and golden hues, conveying warmth and refined indulgence.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm, alongside a cup of strong black coffee or a delicate cup of jasmine tea.
Enjoy as a luxurious breakfast pastry or an elegant afternoon treat.
instructions: Preheat oven to 170°C. Line a baking tray with parchment paper.

Prepare jasmine tea syrup: Combine water and 50g granulated sugar in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer, stirring until sugar dissolves. Remove from heat. Stir in brewed jasmine tea and 15ml framboise eau de vie. Set aside.

Prepare coconut almond frangipane: In a bowl, cream 100g softened butter and 50g granulated sugar until light and fluffy. Beat in eggs one at a time. Mix in ground almonds, shredded coconut, and flour until combined. Do not overmix.
Slice each croissant horizontally, almost but not entirely through, creating a hinge.
Dip the cut sides of each croissant half into the jasmine tea syrup. Ensure the interior is well moistened.
Open each croissant. Spread a generous amount of frangipane onto the bottom half. Close the croissant gently.
Spread a thin layer of frangipane over the top of each croissant. Arrange on the prepared baking tray.
Sprinkle slivered almonds evenly over the frangipane-covered tops.
Bake for 18-22 minutes, or until deeply golden brown and puffed. The frangipane should be set.
Remove from oven. Let cool slightly on the tray.
Drizzle remaining 15ml framboise eau de vie over the warm croissants. Dust generously with powdered sugar. Garnish with toasted shredded coconut.
notes: Using day-old croissants is essential as they absorb the syrup better and achieve the desired texture during the second bake.
Adjust the sweetness of the syrup to your preference, keeping in mind the frangipane is also sweet.

recipes.recipe_name: Framboise-Almond Croissant
recipes.visual_description: A single golden-brown croissant rests on a clean, round white porcelain plate, centered with moderate negative space. The croissant is slightly split, revealing a creamy, baked almond frangipane interior. A translucent, glossy jasmine tea glaze is drizzled artfully over its crisp, flaky surface, with delicate trails of glaze pooling slightly at the base. Lightly toasted coconut flakes are scattered around the croissant and gently cling to the glaze, adding textural contrast. Beside the croissant, a cluster of vibrant red, fresh raspberries provides a pop of color. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple, natural wooden table surface. A silver fork and knife are placed neatly to the right of the plate, and a crisp white cotton napkin is folded beside the cutlery. The scene is illuminated by soft, natural, even lighting, highlighting the pastry's textures and inviting appeal with a professional yet approachable aesthetic.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with coffee or tea
Enjoy as a breakfast pastry or dessert

ingredients.name: Framboise eau de vie
ingredients.quantity: 10 ml (5 ml for frangipane, 5 ml for glaze)

instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Line a baking tray with parchment paper.
Prepare frangipane: Cream softened butter and caster sugar in a bowl until light and fluffy. Add almond flour, mix well. Beat in the egg and 5 ml framboise eau de vie. Mix until smooth.

Prepare croissants: Slice each croissant horizontally, not completely through, creating a pocket. Spread an even layer of frangipane inside each croissant. Place croissants on the prepared baking tray.
Bake croissants for 15-20 minutes, or until golden brown and the frangipane is set and slightly puffed.

Prepare jasmine glaze: While croissants bake, whisk icing sugar, 30 ml strong brewed jasmine tea, and 5 ml framboise eau de vie in a small bowl. Add more tea slowly if needed to reach a smooth, pourable consistency.
Remove croissants from oven. Let cool slightly on a wire rack.
Drizzle the jasmine glaze generously over the warm croissants. Sprinkle with toasted coconut flakes. Garnish plates with fresh raspberries beside each croissant.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Almond Croissant Feuilleté with Coconut Crémeux and Jasmine Raspberry
recipes.visual_description: A minimalist, ultra-sophisticated dessert presented on a pristine white bone china plate set on a grey veined marble surface. The composition features a generous, smooth quenelle of creamy white coconut crémeux, positioned slightly off-center. Leaning elegantly against the crémeux is a rectangular, golden-brown almond croissant feuilleté, showcasing its delicate, flaky layers. Vibrant red fresh raspberries, glistening from a light maceration, are artfully scattered in a natural, flowing cluster beside the crémeux. Small, translucent dots of pale amber jasmine tea gel are precisely placed around the main elements, adding subtle color and aromatic nuance. Abundant negative space surrounds the components, emphasizing their perfect execution and luxurious textures. The scene is lit with dramatic professional lighting, casting soft shadows that enhance depth and sophistication, with a crisp white linen napkin folded into a precise triangle.
instructions: Prepare Almond Croissant Feuilleté: Roll puff pastry dough very thin (2mm).
Combine almond flour, 50g sugar, 50g softened butter, and 1 egg yolk for almond cream. Spread a thin layer of almond cream on half of the rolled pastry.
Fold the pastry in half. Cut into 8x4 cm rectangles.
Bake at 180°C (350°F) for 12-15 minutes until golden and crisp. Cool on a wire rack.
Prepare Coconut Crémeux: Soak gelatin leaf in cold water.
Whisk 3 egg yolks, 75g sugar, and cornstarch in a bowl.
Heat coconut milk in a saucepan until simmering. Pour hot coconut milk slowly into egg mixture, whisking constantly.
Return mixture to saucepan. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until thickened. Do not boil.
Remove from heat. Stir in soaked and squeezed gelatin. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve. Cool completely. Chill for at least 4 hours.
Whip heavy cream to soft peaks. Fold into chilled coconut crémeux until smooth.
Prepare Jasmine Tea Gel: Bring 200ml water to a boil. Remove from heat. Add jasmine tea leaves. Steep for 5 minutes. Strain tea.
Return jasmine tea infusion to saucepan. Add 30g sugar and agar-agar. Bring to a boil, whisking constantly for 1 minute. Remove from heat.
Pour into a shallow dish. Chill until set, about 30 minutes. Once set, blend until smooth and gel-like. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve.
Prepare Framboise Raspberry Garnish: Gently toss fresh raspberries with framboise eau de vie and powdered sugar. Let macerate for 10 minutes.
Assemble: Place a quenelle or artistic smear of coconut crémeux off-center on each plate.
Lean an almond croissant feuilleté crisp against the crémeux.
Arrange a few macerated raspberries artfully around the crémeux.
Dot the plate with small drops of jasmine tea gel.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Exotic Fruit Composition with Jasmine-Coconut Consommé, Toasted Almonds, and Framboise Air
recipes.visual_description: A minimalist, ultra-sophisticated dessert on an exquisite bone china plate. An artful, organic cluster of meticulously cut fresh exotic fruits forms the core: precise 1 cm cubes of vibrant mango and kiwi, translucent halved lychees, delicate dragon fruit spheres, and glistening passion fruit pulp. These elements are arranged naturally, showcasing varied colors and textures. A clear, pale golden Jasmine-Coconut Consommé gently fills the plate's bottom, surrounding the fruit. Adjacent, a delicate, ethereal cloud of light pink Framboise Air floats, adding height. A few crisp, golden toasted almond slivers are scattered sparingly. Abundant negative space highlights the architectural precision. The setting: premium white Carrara marble, pristine white linen napkin, dramatic professional lighting, creating an ultra-minimalist background for culinary artistry.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve chilled as a palate cleanser or light dessert.
Pair with a delicate dessert wine or a glass of chilled champagne.

ingredients.name: Fresh Exotic Fruits (e.g., ripe mango, lychee, passion fruit, kiwi, dragon fruit, red berries)
Soy lecithin (or other food-grade emulsifier for foam)
Micro mint leaves or edible flowers

instructions: Prepare Jasmine-Coconut Consommé: Heat coconut water and sugar in a small saucepan until sugar dissolves. Do not boil. Remove from heat. Add jasmine tea bags. Steep for 10 minutes. Remove tea bags. Chill consommé completely, at least 2 hours.

Prepare Toasted Almonds: Preheat oven to 160°C. Spread slivered almonds on a baking sheet. Toast for 5-7 minutes until lightly golden and fragrant. Watch carefully to prevent burning. Cool completely.
Prepare Framboise Air: In a tall container, combine Framboise Eau de Vie, 100 ml water, and soy lecithin. Use an immersion blender at an angle to create a stable foam on the surface. Set aside.

Prepare Fruits: Wash and meticulously prepare all fruits. Peel mango and cut into small, precise 1 cm cubes. Peel kiwi and cut into similar cubes. Halve lychees. Scoop passion fruit pulp. Cut dragon fruit into small spheres using a melon baller. Gently mix prepared fruits.

Assemble Dish: Ladle chilled Jasmine-Coconut Consommé into the bottom of four wide, shallow designer bowls or plates. Arrange a small, artful cluster of mixed fresh fruit in the center of each bowl. Ensure a natural, organic composition with ample negative space.

Garnish: Carefully spoon a cloud of Framboise Air next to the fruit cluster. Sprinkle a few toasted almond slivers over the fruit and consommé. Place one single micro mint leaf or small edible flower petal delicately on the fruit for a final touch.
notes: Ensure all fruits are perfectly ripe for optimal flavor and texture.
The quality of Framboise Eau de Vie significantly impacts the final aroma and taste of the air.

recipes.recipe_name: Coconut Jasmine Mousse, Almond Praline Crisp, Raspberry Gel
recipes.visual_description: The individual dessert is elegantly presented on a pristine, round white bone china plate, centered on a light superpremium wooden table. A perfectly formed, smooth, pale ivory Jasmine Coconut Mousse dome anchors one side of the plate, its surface catching the light. Beside it, a scattering of irregular, golden-brown Almond Praline Crisp shards provides textural contrast and a warm hue. A few deliberate, glossy ruby-red dots or a delicate swirl of Framboise Fluid Gel are precisely piped around the mousse and praline, offering a vibrant burst of color and a sense of movement. Standing upright or leaning against the mousse is a thin, architectural Croissant Tuile, its golden-amber, delicate layers hinting at flakiness. The composition utilizes abundant negative space, highlighting each element's refined execution. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing the dish's sculptural quality. A precisely folded white linen napkin completes the ultra-minimalist, high-end setting.
instructions: Prepare Jasmine Tea Infusion: Steep jasmine tea in 100 ml hot water for 5 minutes. Strain, pressing solids. Reserve 80 ml strong tea.

Make Jasmine Coconut Mousse: Bloom gelatin in cold water. In a saucepan, combine coconut cream, 50g sugar, and 80 ml jasmine tea infusion. Heat gently until sugar dissolves. Do not boil. Remove from heat. Squeeze excess water from gelatin and stir into hot coconut mixture until fully dissolved. Chill mixture in an ice bath until it starts to thicken but is still liquid (20-30 minutes). Whip heavy cream to soft peaks. Gently fold whipped cream into the chilled coconut-jasmine mixture until homogenous. Pour mousse into desired molds (e.g., small dome or cylinder silicone molds). Chill for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight, until set.

Prepare Almond Praline Crisp: Preheat oven to 160°C. Spread almonds on a baking sheet. Toast for 8-10 minutes until golden. Cool. Melt 50g sugar in a dry saucepan over medium heat until it caramelizes to a light amber. Add toasted almonds. Stir to coat. Pour onto a silicone mat. Let cool completely. Break cooled praline into pieces. Process in a food processor until a coarse, sandy texture forms. In a bowl, combine 20g melted butter, 15g flour, and pinch of salt. Mix in the processed almond praline. Spread mixture thinly on a silicone mat. Bake at 160°C for 10-12 minutes until golden brown and crisp. Cool completely. Break into irregular shards.

Make Framboise Fluid Gel: Blend raspberries with 20g sugar and 50 ml water until smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve to remove seeds. Transfer strained puree to a small saucepan. Whisk in agar-agar powder. Bring to a boil, whisking constantly, and simmer for 1 minute. Remove from heat. Stir in Framboise Eau de Vie. Pour into a shallow dish and chill until set (30 minutes). Once set, transfer the firm gel to a blender. Blend until completely smooth and fluid. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve. Store in a squeeze bottle in the refrigerator.

Bake Croissant Tuile: Preheat oven to 180°C. Roll puff pastry very thinly (1-2 mm thick). Cut into desired shapes (e.g., irregular shards, small rectangles). Brush lightly with melted butter and sprinkle with sugar. Bake on parchment-lined baking sheet for 8-12 minutes, or until golden brown and very crisp. Watch carefully. Let cool completely on a wire rack.

Assembly: Carefully unmold the set Jasmine Coconut Mousse portions. Place one mousse on one side of each chilled serving plate. Arrange a few irregular shards of Almond Praline Crisp beside the mousse. Pipe a few dots or a delicate swirl of Framboise Fluid Gel around the mousse and praline. Gently place one Croissant Tuile piece standing upright or leaning against the mousse.

recipes.recipe_name: Jasmine Coconut Chocolate Entremet
recipes.visual_description: A single, precisely cut slice of a multi-layered entremet stands elegantly centered on a pristine white porcelain plate with a delicate gold rim. The slice, cut with a hot, clean knife, reveals distinct, architectural layers: a light, tender almond financier sponge, a rich, dark chocolate crémeux, and a creamy, airy coconut mousse. The top of the entremet is coated in a glossy, obsidian-black mirror glaze, reflecting the subtle dramatic professional lighting. The glaze's surface is perfectly smooth, hinting at the delicate jasmine tea aroma within. A single, delicate gold leaf is precisely placed on the top corner of the slice, catching the light. The plate features abundant negative space, emphasizing the dessert's refined simplicity and sophisticated construction. The background is an ultra-minimalist white marble surface, allowing the entremet to be the sole focal point, embodying haute patisserie elegance.

ingredients.name: Dark Chocolate Crémeux
ingredients.quantity: 100 g dark chocolate (70% cocoa), finely chopped

ingredients.name: Jasmine Mirror Glaze
ingredients.quantity: 1 tsp jasmine tea extract or 1 tbsp very strong jasmine tea infusion

instructions: Prepare a 15x15 cm square mold or small loaf pan, line with plastic wrap.

For the Almond Financier Sponge: Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat until browned and fragrant (beurre noisette). Strain and cool slightly. Sift powdered sugar, all-purpose flour, and almond flour into a bowl. Add egg whites and whisk until just combined. Gradually whisk in the cooled browned butter until smooth. Pour batter into a 15x15 cm square baking pan lined with parchment paper. Bake at 170°C (340°F) for 12-15 minutes, until golden. Cool completely. Cut into two 14x14 cm squares.
For the Jasmine Tea & Framboise Syrup: Steep jasmine tea bag in 100 ml hot water for 5 minutes. Remove tea bag. Stir in granulated sugar until dissolved. Let cool. Stir in Framboise Eau de Vie.

For the Dark Chocolate Crémeux: Heat heavy cream in a saucepan until simmering. In a separate bowl, whisk egg yolks and granulated sugar. Gradually pour hot cream into egg mixture, whisking constantly. Return mixture to saucepan. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly with a spatula, until thickened slightly and coats the back of a spoon (82°C/180°F). Do not boil. Remove from heat. Pour hot custard over chopped dark chocolate. Let sit for 1 minute, then whisk from the center outwards until smooth and emulsified. Pour into a shallow dish, cover surface with plastic wrap, and chill for at least 2 hours until firm.

For the Coconut Mousse: Bloom gelatin in 15 ml cold water. Heat coconut cream and granulated sugar in a small saucepan until sugar dissolves and cream is warm. Squeeze excess water from gelatin and stir into warm coconut cream until dissolved. Let mixture cool to room temperature. Whip very cold heavy cream to soft peaks. Gently fold cooled coconut mixture into whipped cream until just combined.

Assemble the Entremet: Place one financier sponge layer at the bottom of your prepared square mold. Brush generously with Jasmine Tea & Framboise Syrup. Spread half of the Dark Chocolate Crémeux evenly over the sponge. Carefully spread half of the Coconut Mousse over the crémeux. Place the second financier sponge layer on top. Brush generously with remaining syrup. Spread remaining Dark Chocolate Crémeux, then remaining Coconut Mousse. Smooth the top. Freeze for at least 6 hours, or overnight, until completely solid.

For the Jasmine Mirror Glaze: Bloom gelatin in 40 ml cold water. In a saucepan, combine water, granulated sugar, and glucose syrup. Heat to 103°C (217°F). Remove from heat. Stir in sweetened condensed milk. Add bloomed gelatin and stir until dissolved. Pour mixture over chopped white chocolate. Let sit for 1 minute, then blend with an immersion blender until smooth and emulsified. Be careful not to incorporate air bubbles. Stir in jasmine tea extract/infusion. Let the glaze cool to 32-35°C (90-95°F).

Glaze the Entremet: Remove frozen entremet from the mold and peel off plastic wrap. Place entremet on a wire rack set over a baking sheet to catch excess glaze. Pour the cooled glaze evenly over the frozen entremet, ensuring full coverage. Let excess glaze drip off. Carefully transfer the glazed entremet to a serving plate or board using two spatulas. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours to thaw and set the glaze.
Serve: Using a hot, dry knife, slice the entremet into 4 equal portions. Clean the knife between each cut for sharp edges. Garnish as desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Tom Kha Hoy Lai (Thai Coconut Clam Soup)
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Tom Kha Hoy Lai is presented in a clean, white porcelain bowl, centered on a simple wooden table surface. The soup features a creamy, opaque off-white broth, indicative of rich coconut milk. Visible within the broth are opened, plump clams, their shells slightly contrasting with the liquid. Scattered amongst the clams are sliced oyster mushrooms, adding a subtle brown-grey hue. Thinly sliced red bird's eye chilies provide sharp bursts of color and heat, while vibrant green kaffir lime leaves and pale galangal slices are interspersed, hinting at the aromatic depth. The soup is garnished generously with fresh, bright green coriander leaves on top. A cotton napkin is neatly folded beside the bowl. Adjacent to the soup bowl, a small white rice bowl and a pair of dark wooden chopsticks are placed, completing an authentic Thai dining setup. The lighting is natural and even, highlighting the fresh ingredients and the inviting texture of the soup, with a soft, blurred restaurant-style background that maintains focus on the dish.

ingredients.name: Lemongrass, bruised and cut into 5 cm pieces
Oyster or straw mushrooms, halved if large

instructions: Clean clams thoroughly. Soak in cold water with a pinch of salt for 20 minutes. Drain.
In a large pot, combine coconut milk and stock. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat.
Add galangal, lemongrass, and kaffir lime leaves to the simmering liquid. Simmer for 5 minutes to infuse flavors.
Add mushrooms to the pot. Cook for 2 minutes.
Add cleaned clams to the pot. Cover and cook until all clams open, about 3-5 minutes. Discard any unopened clams.
Stir in fish sauce, lime juice, and palm sugar. Stir until palm sugar dissolves. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Stir in sliced bird's eye chilies.
Ladle soup into individual serving bowls. Garnish with fresh coriander leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Insalata di Granchio con Peperoncino Fermentato e Cipolle Agrodolce
recipes.visual_description: A single starter portion is elegantly presented on a small, handcrafted, unglazed ceramic plate in a natural cream hue. The focal point is a neat mound of delicate, flaked crab meat, its natural pinkish-white color providing a soft base. Nestled atop are thin, ruby-red slices of pickled red onion, their translucent, crisp texture visible. Shaved Parmesan curls delicately over the crab, adding a pale yellow accent and subtle height. A glistening drizzle of golden extra virgin olive oil unifies the components. The dish is subtly garnished with a few vibrant green fresh flat-leaf parsley leaves. The plate is positioned on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige is folded simply beside it. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene from the side, creating gentle shadows and highlighting the ingredients' inherent beauty. The background is clean and minimal, hinting at organic elements.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with small slices of crusty, rustic Italian bread for scooping
Pair with a light, crisp white wine, such as a Vermentino or Greco di Tufo
instructions: Prepare pickled red onions: Thinly slice red onion into rings. In a small saucepan, combine white wine vinegar, water, sugar, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a simmer until sugar dissolves. Pour hot liquid over sliced onions in a heatproof jar. Let cool, then refrigerate for at least 1 hour, or overnight for best flavor. These can be prepared days in advance.

Prepare fermented chili garlic paste: Finely chop red chilies and garlic. In a small, clean jar, combine chilies, garlic, and 5 grams sea salt. Mix well. Press down to remove air. Cover loosely with a lid or fermentation airlock. Store at room temperature for 3-5 days, or until bubbling and a pleasant sour aroma develops. Once fermented, store tightly sealed in the refrigerator. Alternatively, use a high-quality store-bought fermented chili paste.
Flake fresh crab meat. Ensure all shell fragments are removed. Place crab in a mixing bowl.

To the crab, add 15 ml extra virgin olive oil, zest of half a lemon, and a squeeze of lemon juice. Add 5-10 grams of the fermented chili garlic paste, adjusting to your spice preference. Season with salt and black pepper.
Gently fold all ingredients to combine, being careful not to break up the crab too much. Taste and adjust seasoning.
To serve, spoon a single portion of the crab mixture onto the center of each starter plate. Arrange a few slices of pickled red onion on top of the crab.
Using a vegetable peeler, shave Parmesan cheese directly over the dish.
Drizzle with remaining extra virgin olive oil. Garnish with a few fresh parsley leaves.
notes: The fermented chili garlic paste and pickled red onions can be prepared several days in advance, enhancing their flavor and contributing to zero-waste practices by preserving ingredients.
Ensure crab meat is of the highest quality for best flavor and texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Agnolotti di Granchio con Burro al Peperoncino e Limone
recipes.visual_description: A refined individual portion of Agnolotti di Granchio is presented on a minimalist, deep, round bone china plate with a subtle pattern, set on a pristine white Carrara marble surface. Five to seven perfectly formed golden agnolotti, each showcasing a delicate crimped edge, are artfully arranged in a flowing, organic composition on one side of the plate, leaving abundant negative space. A shimmering pool of the emulsified chili-garlic butter sauce surrounds the pasta, reflecting the ambient light. Flecks of bright red minced chili and thin slices of golden garlic are visible within the translucent sauce. The dish is precisely garnished with a sparse sprinkle of finely minced fresh chives and a few delicate curls of microplaned lemon zest, providing a contrasting green and yellow accent. The overall color palette is sophisticated, with warm golden tones of the pasta and butter sauce, contrasted by the creamy white plate. A precisely folded white linen napkin sits beside the plate. Dramatic professional lighting creates soft shadows, enhancing the dish's architectural precision and elegance. The background is ultra-minimalist, drawing full focus to the culinary masterpiece.

ingredients.name: Unsalted butter, cold, cut into cubes

instructions: Combine flours and salt on a clean surface. Form a well. Crack eggs into well. Slowly incorporate flour into eggs with a fork. Knead dough for 10-15 minutes until smooth and elastic. Wrap in cling film. Rest 30 minutes at room temperature.
Gently combine lump crab meat, drained ricotta, lemon zest, minced chives, red pepper flakes. Season with salt and pepper. Mix lightly to preserve crab texture.

Divide pasta dough into four portions. Roll one portion very thinly using a pasta machine (to setting 7 or 8). Place small mounds (approx. 1 teaspoon) of crab filling along one edge, spaced 3cm apart. Fold pasta over filling to create a long strip. Press firmly around filling to seal, expelling air. Cut into individual agnolotti using a fluted pasta wheel or knife. Place agnolotti on a semolina-dusted tray.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Gently add agnolotti. Cook for 2-3 minutes until al dente and floating. Reserve 1 cup pasta water.

While pasta cooks, melt 1 tablespoon butter in a wide pan over medium-low heat. Add thinly sliced garlic and minced chili. Sauté gently for 1 minute until fragrant; do not brown garlic. Add lemon juice.

Transfer cooked agnolotti directly into the pan with the sauce. Add 60ml reserved pasta water. Add remaining cold butter cubes, one at a time, swirling constantly until sauce emulsifies and coats pasta beautifully.
Arrange 5-7 agnolotti artfully on each warm plate. Spoon extra sauce over. Garnish with a sprinkle of finely grated Parmesan and fresh chives. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Crab and Parmesan Risotto
recipes.visual_description: The risotto is plated in a shallow white porcelain bowl, showcasing its fluid, creamy consistency. A generous portion sits centrally, with its natural flow creating soft undulations. Visible are tender, ivory-colored chunks of crab meat interspersed throughout the golden-hued rice grains. Bright flecks of crimson minced chili and vibrant green chopped parsley are scattered across the surface, providing pops of color. The texture is velvety and rich, with the glossy sheen of melted butter and cheese. A light dusting of freshly grated Parmigiano Reggiano rests on top. The plate has moderate negative space. Beside the bowl, a simple white linen napkin and a silver fork are placed. The setting is a clean, natural wood table, evoking a modern Italian bistro. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its warmth and inviting texture.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Warm crusty bread for dipping

ingredients.name: Parmigiano Reggiano
ingredients.quantity: 100g, freshly grated, plus extra for serving

instructions: Heat broth in a saucepan. Keep it hot at a simmer.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and minced chili. Cook for 1-2 minutes until fragrant. Do not brown garlic.
Add Arborio rice to the pot. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until edges of grains are translucent.
Pour in white wine. Stir until wine is completely absorbed.
Begin adding hot broth, one ladleful (about 125ml) at a time. Stir constantly.
Wait until each ladleful is almost completely absorbed before adding the next. This takes about 18-20 minutes.
Continue adding broth and stirring until rice is al dente. It should be creamy but still have a slight bite.
Remove from heat. Stir in cold butter and grated Parmigiano Reggiano. Stir vigorously until butter and cheese are melted and risotto is creamy and fluid.
Gently fold in crab meat. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Ladle risotto immediately into warm bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and extra grated Parmigiano Reggiano.

recipes.recipe_name: Crab and Chili Garlic Linguine
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Crab and Chili Garlic Linguine is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The golden linguine is loosely twirled into a natural mound at the center, allowing for a slight spiral shape. Chunks of succulent white and pink crab meat are generously distributed throughout the pasta, visibly nestled within the strands. Bright red chili slices and vibrant green chopped parsley are sprinkled over the top, providing sharp color contrast and freshness. A delicate sheen of olive oil sauce coats the pasta, indicating a well-emulsified finish. The texture of the al dente pasta is evident, alongside the tender crab and crisp chili. The dish is framed by moderate negative space on the plate. The setting features a simple wooden table surface, a white linen napkin folded neatly beside the plate, and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish from above, highlighting its inviting colors and textures in a professional, approachable manner.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple side salad of mixed greens
Serve with a crusty ciabatta bread to sop up the delicious sauce
instructions: Boil 4 litres of salted water in a large pot. Add 320g linguine. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 250ml pasta water. Drain pasta.
While pasta cooks, heat 60ml extra virgin olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add 1 finely diced small yellow onion or shallot. Sauté 3 minutes until softened.
Add 6 finely sliced garlic cloves and 2 thinly sliced red chilies to the skillet. Sauté 2 minutes until fragrant. Do not brown garlic.
Stir in 15g tomato paste. Cook 1 minute.
Pour in 120ml dry white wine. Bring to a simmer. Cook 2 minutes to reduce slightly.
Add 400g picked crab meat to the skillet. Gently toss to combine. Cook 1 minute to warm through.
Add drained linguine to the skillet. Add 120ml reserved pasta water. Toss vigorously to emulsify the sauce.
Gradually add 80g freshly grated Parmesan cheese, tossing constantly. Add more pasta water if needed for desired consistency.
Remove from heat. Stir in 30g chopped fresh parsley and the zest of 1 lemon. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Fegato alla Veneziana with Creamy Polenta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Fegato alla Veneziana is elegantly presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Pan-seared calf liver medallions, approximately 1 cm thick, exhibit a rich, golden-brown crust with tender interiors. They are nestled beside a generous mound of creamy, soft polenta, its pale yellow hue contrasting beautifully with the deeper tones of the meat. A substantial portion of thinly sliced, deeply caramelized yellow onions, glistening with butter and pan juices, cascades over the liver. A vibrant sprinkle of freshly chopped flat-leaf parsley adds a pop of bright green and freshness. The dish is arranged organically, allowing the textures and colors to speak. The setting features a rustic wooden table, a simple cotton napkin, and classic flatware, embodying a modern bistro aesthetic with authentic Italian simplicity. The lighting is natural and even, highlighting the dish's warmth and inviting textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread to sop up the delicious sauce.
A simple green salad with a light vinaigrette makes a refreshing accompaniment.
instructions: Thinly slice yellow onions. Set aside.

Prepare polenta: Bring 800 ml water or broth to a boil in a heavy-bottomed pot. Slowly whisk in cornmeal. Reduce heat to low. Cook, stirring frequently, for 20-30 minutes until thick and creamy. Stir in 15g butter, grated Parmesan, salt, and pepper. Keep warm.
Pat calf liver slices dry with paper towels. Dust lightly with all-purpose flour, shaking off excess.
Heat 30g butter and 30ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-low heat.
Add sliced onions to the skillet. Cook slowly, stirring occasionally, for 15-20 minutes until very soft and deeply caramelized. Do not rush this step.
Remove cooked onions from skillet. Keep warm.

Increase heat to medium-high. Add remaining 15g butter to the skillet. Sear liver slices in batches for 1-2 minutes per side until browned and cooked through. Avoid overcrowding the pan. Liver should be slightly pink in the center, not grey. Remove liver from skillet and keep warm.
Pour dry white wine into the hot skillet. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom. Simmer for 1-2 minutes until slightly reduced.
Return cooked liver and caramelized onions to the skillet with the wine sauce. Toss gently to combine and coat. Season with salt and freshly ground black pepper.
Finely chop fresh parsley. Stir half of the parsley into the liver and onion mixture.

Serve immediately. Spoon a generous portion of creamy polenta onto each plate. Arrange pan-seared calf liver medallions and caramelized onions beside or over the polenta. Garnish with remaining fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Do not overcook the liver; it becomes tough quickly. It should remain slightly pink inside.
Caramelizing the onions slowly is crucial for developing their sweet flavor and soft texture.
traditional_techniques: Soffritto (for the slow cooking of onions)

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Thai Fried Chicken Wings (Gai Tod Prik)
recipes.visual_description: Golden-brown, crispy fried chicken wings are casually piled on a rustic, round ceramic platter with an earthy glaze. The wings are whole, showcasing their natural shape and crunchy exterior. A small, simple ceramic dipping bowl, perhaps in a complementary dark green or brown, sits alongside, filled with the vibrant red and green chili-garlic-tomato sauce. The sauce shows visible minced garlic, thinly sliced green chilies, and small diced tomato pieces. A few fresh coriander leaves are scattered over the chicken and around the sauce for a fresh accent. The platter rests on a well-worn, light wooden dining table, revealing its natural grain. A casually folded, off-white linen napkin is placed nearby. The scene is illuminated by warm, soft lighting, mimicking natural kitchen light, creating a cozy and inviting atmosphere. The background is minimal, showing only a blurred hint of a home kitchen setting. The platter holds a generous, shareable portion of about 12-16 chicken wings, arranged to invite communal eating.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Enjoy as a shared snack or appetizer.
Often served with sticky rice (khao niao) or as part of a larger meal.
Eaten with hands or chopsticks.
instructions: Pat chicken wings dry with paper towels.

In a large bowl, combine 30 ml fish sauce, 15 ml soy sauce, and 5 g sugar. Add chicken wings. Mix well to coat. Marinate for at least 30 minutes at room temperature, or up to 2 hours in the refrigerator.
Mince 3 garlic cloves, 2-3 green chilies, and half of the red onion. Dice the tomato into small cubes.

In a small bowl, combine remaining 30 ml fish sauce, 15 ml soy sauce, 10 g sugar, and 30 ml lime juice. Stir until sugar dissolves. Add minced garlic, chilies, onion, and diced tomato. Mix well to create the dipping sauce.
Just before frying, add rice flour or cornstarch to the marinated chicken wings. Toss until each wing is lightly coated.
Pour vegetable oil into a deep pot or wok. Heat to 175°C.
Carefully add chicken wings to the hot oil in batches. Do not overcrowd the pot. Fry for 8-10 minutes. Turn occasionally.
Chicken is cooked when golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken with a slotted spoon.
Place fried chicken on a wire rack over paper towels to drain excess oil.
Arrange fried chicken wings on a serving platter. Serve immediately with the spicy dipping sauce. Garnish with fresh coriander.
notes: For extra crispiness, consider a double-fry: fry once at 160°C for 6-7 minutes, then increase heat to 190°C and fry again for 2-3 minutes until deeply golden and crisp.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Tomato and Pickled Red Onion Salad
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a handcrafted, natural beige ceramic plate, resting on a light reclaimed wood surface. Diced fresh and fermented tomatoes, vibrant red and slightly varied in texture, are artfully arranged with thinly sliced, deep purple pickled red onions. Each component maintains its distinct shape. A light, glistening chili-garlic dressing is subtly drizzled over, catching the soft natural light. Fresh green parsley leaves are scattered sparingly for a pop of color. Crispy, golden-brown garlic skin crisps are strategically placed as a zero-waste garnish, adding textural contrast. The composition is minimalistic, emphasizing natural colors and textures, with ample negative space. A natural undyed linen napkin and a simple glass of water complete the eco-conscious setting, against a clean background with subtle green plant elements.
instructions: Prepare fermented tomatoes: Dice 250g tomatoes. Place in a clean, sanitized jar. Add 1 teaspoon salt. Cover with non-chlorinated water. Seal loosely. Ferment at room temperature for 2-3 days until slightly bubbly and tangy. Drain before use.

Prepare pickled red onions: Thinly slice red onions. Pack into a clean, sanitized jar. In a small saucepan, heat 120ml water, 30ml apple cider vinegar, 1 teaspoon salt, and 1/2 teaspoon sugar until dissolved. Pour hot brine over onions. Seal. Refrigerate for a minimum of 1 hour, ideally overnight. Drain before use.

Prepare garlic skin crisps: Peel garlic cloves, reserving the skins. Toss skins with a tiny amount of olive oil and a pinch of salt. Spread on a baking sheet. Bake at 160°C until crispy and golden. Watch carefully to prevent burning.

Make chili-garlic dressing: Mince remaining 2 garlic cloves and the fresh red chili finely. In a small bowl, combine minced garlic, chili, 60ml olive oil, 30ml apple cider vinegar, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Whisk well until emulsified.
Assemble salad: Dice remaining fresh tomatoes. In a large bowl, combine the diced fresh tomatoes, drained fermented tomatoes, and drained pickled red onions.

Dress and serve: Pour the prepared chili-garlic dressing over the salad ingredients. Gently toss to combine. Plate the salad. Garnish with fresh parsley or basil and the crispy garlic skin crisps. Serve immediately.
notes: Use ripe, seasonal tomatoes for the best flavor and texture.
Ensure all jars for fermentation and pickling are thoroughly cleaned and sanitized.

recipes.recipe_name: Pad Prik Gaeng Gai (Stir-fried Chicken with Red Curry Paste)
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pad Prik Gaeng Gai is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The dish features irregular chunks of seared chicken, vibrant red cherry tomato halves, green long bean pieces, and translucent onion wedges, all coated in a glossy, rich red curry sauce. A generous scattering of fresh green Thai basil leaves rests on top. The chicken pieces are whole and not fanned. A small, neat mound of white jasmine rice is placed beside the stir-fry. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface. A neatly folded cotton napkin is placed to the side. Traditional Thai eating utensils, a spoon and a fork, are arranged beside the plate. The scene is illuminated with natural, even lighting, creating a warm and inviting atmosphere. The background is minimal and unobtrusive, focusing entirely on the vibrant dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with freshly steamed jasmine rice.
Offer additional fish sauce or sliced chilies on the side for individual seasoning.
instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a large wok or deep skillet over medium-high heat.
Add Thai red curry paste to the hot oil. Stir-fry for 1-2 minutes until very fragrant.
Add chicken chunks to the wok. Stir-fry for 5-7 minutes until chicken is cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Add minced garlic, sliced red chilies, onion wedges, and long bean pieces to the wok. Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until vegetables are tender-crisp.
Stir in halved cherry tomatoes and torn kaffir lime leaves.
Season the dish with fish sauce and palm sugar. Stir well to dissolve the sugar and combine flavors.
Remove from heat. Stir in Thai basil leaves until just wilted.
Serve immediately with steamed jasmine rice.
traditional_techniques: Balancing sweet, sour, salty, and spicy flavors

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Spiced Squash Pie
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous slice of Classic Spiced Squash Pie rests on a simple, round ceramic plate. The pie slice is cleanly cut, revealing a flaky, golden-brown crust and a smooth, creamy, vibrant orange filling. A dollop of unsweetened whipped cream sits atop the pie slice. The plate is placed on a well-used wooden dining table, characteristic of a homely family kitchen. A simple, everyday fork is casually positioned beside the plate. The scene is bathed in warm, cozy lighting, creating a relaxed, lived-in atmosphere typical of a family meal. The background is minimal, focusing attention on the comforting dessert. No decorative elements are present, just the inviting pie ready to be enjoyed.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Combine squash puree, brown sugar, eggs, evaporated milk, cinnamon, nutmeg, ginger, cloves, and salt in a large bowl. Whisk until smooth.
Pour mixture into the pie crust.
Bake for 45-55 minutes, or until a knife inserted near the center comes out clean.
Cool completely on a wire rack.
Serve chilled, optionally with whipped cream.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Turkey and Vegetable Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of hearty turkey and vegetable soup is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl on a well-worn wooden kitchen table. The soup is filled to a natural level, showcasing abundant ingredients. Visible are substantial chunks of cooked turkey, 2 cm cubes, interspersed with vibrant orange carrot rounds and pale green celery slices, both 1 cm thick. Small, tender potato cubes, 1.5 cm, add comforting texture. Bright green peas are scattered throughout. The clear, golden broth allows ingredients to stand out. Fresh, roughly chopped parsley is casually sprinkled on top as a simple garnish. A plain metal spoon rests beside the bowl. A folded cloth napkin is nearby. Warm kitchen lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing the homely atmosphere. The background is minimal.

ingredients.name: Cooked turkey breast, cut into 2 cm cubes
Carrots, peeled and cut into 1 cm rounds
Celery stalks, cut into 1 cm slices
Potatoes, peeled and cut into 1.5 cm cubes

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add carrot rounds and celery slices. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly tender.
Add chicken broth, dried thyme, and bay leaf. Bring to a boil.
Add potato cubes. Reduce heat to medium-low. Simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until potatoes are tender.
Stir in cooked turkey cubes and frozen green peas. Cook for 3-5 minutes, until turkey is heated through and peas are bright green.
Remove bay leaf. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Ladle hot soup into individual bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Scallop Lemon Garlic Linguine
recipes.visual_description: A generous swirl of golden linguine forms the base, centrally placed on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The pasta glistens with a light lemon-garlic sauce, showing hints of fresh green parsley flecks and a subtle warmth from red pepper flakes. Four to five perfectly seared large sea scallops are arranged artfully on top of the pasta swirl. Each scallop has a beautiful golden-brown crust on both sides, contrasting with their translucent white interior. The vibrant yellow of the pasta and lemon zest contrasts with the rich golden-brown of the scallops. Bright green parsley provides fresh accents. The dish is presented on a simple light wooden table surface. A white cotton napkin is neatly folded beside the plate. A silver fork is placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish from above, highlighting textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty artisanal bread for dipping in the sauce.
A light green salad with a vinaigrette complements the dish.
instructions: Cook linguine according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 120ml pasta water. Drain.
Pat scallops very dry with paper towels. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add half the scallops. Sear 2-3 minutes per side until golden-brown and opaque. Remove. Repeat with remaining scallops.
Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 15ml olive oil and butter to the skillet. Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits. Simmer 2 minutes until slightly reduced.
Add chicken broth and lemon juice. Bring to a simmer. Cook 3-4 minutes until sauce thickens slightly.
Add cooked linguine to the skillet. Toss to coat. Add reserved pasta water as needed for desired consistency.
Stir in lemon zest and chopped parsley.
Divide pasta among 4 plates. Arrange seared scallops on top of each pasta portion. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure scallops are very dry before searing for best crust.
Do not overcrowd the pan when searing scallops.

recipes.recipe_name: Tagliatelle with Wild Mushroom Ragu
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Tagliatelle with Wild Mushroom Ragu is presented in a shallow, white porcelain pasta bowl. The long, flat tagliatelle noodles are gracefully intertwined with rich, dark brown mushroom ragu. The ragu features tender, varied mushroom pieces, some sliced and some whole, showcasing their natural shapes and earthy tones. Small, finely diced pieces of carrot and celery are visible within the robust sauce, adding subtle color. A vibrant sprinkle of fresh, chopped flat-leaf parsley is scattered over the top, providing a pop of green. A generous mound of freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese rests centrally, adding a creamy white contrast. The dish has a natural, flowing arrangement, indicating it has been tossed directly with the sauce. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a silver fork and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and deep colors of the dish, creating an inviting, casual dining ambiance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with extra grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese at the table.
Offer crusty Italian bread for 'scarpetta' (soaking up leftover sauce).
instructions: Clean mushrooms. Slice larger mushrooms; leave smaller ones whole.
Dice onion, carrot, and celery into small, uniform pieces for soffritto.
Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced onion, carrot, and celery. Cook 8-10 minutes until softened and translucent. Do not brown.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add sliced mushrooms to the pot. Increase heat to medium-high. Sauté mushrooms 8-10 minutes until browned and tender. Cook off moisture.
Pour in red wine. Deglaze the pot, scraping up any browned bits. Simmer 3-5 minutes until wine reduces by half.
Add vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook 20-25 minutes, allowing flavors to meld and sauce to thicken slightly.
Season mushroom ragu with salt and pepper to taste.
While ragu simmers, cook tagliatelle according to package directions in salted boiling water until al dente.
Reserve 120 ml pasta cooking water. Drain pasta.
Add drained tagliatelle directly to the mushroom ragu. Toss to coat pasta evenly.
If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water a little at a time until desired consistency is reached.
Chop fresh parsley.
Serve immediately. Garnish each portion with chopped parsley and grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese.

recipes.recipe_name: Pappardelle with Slow-Braised Beef Ragu
recipes.visual_description: A generous portion of wide, flat pappardelle pasta is artfully swirled on a clean white porcelain plate. The pasta is richly coated in a deep, glossy, reddish-brown beef ragu. Visible within the sauce are tender, pulled chunks of slow-braised beef short ribs, showcasing their dark, caramelized edges and succulent texture. Small, finely diced pieces of softened carrots, celery, and onion from the soffritto are interspersed throughout the rich sauce, adding subtle pops of color and texture. A sprinkle of vibrant green, freshly chopped parsley is scattered over the top, providing a fresh contrast. A generous dusting of finely grated pale yellow Parmesan cheese melts slightly into the warm ragu. The dish is presented with moderate negative space, highlighting the rustic elegance of the pasta and ragu.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping.
Pair with a robust red wine like Chianti or Merlot.

ingredients.name: Beef Short Ribs
ingredients.quantity: 1 kg, bone-in, cut into 5-7 cm chunks

instructions: Pat beef short ribs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear short ribs on all sides until deeply browned. Remove ribs and set aside.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until fragrant and tomato paste darkens slightly.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer and cook until wine is mostly reduced, about 5-7 minutes.
Return seared short ribs to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes, beef stock, rosemary, thyme, and bay leaf. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot and braise for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender. Stir occasionally.
Remove short ribs from the pot. Shred the meat from the bones using two forks. Discard bones and any excess fat/gristle. Return shredded meat to the sauce.
If sauce is too thin, simmer uncovered for 10-15 minutes to reduce. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Cook pappardelle in a large pot of salted boiling water according to package directions until al dente.
Drain pasta. Add drained pasta directly to the ragu in the pot. Toss well to coat the pasta.
Serve immediately. Garnish with freshly grated Parmesan cheese and chopped fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Pork Chops with Caramelized Apples and Cider Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A pan-seared pork chop, golden-brown with a distinct seared crust, is positioned centrally on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Beside it, tender, caramelized apple wedges and soft, translucent thin onion rings are artfully arranged, glistening with a rich, glossy cider glaze. The glaze, a warm amber hue, pools invitingly around the elements. A few vibrant green fresh sage leaves are scattered for a pop of color and aromatic freshness. The pork chop is presented as a whole piece, showcasing its succulent interior. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple, light wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cream-colored linen napkin and classic silver flatware, evoking a modern bistro ambiance under natural, even lighting.

ingredients.name: Firm apples (e.g., Honeycrisp, Fuji)
ingredients.quantity: 2 large, cored and cut into 8 wedges each

ingredients.name: Fresh sage leaves
ingredients.quantity: 5g, roughly chopped, plus a few whole leaves for garnish

instructions: Season pork chops generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Sear pork chops for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Internal temperature should reach 70°C. Remove chops and set aside.
Add butter to the same skillet. Add onion slices. Sauté for 5 minutes until softened and translucent.
Add apple wedges to the skillet. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until apples are tender and slightly caramelized.
Pour in apple cider and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet.
Add chopped sage. Reduce heat to medium-low. Simmer for 8-10 minutes, or until the sauce slightly thickens.
Return pork chops to the skillet. Spoon the sauce over the chops. Cook for 1-2 minutes to warm through. Ensure internal temperature of pork reaches 75°C.
Serve immediately with the caramelized apples, onions, and cider glaze. Garnish each plate with a few fresh whole sage leaves.
notes: Choose firm, sweet-tart apples that hold their shape well when cooked, such as Honeycrisp, Fuji, or Granny Smith.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Italian Sausage & White Bean Ragout with Creamy Polenta
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple wooden table surface. A generous, creamy mound of golden-yellow polenta forms the base, its soft texture visible. Over the polenta, a rich, rustic ragout of chunky Italian sausage and cannellini beans is spooned, creating a vibrant contrast of colors and textures. The sausage pieces are browned and irregular chunks, not sliced, showcasing their hearty nature. Diced red bell peppers and onion are interspersed throughout the deep red tomato-based sauce. A sprinkle of bright green, freshly chopped parsley or basil adds a pop of color and freshness. Grated Parmesan cheese lightly dusts the ragout. The overall presentation is inviting and abundant, with moderate negative space. Beside the plate, a simple cotton napkin and traditional silver flatware are neatly arranged. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's warmth and inviting textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread
Serve with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette
instructions: Remove sausage from casings. Break into large, irregular chunks.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Brown sausage chunks until cooked through and lightly caramelized. Remove sausage and set aside.
Add diced onion and red bell pepper to the pot. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and cannellini beans. Bring to a simmer.
Return sausage chunks to the pot. Reduce heat to low. Simmer gently 20 minutes, allowing flavors to meld. Season with salt and pepper.
While ragout simmers, prepare polenta. Bring 800ml water or broth to a boil in a separate saucepan. Slowly whisk in polenta.
Reduce heat to low. Cook polenta, stirring frequently, 15-20 minutes until creamy and thick.
Stir in butter and grated Parmesan cheese until melted and smooth. Season with salt.
Ladle creamy polenta onto individual plates. Top with generous portions of the sausage and white bean ragout.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley or basil and extra grated Parmesan.
notes: Adjust red pepper flakes to desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Italian Sausage with Creamy Polenta and Broccolini
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A generous dollop of creamy, golden polenta forms the base, its soft, inviting texture visible. Resting atop the polenta are two perfectly browned Italian sausages, their skins caramelized to a rich mahogany, showing slight char marks. The sausages are whole, plump, and uncut. Alongside, a vibrant cluster of bright green broccolini spears, tender-crisp with visible char, is artfully arranged. Thin slices of golden garlic cling to the broccolini. A scattering of fresh, finely chopped dark green parsley adds a final pop of color and freshness. The composition is balanced with moderate negative space, highlighting the rich colors and varying textures. The plate sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware, under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Offer crusty Italian bread for dipping in leftover polenta.
Pair with a robust red wine like Chianti.
instructions: Bring broth to a simmer in a large saucepan. Gradually whisk in polenta. Reduce heat to low. Stir frequently for 20-25 minutes until thick and creamy. Stir in butter and Parmigiano Reggiano. Season with salt. Keep warm.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add sausages. Cook for 12-15 minutes, turning occasionally, until browned and cooked through. Remove sausages from skillet. Keep warm.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil to the same skillet. Add sliced garlic. Sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add broccolini. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until tender-crisp. Season with salt and pepper.
Spoon creamy polenta onto individual plates. Place cooked sausages on top of polenta. Arrange sautéed broccolini alongside. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Pasta Fagioli Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chicken and Pasta Fagioli Soup is presented in a deep, clean white porcelain bowl, resting on a simple wooden table surface. The rich, rustic red-orange broth is visible, holding tender, golden-brown chicken chunks, creamy white cannellini beans, small al dente ditalini pasta, and vibrant diced red bell pepper and onion. A generous sprinkle of freshly grated Parmesan cheese melts slightly on top, with a few fresh green basil leaves placed delicately as a garnish. The soup's textures are varied: the softness of beans, the chew of pasta, and the tender chicken. Natural, even lighting highlights the steam rising gently from the hot soup. A white cotton napkin is folded neatly beside the bowl, and a traditional silver soup spoon rests on the table, contributing to a modern bistro setting with an authentic Italian feel. The background is minimal, allowing the dish to be the focal point while suggesting a casual restaurant ambiance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping.
Offer additional grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 2-3 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks. Sear until browned on all sides, about 5-7 minutes. Remove chicken and set aside.
Dice onion and red bell pepper into 1 cm pieces. Mince garlic.
Add diced onion and bell pepper to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes, chicken broth, dried oregano, and dried basil. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken to the pot. Reduce heat to medium-low. Simmer for 15 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Add pasta to the soup. Cook according to package directions until al dente, about 8-10 minutes.
